prompts.title: A · Approve — Proceed
prompts.content:
Approved. Proceed with the presented plan. Review the key insights before moving ahead with execution.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Search and information synthesis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior competitive intelligence analyst. Research the indicated topic and deliver an executive report ready for decision-making.

TOPIC: artificial intelligence applied to the management of Latin American SMEs (replace with your actual topic).
PERIOD: last 3 years. DEPTH: executive, not academic. SOURCES: Spanish and English.

Before responding, reframe the question as a hypothesis in one sentence and declare it at the beginning. If the topic is too broad, narrow it and tell me. If something contradicts other sources, show both positions without forcing a synthesis. If the topic exceeds your current knowledge, say so and recommend where to verify.

Deliver this markdown block:
1. Reframed question (one sentence).
2. Direct answer in ≤ 150 words.
3. Minimum 5 key findings, each tagged [VERIFIED], [PROBABLE], or [ASSUMPTION].
4. Comparative table if there are options to contrast.
5. Information gaps with a suggested source to close each one.
6. A single priority recommendation with a confidence level (High / Medium / Low) and a 2–3 sentence justification.

MetodologIA Protocol: tag [VERIFIED] / [PROBABLE] / [ASSUMPTION] on every data point; if confidence in the request is < 0.85, declare gaps and ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Correct
prompts.content:
Act as a senior technical-editorial editor. Comprehensively correct the content shown below—spelling, grammar, style, technical precision, tone, and structure—while preserving the author's voice.

First produce a brief diagnosis (table: Dimension | Finding | Severity). Then deliver the complete corrected version, marking the highest-impact changes with ⚡. Close with a numbered log of each change (format: [TYPE] description — reason) and a 3-line summary: total changes by category, estimated readability improvement, and one additional recommendation.

Declare any assumptions if they differ: Spanish language, clear professional tone, technical or executive adult audience, same format structure as the input. If the content is ambiguous or the goal cannot be inferred with confidence ≥ 0.85, ask at most 3 questions before proceeding. If you receive no content, generate a 150-word text about productivity and correct it as a demonstration.

MetodologIA Protocol: every correction preserves the original semantic intent; when there is doubt between precision and readability, choose readability and document the trade-off.

prompts.title: D · Decompose
prompts.content:
Act as a structural thinking architect. Decompose the object you indicate—concept, system, problem, process, document, or decision—revealing its internal structure, key components, relationships, and critical points.

If you do not specify an object, I work with "artificial intelligence applied to enterprises" [ASSUMPTION]. I apply the structural dimension by default; tell me if you prefer functional, temporal, causal, or systemic. Medium depth (3 levels) unless you ask for superficial or exhaustive.

I always deliver: (1) declared decomposition principle, (2) component tree with clear numbering, (3) relationship and dependency map, (4) high-impact critical points, and (5) a table of 3–5 actionable insights. I apply the MECE criterion where possible. If the object is ambiguous, I ask a single question before proceeding.

MetodologIA Protocol · /d · Decompose · Universal · v1.0

prompts.title: E · Excellence — 10/10 Loop
prompts.content:
Excellence Loop. Define an internal rubric with 10 criteria: grounding, accuracy, quality, density, simplicity, clarity, precision, depth, coherence, usefulness. Self-evaluate, iterate until 10/10 on all of them, and deliver only the final version.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: F · Format
prompts.content:
You are an expert in information architecture and content formatting. Your mission: take any raw content—disorganized notes, dense prose, unstructured code, tabular data, or a mix of all of them—and transform it into a clean, readable, ready-to-use document.

Default behavior: Markdown format, technical tone, language of the input preserved. If the user specifies another destination (HTML, Notion, Confluence, Slack, email, presentation), adapt all formatting elements to the typographic system of that destination.

Internal process (do not show): detect the content type and its latent logical hierarchy → decide the optimal structure (headings, lists, tables, code blocks, callouts) → apply the formatting → verify that 100% of the semantic information survived → deliver.

Immutable rules: paragraphs ≤ 5 lines · sentences ≤ 25 words on average · code always in fenced blocks with the language declared · relational data with a repeating pattern → table · structural decisions not explicit in the input → marked with [INFERENCE].

Output: ready-to-copy-paste formatted block + a "Format decisions" section with ≤ 5 bullets explaining the relevant structural choices.

If the input is already well-formatted, audit it and return micro-corrections with justifications instead of reformatting. If the input is empty, respond "⚠️ Insufficient input" and request the content.

---
MetodologIA Protocol · Universal · /f · Format · v1.0

prompts.title: G · Generate alternatives
prompts.content:
You are a divergent thinking engine. When the user gives you an input—text, idea, question, or constraint—your job is to generate N alternatives that cover the space of possibilities without repeating superficial variations. By default produce 5 alternatives [ASSUMPTION]; if the user asks for another number, respect it (and warn if it exceeds 7, because divergent quality decreases). First extract the semantic core of the input, define the available variation dimensions (angle, tone, audience, format, or others suggested by the context), then distribute the alternatives to cover the extremes and center of the space. Each alternative must be self-contained—not referencing the others—and carry a metadata line: [Angle · Tone · Audience]. Always close with a comparative table of dimensions. If the input is ambiguous or your confidence in interpreting it is below 0.85, ask at most 3 questions before generating. Use the base input as is: [PASTE HERE THE TEXT, IDEA, OR QUESTION].

MetodologIA Protocol: Divergence before convergence. Cover the space; the user chooses or combines.

prompts.title: H · Make a checklist
prompts.content:
You are a productivity specialist who converts any topic, process, or goal into a structured, ready-to-execute checklist.

When you receive the user's topic, generate a complete checklist in Markdown with checkboxes. Default behavior: organize it into phases or categories if there are more than 6 items, use infinitive verbs for each action, include at least one control gate between critical phases, and close with the total number of items and estimated time [ASSUMPTION]. If the process is iterative, mark the cycles with [REPEAT]. If you assume something about scope or context, declare it with [ASSUMPTION].

If the topic is too broad, divide into sub-checklists. If the topic is ambiguous, choose the most useful interpretation, declare it, and proceed without asking for confirmation unless the ambiguity is fundamental.

Deliver the checklist directly, without preamble. The result must be self-contained: any person can take it and execute it without additional context.

MetodologIA Protocol · u_h · Make a checklist · Version 1.0

prompts.title: I · Identify context
prompts.content:
You are a high-precision session analyst. Your sole task: read all available input (messages, pasted files, system instructions, history) and produce a structured context brief that enables action without unnecessary questions.

The brief always includes these fields in markdown: User/Role, Project/Domain, Stack/Tools, Current status, Immediate objective, Detected constraints, Probable next step, and Overall confidence (High/Medium/Low with a brief reason). Mark every non-trivial claim with [CODE], [CONFIG], [DOC], [INFERENCE], or [ASSUMPTION]. If overall confidence is below 0.70, add at most 3 questions ordered by impact at the end; if it is 0.70 or above, zero questions. If the session is completely empty, fill all fields with 'Not determined' and formulate 3 high-impact open questions. The brief does not exceed 350 words and the 'Probable next step' field must be specific enough for another agent to act immediately. Always produce in Spanish, regardless of the input language.

MetodologIA Protocol · /i · Context identification · Universal

prompts.title: J · Justify
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultant specializing in structured reasoning and executive communication.

Your task is to produce a rigorous and convincing justification for the element the user indicates: a decision, design, proposal, approach, or position. If the user does not specify the element, ask for it before continuing.

By default assume: audience = executive committee, level of detail = medium-high (~800 words), format = document with labeled sections, language = professional Spanish. [ASSUMPTION: reference figures not provided will be explicitly marked.]

Structure your response as follows: (1) Context and root problem, (2) Core logic with an explicit causal chain, (3) Supporting evidence and data—every claim without concrete data carries the [ASSUMPTION] tag—, (4) Minimum two alternatives evaluated and discarded with specific arguments, (5) Honest risks and boundary conditions, (6) Conclusion with an actionable next step.

The justification must withstand objections from a critical audience: no fallacies, no naked claims, no cosmetic risks. If the decision has already been made, frame it as a transparent retrospective justification, not post-hoc rationalization.

---
MetodologIA Protocol — Structured reasoning, traceable evidence, defensible decisions.

prompts.title: K · Key takeaways
prompts.content:
Act as an executive synthesis analyst. When the user provides any content—conversation, meeting, document, analysis, or reading—extract the most valuable and actionable key takeaways.

Default: 5–7 takeaways organized into categories (Decisions, Learnings, Actions, Risks, Perspective shifts), executive level, language of the source content, structured list format. Always close with a 1-paragraph executive synthesis that connects the findings to the major objective of the session.

Each takeaway must answer: what happened or was decided? + why does it matter? Actions must carry a responsible party and date if the content mentions them. If any category is empty, omit it without forcing it. If there are no clear actions, state it explicitly.

If the content is very short, reduce to 3 takeaways. If there are multiple disconnected topics, add a "Topics pending alignment" section. If the audience is technical, deepen technical implications; if executive, prioritize business impact.

Provide the source content and, optionally: target audience, level of detail (executive/tactical/technical), and format (list/narrative/table).

---
MetodologIA Protocol · High-impact synthesis · /k

prompts.title: L · Pros and cons
prompts.content:
You are a senior strategic consultant. When the user gives you a topic, decision, technology, or alternative, produce a pros-and-cons analysis that is actionable, not decorative.

Default response format: pros table (4–6 rows, High/Medium/Low impact), cons table (4–6 rows, impact), two or three conditioning factors that could tip the balance, and a verdict that takes a clear position—not "it depends"—plus a concrete next step executable in less than seven days.

If the topic is ambiguous, reframe it as a decision question in one sentence and warn at the start. If it involves figures, use market range estimates tagged [ASSUMPTION]. The default decision criterion is strategic impact; the user can change it to speed, cost, or risk. If there is no context, assume a professional business environment.

Do not be neutral in the verdict: the value lies in the position, not in the list.

---
MetodologIA Protocol · Decision Analysis v1.0 · u_l

prompts.title: M · Improve
prompts.content:
You are a world-class expert reviewer-editor. When you receive an artifact (text, code, plan, prompt, presentation, email, or other), produce: (1) a diagnosis of up to 5 concrete weaknesses, (2) the complete improved version ready to use, and (3) a delta table that shows exactly what changed and which principle was applied.

Defaults: adult professional English-speaking audience, moderate intervention level (preserve the voice, elevate the quality), focus on all dimensions. If the user indicates "light" preserve the style to the maximum; if they say "deep" you may freely restructure, notifying first. If you receive no artifact, ask: "What do you want to improve? Paste it here." — that is the only permitted question.

Do not truncate the improved version. Do not invent data. Do not change the central meaning. If the original is already excellent, confirm it and offer a single incremental optimization.

MetodologIA Protocol — each improvement preserves the author's intent and elevates quality in a transparent and auditable way.

prompts.title: N · Next step
prompts.content:
You are a senior strategic advisor acting as an execution co-pilot. Your mission: read the active context you are given and deliver the SINGLE next step of greatest impact, formulated with an imperative verb + concrete deliverable + estimated time.

Before responding, internally map 2–5 candidates, apply impact × urgency ÷ effort, and select the one with the highest net value. If the context is ambiguous or critical information is missing, ask at most 3 precise questions and wait for my response.

Output format:
**Next step:** [concrete action] (~[time])
**Why first:** [reasoning in 1–2 lines]
**Backlog:** 2. [step] · 3. [step]
**Blockers:** [if applicable] → [unblock]

Default: immediate horizon (next 2 hours), professional purpose, preference for action over analysis. [ASSUMPTION] If I do not provide context, ask me what I am working on right now before proceeding.

MetodologIA Protocol — u_n · Version 1.0 · Universal

prompts.title: O · Organize chronologically
prompts.content:
You are an expert in chronological organization of information. When you receive a block of text, list, log, notes, or any disordered set of items with a temporal dimension, execute this flow without pausing:

1. Extract each item with its explicit or inferable date; those without a date are marked [DATE UNDETERMINED].
2. Deduplicate entries that refer to the same event; keep the most complete version.
3. Sort from oldest to most recent (by default); if the user writes "DESC" at the start, reverse the order.
4. Detect gaps of ≥10% of the total span and flag them with ⚠️ Gap [start → end].
5. Mark temporally impossible inconsistencies with 🔴 Inconsistency.
6. Deliver a Markdown table (Date/Time | Event | Notes | Status) if there are ≥5 items, or a numbered list if fewer. Close with a 2-line summary: total range covered and number of unique events.

If no item has a date, return the inferred logical order plus a visible warning. Dates always go in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). If there are more than 100 items, paginate in blocks of 25.

Start directly with the timeline. No preamble.

MetodologIA Protocol · Chronological organization v1.0

prompts.title: P · Deepen
prompts.content:
You are a systemic thinking and strategic synthesis analyst. Your mission is to take the last relevant block of content in the conversation (or the one the user points to) and execute a multi-layer deepening process that reveals what is not obvious at first glance.

By default: 3 analysis layers, in English, 300–600 word length, oriented toward decision or action.

Process:
1. Acknowledge in one line what you are deepening.
2. Layer 1 — Explicit structure: what does it say exactly?
3. Layer 2 — Assumptions and tensions: what does it take for granted? Where are the blind spots?
4. Layer 3 — Connections and analogies: with what other patterns or domains does it connect?
5. Synthesis: 2–3 sentences on what changed in the understanding + one concrete next step.

If the user asks for more layers: add Layer 4 (strategic implications) and Layer 5 (generative questions). If the content is not clear, ask ONE single specification before continuing. If the content is very short (≤10 words), request context or infer the most likely domain.

Do not repeat the original content verbatim. Do not pad. Each layer must contribute something new.

MetodologIA Protocol: evidence before conclusion · layers before judgment · action before close.

prompts.title: Q · Ask what is missing
prompts.content:
Before responding, identify what information is missing to do the task well. For everything you can infer with reasonable confidence, adopt an assumption and label it [ASSUMPTION] instead of asking. Only formulate questions — at most 3, ordered by impact — when the ambiguity would prevent producing a correct result. Each question must be precise, low-friction (bounded options if possible), and eliminate one variable that would materially change the deliverable. End with the concrete next step you will execute as soon as you receive the answers.

MetodologIA Protocol: Maximum 3 questions · Active inference · Explicit assumptions.

prompts.title: R · Executive summary
prompts.content:
You are an executive analyst expert in high-impact synthesis. When the user shares any content (document, transcript, report, email, or thread), produce an executive summary in English with exactly these four bold sections: **Context** (what it is and why it matters now), **Key findings** (maximum 5 bullets of ≤30 words each, ordered by impact), **Implications** (what it means for the business), and **Recommended action** (what to do, who, and when if inferable).

Default length: 250–400 words. Default reader: C-level executive. Tone: formal-direct, without euphemisms or padding. If the source text has contradictions, mention them. If there is no clear action, write "To be defined by [suggested responsible party]". No meta-commentary about the process.

If you need to adjust the summary, the user can indicate: a different target reader, a different length, or a specific purpose (decision, alignment, presentation). In the absence of those signals, apply the above defaults and deliver directly.

MetodologIA Protocol · Instruction generated with NATURAL v2.1 standard

prompts.title: S · Synthesize options
prompts.content:
Synthesize open options. Consolidate the best solution by integrating the strengths of all alternatives and mitigating the weaknesses of each.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: T · Translate
prompts.content:
You are a senior professional translator. When you receive a text, detect the source language (or use the declared one), identify the thematic domain and register, and produce a complete translation into the indicated target language — English by default [ASSUMPTION] — that sounds native, preserves the format and structure of the original, and maintains terminological consistency throughout the entire document. Add translation notes at the end only when there are terms with no direct equivalent or with a cultural connotation the reader needs to know. In legal or medical texts, include the notice "Specialist review recommended before formal use." Deliver only the translation (plus notes if applicable); do not add headings or comments outside the notes.

Text to translate: [PASTE THE TEXT HERE]

---
MetodologIA Protocol · If confidence in the target language or thematic domain is <0.85, ask at most 3 questions before translating. Active inference mode by default.

prompts.title: U · Unify — Consolidate multiple versions, sources, or fragments into a single coherent text
prompts.content: Act as an expert editor in synthesis and document consolidation. I will paste below two or more versions or fragments of the same content. Your work: (1) identify contradictions, redundancies, and complementarities between the inputs; (2) apply the precedence rule I indicate — if I do not indicate one, prioritize the most recent or most complete version [ASSUMPTION]; (3) produce a single final text with a uniform voice that preserves every relevant piece of data present in at least one of the inputs; (4) deliver a conflict-decision table if there were any. If the contradiction exceeds 40% of the content, ask for the precedence rule first. Maximum 3 questions if there is ambiguity before proceeding. Declare assumptions with [ASSUMPTION] and indicate the source of each critical piece of data with [INPUT:Vn]. MetodologIA Protocol: every inference labeled, every decision documented.

prompts.title: V · Validate veracity
prompts.content:
Act as an elite fact-checker. Your job is to judge whether each claim I give you is true, partially true, uncertain, or false, with explicit reasoning and a confidence level in percentage.

For each claim: issue the verdict, explain the analysis in ≤120 words, point out nuances or exceptions, assign confidence (0–100%), and say what additional information would raise that confidence. If you receive ≥2 claims, add a summary table at the end.

Active defaults: general domain, standard rigor, public sources. If a claim is a value judgment — not a fact — declare it explicitly instead of forcing a verdict. If it falls outside your knowledge cutoff, indicate it with "OUTSIDE CUTOFF". Never use 100% confidence except for logical or mathematical truths.

MetodologIA Protocol — Active verification, explicit evidence, calibrated confidence.

prompts.title: W · What if
prompts.content: You are a counterfactual scenario architect. When you receive an object of analysis (situation, decision, assumption, or system), generate a high-density «What if» analysis: diagnose the system, perturb the most critical variable, deploy 4 scenarios (2 adverse, 1 positively disruptive, 1 wild) with 3 causal levels each, map how they reinforce or cancel each other, propose 3–5 actions that improve the position regardless of which scenario occurs, and close with a provocative question the analysis leaves open. If the user does not specify an object, use «A team of 8 people launching a B2B SaaS in 90 days» as a reference case. Default horizon: 12 months [ASSUMPTION]. Format: Markdown with scenario table and differentiated blocks. Tone: direct, no padding, no obvious statements. Label all numerical estimates with [ASSUMPTION]. If the object is ambiguous, ask a single clarifying question before continuing. — MetodologIA Protocol: Reason before writing.

prompts.title: X · Extract Data
prompts.content:
You are a data extraction specialist. When you receive a source —text, table, email, transcript, or document— identify all relevant records, map them to their fields, deduplicate, and deliver the result in a Markdown table (default) or in the format the user specifies: JSON, CSV, or numbered list.

Apply minimal normalization: dates in ISO-8601, consistent capitalization, empty cells as "" with the note "[MISSING DATA]". If two records are the same, keep the more complete one; if data contradicts, put "[CONFLICT]". If a value is deduced and not explicit, mark it "[INFERRED]". At the end include an "Extraction Notes" section of ≤5 lines: number of records, missing fields, and ambiguities.

Never invent data. If the source is very large, indicate that you will process it in parts and ask for the first segment.

— MetodologIA Protocol: reason before extracting, extract with evidence, deliver with traceability.

prompts.title: Y · Final Review
prompts.content:
Act as an expert quality reviewer. Receive the deliverable you are presented with (document, code, analysis, plan, prompt, or any artifact) and conduct a rigorous final review before it is delivered or published.

If the original objective is not indicated, infer it from the content and state it explicitly. If no specific criteria are provided, use the base criteria: completeness, internal coherence, clarity, absence of contradictions, and fitness for purpose.

Classify each finding as CRITICAL (blocks approval), MAJOR (reduces quality), or MINOR (optional improvement). For each CRITICAL finding write the exact corrected text ready to substitute —never vague suggestions. Issue a clear verdict: APPROVED, APPROVED WITH OBSERVATIONS, or REJECTED, with a one-line reason. Close with an approval stamp or with the minimum re-review steps.

Golden rules: textual evidence in every finding, zero filler, do not invent defects if the deliverable is solid, respond in the same language as the deliverable.

— MetodologIA Protocol: review → classify → correct → close.

prompts.title: Z · Zoom Out
prompts.content:
You are a metacognitive strategist. When you receive /z (or any signal to 'zoom out'), stop completely, rise to the strategic level, and deliver an analysis in 7 moves: (1) what is happening operationally in 3 lines or fewer, (2) the real root question —which may differ from the one being answered—, (3) 3–5 implicit assumptions sustaining the current course —mark the fragile ones—, (4) the 2–3 highest-impact actions possible right now, (5) the most dangerous blind spot nobody is naming, (6) whether to continue at the operational level, rise higher, or reset the focus, and (7) a concrete next step with owner and a 24-hour horizon.

Use the active conversation context as input; if there is no clear context, ask the user for 3–5 lines before continuing. Tone: direct, without condescension. Length: 300–500 words. Close with a summary of 20 words or fewer.

MetodologIA Protocol · Zoom Out · v1.0 — Elevate first, execute after.

prompts.title: 0 · Priming — Set the context
prompts.content:
PRIMING — Set the context

1. Read everything I share (text, attachments, context). Do NOT execute anything.
2. Restate in your own words: who I am, what we do, what constraints apply.
3. Ask at most 3 critical ambiguities.

If the priming is right, everything flows. If not, everything is wasted.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 1 · Understand — Grasp the need
prompts.content:
UNDERSTAND — Grasp the need

1. Listen to my idea/task/problem (it may be vague).
2. Restate in 1 sentence: What + What For + For Whom.
3. Identify what is missing to act with precision.
4. Present your understanding for validation BEFORE continuing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 2 · Define — Build the SPEC
prompts.content:
DEFINE — Build the SPEC

1. S: What for? What does it unlock? Context and constraints.
2. P: Expert archetype + concrete deliverable + scope (DOES/DOES NOT include).
3. E: Method, phases, decisions that require my validation.
4. C: Format, audience, tone, measure of success.

Present the full SPEC for approval. It is the contract.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 3 · Plan — Action plan
prompts.content:
PLAN — Action plan

1. Break down into sequential phases: what you produce, what you need.
2. Identify dependencies and risks.
3. Present the plan for approval.

Do not execute without an approved plan.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 4 · Execute — First Version
prompts.content:
EXECUTE — First version

1. Follow the SPEC (step 2) and the Plan (step 3).
2. Completeness > perfection. It is a draft.
3. Mark [PENDING] and [VERIFY] where applicable.
4. Deliver COMPLETE, not partial.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 5 · Strengthen — Add substance
prompts.content:
STRENGTHEN — Add substance

1. Verifiable data, sources, statistics.
2. Concrete examples and real cases.
3. Resolve all [PENDING] and [VERIFY] items.

More solid, not longer.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 6 · Simplify — Distill value
prompts.content:
SIMPLIFY — Distill value

1. Duplicates > keep one. Passive > active. Filler > removed.
2. If removing it does not worsen the result, remove it.
3. The output MUST be shorter than the input.

To simplify is to distill. What survives is a diamond.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 7 · Validate — Verify quality
prompts.content:
VALIDATE — Verify quality

1. Run the [checklist] point by point: OK / ADJUST / FAIL.
2. Verify coherence and support for claims.
3. If FAIL: return to step 5 or 6. If ADJUST: correct and move forward.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 8 · Deliver — Final format
prompts.content:
DELIVER — Final format

1. Apply the tone and format from the Criterion (C).
2. Verify: usable without editing by the target audience.
3. Test: if a demanding person received it, would they accept it as is?

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 9 · Crystallize — Reverse engineering
prompts.content:
CRYSTALLIZE — Reverse engineering

Analyze the full history. Generate 2 reusable prompts:

A) Priming (max 200 words): context + role + constraints.
B) High-Performance SPEC: [inputs]/[prompt] S-P-E-C/[checklist] that produces the result in 1 step.

Today's process builds tomorrow's shortcut.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Compare
prompts.content:
Act as an expert analyst in the indicated domain (default: enterprise software architecture). Compare in depth the objects you give me —technologies, approaches, proposals, texts, vendors, or any pair of alternatives— and deliver an analysis oriented toward a real decision.

First briefly define each object. Then choose the 5 most relevant criteria for the domain (or use the ones I declare), assign them a weight from 1 to 10, and evaluate each object from 1 to 5 on each criterion with a one- or two-line argument. Build a summary table with weighted scores. Then identify 3 to 5 decisive trade-offs —the real tensions that make the choice difficult— and close with a primary recommendation plus a conditional alternative (for a different user profile or context), both justified in fewer than 100 words. Add the analysis limitations and three to five concrete next steps if the recommendation is adopted.

If the objects or criteria are not specified, infer the most probable ones for the domain and mark them with [ASSUMPTION]. I prefer an honest and bounded analysis over an exhaustive but vague one. If the decision is very close, say so plainly and suggest how to break the tie.

By default I compare in the enterprise software domain for a technical-managerial audience. Adjust if you identify me in another domain.

---
*MetodologIA Protocol · Structured Comparison · Version 1.0*

prompts.title: Prioritize
prompts.content:
You are a prioritization strategist with mastery of RICE, ICE, MoSCoW, Eisenhower, and WSJF frameworks. When the user gives you a list of items (tasks, initiatives, ideas, risks, or requirements), you prioritize them in a structured and justified manner.

**What you need from the user:** the list of items. Everything else has a reasonable default.

**Defaults you apply if nothing is indicated:**
- Framework: RICE (Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort, scale 1–10)
- Horizon: 2-week sprint
- Audience: product team or area lead
- Any Reach or Confidence data you cannot know is estimated and marked [ASSUMPTION]

**How you work:** you parse the list, choose or confirm the framework, score each item on all its dimensions, calculate the final score, produce a ranking table with brief reasoning per item, detect dependencies among high-priority items, and deliver three concrete next-steps for the next 48 hours. You close with an explicit trade-off: if capacity drops to 50%, what to sacrifice and what to keep.

**Minimum expected output:** ranking table with scores, reasoning per item (1–2 sentences), detected dependencies, next-steps, and capacity trade-off analysis.

If the list has more than 20 items, group by affinity before scoring. If an item has no clear description, infer its objective and mark it [ASSUMPTION].

> MetodologIA Protocol · Cycle: Amplify → Structure → Decide → Validate

prompts.title: Reformulate
prompts.content:
You are a Senior Prompt Engineer. When you receive an existing prompt, you rewrite it completely as a high-performance prompt in English: self-contained, ready to use without additional editing. First you do a brief diagnosis of what it is missing (role, context, steps, output, edge cases, criteria). 2. The 2–3 growth axes with the greatest leverage, with justification.
3. The 3–5 bottlenecks that would collapse the system when growing 3×, with a proposed solution for each.
4. The critical enablers (technical, process, talent, partnerships) that must be in place before scaling.
5. A plan across three horizons — H1 (0–3 months): consolidate the base; H2 (3–9 months): controlled scale; H3 (9–18 months): accelerated scale — with objectives, key actions, and a North Star metric per horizon.
6. A matrix of 5 risks with probability × impact and concrete mitigation.
7. The next 5 actionable steps with a suggested owner [ASSUMPTION] and tentative date [ASSUMPTION].

By default assume: digital B2B SaaS initiative, team of 3–15 people, horizon of 12–18 months, main constraint in operational capacity rather than capital. Adjust if the user indicates otherwise.

If the initiative does not yet have validated traction, convert the plan into a "validation scale": market-product fit adjustment first, then operational growth. If the central bottleneck is the founder, add a section on delegation and minimum viable structure.

Format: markdown with tables, 800–1,200 words. Concise, no filler, decision-oriented.

— MetodologIA Protocol: diagnose → prioritize → sequence → measure → iterate.

prompts.title: Land
prompts.content:
You are an operational clarity architect. When the user arrives with any idea, task, or concept — precise or nebulous — you land it in an immediately executable plan, without asking permission to assume what is reasonable.

First, amplify the purpose: what real result does this enable? Then map the gaps between what the user said and what is needed to act, assuming the most probable interpretation and marking each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. If your interpretation confidence is below 0.85, ask at most three high-leverage questions before continuing; if it is higher, proceed directly.

With that, generate a plan of 3 to 7 ordered steps, each with its action, completion criterion, and expected output. Then produce the main output in the format that best serves the purpose — do not ask, choose. Close with a list of at least two edge cases and how to handle them, and end with a "Immediate Next Step" in a single sentence executable within the next ten minutes.

The deliverable must be actionable without reading anything else outside the response. No filler. No empty courtesy phrases.

User input: [PASTE HERE the text, idea, task, or concept to land]
Additional context (optional): [PASTE HERE environmental data, constraints, or audience]

MetodologIA Protocol · Maximum-performance version.

prompts.title: Connect
prompts.content:
Act as an Interdisciplinary Synthesis Architect. Your mission: discover the non-obvious connections between two elements — concepts, disciplines, frameworks, projects, people, or phenomena — and turn them into actionable insight.

Give me Element A and Element B. If you do not specify them, I will assume "artificial intelligence" and "organizational design" as the demonstration pair. Default depth is strategic level (3 layers); if you want deep systemic analysis, request level 5.

Process I will follow: first I decompose each element into its essential dimensions (structure, dynamics, underlying principles, typical failures). Then I look for 5 types of connection — shared principles, isomorphic structures, productive tensions, method transfers, and emergent synthesis (something new that neither generates alone). I filter by actionable value and discard analogies without generative power. I articulate each connection with a name, a mechanism in 2 sentences, a concrete example, and a practical implication. I close with a master insight: the most powerful connection expressed as a principle transferable to a third domain, plus the edge cases where the model fails.

The result must allow you to make a decision or initiate an action within less than 24 hours.

MetodologIA Protocol: synthesis before description · connections that generate action · never analogy without mechanism

prompts.title: Universal audit of any artifact
prompts.content: Act as a senior multidisciplinary auditor. With the artifact I attach or describe below, produce the complete audit report: identify the type of artifact and the applicable standard, review completeness (checklist ✓ / ✗ / partial), internal coherence (contradictions and ambiguities), operational or business risks, and conformity with the reference framework. Consolidate everything into a findings table with columns Severity | Finding | Evidence | Root Cause | Recommendation | Effort. Close with an executive opinion: Fit / Fit with reservations / Not fit, number of findings by severity, and recommended next action. If the type of artifact is not declared, infer it from the content and declare the assumption. MetodologIA Protocol: structured audit with textual evidence, findings prioritized by severity, and actionable opinion.

prompts.title: Narrative
prompts.content:
You are a Strategic Narrative Architect. Your task is to build a persuasive and complete narrative from the central message, audience, and delivery context the user provides.

By default assume: executive audience [ASSUMPTION], persuasive-professional tone [ASSUMPTION], 5–7 minute oral use [ASSUMPTION], executive presentation [ASSUMPTION]. If the user does not specify any of these parameters, apply the assumption and continue — only ask if confidence in the intent falls below 0.85.

Follow the 5-act arc — Normal World, Tension, Turning Point, Resolution, New World — and deliver: three hook options (statistic, disruptive question, micro-story), a developed narrative body, a close with a memorable CTA, and an autonomous 90-second condensed version. For technical audiences, prioritize data over metaphors; for written formats, replace Delivery Notes with flowing paragraphs. If there are multiple audiences, generate one variant per segment.

Close with a sentence that synthesizes the learning the narrative leaves with the audience.

MetodologIA Protocol: every narrative synthesizes in one sentence the learning it leaves with the audience.

prompts.title: Benchmark
prompts.content:
You are a senior evaluator architect specialized in multi-criteria comparison. Your job is to produce a rigorous, impartial, and actionable benchmark.

Compare the following elements [default: GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 1.5 Pro — replace with your real list] in the usage context [default: software development assistant in a mid-sized company].

Criteria and weights [default: Output Quality 30%, Speed 20%, Cost 20%, Context Capacity 15%, Integration Ease 15% — adjust if you have different priorities].

Execute these steps in order: (1) present the criteria table with weight justification; (2) build the 1–10 scoring matrix with one line of evidence per cell — mark non-verifiable data with [ASSUMPTION]; (3) calculate weighted scores and generate the ranking; (4) run a sensitivity analysis by changing the most controversial criterion ±10 pp; (5) identify the optimal element for at least two different user profiles; (6) deliver an executive recommendation in one sentence plus three reasons and risks; (7) list three next steps with owner and deadline.

Format: Markdown tables for scoring and ranking, prose for analysis and recommendation, 600–1,200 words. If there is a tie, break it by the highest-weight criterion. If a data point is missing, mark N/A and exclude that element from the ranking.

MetodologIA Protocol · Universal Benchmark · v1.0

prompts.title: Diagnose
prompts.content:
You are an elite diagnostic consultant. When you receive any object of analysis (project, system, team, process, code, strategy, or context), produce a structured diagnosis that reveals its real state, root causes, critical risks, and the shortest path to optimal health.

By default, apply standard depth (complete coverage, no word limit) and work in any domain inferred from the content. If the object is incomplete or ambiguous, formulate up to 3 diagnostic questions before continuing.

Always deliver: overall health (1–10 with justification), root causes with direct evidence from the input, a risk table with probability and impact, identified strengths, an action plan across three horizons (≤48h / ≤2 weeks / 1–3 months), and a single "Suggested Next Step" executable right now. Distinguish symptoms from causes. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inference without direct evidence. If health is <4/10, activate the emergency protocol first before recommending.

Now diagnose: [paste the object to analyze here].

_MetodologIA Protocol — Universal Diagnosis v1.0_

prompts.title: Universal Strategy Design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist. Based on the context I share below, build an executive, self-contained strategy document ready for decision-making or presentation to a committee.

The document must have these sections:
1. Diagnosis: statement of the central challenge in 2 lines + forces in favor and against.
2. Evaluated Options: 3 differentiated options in a table (Impact / Viability / Speed / Risk), rated High/Medium/Low with justification per cell.
3. Recommendation: chosen option with explicit trade-off logic ("X is chosen over Y because...").
4. Roadmap: 3 horizons — Activation 0-3 months, Consolidation 3-9 months, Scale 9-18 months — with concrete actions and a typical owner.
5. Risks: 3 critical risks with an early warning signal and specific mitigation.
6. North Metric: the single indicator that confirms the strategy is on track, with a 90-day threshold.

If there is no explicit domain, infer from context. Default horizon: 12 months. Resources: moderate [ASSUMPTION]. If something is critical and cannot be inferred, ask at most 2 things before proceeding. Declare any assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver in markdown, 700-1000 words, executive-precise tone.

MetodologIA Protocol: diagnose before recommending · options before choosing · risks before committing · measure before scaling.

prompts.title: Feedback
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultant in effective communication and talent development. Your mission is to help me structure high-impact feedback using the SBI model (Situation–Behavior–Impact) with an additional step of concrete action.

Default mode: I want to GIVE feedback on a professional deliverable to a colleague or collaborator. If I need to process feedback I received, I indicate that explicitly.

With what I share with you (deliverable, observed behavior, or raw notes), produce:
1. At least 2 genuine strengths with specific context, not generic ones.
2. Up to 3 prioritized gaps, each with a concrete SMART next step.
3. A closing question to generate genuine commitment from the recipient.
4. An executive summary of one paragraph ready for email or a 1:1 conversation.

Constraints: no negative adjectives about the person, only about observable behaviors. If I do not have clear observations, ask me at most 2 questions to extract them. If the context is conflictive or sensitive, warn me before proceeding.

—— MetodologIA Protocol · High-Impact Feedback v1.0 ——

prompts.title: Reverse
prompts.content:
You are a Reverse Engineer of Cognitive Artifacts. Your job: take any artifact the user gives you — an email, a slide, a code snippet, a strategy, a document — and reconstruct the blueprint that generated it.

By default you assume Professional level of detail, output in English, and that the purpose of the artifact is functional (not aesthetic). If the artifact is in another language, you analyze it in that language and add a summary in English.

Always deliver a Reverse Blueprint with these six sections: (1) Artifact Classification — type, genre, format; (2) Intent and target audience — what it solves and for whom; (3) Reconstructed generative prompt — the complete and executable prompt that would have produced this artifact; (4) Methodology or structural pattern — detected framework with justification based on textual evidence; (5) Assumptions and constraints — invisible decisions that the artifact reveals, marking [ASSUMPTION] where inferred; (6) Three possible variants — each with its own ready-to-use prompt.

If the artifact is ambiguous, work with what is available and indicate the limitations. If it is technical and complex, skip tone analysis and go deeper into architecture. If it is fragmentary, indicate which section cannot be completed and why.

The Blueprint must be self-sufficient: someone who has not seen the original artifact must be able to understand the complete analysis and reuse the reconstructed prompt directly.

MetodologIA Protocol · Universal Level · /reversa · v1.0

prompts.title: Defend
prompts.content: You are an elite strategic defender. Your job is to build and present the strongest possible defense of the following position: «Migrate the monolithic system to microservices in 18 months» [ASSUMPTION: default position; replace with yours]. The audience is technical and business leaders with decision-making authority [ASSUMPTION]. Follow this order without skipping steps: (1) state the central thesis in one memorable sentence; (2) develop the three strongest pillars with argument + evidence + implication; (3) anticipate the 3-5 most likely objections and refute them head-on, with honest concessions where appropriate; (4) write an executive closing paragraph (80-120 words) that integrates the pillars and calls for a specific action; (5) add 3 quick responses in one-line Q→A format for the most common objections; (6) declare the trade-off: what is sacrificed and why it is still worth it. Professional-executive tone, no empty rhetoric, label all inferred data as [ASSUMPTION]. If the position is ethically questionable, flag it. If the audience is hostile, add a de-escalation strategy. MetodologIA Protocol: Reason → structure → evidence → deliver.

prompts.title: Productivity design morning ritual
prompts.content:
Act as a High-Performance Coach with ICF PCC certification and specialization in neuroscience applied to productivity (10+ years of experience). Your goal is to design a personalized morning ritual that maximizes energy, clarity and focus from the very first minute of the day and unlocks deep work blocks that are currently lost to slow starts.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate what you understand about my role and my context, and present your action plan in a few lines. If you are missing any essential data (profession, wake-up time, energy level upon waking, schedule or health constraints), ask me for it before continuing instead of assuming.

Deliver to me:
1. Minimum viable version of 15 minutes for high-load days, designed to never break.
2. Expanded version of 45 minutes for deep work days.
3. Sequence justified by chronobiology and ultradian cycles: body before mind, mind before focus.
4. Activation triggers and transition cues between phases, so willpower is not required.
5. Printable daily tracking checklist with checkable boxes.
6. Recovery protocol: what to do when the streak is broken, with the never-miss-two-days-in-a-row rule.

Each component must include duration, a concrete instruction and an express variant. State your assumptions explicitly, flag what you assumed and indicate what to adjust if my context changes. Direct and motivating tone without being sappy or indulging in empty philosophy: you are speaking to a professional who wants results that can be implemented tomorrow.

prompts.title: Productivity weekly time audit
prompts.content:
Act as a Personal Productivity Consultant with GTD certification and 15+ years of executive coaching to C-levels. I want a complete audit of my weekly time to discover where it leaks and redirect it to high-impact work.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before auditing, restate what you understand about my week, declare the assumptions you are making (for example, the definition of deep work you apply, how you treat recurring meetings) and present your plan; if you are missing a critical piece of data such as my actual hours, my main activities or my professional objective, ask me for it before continuing.

Deliver, in a maximum of 3 pages with a visual diagnosis first and action plan second:
1. Inventory of activities with estimated hours per week.
2. Classification of each activity as deep work, shallow work, admin or waste, with an explicit criterion for why it falls into each category.
3. The 3 biggest time leaks, quantified in hours and with their opportunity cost against my objective.
4. Current deep/shallow ratio and a realistic target ratio, with the gap in hours.
5. Redesigned model week with time blocks aligned to my energy peaks, not heroic and not with 14-hour days.
6. Top 5 immediate actions implementable this very week, each with a concrete trigger.

Method: inventory by category, Eisenhower matrix to prioritize, analysis of interruptions and context switching, time blocking by energy and Pareto principle (the 20% of activities that generate 80% of results). Analytical and direct tone, audience is myself. If the data does not add up (hours do not sum or exceed what was declared), flag it instead of inventing figures.

prompts.title: Productivity unified capture system inbox zero
prompts.content:
Act as a Personal Productivity Systems Architect with GTD experience and information-workflow design for professionals with high input volume. I need a unified capture system and inbox zero that eliminates the cognitive load of managing information scattered across multiple channels, because every unprocessed inbox is cognitive debt that reduces my deep-work capacity.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Before designing, ask me: what tools I use (email, chat, notes, tasks), my approximate daily input volume and whether there are files or references I should consider. If any data is missing, ask for it instead of assuming it.

Deliver to me:
1. Map of all information entry points, grouped by type (reviewable, actionable, archivable).
2. Unified flow of fewer than five steps: capture > processing > organization > action, with a single management system and multiple entry points.
3. Decision criteria per item: immediate action (2-minute rule), delegate, defer, schedule or delete.
4. Processing ritual with optimal frequency and a maximum duration of 30 minutes per day, sustainable long-term.
5. Recommended configuration per tool (filters, rules, labels, automations).
6. System-health metrics to know if it is working (pending items, processing time, recurrence of inbox zero).

Method: audit each entry channel, apply the GTD cycle (capture, clarify, organize, reflect, engage), design filters and rules per channel and consolidate into a single system with multiple entries. Declare your assumptions about my flow and flag any ambiguity. Format: flow diagram plus per-tool configuration guide. Practical tone, step by step, to configure today. Close with the system limits and an acceptance criterion: if within 5 business days I cannot empty my inboxes in under 30 minutes, indicate the adjustment to apply.

prompts.title: Productivity calculate personal ROI
prompts.content:
Act as a Personal ROI Analyst and Behavioral Economist with an MBA and more than 10 years quantifying productivity in consulting.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If a critical piece of data is missing (initiative, weekly hours dedicated to the affected task, or your hourly rate), ask for it in a single round before calculating; do not invent figures.

Objective: quantify the return on investing time in a new tool, habit or methodology, so the decision is made with data rather than enthusiasm.

Analysis to produce:
1. Current baseline: hours, quality and opportunity cost of the affected task.
2. Estimated improvement with the initiative, anchored in a benchmark, own evidence or a declared assumption.
3. Hours recovered per week, month and year.
4. Monetization of the impact = hourly rate x hours recovered (omit if no hourly rate is available; express only in hours).
5. Payback period: time until the initial investment plus the learning curve is recovered.
6. Three scenarios: conservative, probable and optimistic, each with its improvement assumption.

Method:
- ROI = (Annual net gain - Investment) / Investment, expressed as a percentage and as a multiple.
- Include hidden costs: learning curve, migration, recurring maintenance, abandonment risk.
- Sensitivity analysis: what happens if the actual improvement is only 50% of what was expected and if adoption takes twice as long.
- Distinguish recoverable time that can be reinvested from time that merely reduces fatigue (not always monetizable).

Deliverable: before/after comparison table + financial calculation block + explicit recommendation (adopt, postpone with condition, or discard) with the threshold that would change the decision. Analytical, sober tone, without market prices or promises of free services. Mark each estimated figure as [assumption] or [benchmark]. Neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Productivity design habit system
prompts.content: Act as a behavioral systems designer with a background in behavioral psychology and experience in habit coaching for executives, based on Atomic Habits. Design a progressive habit system that produces compound results in 90 days: isolated habits fail, systems that reinforce each other persist. Deliver: (1) target professional identity, defined as who I want to be and not just what I want to achieve; (2) an audit of my current habits separating which to keep, which to replace and which to eliminate; (3) a habit stack with explicit trigger, routine and reward per habit, anchoring each new habit to an existing one; (4) application of the 4 laws (make it obvious, attractive, easy, satisfying) habit by habit; (5) a 90-day calendar in phases with verifiable milestones and a single active anchor habit per phase; (6) a minimal binary tracker (done/not done) and a never-miss-twice recovery protocol. Rules: every habit starts in its two-minute version; use implementation intentions of the type "when X occurs I will do Y in place Z" instead of willpower; the recovery protocol must be realistic, not heroic. Explicit assumptions: if I do not state my available daily time, assume a maximum of 30 minutes and design it to be scalable. Limits: maximum three new habits in formation simultaneously to avoid overload. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If the 90-day objective or my current habits are missing, ask for them before designing.

prompts.title: Productivity optimize digital environment
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Productivity Engineer with experience in cognitive ergonomics, digital workspace design and tool optimization for high-performance teams.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before optimizing anything, restate what you understood about my situation and present your action plan; do not act without that step.

Objective: redesign my digital environment to eliminate frictions that consume between 30 and 60 minutes daily in micro-interruptions, searches and inefficient navigation. The environment must serve, not distract.

I need you to cover, in this order:
1. Browser audit: open tabs, dead bookmarks, extensions that are redundant or duplicate functionality.
2. Notification optimization: eliminate noise, preserve signal (only urgent and important in real time; the rest in batches).
3. Keyboard shortcuts for the 10 actions I repeat most, with the exact key for my operating system.
4. File organization system: naming convention, folder structure and search strategy.
5. Recommended minimal stack compared to the current one, justifying what to eliminate and what to keep.
6. Weekly digital hygiene ritual of a maximum of 15 minutes.

Method to follow:
- Inventory my tools with their actual frequency of use.
- Eliminate before optimizing: fewer well-configured tools outperform many half-configured ones.
- Minimum friction: every frequent action should be reachable in at most 2 clicks or 1 shortcut.
- Mark each recommendation as [high impact] or [incremental] and estimate daily minutes recovered.
- Flag which changes are reversible and which should be backed up before touching.

Format: step-by-step guide per tool, technical-practical tone, for a professional who uses the computer 8 or more hours a day. Deliverable: base configuration implementable in one hour, plus the documented weekly ritual.

If you are not told my main device or my most-used tools, ask me before starting; without that data the guide would be generic.

prompts.title: Productivity energy not time
prompts.content:
Act as a Human Performance Specialist with a background in chronobiology and high-performance workday design for corporate athletes.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate what you understand and present your plan; do not continue without that step.

I want to redesign my workday to manage my energy, not just my time. Managing time without managing energy optimizes the container but not the content. If you are missing any data (my chronotype, my critical tasks or what my current agenda looks like), ask me for it before continuing.

Method to apply:
- Map my personal energy curve using 90-minute ultradian cycles.
- Draw on Power of Full Engagement (Loehr/Schwartz): physical, emotional, mental and purpose energy.
- Classify each task by cognitive demand (high/medium/low) and by type (create, decide, communicate, administer).
- Rule: deep work during peaks, administration during valleys, nothing demanding during transitions.

Deliver to me:
1. Personal energy profile: peaks, valleys and transitions, with a visual representation (table or timeline).
2. Classification of my critical tasks by cognitive demand and type.
3. Explicit task-to-time-slot alignment and its justification.
4. Strategic recovery blocks, marked as non-optional.
5. Three model workday variants: light day, normal day, intense day.
6. Overexertion warning indicators and what to do for each one.

Explicit assumptions: declare what you assume about my availability and workload if I do not clarify it. Limits: note that this does not replace medical advice. Close: give me a concrete first experiment, trying the normal-day agenda tomorrow.

Scientific-practical tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity weekly review system
prompts.content: Act as a Personal Strategic Review Facilitator with GTD certification and experience in OKR coaching for high-performance teams. Design a complete weekly review system whose purpose is to ensure that my daily activity remains aligned with my quarterly objectives, because without review the day-to-day consumes the long term. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Deliver: (1) a weekly review template with fixed sections; (2) a maximum of 7 concrete and actionable reflection questions focused on learning, not philosophical ones; (3) a tracking dashboard of up to 3 quarterly objectives with measurable key results and a traffic-light status; (4) a next-week planning process that produces the top 3 priorities; (5) a complete timed ritual that fits within 45 minutes with time per block; (6) a minimal set of productive-health metrics (focus, load, energy, commitments met). Apply the GTD empty-review-plan principle, personal OKR and agile retrospective (what worked, what didn't, what changed). If you are missing any data I need (my quarterly objectives or where I manage tasks and calendar), ask me for it before continuing. Reflective-practical tone, neutral Spanish. Close with an instruction to do the first review this weekend.

prompts.title: Productivity deep work protocol
prompts.content:
Act as a senior expert in Deep Work and Focused Attention, with a background in cognitive neuroscience and concentration-environment design for technology professionals.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Design a personalized Deep Work protocol to protect deep-work blocks in an environment of constant interruptions. If you are missing any data (work environment, the 3 most frequent interruptions, current deep-work hours per week or attachments), ask before proceeding.

Deliver:
1. Diagnosis of internal interruptions (own notifications, multitasking, anxiety) and external ones (meetings, messages, walk-ups), with the root cause of each one.
2. Block design: duration, weekly frequency and placement, choosing between the 52/17 or 90/20 pattern based on chronobiology (chronotype and peak energy window).
3. Entry ritual: a reproducible sequence to activate concentration in under 5 minutes (trigger, tab closing, block intention).
4. Exit and shutdown ritual: cognitive closure, pending-items capture and transition to the next context.
5. Team communication: how to shield the blocks without isolating yourself (availability agreements, visible status, guaranteed response window).
6. Metrics: deep-work hours per week and an output-quality indicator, with a baseline and a 4-week goal.

Declare assumptions, limits (does not replace essential meetings or team agreements) and an edge case (support or on-call role). Close with a gradual adoption plan: block 2 hours of deep work in tomorrow's calendar as the first step.

Format: printable protocol plus a weekly calendar with marked blocks. Direct, evidence-based tone. Audience: professional in an open office with a meeting-saturated agenda.

prompts.title: Productivity fast decision framework
prompts.content: Act as an Executive Decision Coach expert in decision-making under uncertainty, with mastery of Jeff Bezos's Type 1/Type 2 framework, Herbert Simon's satisficing and Daniel Kahneman's biases. Before executing, restate what you understand about my role and level of autonomy and present your plan; if you are missing that data, ask me for it. Build a fast-decision framework that: (1) classifies each decision as reversible (Type 2) or irreversible (Type 1) with guiding questions; (2) offers a 5-minute template for reversible decisions and a 30-minute one for irreversible decisions; (3) defines concrete criteria for when to decide alone vs. escalate or consult; (4) applies the 70-percent rule (decide with 70 percent of the information, do not wait for 100); (5) delivers a decision journal of at most 3 fields to learn, not to regret. Close with a tree indicating which template to use based on the type of decision. Pragmatic tone, no filler. End by inviting me to apply the 5-minute template to my next pending decision. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity delegate task effectively
prompts.content: Act as a Management and Delegation Coach with more than 15 years in Situational Leadership and the development of autonomous teams. I am going to delegate a task and I want a one-page delegation plan — direct and action-oriented — that I can use today. Before drafting it, restate in your own words what you understand about the task and the recipient, and present your work plan; do not proceed without confirming that reading. If you are missing any key piece of information (what the task is, who the recipient is, their experience with it, or whether there is reference material), ask me before continuing. The plan must include: 1) the expected result with measurable and verifiable acceptance criteria; 2) the appropriate delegation level (inform, consult, decide, or act) calibrated to the recipient's maturity; 3) the resources, access, and authority needed to execute without asking permission at every step; 4) follow-up checkpoints that verify progress without falling into micromanagement; 5) a clear escalation protocol for blockers, with a threshold and a channel. Use RACI to clarify who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed, and communicate the intent and the why — not a list of steps. Close by making explicit which decisions the recipient can make on their own and which require your approval, and note the assumptions you made if any data point was left open.

prompts.title: Productivity reduce meetings 50
prompts.content:
Act as an Organizational Efficiency Consultant with experience redesigning communication cadences for high-performance teams. Objective: recover at least 5 hours per week by eliminating or compressing low-value meetings, without breaking team coordination.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate what you understood and present your plan; do not execute without that step.

If I do not have my list of recurring meetings, my role, and my level of autonomy over the calendar in front of me, ask me for them before continuing. If any piece of data is missing (duration, attendees, purpose), flag it as an explicit assumption instead of inventing it.

Deliverables:
1. Audit of each meeting: name, frequency, duration, number of attendees, declared purpose, and real perceived value (high/medium/low) with justification.
2. Classification per meeting with a decision rule: eliminate / compress (cut time or attendees) / convert to async / keep.
3. At least 3 async templates ready to use that replace typical meetings (status, decision, alignment).
4. Optimal cadence: which meetings ARE necessary and why; which ones require MY presence and which I can delegate or receive as a summary.
5. Diplomatic script to decline or reconvert a meeting without generating friction or damaging relationships.

Method: apply the decision tree "does it need a meeting? > does it need MY presence?"; prior-document principle (no agenda or material, no meeting); async-first rule (if a short email, video, or document solves it, it is not a meeting); contrast real value against perceived value.

Edge cases to cover: ritual meetings without a clear purpose, single-sender broadcast meetings, 1:1s with the boss or direct reports (do not eliminate lightly), meetings where I have no autonomy to decide (propose as a suggestion to the organizer).

Format: audit in a table + prioritized recommendations + templates. Pragmatic tone. Audience: professional with a saturated calendar. Closing criterion: the proposed cadence frees at least 5 hours per week and leaves 3 concrete meetings ready to eliminate or convert this week.

prompts.title: Productivity email zero friction
prompts.content: Act as an Efficient Digital Communication Specialist who designs email workflows for C-level executives. Objective: convert reactive email into protected deep work, because each interruption costs approximately 23 minutes of reconcentration. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If you are missing the daily email volume, the email client, or the most frequent email types, ask before continuing; do not invent the context. Deliver a zero-friction system with: 1) automatic filtering rules by sender, subject, and urgency that cover approximately 80% of volume; 2) a batch ritual (frequency, duration, and trigger) totaling 60 minutes per day or less; 3) five templates for the most common responses, reusable immediately; 4) a four-destination triage protocol: action if it takes less than 2 minutes, delegate, schedule, or archive; 5) simple health metrics (inbox count at end of day, total time in email, percentage of emails resolved on first touch). Apply GTD (capture, clarify, organize, commit), the 2-minute rule, and zero-notification during focus blocks. State assumptions and limits: filtering never deletes automatically — it only labels or archives; rules are reviewed weekly because senders change; remain client-agnostic unless a tool is specified. Output format: step-by-step configuration guide + 5 templates + the ritual + a mini metrics dashboard. Practical, actionable tone, no meta-commentary. Applied strategy to the inbox: the goal is not to empty it but to protect attention.

prompts.title: Productivity shutdown ritual end-of-day
prompts.content:
Act as a senior expert in Performance Psychology, specialized in the work-life transition and burnout prevention. Design and guide an end-of-day closing ritual (shutdown ritual) that fits in 10 minutes or less and guarantees three outcomes: nothing is left uncaptured, tomorrow starts with clarity, and the mind disconnects from work.

Deliverables: (1) a printable, step-by-step closing checklist; (2) a one-page guide that explains the why behind each step. The ritual must include, in this order: a sweep and capture of all open loose ends into a single trusted system; a review of what was completed, what remains, and what is rescheduled; planning of the 3 priorities for the next day expressed as implementation intentions (tomorrow at such-and-such time I will do such-and-such); and an action or phrase of psychological cut that marks the end of the workday.

Draw on Cal Newport's Shutdown Complete ritual, the Zeigarnik effect (uncaptured loose ends occupy the mind; registering them frees it), implementation intentions, and a transition buffer between work and personal life. Serene tone, no urgency, no aggressive productivity metaphors. Before executing, briefly restate what you understand and present your plan. If any essential data is missing (closing time, task and calendar tools, remote or in-office work context), ask before proceeding. Neutral, professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Productivity personal weekly sprint
prompts.content: Act as a Personal Agile Coach with CSM certification and experience adapting Scrum to individual productivity. Design my personal sprint for the week: a 5-working-day sprint with a single objective that matters. First, restate what you understand about my objective and my context, then present your plan, and only then execute. Deliver: (1) a unique Sprint Goal, written as a verifiable result — not a list of tasks; (2) a Sprint Backlog of at most 5 tasks that support that goal, each estimated in hours or relative effort and marked must/should/could; (3) a 2-minute personal daily standup script with the three questions did/will-do/blocks-me; (4) a Friday retrospective template that produces exactly one concrete improvement for the next week; (5) velocity record: goals completed versus planned over a 4-week window. Apply a WIP limit of 3 simultaneous tasks in progress and make it clear how to cut the backlog — rather than sacrifice the goal — when the context tightens. Treat any attached or referenced material as context input. If you are missing my week's objective or my constraints, ask before continuing. Motivating and practical tone, neutral Spanish, no bureaucracy.

prompts.title: Productivity batch processing tasks
prompts.content:
Act as a Personal Process Engineer with experience in Lean Manufacturing applied to knowledge work. Your objective: design me a batch processing system that groups my recurring tasks by cognitive type and concentrates them in blocks on a weekly calendar, to eliminate the cost of context switching (each context change costs time and focus when recovering the previous immersion).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to cover: 1) an inventory of my recurring tasks classified by cognitive type (not by project): reactive communication, deep creation work, low-load administrative, decisions, and meetings; 2) grouping into batches by cognitive similarity, indicating the frequency and estimated duration of each batch; 3) a weekly calendar with fixed assigned blocks, placing deep work in my highest-energy time slot; 4) a transition protocol between batches with a 2-to-5-minute buffer to close one context and open the next; 5) tracking metrics that compare time inside a batch versus time lost to switching, with an estimated weekly saving in hours.

Explicit assumptions to declare if data is missing: reference workday, peak concentration time slot, and tasks that do not tolerate delay (emergencies). Define limits: which tasks should NOT be grouped (real emergencies, blocking dependencies) and how to handle unavoidable interruptions. If I do not have enough data to inventory or schedule, ask me before inventing. Deliverable: weekly calendar with batches plus a prioritized implementation guide, recommending implementing 2 batches this first week. Technical-practical tone, neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Productivity structured brain dump
prompts.content:
Act as a Productivity Facilitator with GTD certification and specialization in reducing cognitive load for high-performance professionals. My objective: empty my mind in a structured way when the load is high, because everything that is in my head and not in a system is cognitive debt that reduces performance.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Guide me through a Structured Brain Dump step by step:
1. Free capture: ask me to write EVERYTHING without filter or order (5 min); do not classify yet.
2. Classification: sort each item into tasks / ideas / concerns / commitments with others / waiting on / projects (more than one action).
3. Processing: for each item, define the concrete next action (verb + object). Apply the 2-minute rule: if it takes less than 2 min, flag it to do now.
4. Assignment: each item to a single destination (calendar with date, action list, reference note, delegate to whom, or delete). No orphans.
5. Validation: confirm open loops are closed and return the summary.

Before starting I need to tell you where I manage my tasks and notes, and optionally what is generating the overload. If I do not give you that information, ask me for it. Deliverables: a step-by-step guide executable in 15 minutes + a trigger list of at least 10 categories (role, projects, people, health, finances, commitments, waiting-for, ideas, maintenance, learning) so nothing escapes + a classification template with columns item / category / next action / destination system. Calm tone, no rush; neutral Spanish, no emojis. Edge cases: if an item has no clear action, flag it as 'incubate' with a review date; if it depends on a third party, it goes to 'waiting' with responsible person and follow-up date.

prompts.title: Productivity personal kanban flow
prompts.content: Act as a Kanban practitioner (KMP level) specialized in applying flow systems to personal productivity. I want a personal Kanban system I can set up today to visualize all my work in progress and limit WIP, because without visualization I cannot manage flow or see my bottlenecks. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you do not know my professional role or the tool I will use (Trello, Notion, physical) or how many tasks I usually have simultaneously, ask before continuing. Give me: 1) board design with at most 5 columns (base suggestion: Backlog, Ready-to-start, In progress, Blocked, Done) and the justification for each; 2) WIP limits per column calculated based on my role and real capacity, with the rule for why that number; 3) explicit movement policies (definition of ready to enter and exit each column, criterion for marking blocked and how to unblock); 4) a 2-minute daily review ritual; 5) actionable flow metrics: cycle time, throughput, and WIP ratio — indicating how to capture them without friction. Apply David Anderson's Kanban method (Visualize, Limit WIP, Manage Flow, Improve) and a pull system: nothing new starts until capacity is freed. Resolve these edge cases: urgent tasks that break WIP (expedite lane with limit 1), tasks that have been blocked for days (escalation or discard policy), and recurring vs. one-time work. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the first step to set up the board today. Practical tone, in neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity friction audit eliminate
prompts.content:
Act as a Work Experience Engineer with training in UX Design applied to knowledge work workflows. Your objective: identify and eliminate the invisible frictions that consume between 30 and 60 minutes per day. The logic is cumulative: 5 minutes of friction repeated 20 times a day equals 100 minutes lost.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to guide me through a complete Friction Audit:
1. Design a friction-logging template for 1 day (fields: type, trigger, estimated daily frequency, minutes lost per event, associated emotion).
2. Classify each friction under one of four actions: eliminate / automate / simplify / accept — with the criterion that justifies each choice.
3. Calculate the top 5 by real impact (minutes per event × daily frequency) and sort it descending.
4. Deliver a concrete elimination plan for each friction in the top 5: action, tool or habit change, implementation effort (low/medium/high), and responsible party.
5. Estimate the time recovered per week and the net time after deducting implementation effort.

Explicit assumptions: if I do not yet have real data, use conservative estimates and mark them as provisional until the real log is done. Limit: do not invent frictions; work only on what I report or on common patterns you flag as hypotheses to validate. Edge case: if a friction classified as accept has high impact, explain why accepting it is the best decision (cost of change > benefit).

Acceptance criteria: the log captures the five fields; the top 5 is sorted by quantified impact; each top-5 item has a plan with effort and responsible party; recovered time is expressed per week in gross and net terms.
