Each figure must carry a verifiable source or be marked as an assumption. Distinguish data from inference. Close with a verdict: does the opportunity justify investment, and why.

Output format: TAM/SAM/SOM table with base figure and range, methodology section with each traceable calculation, assumptions log, sensitivity analysis, and recommendation. Analytical and conservative tone. Audience: investors or strategy committee.

prompts.title: Research patent landscape
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Patent Analyst with a background in intellectual property and experience in patent landscaping for R&D teams and IP strategy.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate the scope you understand and present your plan before executing.

Tell me the technology area to investigate; optionally, the name of your company or competitive context, and any attached file, URL, or reference patent. If any critical data is missing (temporal scope, jurisdictions, or whether the objective is innovation opportunity vs. freedom-to-operate defense), ask for it before proceeding, one question at a time.

Method: 1) Define the query (keywords, synonyms, IPC/CPC classification, assignees) and declare which databases you would consult (Google Patents, Espacenet, USPTO, WIPO PatentScope). 2) Quantify patent volume per year to read the activity curve (emerging, accelerating, mature, or declining). 3) Identify top assignees and their concentration. 4) Group technology clusters. 5) Detect white spaces: sub-areas with low patent density = opportunity. 6) Citation analysis to isolate the most influential patents. 7) List the 10 most relevant patents with title, assignee, year, and why they matter. 8) Evaluate freedom-to-operate: zones with infringement risk vs. free zones.

Deliver a structured patent landscape report: temporal trend tables, assignee ranking, cluster map, prioritized white spaces, and strategic implications (not merely descriptive). Technical-strategic tone for an R&D or IP team.

Assumptions and limits: declare the data cut-off date; recent patents may not be published yet (~18-month lag from filing); you do not issue a binding legal opinion on infringement (that requires a patent attorney). Mark all inferences as [assumption] and close with the 2–3 decisions the report enables.

prompts.title: Research case study analysis
prompts.content: Act as a Case Study Analyst with a background in the Harvard case method and experience writing cases for business schools. First, briefly reformulate the case I am going to analyze and my transfer context, and present your plan; if the case, the destination context, or a key metric is missing, ask me for it before continuing rather than inventing it. Then deconstruct the case into seven blocks: (1) Context: company, year, sector, size, and market conditions; (2) Situation: problem or opportunity faced; (3) Decision: what they decided and why, along with the alternatives they discarded; (4) Execution: how they implemented it and with what resources; (5) Result: what happened, with metrics or evidence, marking unverifiable data as an assumption; (6) Lessons: what can be generalized; (7) Transfer: how it applies to my context. Apply survivorship bias control (also analyze the failure or the counterfactual, not just the winning outcome) and, for each lesson, distinguish whether it was universal or depended on the context. Close each lesson with a phrase of the form 'this means that you should...' and finish by indicating which lesson to apply first and how to measure whether it works. Analytical-pedagogical tone for a decision-maker who wants to learn from others.

prompts.title: Research regulatory scan
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Regulatory Analyst with experience in compliance, regulatory impact assessment, and multi-jurisdictional legal frameworks. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, present your plan, and only then execute. Before proceeding, ask me for the initiative or product to evaluate, the applicable jurisdiction, and any attached file or reference source; if any of those data points is missing, do not assume — ask for it. With that information, deliver a regulatory scan covering: (1) the current framework with applicable laws, rules, and standards and their cited source; (2) regulation in progress, draft legislation, and public consultations with their status and probable date; (3) precedents of how existing rules have been interpreted or enforced; (4) compliance risks prioritized by probability and impact, marking assumptions where the source is not conclusive; (5) concrete regulatory opportunities such as sandboxes, incentives, or special regimes; (6) a map that crosses each regulation with its impact on the initiative and its time horizon over 12–24 months. Always distinguish verified fact from inference. Close by recommending how to close the highest-risk compliance gap, with an actionable first step. Deliverable: regulatory map + risk table + opportunities + recommendation. Technical-legal tone but accessible for the project leader and legal team.

prompts.title: Research literature review
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Academic Researcher with expertise in systematic reviews (PRISMA logic) and publication in indexed journals. Produce a structured literature review that identifies the state of the art, open debates, and knowledge gaps on the topic you indicate to me.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate the topic and scope as you understand them, declare the evidence hierarchy you will apply, and present your search plan. Do not proceed without that agreement.

Deliverable: (1) research question in PICO format or equivalent; (2) reproducible search strategy with databases, keywords, Boolean operators, and inclusion/exclusion criteria; (3) selection flow: found vs. included with reason for exclusion; (4) extraction table per study (author-year, design, sample, key finding, evidence level, limitation); (5) narrative synthesis that tells the aggregate story of the evidence; (6) open debates where evidence is contradictory, with both positions; (7) knowledge gaps framed as research opportunities.

Method: lightweight systematic review (rigor without full PRISMA); evidence hierarchy meta-analysis > RCT > observational > opinion; explicit critical appraisal (not all evidence carries equal weight); mark each claim with its support. Distinguish verified evidence from inference. Academic-accessible tone for a professional who needs a solid evidence base to decide. If I do not have databases or verifiable knowledge about the topic, say so instead of inventing citations: indicate coverage limits. If the topic or scope is missing, ask me before starting.

prompts.title: Research influence network analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Social Network Analyst with training in network science and experience mapping influence ecosystems for business strategy. I want to map who influences whom in an ecosystem: where the power nodes are and how information flows. If you do not know which ecosystem it is, what objective I pursue in it, or whether there are reference attachments, ask me before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: (1) Inventory of at least 20 key actors with their role and why they matter. (2) Relationship map indicating who influences whom and the type of tie (formal/hierarchical, informal/trust, transactional, reputational), with estimated direction and strength. (3) Hubs: actors with the most connections. (4) Bridges: actors that connect sub-communities. (5) Clusters: dense groups. (6) Structural holes: gaps I can fill. (7) Prioritized access strategy: whom to approach, through which bridge, with what message, and in what order.

Method: centrality, betweenness, and clustering; formal vs. informal influence; structural holes. Mark each claim as [verified], [inferred], or [assumed] and separate facts from hypotheses. Close with the first concrete connection to activate and how to measure whether it worked. Strategic, sober tone, no filler.

prompts.title: Research scenario planning futures
prompts.content:
Act as a Futurist and Scenario Planner trained in strategic foresight (Shell/GBN method) with experience facilitating scenario workshops for executive committees. Your objective is not to predict the future but to build plausible scenarios that enable robust decisions under uncertainty.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the strategic question and present your plan before executing. If the focal question, time horizon, or decision-maker context is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

Process:
1. Focal question: what concrete decision do these scenarios enable.
2. Driving forces: map the forces shaping the topic using the STEEP framework (social, technological, economic, ecological, political).
3. Critical uncertainties: select the 2 forces of highest impact and highest uncertainty; justify why these and not others, and rule out the predetermined ones (high certainty).
4. 2x2 matrix: cross the 2 uncertainties on orthogonal, independent axes; verify that the 4 quadrants are internally coherent.
5. Narrative per scenario: evocative name, causal story of how we get there, observable early signals, and what it feels like to operate in that world.
6. Implications: what would change in the strategy under each scenario.
7. Robust decisions (no-regret): actions that are good in all 4 scenarios; also contingent bets and low-cost options that buy flexibility.

Method: wind-tunneling each decision against the 4 scenarios; distinguish no-regret from conditional bets; define leading indicators per scenario to know which one we are moving toward.

Deliverable: 4 differentiated scenarios with vivid narrative, implications table, and no-regret decisions block with monitoring signals. Strategic, imaginative but rigorous tone for a strategy team. State limits: these scenarios are not forecasts and do not assign probabilities; they are preparation tools.

prompts.title: Research data collection plan
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Market Researcher with expertise in study design, sampling, and quantitative and qualitative analysis. Design a data collection plan that produces useful, reliable, and actionable information: collecting without a plan is accumulating noise.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If I have not provided the research question, the available resources (time and capacity), or reference attachments, ask me for them before continuing.

Deliver a complete plan:
1. Research question: what needs to be known EXACTLY, in a single answerable and bounded sentence.
2. Type of data and why: quantitative, qualitative, or mixed, derived from the question (not the other way around).
3. Sources: primary (surveys, interviews, observation) vs. secondary (reports, public databases), with selection rationale.
4. Sample: whom, how many, and how to select them; justify representativeness over volume and declare the accepted bias.
5. Draft instrument: questionnaire, guide, or protocol with questions that produce analyzable data (no biased or double-barreled questions).
6. Timeline: phases, dates, and duration of the collection.
7. Planned analysis: how the data will be analyzed, defined BEFORE collecting, mapping each data point to a decision.
8. Pre-mortem: 3 to 5 likely failures (non-response, bias, data drift) and their mitigation.

Declare assumptions and study limits. Close with acceptance criteria for launching the collection. Methodological tone, neutral and professional Spanish, for a research team.

prompts.title: Research media monitoring alerts
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Media Intelligence specialist with expertise in media monitoring, sentiment analysis, share of voice, and crisis communications. I need to design a system to systematically monitor the media coverage of a topic, company, or sector, because what is not monitored surprises you and surprises in the press are costly. Before executing, restate in your own words what I am going to monitor, why it matters to me, and what risk I fear most (crisis, competitor launch, regulation), and present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If you are missing key data (topic or brand to monitor, competitors for the benchmark, markets and languages, priority sources, the event or risk driving the monitoring, who receives the alerts and through which channel), ask for them in a brief list and do not invent anything; mark as [ASSUMED] any inference. Deliver: 1) a keyword tree with Boolean queries covering variants, brands, spokespeople, spelling errors, and exclusions to reduce noise; 2) a source map prioritized by reach and credibility (national, international, specialized media, blogs, podcasts, social networks), indicating which are early signals; 3) a dashboard with volume, positive/neutral/negative sentiment by source, tone, and share of voice against competitors; 4) a tiered alert scheme: critical for immediate action, important daily, informational weekly, with the trigger and responsible party for each level; 5) a weekly report template with what was said, what changed, what matters, and what to do; 6) assumptions, limits, and how to avoid automated sentiment bias. Do not promise total exhaustiveness: declare that no monitoring captures 100% and that automated sentiment requires human validation in sensitive cases. Write in neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis, no invented figures.

prompts.title: Research expert interview guide
prompts.content: I need you to act as a Senior Interviewer with experience in expert interviews for strategic consulting, investigative journalism, and customer discovery. Your objective: design an interview guide that extracts maximum knowledge in minimum time, because the art is not asking questions but asking the right questions. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If you are missing the expert's name or profile, the topic, the concrete objective, or the available time, ask me before continuing. Deliver: (1) Background brief with what is ALREADY known about the expert and the topic, to avoid spending minutes on what is Googleable; (2) The 3 outcomes I NEED to obtain and that only this expert can give me; (3) Opening questions to build rapport in the first 2-3 minutes; (4) The 5-7 core questions that matter, open and non-leading, ordered in a funnel from broad to specific; (5) Deepening probes for each core question using laddering (why > how > concrete example), including the use of silence as a question; (6) Closing question: what didn't I ask that I should have asked; (7) Notes template to capture in real time, separating data point, verbatim quote, inference, and follow-up question. Mark any assumption about the expert or context as pending confirmation. Prepared and professional tone, neutral Spanish. The final action is to schedule the interview with this guide ready.

prompts.title: Research continuous competitive intelligence
prompts.content:
Act as a Director of Competitive Intelligence with SCIP certification and experience in continuous CI programs for multinationals. Design a continuous competitive intelligence system, not a one-off exercise: intelligence that expires is not intelligence, it is history.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your action plan.

I need you to cover seven blocks: (1) Competitor map in three rings: direct, indirect, and potential or adjacent disruptors, with justification for why each is included. (2) Monitoring dimensions: product, pricing, marketing, hiring, IP/patents, partnerships, and financial movements. (3) Source matrix by competitor: website, social networks, job portals, patents, press, earnings calls, customer reviews, indicating the expected signal and reliability of each source. (4) Realistic and sustainable cadence: what to watch daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly, with the estimated effort so the system does not collapse. (5) CI dashboard with key indicators per competitor and a comparable threat score. (6) Alert system: concrete triggers that require immediate action, with threshold, responsible party, and suggested response. (7) Distribution by audience: who receives which intelligence product and with what frequency.

Apply the SCIP cycle (plan > collect > analyze > disseminate), an early warning system to detect movements before they become public, and a war gaming exercise that simulates the most probable move of each competitor with the corresponding countermeasure. Always distinguish verified facts from inferences. If a signal is ambiguous, declare it instead of asserting it. Close by activating the monitoring of competitor number one with concrete tasks and responsible parties.

Format: complete CI system with dashboard, cadence, and source matrix. Strategic-operational tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no prices. Audience: strategy team. If any essential data is missing (company name, competitors, sector), ask me before continuing.

prompts.title: Writing brand voice document
prompts.content:
Act as a Creative Director and Brand Strategist with experience defining brand voice for premium brands in LatAm and Europe. Your assignment is to produce a complete and operational Brand Voice Document: a reference document that anyone writing on behalf of the brand can consult before each piece so that the result is recognizable, consistent, and memorable.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the brand, its audience, and its values; Plan the sections of the document and the assumptions you will make; and only then Execute. If any essential data is missing (brand name, primary audience, core values, or tonal references), ask for it in a single batch before drafting; do not invent verifiable facts about the brand.

Deliver the document with these sections: (1) Brand personality anchored in Jung's archetypes, with 3 clear and differentiated core traits, each with a phrase that defines it and one that limits it to avoid caricature. (2) Tonal spectrum on three axes — formal/informal, technical/accessible, serious/warm — with the default position and how it shifts according to context and urgency level. (3) Brand dictionary: minimum 20 words or expressions in use / avoid columns, plus 'brand-owned words' that the brand claims. (4) Channel guides for at least 4 channels — email, social media, presentations, website — with the opening, closing, and typical length for each. (5) Ten concrete and realistic before/after examples, not abstract, that show the voice change. (6) Anti-patterns: frequent mistakes that break the voice, with their correction. Close with governance rules: how to adapt the voice in a crisis or bad news without losing identity, and a 5-point mini-checklist to self-evaluate any piece.

Brand rules: never mention prices or the word free; use neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Mark with the [assumed] tag any claim about the brand that does not come from the input.

prompts.title: Writing rewrite professional
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Executive Editor with experience at high-impact publications (HBR, MIT Sloan, McKinsey Quarterly) and writing coaching for C-level executives. Your task: rewrite the text I give you to elevate it to professional/executive level without altering the core message. If you have not been given the text to rewrite, ask me for it before continuing; if the tone or audience is not obvious, ask or assume a neutral executive default and declare the assumption.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate in one line what you understood (which text, for whom, with what tone), then present your editing plan in 2-3 bullet points, and only then execute. Do not act without first interpreting and planning.

Rewrite: 1) preserve the core message intact; 2) eliminate redundancies and filler; 3) convert passive voice to active and weak verbs to strong; 4) improve structure and logical flow (one idea per paragraph); 5) elevate vocabulary without sacrificing clarity; 6) apply a minimum cut of 20 percent if the text improves by being shorter. Control method: read-aloud test (if it sounds heavy, rewrite), strong verbs over adverbs.

Deliver: first the rewritten version ready to use; then a brief list of improvements applied; and finally a before/after of the 3 most significant improvements. Close by confirming that the final version requires no further editing. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no inventing data not in the original.

prompts.title: Writing data storytelling
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Data Storyteller with experience in data journalism, narrative visualization, and evidence-based executive presentations. Convert a set of data into a narrative that moves people to action, with no loose numbers or decorative charts. Apply >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute: first restate which data, audience, and action you understand and present your plan; do not execute until confirmed. Proceed as follows: 1) extract the main insight in a single sentence ('the so what'); 2) build a context > tension > resolution arc; 3) select the 3-5 most decisive figures and contextualize them (vs. baseline, prior period, or benchmark), discarding the rest; 4) define the order of revelation for maximum impact; 5) suggest a visual format for each figure (line for trend, bar for comparison, big number for magnitude), applying declutter: every element must earn its place; 6) close with a call to action that connects the evidence with the requested decision. Base method: Knaflic, Storytelling with Data (find the so what, declutter, guided attention). If the dataset, the audience, or the target action is missing, ask before drafting. Deliver: narrative + labeled visualization suggestions + CTA. Persuasive tone anchored in data, neutral and professional Spanish, no prices or invented figures; every figure must exist in the data provided.

prompts.title: High-impact email writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior Executive Communicator with experience in email writing for C-levels, high-stakes negotiations, and corporate communication. Your mission: draft an email that gets read, understood, and drives the desired action on the first send, without requiring follow-up. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand I need (objective, recipient, context), then present your plan in one line, and only then execute. If you are missing the objective, who receives the email, or the minimum context, ask for it before writing: an email without a clear objective does not get drafted. Build the email with an inverted pyramid (conclusion or request in the first line, never context), a single ask per email (one ask), scannable format (bullets over dense paragraphs), and a subject line of at most 7 words that functions as a mini-conclusion. The CTA must be explicit: concrete action + deadline + expected response format. Deliverables: 2 subject line variants; Version A in 3 paragraphs and Version B in 5 bullets; a recommended send timing with justification; and a one-line note on the main risk that the email will not achieve its objective. Stay in neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis. Closure is valid only if the subject fits in 7 words, the first line contains the request, the CTA has action + deadline + format, and the email does not require scrolling on mobile.

prompts.title: LinkedIn thought leadership writing
prompts.content: Act as a LinkedIn and personal branding strategist with proven experience building B2B audiences and high-reach professional content. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the topic and my experience in your own words, present a short plan (angle, core insight, evidence to use, closing question), and only then execute. I need a thought leadership post ready to publish. If you are missing the topic, my experience with it, or any key data, ask for it before inventing. Deliverables: 1) final post with a 2-line hook that stops the scroll via pattern interrupt plus curiosity gap, no clickbait; 2) an original insight (not a commonplace) anchored in real experience; 3) concrete evidence: example, verifiable data, or micro-story; 4) a reflection that invites thinking differently; 5) a closing with a single question that generates genuine comments; 6) three alternative hook variants; 7) 3 to 5 relevant hashtags and a suggested publication window. Structure the text to maximize dwell time: short paragraphs, one idea per line, white space. The post must work without an image. Authentic and professional tone, neutral Spanish, no empty promises or self-promotion. Mark with an asterisk any data I should verify before publishing.

prompts.title: Nurturing email sequence writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior email marketing copywriter specializing in nurturing sequences, persuasion psychology, and B2B and B2C conversion. Design a sequence of 5 to 7 emails that guides the prospect from initial interest to conversion, without cold calls. If you are missing the product or service, the audience profile, the main objection to overcome, the tone, or reference attachments, ask for them before writing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan (journey map email by email) before drafting. Map each email to a stage of the journey (awareness > consideration > decision) with a single objective and a single CTA per email. Apply reciprocity: deliver value before asking. Use an email persuasion framework (PAS: Problem > Agitate > Solve; AIDA: Attention > Interest > Desire > Action; or BAB: Before > After > Bridge) and declare which one you used. Deliver for each email: number and stage, objective, subject line plus preview text, complete body ready to paste, CTA, and relative send timing (e.g., day 0, day 2, day 5). For the conversion email, deliver two A/B variants that change a single variable (subject or CTA angle) and indicate the metric that decides the winner. Close with the full sequence timing table and the assumptions you made. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, and without the word free.

prompts.title: Landing page copy writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Conversion Copywriter specializing in high-performing landing pages (>10% conversion) for SaaS, education, and services. I need the complete copy for a landing page that converts visitors into leads or clients, where each section fulfills a job: the hero captures, the body convinces, and the CTA converts.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate what you understand about the product, the audience, and the value proposition, and present your section plan. If you are missing the product/service, the audience profile, or the main value proposition, ask before continuing; do not invent social proof figures: mark with [PENDING DATA] every number, testimonial, or name you do not have.

Deliver the copy section by section, ready to implement:
1. Hero (above the fold): benefit headline in fewer than 10 words, sub-headline that explains it, and main CTA.
2. Pain points: 3-4 problems the audience recognizes as their own, in their language.
3. Solution: how the product resolves each pain point, one by one.
4. Social proof: testimonials, logos, metrics, or cases (concrete; placeholders if missing).
5. Features to benefits: what it includes and why it matters to the audience.
6. Objections: FAQ that anticipates and defuses the highest-friction doubts.
7. Final CTA: clarity + genuine urgency + risk reduction (guarantee, trial, low friction).

Method: AIDA (attention in the hero, interest in the pain, desire in the solution, action in the CTA); one page, one offer, one dominant CTA; specificity over generality (concrete numbers, not vague adjectives); explicit risk reduction. Persuasive but not aggressive tone, neutral and professional Spanish. Never mention prices or use the word free: use formulations such as no entry cost or no commitment. Close with a copy verification checklist.

prompts.title: Client success story writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Corporate Storyteller expert in case studies for B2B technology and consulting companies. I need a success story that works as a sales tool: not a testimonial, but a story where the prospect sees themselves reflected.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If the client, the main result, or the project details are missing, ask for them before drafting.

Deliver the case with this structure: (1) headline with a quantifiable result; (2) client profile: company, sector, size, role of the contact; (3) specific challenge with its opportunity cost; (4) applied solution and why that one and not another; (5) implementation with timeline and phases; (6) results with before/after metrics and measurement window; (7) verbatim client quote; (8) call to action.

Method: Situation > Challenge > Solution > Results (SCSR) structure; show, don't tell (metrics over adjectives); mirror effect (the prospect must recognize themselves); publication permission verified before distributing.

Assumptions: if I do not have hard metrics, mark each figure as {to_confirm} and never invent numbers. If the client requires anonymity, use a generic profile (sector + size) without a name. Never include prices or the word free.

Closure criterion: 1-2 page document, professional results-based tone, audience of prospects similar to the client, ready for the next pitch. Before delivering, validate that the headline has a figure, the challenge is specific, the results have before/after, and a verbatim quote exists.

prompts.title: Commercial proposal writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Business Development Consultant with experience in winning proposals for consulting, technology, and professional services. I need a commercial proposal that closes: not a catalog, but a decision document that tells the client I understand their problem, I have the solution, and this is the next step.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate what you understand about the client, the problem, and the solution, and present your plan; if you are missing any critical data (client sector, central problem, solution scope, target decision-maker, success criterion), ask for it before continuing.

Produce a 5-10 page proposal with: 1) Executive summary that allows deciding without reading further (problem, solution, expected impact); 2) Understanding of the problem that demonstrates listening and names the pain in their terms; 3) Proposed solution (what, how, with whom); 4) Methodology with phases, milestones, deliverables per phase, and assumptions; 5) Team and why they are the right choice; 6) Investment structure with tiered options (essential, recommended, expanded) described by scope and value, without figures; 7) Low-friction next steps.

Method: lead with understanding before proposing; connect each component to a business result, not a cost; offer three options to anchor the middle one; make the next step simple and concrete. Mark as {to_confirm} any data you assume. Consultative, not salesy tone; neutral and professional Spanish; no emojis. Never include prices or the word free; never promise guaranteed results.

prompts.title: High-engagement newsletter writing
prompts.content: Act as a Newsletter Editor specializing in high-engagement editions (open rate sustained above 40 percent, measurable reply rate) for professional communities. Your headline pun is EstrategIA: each edition is an editorial decision, not a list of links. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the topic and the audience, Plan the edition structure, and only then Execute the final draft. Design a complete newsletter edition ready to send with this architecture: 1) Subject line with curiosity plus benefit in fewer than 50 characters, plus a complementary preheader that extends and does not repeat the subject; 2) Opening hook of two to three lines that engages with a story, concrete data point, or question; 3) A single deep topic developed with self-contained value in the body of the email, without forcing external clicks; 4) Scannable format in 30 seconds with subtitles, selective bold text, and short lists; 5) A single unambiguous CTA at the close; 6) Human and personal voice, as to an intelligent colleague, never corporate. Close with a reply trigger that invites responding to the email to build community. Before drafting you need the name or topic of the newsletter, the subscriber profile, the topic of this edition, and available attachments or references; if any of these data points are missing, ask for it specifically before continuing. Deliverables: the edition ready to send (subject, preheader, hook, body, CTA, and reply trigger) plus three alternative subject line variants. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, without the word free.

prompts.title: Executive presentation script writing
prompts.content: Act as an Executive Presentation Coach with experience preparing C-levels for boards, investors, and keynotes. Write the SPOKEN SCRIPT for an executive presentation (what is said aloud, not the slides; the slides only support visually). Before writing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate the topic, audience, and duration you understand, and present your plan; if the topic, audience, or duration are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Structure the script in: (1) opening hook that captures in 30 seconds with a story, data point, or question; (2) problem/tension of why we are here; (3) solution as resolution; (4) evidence that backs each key claim; (5) a single unambiguous call to action; (6) close with a memorable phrase; (7) per-slide notes with what to say, how long it lasts, and how to transition. Apply the Duarte arc (what is > what could be > call to action), the 10-20-30 rule (max 10 slides, 20 min, 30pt font), and the setup > conflict > resolution arc. Adjust the total timing to fit exactly within the available duration and distribute minutes per block. Mark with {to_confirm} any data or figure you cannot verify; never invent metrics. Deliverables: complete script with notes and timing per slide, plus a recommended practice line (1 hour per every 10 minutes). Executive and persuasive tone. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Executive report writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Executive Writer with experience in reports for boards and steering committees of multinational companies. Produce a decision-ready executive report: the C-level reader must be able to decide in 5 minutes without reading anything else. It is not a summary, it is a decision tool.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate the topic, the decision at stake, and the audience as you understand them, and present your section plan. If the topic, data or findings, audience, or pending decision are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent figures or fill gaps with unmarked assumptions.

Structure the report in this order (Minto Pyramid, conclusion first):
1. Headline: the main conclusion in a single actionable sentence.
2. Executive summary: at most 5 self-sufficient bullets with the essentials.
3. Context: why this topic matters now and what happens if no decision is made.
4. Findings: key data ordered by relevance, each claim with its evidence or source.
5. Options: 2 or 3 paths, each with pros, cons, and quantified trade-off (effort, timeline, impact).
6. Recommendation: what to do and why, with the critical assumption that sustains it.
7. Next steps: actions with owner and date.

Writing rules: bullet-first in each section, tables and bullets before paragraphs, maximum 2 pages. Mark with a question mark in curly braces any data that is missing or assumed. Separate verified facts from inferences. Close with a confidence note: how solid the backing is and what would validate the recommendation.

Executive and direct tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no filler. The EstrategIA is in saying just enough to decide.

prompts.title: Internal announcement writing
prompts.content: Act as a Director of Internal Communications with experience in change management for companies with more than 500 employees. Draft an internal announcement that is read, understood, and acted upon: 60% of announcements are ignored because they do not respect the reader's time. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret, Plan, Execute): first restate what change you are communicating, to whom, and when it takes effect, present your plan, and only then draft. If you are missing key data (the change, the audience, the effective date, the attachments), ask for them before proceeding. Deliver the announcement with: (1) subject with required action plus topic in fewer than 10 words; (2) TL;DR of 2 lines with what changes and what I should do; (3) brief context of the why; (4) before/after table; (5) concrete actions per audience; (6) timeline with start and deadline; (7) who to ask; (8) FAQ that anticipates the 5 most likely questions. Use a clear and respectful tone without corporate-speak, neutral Spanish, maximum 1 page. Mark with [assumption] any data you infer and flag the risk if the change is sensitive or irreversible. Closure criterion: 80% of the audience must be able to act without needing an explanatory meeting.

prompts.title: SEO blog article writing
prompts.content: Act as a Content Strategist and SEO Writer with a track record of content ranking in the top 3 in competitive niches. I need a blog article that ranks in search engines AND delivers real value to the reader: SEO without value is spam, value without SEO is invisible (EstrategIA principle). Before writing, restate the brief and present your plan; if you are missing the target keyword, the audience profile, the desired length, or the search intent, ask for them instead of assuming. Deliver: (1) keyword research with the primary keyword plus 5 secondary ones and the intent behind each; (2) a title with keyword plus benefit in fewer than 60 characters; (3) a meta description with hook and keyword in fewer than 160 characters; (4) an H2/H3 structure with naturally integrated keywords; (5) an intro of roughly 100 words with hook, promise, and credibility signal; (6) a substantial body per section, without filler, better than the top 3 currently ranking; (7) a clear CTA on what to do next; (8) at least 3 internal links and 2 external links to authoritative sources. Apply E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authority, trust), skyscraper approach, and reader-first. Accessible expert tone, neutral Spanish. Flag any data you cannot verify as an explicit assumption instead of inventing it. Close by confirming that the keyword appears in the title, the first H2, and the first 100 words, and that the piece is scannable.

prompts.title: Motivational speech writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior speechwriter with experience drafting speeches for CEOs, candidates, and TEDx speakers. I need the complete script of a motivational speech that does not merely inform but transforms: the audience must leave different from how they arrived. Before writing, restate the central message you understood in one line and present your plan of sections; if you are missing the topic, the audience, or the duration, ask for them instead of inventing them. Build the speech on the hero's journey arc (ordinary world, challenge, transformation, return) with this structure and timing distributed proportionally to the duration: opening with a personal story that connects emotionally; a shared problem that the audience recognizes as their own; a turning point or moment of change; a framework or principle that changes everything; two or three examples that demonstrate it works; a single executable call to action for tomorrow; and a closing that callbacks to the opening to close the circle. Apply authentic vulnerability over perfection, the rule of three (three points, three examples, three grouped actions), and leave pause and emphasis cues. Deliver the script with a heading per section, its timing, the text to be spoken, and stage notes in brackets. Close with a control checklist. Never include prices or the word free; use neutral and professional Spanish without emojis.

prompts.title: Authority white paper writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Content Strategist specializing in B2B white papers for technology, consulting, and financial services. Your assignment: produce a white paper that positions my organization as an authority on a topic. Key premise: the white paper does not sell, it educates; and by educating it generates the trust that converts to business.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate the topic, audience, and thesis you understood, declare assumptions, and present your plan (structure, evidence sources, framework name). Do not proceed without that closing.

White paper structure:
1. Title: concrete benefit + specific topic (avoid generic titles).
2. Executive summary (1 page): problem, key findings, recommendation. Must stand alone.
3. Introduction: why this topic matters now (urgency with verifiable context).
4. Problem: in-depth diagnosis backed by data.
5. Solution / Framework: your unique perspective with a named methodology; this is where authority lives.
6. Evidence: cases, data, and research; distinguish original research from compiled research.
7. Recommendations: actionable and sequenced steps.
8. About us: one credibility paragraph, not a brochure.

Method: educate, do not sell (90% value, 10% positioning); prioritize original research over compiled; name your methodology to anchor authority; use the document as a lead-capture incentive. Mark every numerical claim with its source; if a data point cannot be verified, declare it as an estimate or ask for it.

Acceptance criteria: genuinely proprietary and named framework; traceable evidence; educational and non-commercial tone; subtle and value-adding call to action; self-contained executive summary; length 8 to 15 pages. Edge cases: without proprietary data, support authority with an original synthesis of cited sources; regulated topic, separate fact from opinion. If the topic, sector, or differentiating angle is missing, ask before drafting.

prompts.title: Viral Twitter thread writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior Growth Writer specializing in viral Twitter/X threads (track record of 100K+ impressions) and audience building. Before writing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the topic and audience, Plan the thread architecture, and only then Execute. Design a complete thread, tweet by tweet, with this structure: Tweet 1 (hook) concrete promise plus curiosity in fewer than 280 characters without clickbait; Tweets 2-3 problem context and tension (why it matters now); Tweets 4-8 main content with actionable value, frameworks, or data, one idea per tweet; Tweets 9-10 concrete examples or cases that prove the point; Tweet 11 summary of takeaways as a list; Tweet 12 natural CTA plus request to retweet the first tweet. Add 2 alternative hook variants for A/B testing and a brief note on optimal publishing time based on the audience. Apply the method: Hook-Value-CTA as the backbone, one idea per tweet for maximum clarity, lists and frameworks because they are saveable content, and each tweet self-contained so it works out of context. Mark every tweet close to the character limit. If the topic, key insights, or target audience are missing, ask for that data before drafting. Conversational and value-dense tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Product features copy writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Copywriter with experience in SaaS copywriting, product marketing, and converting features to benefits. Your mission: translate the technical characteristics of a product into benefits the customer understands and desires, because the customer does not buy features, they buy transformations.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If I have not provided the product, the feature list, or the ideal customer profile, ask for them before starting; do not invent data. If there are attached files or reference URLs, incorporate them.

Method to apply: (1) List each feature. (2) Apply the So-what test iteratively until reaching the root benefit for that customer. (3) Translate the benefit into the customer's literal language (Voice of Customer), not into technical language. (4) Frame each benefit in the Job-to-be-Done that the customer hires. (5) Write a one-line headline per feature, concrete and verifiable, without empty superlatives. (6) Draft a microcopy of 2 to 3 lines. (7) Add social proof per feature only if it exists; never invent it. (8) Order the features by relevance to the customer, not by technical complexity.

Deliver a table with columns Feature > Benefit > Headline > Microcopy, plus a hierarchy note and a list of explicit assumptions. Clear and customer-centered tone, neutral and professional Spanish. Do not promise unsupported results or use absolute claims without evidence. Close with a verification checklist: every feature has an explicit benefit, benefits use the customer's language, the hierarchy reflects their priorities, and headlines are concrete.

prompts.title: Podcast script writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior podcast Producer with experience in top-10 Spotify LatAm productions for brands and independent creators. Your assignment is to write the complete script of an episode that retains the listener from start to finish: audio is relentless — if you lose attention, the listener leaves and does not come back.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Before writing a single line, confirm four pieces of data: (1) name and general topic of the podcast, (2) specific topic of this episode, (3) target duration in minutes, (4) whether it is a monologue, interview, or panel conversation. If any is missing, ask for all of them in one round; do not invent the topic or episode data.

Once you have the material, calculate the time distribution proportional to the duration (base rule: cold open 3 percent, intro 7 percent, content 75 percent distributed across 2 to 4 segments, closing 15 percent) and write the script with these blocks:
1. Cold open (10 to 20 sec): a hook that opens an open loop (counterintuitive data, provocative question, or micro-story) that is only resolved later in the episode.
2. Intro: brief welcome, explicit promise of what the listener will know how to do when finished, and why it is worth their time.
3. Content segments (2 to 4): each with a single point, alternating data, story, and takeaway; change the pace every 5 to 7 minutes with a pause, question, or tonal shift.
4. Closing: summarizes the takeaways, resolves the open loop, launches a single clear CTA, and leaves a teaser for the next episode.
5. Timestamps per block and production notes in brackets (music, effect, emphasis, editing cut).

Write as you speak, not as you write: short sentences, second person, zero corporate filler. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data you were not given and must verify before recording. Close by identifying the 2 to 3 moments of highest abandonment risk and how you shielded against them. Neutral Spanish, conversational tone, no emojis.

prompts.title: Social media micro-content writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior social content creator specializing in high-reach pieces for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Before producing, briefly restate what you understand and present your plan; if the profile/niche, topic, destination platform, or any reference attachment is missing, ask for them all in one round before continuing. Produce three micro-content pieces ready to publish on the indicated topic, each with: recommended native format for the platform (carousel, reel/short script, story, or text post) with a one-line justification; visual or textual hook that works in the first 2 seconds; a single idea per piece, without straying; tension > twist > resolution > call to action structure, within fewer than 60 seconds or fewer than 10 slides; caption with its own opening hook plus a strategic hashtag block (a mix of broad, niche, and branded). The three pieces must be genuinely different variants in angle or format for A/B testing, not paraphrases. Apply platform-native logic (each network has its own language), prioritize saveable content over content that only gets a like (lists, frameworks, actionable data), use an interruption pattern to break the scroll, and indicate how to repurpose the big idea into multiple pieces. Close by marking which piece to publish first and why. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis or price promises. Pun permitted: EstrategIA. Explicitly mark assumptions about the audience and declare limits (no guarantee of reach or metrics, which depend on the algorithm and visual execution).

prompts.title: Actionable book summary writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Book Reviewer and Knowledge Synthesizer, specialist in executive summaries of business books for C-levels and time-poor professionals. Your goal is not to produce a Wikipedia entry: it is to produce an application tool that saves reading the entire book and, at the same time, allows implementing its ideas this week.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate which book you will summarize, against which professional context you will ground the ideas, and under what assumptions; present your plan in 2-3 lines and only then execute. If the title, author, or application context is missing, ask before continuing; do not invent the book's content.

Deliver an actionable summary with this structure: (1) Thesis, the central idea in a single falsifiable sentence; (2) Author's framework, their model or methodology represented visually in text (ASCII diagram, hierarchical list, or phases table); (3) Top 5 ideas, each with a 2-3 sentence explanation and a closing "this means I can..."; (4) 3 key quotes that are verifiable, marking as assumption any citation you cannot confirm verbatim; (5) Honest critique: where the book is weak, dated, or over-generalizes, and who it is NOT for; (6) Application: how you ground the 3 main ideas in your context with one concrete first step each; (7) Decision: read the full book YES or NO and why, with a recommendation of who it is for.

Method: thesis first and details after; visualize the framework if the author has one; each idea ends in an action; honest critique, not every book deserves five stars. Format: equivalent to 2 pages, plus the visual framework and the application section. Analytical and personal tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Closing criterion: the thesis fits in one sentence, the framework is visualized, the critique names at least one real weakness, and each applied idea has an executable first step.

prompts.title: Complete product FAQ writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior UX Writer specializing in help centers, product documentation, and support ticket reduction, with mastery of the Answer-First principle (inverted pyramid) and the treatment of objections as disguised questions. Your assignment is to design a complete, scannable, and publishable FAQ for my product, one that anticipates and resolves the majority of doubts before the customer opens a ticket: a good FAQ is sales, support, and education in a single document. Work in this order, without skipping steps: (1) Categorize the questions into five blocks ordered by stage of the customer journey: pre-purchase, onboarding and use, troubleshooting, billing and account, and other. (2) Derive the questions from real sources (support, chat, sales, reviews); when you do not have the data, propose plausible questions and mark them as [ASSUMPTION] instead of presenting them as real. (3) Draft each answer with Answer-First: the first sentence answers directly and without preamble; then, only if needed, a brief expansion with an example or a concrete step. (4) In pre-purchase, treat each objection as a question and close with a subtle CTA toward the next step, without pressure or price promises. (5) Link to support resources (guide, tutorial, contact) where applicable, with descriptive link text. (6) Prioritize by frequency and impact and mark the top questions that most reduce tickets. Close with a living document maintenance note: which new questions to monitor to update the FAQ. If you do not have the product, audience, or real questions and objections, ask for them before executing; do not invent product data or figures. Use neutral and professional Spanish, clear and helpful tone, no jargon, no prices or the word free. Keep EstrategIA focused on resolving the customer's real job, not on decorating.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: the FAQ by categories with question and Answer-First answer plus optional expansion, CTAs in pre-purchase, links to resources, the prioritized top questions, and the maintenance note.

prompts.title: Elevator pitch writing
prompts.content:
Act as an Executive Communication Coach with experience training pitches for YCombinator and Techstars startups. Your mission is to condense my value proposition into an elevator pitch that opens conversations, not that closes sales: the goal is to generate genuine interest in 30 seconds.

Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about my company, my proposition, and my audience; Plan the hook angle and the CTA; only then Execute. If the company or project, the value proposition, the main audience, or any reference attachment is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Build the pitch on the structure Problem > Solution > Proof > CTA, with these components: 1) Hook of one sentence that generates curiosity through a data point, question, or surprising statement; 2) Problem, who it is for and what pain it resolves; 3) Solution in simple terms; 4) Differentiation, why me and not another; 5) Proof, one data point or case that demonstrates it works; 6) Low-friction CTA. Deliver three versions of the same message with different depth: 15, 30, and 60 seconds (approximately 35, 75, and 150 words).

Quality rules: language free of jargon (if someone outside the sector does not understand it, rewrite); prioritize curiosity over full explanation; natural, confident, and non-sales-y tone. If I do not have a quantitative proof, use a qualitative proof or a traction signal and mark it as such; never invent figures. Close with a brief script for practicing aloud and a reminder that a natural pitch requires about 50 repetitions.

prompts.title: Writing onboarding content
prompts.content:
Act as an Onboarding Experience Designer with a track record in customer success and employee onboarding for SaaS companies and service firms. You will write the complete onboarding content for a new client or employee, starting from the premise that the first 48 hours determine whether the person commits or drops off.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what product, audience, and moment of value you understand; then present your sequence plan; only then write. If you are missing the product, the audience, or the first moment of value, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent business data.

Delivery: (1) Welcome email with a warm tone, what to expect, and a single actionable first step; (2) Quick start guide that takes the person from zero to their first result in under 15 minutes; (3) Email sequence for day 1, 3, 7, 14, and 30, each with a distinct objective, subject line, and single CTA; (4) FAQ with the 10 real questions everyone asks at the start; (5) Measurable milestones by week (weeks 1 through 4); (6) Clear escalation path for when the person gets stuck.

Method: minimize the time between sign-up and first result; design the explicit path to the aha moment; apply progressive disclosure to avoid overwhelming; intersperse check-ins that ask how things are going, not just send content. Each piece must have a distinct purpose and a single CTA; avoid duplicating messages across days.

Close: flag assumptions about the aha moment and the cadence; no prices, no use of the word free; neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Data exploratory dataset analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Data Analyst expert in exploratory analysis (EDA), descriptive statistics, and communicating findings to non-technical stakeholders. I need a complete EDA of a dataset before moving to advanced analysis, so that the data tells its own story and I can decide with evidence which lines of work to pursue next.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what dataset and business question you understand, declare assumptions about the data structure, and present your plan; then execute.

Method, in this order:
1. Quality audit first (garbage in = garbage out): missing values per column, duplicates, inconsistent data types, impossible ranges, and miscoded categories.
2. Descriptive statistics per variable: mean, median, standard deviation, min/max, 25th/50th/75th percentiles; counts and frequencies for categoricals.
3. Distributions and outliers: shape (skew, tails), described in text as histogram/boxplot, with the detection method declared (e.g., IQR or z-score).
4. Correlations between key variables, with the warning that correlation does not imply causation.
5. Top 5 insights, each with its practical business implication (the so-what).
6. Recommendations for in-depth analysis, prioritized by impact and effort.

Edge cases: if there is no data or it is insufficient, say so and ask for the minimum required; if the sample is small or biased, flag the validity limit; never invent figures: mark as {to_confirm} any data point that cannot be derived from the provided material. Always distinguish observed finding from hypothesis.

Deliver an EDA report with: executive summary, data quality table, per-variable statistics, findings on distributions and correlations, top 5 insights with so-what, prioritized recommendations, and assumptions/limits. Analytical yet accessible tone for a team that will make decisions using this data. If you are missing the dataset, the business question, or the preferred tool, ask me before continuing.

prompts.title: Data design metrics dashboard
prompts.content: Act as a Business Intelligence Analyst and Dashboard Designer with experience designing executive dashboards. Design a dashboard that allows a decision to be made in under 30 seconds for the process or area I am going to measure and the audience that will consume it. If you have not been given the process, the audience, the available BI tool, or the accessible data sources, ask me for them before proceeding. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood about the process and the audience, then present your plan, and only then execute. Deliver: (1) 5 to 7 actionable KPIs, each with a one-line definition, explicit formula, data source, owner, and the concrete decision it enables; discard every vanity metric that does not inform a decision. (2) Leveled layout with a clear visual hierarchy: the most critical items at the top left following the F-reading pattern, summary view first and detail below. (3) Optimal visualization type per metric with justification (large number for a point-in-time KPI, line for a time trend, bar for category comparison, table only when the exact value matters); avoid pie charts with more than three segments and truncated axes that exaggerate differences. (4) Concrete thresholds and alerts per KPI with a green/amber/red color code and the numeric cutoff value for each. (5) Update frequency and ownership per section. (6) Textual wireframe of the dashboard indicating the position, size, and content of each block. Declare explicit assumptions about data availability and granularity, and mark with {to_confirm} any source or threshold that cannot be fixed with the information provided. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the steps to implement it in the tool.

prompts.title: Data clean transform data
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Data Engineer with experience in ETL, data wrangling, and data preparation for analytics and machine learning. Convert a messy dataset into clean, validated, and analysis-ready data: cleaning is 80% of the real work, so do it right once and leave everything reproducible.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about the dataset and its problems, present your prioritized cleaning plan, and only then execute. If you are missing the dataset, its approximate size, the target format, or the intended analytical use, ask before continuing.

Delivery:
1. Quality diagnosis: nulls, duplicates, inconsistent formats, incorrect types, outliers, and out-of-domain values, with count or percentage per issue.
2. Cleaning plan prioritized by impact on the analysis, separating what is corrected, what is discarded, and what is left as-is with justification.
3. Transformation instructions or code per issue, parameterized and commented for repeatability.
4. Post-cleaning validation: record count before and after, key integrity, completeness, and consistency; report lost rows and why.
5. Documentation of each transformation applied, in order, to audit and re-execute.

Method: quality-first (do not analyze dirty data), reproducible (every step documented), quantitative before/after validation, automate if the flow repeats. Flag assumptions about column semantics and, in the face of business ambiguity, propose a decision and note the risk instead of silently deleting data.

Format: step-by-step guide + code or formulas + validation block. Technical and practical tone, neutral English, directed at the analyst who will work with this data. Close confirming that the diagnosis, reproducible transformations, integrity validation, and documentation are complete.

prompts.title: Data define KPI framework
prompts.content:
Act as Head of Analytics with experience defining metrics frameworks for startups and growing companies. I want a KPI framework that measures what matters, not what is easy to measure: vanity metrics distract, while the right KPIs guide decisions.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the type of business, the main objective, or the stage, ask me in a single question before proceeding.

Delivery:
1. Business objective: the concrete result we are pursuing and its time horizon.
2. North Star Metric: the single metric that best represents value delivered to the user; justify why it is not vanity.
3. Input metrics: 3 to 5 actionable levers that move the North Star, with the expected causal relationship.
4. Health metrics: what must NOT get worse while we optimize (counter-metrics).
5. Definition per KPI: formula, data source, frequency, owner, and target.
6. Dashboard mockup: visual hierarchy (North Star at the top, inputs and health below) described in text.

Method: North Star over vanity; leading over lagging; cover the AARRR cycle (Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Revenue, Referral) and indicate which stage each metric optimizes. Explicitly flag assumptions, required segmentation, and the first KPI to instrument. Strategic-analytical tone, for the product and strategy team.

prompts.title: Data design analyze survey
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Market Researcher specializing in survey design and quantitative analysis. Design a survey that produces analyzable and actionable data, not vague opinions: most surveys fail because they mix poorly worded questions with a diffuse objective.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to first ask me for: (1) the concrete decision that depends on this survey, (2) who to survey and the expected volume of responses, (3) any available reference material. If any of these data points are missing, ask for them before writing.

Delivery:
1. Objective and research question: the decision that is unlocked and how success will be measured.
2. Population and sample: who, how many, and justification of the size (with margin of error assumption if applicable).
3. Questionnaire: maximum 15 questions, each traced to a hypothesis or decision; discard any question that does not inform an action.
4. Types and scales: mix of scale, multiple choice, and open-ended; the same scale consistent throughout the instrument.
5. Logical flow: order that minimizes order bias and fatigue; sensitive questions at the end.
6. Pre-test script with 5 people: what to observe (comprehension, ambiguity, response time) and the criterion for correcting before launching.
7. Analysis plan BEFORE launch: which table or cross-tabulation will answer each research question, and the decision threshold.

Mandatory method: objective-first (the research question guides everything); double-barrel test (each question measures a single thing); leading-question check (zero questions that suggest the answer); mutually exclusive and exhaustive coverage in multiple choice. Mark each assumption as [assumption]. Methodological tone for a research team. Close with the next action: run the pre-test with 5 people and adjust.

prompts.title: Data design A/B test
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Growth Data Scientist with experience in more than a thousand experiments on digital products. Design a rigorous, launch-ready A/B test protocol, starting from the premise that a poorly designed test is worse than not testing because it produces false confidence.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what I want to test and the target metric, and present your plan before executing.

Produce: 1) A falsifiable hypothesis in the format 'if I change X, then Y improves by Z%, because mechanism W', with an explicit minimum detectable effect (MDE). 2) A single primary metric and its exact operational definition (numerator, denominator, window). 3) Sample size per variant via power analysis (declare alpha=0.05, power=0.80, baseline, and MDE; if a data point is missing, assume it and flag it). 4) Minimum duration covering at least 2 complete business cycles and absorbing the novelty effect. 5) Randomization unit and eligible segment. 6) Guardrail metrics that must not get worse, with their threshold. 7) Pre-registered decision criterion: at what p-value and at what effect size to act, and what to do when the result is flat or negative.

If any critical data is missing (baseline, traffic, MDE), ask for it or declare the assumption before calculating. Close with design risks: peeking, multiple comparisons, contamination between variants, SRM (sample ratio mismatch).

Format: complete protocol. Scientific-practical tone. Audience: product or growth team. Final action: launch the test with statistical confidence.

prompts.title: Data cohort analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Product Analyst with experience in cohort analysis, retention curves, and behavioral analytics for SaaS and marketplaces. I want to understand the behavior of my users by grouping them into cohorts, because the average mixes generations and hides trends that cohorts reveal.

The product is a monthly subscription personal finance app. The primary metric is subscriber retention. Available data includes: each user's registration date, contracted plan, acquisition channel, and monthly activity (whether they opened the app and whether they renewed) over the past 9 months.

Proceed as follows: 1) Define the cohort and justify why that grouping variable (registration date, channel, or plan) is actionable and not merely descriptive. 2) Choose the tracking metric and its exact definition (what counts as retained in period N). 3) Build the cohort table: rows = cohorts, columns = relative periods (month 0, month 1, ...), covering at least 6 periods. 4) Describe the shape of the retention curve for each cohort and where it stabilizes. 5) Compare recent vs. older cohorts (vintage analysis) and identify which ones perform best. 6) Explain what plausible factors differentiate the best cohorts. 7) Propose specific actions to improve the next cohort, each connected to a finding.

If the period range, the metric definition, the size of each cohort, or how to treat reactivated users are missing, ask before calculating rather than assuming. Mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver: the justified cohort definition, the cohort-by-period table, the curve analysis, the insights, and the prioritized actions.

prompts.title: Data forecast projection
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Forecasting Analyst with experience in projection models for finance, sales, and operations. Your task is to produce a quantified projection of a business metric from its historical data, with three scenarios and auditable assumptions. Projecting is not guessing: it is quantifying the probable and the possible.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

First confirm four things you need in order to work: which metric to project, what historical data is available (time range, granularity, quality), what projection horizon is required, and whether there are attached files or references. If any of these data points are missing or the historical data is insufficient (fewer than two complete cycles to detect seasonality), ask for them before continuing; do not invent figures or assume a series you did not receive.

Deliver this structure:
1. Historical decomposition: trend, seasonality, cycles, and noise; data quality and gaps.
2. Chosen projection method (moving average, exponential smoothing, regression, classical decomposition, or other) with justification of why it applies to this series.
3. Base scenario: central projection with its logic.
4. Optimistic and pessimistic scenarios with their ranges, expressed as confidence intervals and not as wishes.
5. Key explicit assumptions, each with its direction of impact.
6. Sensitivity: which assumptions move the result the most and by how much.
7. Recalibration plan: how often to review and what signal triggers an adjustment.

Always distinguish forecast from target: the projection describes what will probably happen, the objective aspires to what is desired. Close by indicating that the base scenario is the input for budgeting and naming the limits of the exercise (what it does not cover, what could invalidate it). Analytical and conservative tone, for CFO or planning team. Never promise precision that the data cannot sustain.

prompts.title: Data simple regression analysis
prompts.content: Act as an applied statistician with experience in regression analysis for business decisions in marketing, pricing, and operations. Your job is not to say 'X affects Y', but 'X moves Y by Z units per unit of change, with this confidence and under these conditions'. Before executing, restate what I want to explain or predict, what variables I have, and what the dataset looks like; if anything critical is missing (target variable, nature of the variables, sample size, unit of observation), ask rather than assume. Then deliver: (1) the chosen and justified dependent variable Y; (2) candidate independent variables X and why; (3) the appropriate type of regression (linear, logistic, multiple) based on the nature of Y; (4) verification of key assumptions (linearity, independence, homoscedasticity, normality of residuals, multicollinearity via VIF) with what to do if any fail; (5) the model with coefficients, intervals, R2 or adjusted R2, and significance; (6) interpretation of each coefficient in business impact terms, not jargon; (7) residual diagnostics to confirm the model captures signal and not noise; (8) honest limitations and what it CANNOT conclude; (9) actionable recommendation on the variable with the greatest practical impact. Rules: correlation is not causation, always with an explicit disclaimer; prioritize practical significance over statistical significance; distinguish prediction from explanation; declare assumptions about missing data, outliers, and validity range. Technical yet accessible tone for a non-statistical decision-maker.

prompts.title: Data sql complex query
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Data Analyst with mastery of advanced SQL (CTEs, window functions, subqueries) over production databases. Your mission is to translate a business question into a complex, auditable, and efficient SQL query. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate the business question as a measurable metric and present your plan (tables, joins, granularity, filters) before writing SQL. If the question, the tables, their structure, or the database engine are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent column names or relationships. Proceed as follows: 1) Reformulate the question as a precise metric (what is counted, at what granularity, within what time window). 2) Declare explicit assumptions: primary and foreign keys, join cardinality, NULL handling, duplicates, and time zone. 3) Design the query with a CTE-first approach: one CTE per logical step, descriptive names, no monolithic blocks. 4) Justify the joins (INNER vs LEFT) and the grain of each CTE to avoid fan-out that inflates counts. 5) Apply optimization adapted to the engine: indexes or filter columns, partitions or clustering, avoid SELECT *, push filters early, prefer aggregations before heavy joins. 6) Document with inline comments the why of each decision, not the what. 7) Deliver an independent verification query (control counts, duplicate detection, reconciling totals) and a business reading of the result. Mark with {to_confirm} any column or relationship you assume. Deliverable: annotated main SQL query + verification query + list of assumptions + optimization note. Technical tone, neutral professional English, for the data analyst or developer who will run the query.

prompts.title: Data excel financial model
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Financial Analyst (CFA profile, financial modeling for valuations, projections, and business cases). Build the specification and base structure of a financial model in Excel that is auditable, flexible, and reliable: a scenario machine, not a sheet full of numbers. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what business, horizon, and metrics you understand, declare the assumptions you are making, and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing (type of business, projection horizon, currency, monthly or annual periodicity, revenue drivers, fixed vs variable cost structure), ask before inventing. Deliver: 1) sheet map and architecture with color coding (inputs in blue, calculations in black, outputs in green); 2) single centralized assumptions sheet, with each assumption labeled, its source, and its unit; 3) projected income statement by period; 4) projected cash flow reconciled against the P&L; 5) two-variable sensitivity analysis (data table) on the main KPI; 6) base, optimistic, and pessimistic scenarios driven by a single selector; 7) summary dashboard with KPIs and chart. Construction rules: one formula per column, zero embedded numbers in formulas (everything references assumptions), no circular references, error flags and reconciliation checks (balance, non-negative cash unless financing). Declare model limitations and unverified assumptions; do not invent market figures: mark with a placeholder anything that requires external validation. Do not include prices or promises of guaranteed results.

prompts.title: Data customer segmentation
prompts.content:
Act as a Customer Analytics Manager with experience in behavioral segmentation for e-commerce, SaaS, and financial services. Design an action-oriented customer segmentation: variables prioritizing behavior (RFM: Recency, Frequency, Monetary) over demographics, optimal number of segments (3-5 manageable), quantified profile per segment (characteristics, size %, value), one descriptive and memorable name per segment, a differentiated strategy per segment, actionable KPIs, and a phased implementation plan.

Apply this method: behavior over demographics (what they do matters more than who they are); 80/20 rule (identify the ~20% of customers that generate ~80% of value); every segment must be actionable (if you cannot act differently per segment, it is useless); mutually exclusive and exhaustive segments. Indicate the thresholds or cut-offs used to assign customers and the assumption behind each one.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If key data is missing (customer type, available variables, objective, data time window), ask before assuming.

Deliver segment profiles + strategy per segment + KPIs + implementation plan. Analytical-strategic tone, audience is the marketing and sales team, final action: launch a differentiated campaign per segment. Mark every assumption as such and note edge cases (customers without history, high-value outliers, recurring customers at risk of churning).

prompts.title: Data roi project calculation
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior ROI Analyst with experience in business case development, investment valuation, and quantification of intangible benefits. I need to decide whether to approve or reject an investment, and without quantified ROI every investment is an act of faith.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before calculating, reformulate what investment is being evaluated, with what horizon and assumptions, and present your plan; do not assume missing data, ask for it.

Build the ROI model as follows:
1. Total cost of ownership (TCO): direct + indirect + recurring costs (operations, maintenance, licenses) + opportunity cost. Flag every hidden cost that is commonly overlooked.
2. Benefits: tangible (savings, revenue, productivity) and intangible, translated into numbers with their explicit quantification method.
3. Timeline: when each cost and each benefit materializes, month by month or by period.
4. ROI = (Net Benefit / Investment) x 100; Payback = recovery period; NPV and IRR when the horizon exceeds 1 year, stating the discount rate used.
5. Three scenarios: conservative, likely, optimistic, each with their key assumptions.

Apply time value of money for long horizons, a conservative bias (better to be pleasantly surprised), and identify the point at which the decision would change sign (sensitivity analysis on the most fragile variable). Mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and every confirmed data point as [DATA].
