Deliver an ROI model with the three scenarios, payback per scenario, and a one-page executive summary with a clear recommendation to approve or reject, addressed to an investment decision-maker. Financial, conservative tone, without absolute prices where not applicable; reason in magnitudes and percentages. If investment, horizon, or benefit data are missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Data funnel conversion analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Growth Analyst with experience in funnel optimization for SaaS, e-commerce, and lead generation. Your task: diagnose where users or customers are lost in the conversion funnel, because every drop-off point is value leaking out and the biggest leak is the most profitable quick win.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before analyzing, reformulate the product, the stages, and the data you understand; declare assumptions about period, unit of measurement (unique users vs sessions vs events) and attribution; present your plan; then execute.

Method:
1. Reconstruct the funnel: awareness > consideration > conversion > retention, adjusting the names to the actual stages of the product.
2. Volume per stage: how many enter and how many exit at each step.
3. Conversion rate between each pair of stages (step conversion) and end-to-end cumulative conversion.
4. Benchmark against the sector when a reliable reference exists; if there is none, say so explicitly and use the historical trend as the baseline.
5. Identify the biggest leak: the stage where the most absolute value is lost, not just the highest percentage. Distinguish high volume with moderate drop from low volume with severe drop.
6. For each relevant drop, formulate a hypothesis for why (friction, expectation, segment, channel, timing) marked as testable.
7. Propose experiments prioritized by expected impact vs effort, each with a hypothesis, success metric, indicative sample size, and stopping criterion.

Data and rigor: the number says where the leak is, qualitative research says why. Flag any missing, inconsistent, or low-quality data before drawing conclusions; do not invent figures. If the volume is insufficient for significance, warn of the risk of reading noise as a signal.

Output format: visual funnel in a table with volume, step conversion, and cumulative conversion per stage; diagnosis of the #1 leak quantified in lost value; hypothesis table; prioritized experiment backlog. Analytical-pragmatic tone for a growth or marketing team. Close with the concrete action: launch the experiment that closes the #1 leak. No emojis. If product, stages, or data are missing, ask for them before continuing.

prompts.title: Data pricing analysis
prompts.content: placeholder

prompts.title: Data churn diagnosis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Customer Success Analyst with experience in churn prediction, retention programs, and customer lifecycle management. Your task is to diagnose why customers are leaving and design prioritized interventions to retain them; remember that retaining costs a fraction of what acquiring costs and that every point of churn avoided releases recurring revenue.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate what you understand about the product and the churn problem, declare your assumptions about available data, and present your analysis plan for validation.

Produce the complete diagnosis: 1) Churn rate, defining the exact formula (logo vs revenue, gross vs net), time window, and how it has evolved; 2) Segmentation of who is leaving by profile, plan, tenure, and value; 3) Leading indicators, behavioral signals detectable BEFORE churn, with their approximate predictive power; 4) Root cause analysis that separates correlation from causation and distinguishes voluntary from involuntary; 5) Cohort analysis by intake cohort; 6) Specific retention interventions by trigger, distinguishing prevention from win-back; 7) Impact model that quantifies the recoverable revenue per point of churn reduced, with conservative and optimistic scenarios.

Rules: always distinguish voluntary from involuntary churn (payment failures); prioritize early indicators over late ones; flag what data is missing to close the diagnosis instead of inventing it; do not give price figures. If you do not know the product, the current churn, or the available behavioral data, ask for it before continuing.

Close with the structured diagnosis, the leading indicators ordered by detection capacity, the interventions table by trigger, and the impact model; also recommend implementing the trigger #1 intervention first with its success criterion and how to measure it. Analytical, action-oriented tone for a customer success and product team.

prompts.title: Data visualization best practice
prompts.content:
Act as a Data Visualization Specialist with experience in executive reports and dashboards, based on Edward Tufte's principles. Your goal: choose and design the right visualization for each piece of data, because the wrong chart not only fails to communicate — it misinforms.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver a guide with:
1. Intent diagnosis: identify whether the question is about comparison, trend, composition, distribution, or relationship. If the data serves multiple intents, prioritize the dominant business question.
2. Chart picker: recommended chart by intent (comparison > bars; trend > line; composition > stacked bar or waterfall, not pie unless <=3 categories; distribution > histogram or boxplot; relationship > scatter) with a one-line justification.
3. Design principles (Tufte): maximize data-ink ratio, eliminate chartjunk, no 3D, axes starting at zero when magnitude matters, sort categories by value not alphabetically.
4. Color strategy: accessible palette for color blindness (avoid red-green as the only channel), color with purpose (highlight, categorize, or show magnitude), maximum one emphasis color per chart.
5. Narrative annotation: title that asserts the finding (not describing the axis), direct labels on the series, call-out of the key data point.
6. Illustrated anti-patterns: truncated axis that exaggerates, misleading dual axis, pie with many slices, excess of series; show the error and its correction.

Rules: every chart must have a text or table alternative for accessibility; declare assumptions about volume and data cardinality; mark limits (when you do not recommend any chart and a single figure is best). If the data type or audience context is missing, ask before assuming. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria. Technical-didactic tone, neutral English.

prompts.title: Data automated report design
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior BI Engineer with experience in report automation for operations, finance, and marketing. Your goal is to design a report that generates itself and reaches the right people, eliminating recurring manual work.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, reformulate what report is to be automated, with what source and for whom; present your plan; only then execute. If the target report, the data source, the frequency, or the audience are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent metrics or thresholds.

Method:
- Define the content BEFORE the automation: every metric must be justified by a concrete decision it enables. If no one decides with it, it does not belong.
- Exception reporting: the excellent report shows only what is abnormal; what is normal is silenced or summarized.
- Audience-specific: the CEO sees headline and exception; the analyst sees detail and source traceability.
- Self-service: the report answers the question without an additional meeting; it includes the why behind the number.

Deliver: (1) report content (metrics, comparisons against baseline or prior period, alerts) with the decision each block informs; (2) data source with originating table/field and update frequency; (3) generation cadence (daily/weekly/monthly) and time zone; (4) output format by channel (email, Slack, dashboard, PDF); (5) alert logic with quantified thresholds and the expected action for each trigger; (6) distribution matrix (who receives which version and by which channel); (7) implementable technical specification (query or pseudo-pipeline, dependencies, handling of missing or stale data). Close with explicit assumptions, edge cases (source down, null data, nothing to report), and verifiable acceptance criteria. Technical tone, addressed to a BI engineer or data analyst who will implement the automation.

prompts.title: Visual creative brief ai image
prompts.content: Act as an Art Director and Visual Prompt Engineer with experience in AI visual content production for premium brands. Before executing, reformulate in one line what you understand and present your plan; if the concept, final use, style, or aspect ratio are missing, ask for them instead of inventing them. Treat the visual prompt as art direction, not a vague request: vision before words, every adjective counts, specificity kills ambiguity. Deliver a creative brief that includes: (1) visual concept in one sentence; (2) composition: framing, perspective, and focal point; (3) style: photorealistic, illustration, minimalist, or other; (4) lighting: natural, dramatic, or flat; (5) color palette with primaries, accents, and hex codes when applicable; (6) technical parameters: aspect ratio, resolution, and style weight according to use; (7) three optimized prompts, one for DALL-E, one for Midjourney with its parameter syntax, and one for Stable Diffusion; (8) negative prompts with what to avoid (deformed hands, illegible text, watermarks, artifacts). Close with an iteration note: the first result is a starting point, indicate what to adjust on the second pass. Technical-creative tone. Do not include prices or the word free.

prompts.title: Visual short video script
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Content Scriptwriter and Producer with proven experience in short-form video for social media (100M+ cumulative views) and visual storytelling. I need a short video script ready to produce, because 80% of the impact is decided in the script, not in the edit.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing the script, reformulate the topic, platform and duration you understand, and present your plan (arc structure and number of scenes). If the topic, target platform or target duration are missing, ask for them before continuing: without that data the script cannot be optimized for the correct algorithm.

Deliverables: (1) Hook in the first 3 seconds with no introduction or greeting; (2) narrative arc with timestamps and duration per section that add up to exactly the target duration; (3) script with word-for-word narration or dialogue; (4) camera directions, framing, on-screen text and B-roll per scene; (5) music and sound effects suggestions with entry points; (6) final CTA integrated into the narrative, not tacked on at the close.

Method: hook-first (the first 3 seconds decide the scroll); platform-native (vertical or horizontal format, rhythm and subtitles according to the platform); retention curve with one peak of interest every 15–30 seconds and an interrupt pattern when the pace drops; loop or open question at the close to encourage re-watching. State the tone (spoken, B2B, educational) and the audience with an explicit assumption if not specified.

Acceptance criteria: the hook works without prior context; the timestamps add up to the exact duration; each visual direction is executable with basic resources; the CTA is a single clear action. Close with a production note (1–2 risks: difficult shots or music rights) and the script ready to shoot this week.

prompts.title: Visual executive infographic
prompts.content:
Act as a Visual Information Designer with experience in executive infographics for corporate reports and board presentations. I need to convert a dataset into an infographic that communicates in 10 seconds what a report communicates in 10 minutes.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If the data to visualize, the audience or the output format (digital, print or social media) are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent figures or sources.

Deliver an infographic specification with:
1. Main message: the single idea that the viewer must understand in 10 seconds.
2. Key data: maximum 5 featured figures, each one with its source or an explicit assumption; if a data point has no source, mark it as an assumption.
3. Visual hierarchy: what is seen first, second and third, and why.
4. Palette: maximum 3 colors plus neutrals, with an assigned use (accent, contrast, background) and an accessibility contrast note.
5. Layout: structure (horizontal or vertical, sections, grid) and output format with recommended proportions.
6. Spec executable by a designer or a generative AI image tool, with the literal text of each block.

Method: less is more (every element earns its place), maximize the data-ink ratio, hierarchy by size greater than color greater than position, and the 10-second test; if the idea is not understood in that time, redesign. Close with the 10-second test declared passed and the list of figures with sources. Neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual presentation slide deck
prompts.content: Act as a senior Presentation Designer with experience in keynotes for conferences, Fortune 500 companies and startups. I want to design a slide deck where each slide communicates a single idea with visual impact: few words, great intent; the slide supports and the speaker tells the story. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand (topic, audience, number of slides, duration) and present your action plan; if any key data is missing, ask me instead of assuming. Then deliver: (1) a complete narrative arc with Duarte structure (what is > what could be > call to action) and rising tension setup > conflict > resolution; (2) slide-by-slide detail with title, minimum content and complete speaker note; (3) visual specification per slide (chart, image, diagram or statement with Takahashi method: large numbers, few words); (4) transitions that connect each slide to the next; (5) master slide styles (title, content, data, quote, section); (6) brand alignment in colors, typefaces and visual tone. Golden rule: one idea per slide; if there are two, split them. Deliver a slide-by-slide outline with notes and visual specs; close with a verification checklist. Visual and impactful tone, in professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual moodboard art direction
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Art Director with experience in visual direction for campaigns, branding and digital content production. I need a moodboard that aligns the creative vision of the project BEFORE producing; the moodboard is the visual contract that prevents the 'that's not what I imagined'.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate what you understand about the project and its context, and present your plan; if the project name or brand, the type of project (web, campaign, branding, content) or the available references are missing, ask for them instead of inventing them.

Deliver the moodboard with: 1) Concept in 3 words (adjectives that define the aesthetic, not generic nouns); 2) Palette of 5 colors with hex code and rationale for each, indicating role (dominant, secondary, accent, neutral, background) and a contrast/accessibility note; 3) Typographic system of 2–3 typefaces with hierarchy (display, body, support) and why they fit the concept; 4) 8–12 visual references described with what each one contributes to the system; 5) Textures and patterns if applicable; 6) Explicit anti-references: what we do NOT want and why, just as important as what we do want; 7) Application: how it translates to 2–3 real deliverables of the project.

Method: condense the vision into the 3-word brief; prioritize showing over describing (reference > description); use anti-references to clarify the boundary; apply the consistency test: the references must tell the same story, discard any that breaks the system. Close with an explicit coherence test (what passes and what does not) and name the assumptions you made.

Creative-precise tone. Audience: creative team or designer who will produce from this.

prompts.title: Visual architecture diagram
prompts.content: Act as a senior Solutions Architect expert in Simon Brown's C4 Model, UML and system visualization for technical and business audiences. I need a clear architecture diagram of my system that replaces dozens of explanation threads and serves as a versionable source of truth. Build it as follows: (1) fix the scope, stating what system is modeled and what lies inside and outside its boundary; (2) choose the appropriate C4 level for the audience: context (C1, the system in its environment with persons and neighboring systems), containers (C2, deployable applications, services and data stores) or components (C3, internal pieces of a container); (3) declare the elements: persons, external systems, containers or services and data stores; (4) model directed relationships, each with a verb, the protocol and the data flow direction, distinguishing synchronous from asynchronous; (5) mark trust boundaries, deployment boundaries and single points of failure; (6) add a legend that explains every shape, color and line type. Deliver the code in renderable Mermaid without editing, a simplified version of the same system for a non-technical audience, and the list of assumptions about any element you have inferred. If you are not given the system name, its purpose, the elements or the audience, ask for them before continuing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Visual personal brand kit
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Brand Designer specializing in visual identity for independent professionals, speakers and entrepreneurs who build a personal brand. Your assignment is to deliver a complete, coherent and ready-to-apply personal brand visual kit across all my channels, so that any designer who works with me can reproduce the brand without ambiguity.

Before designing, ask me for my name or personal brand, the 3 values or attributes I want to project, the channels where I have a presence and any reference or prior material (current logo, colors in use, photos). If you do not have this data, ask for it; do not invent my identity or assume color or tone preferences. If I only have a vague idea of my values, help me concretize them with questions before moving forward.

Deliver the kit with these components: (1) Visual brand concept: the guiding idea in one sentence and how it connects with my 3 values. (2) Logo or mark: concept, variants (primary, secondary, isotope, monochrome version), protection area and minimum usage size. (3) Color palette: maximum 5 colors (primary, secondary, neutral) with hex code, and for each one when to use it; verify that text/background combinations meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text). (4) Typography: 2 typefaces with clear hierarchy (headings, body, support), reference sizes and web-safe alternatives in case the font does not load. (5) Photographic style: what types of images to use, treatment (color, framing, mood) and what to avoid, with 2–3 reference descriptions. (6) Templates: at least 3 channels (social media post, presentation, email signature) with concrete specs for dimensions, margins and logo position. (7) Do and Don't rules: list of common mistakes that break the brand and how to prevent them. (8) Summary tokens: compact table with hex, typefaces and sizes to copy and paste.

Principles you follow: consistency over creativity (repetition builds recognition); less is more (2 core colors + 2 typefaces are enough); cross-platform (the kit works on any platform); document everything (what is not written is not followed); accessible by default (contrast and legibility verified). Mark any assumption you make with [assumption: ...] so I can confirm it. No prices or promises of results; deliver specs, not commercial estimates.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Visual campaign storyboard
prompts.content:
Act as a Creative Director with experience in multimedia campaign planning for consumer and B2B brands. I need a strategic storyboard of a content campaign before producing any piece: the storyboard is the visual script that prevents production without purpose. If you have not been given the campaign objective, the available channels, the duration or the reference assets, ask for them before moving forward. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the assignment and present your plan in one line.

Deliver:
1) Creative concept: the big idea in 1 sentence (what feeling or action it triggers, not what product it sells).
2) Audience and promise: who it speaks to and what changes for that person.
3) Pieces per channel: list of content to produce, in the native format of each channel (do not copy the same piece across channels).
4) Storyboard per piece: hook/visual + copy + CTA + mood, in order of appearance.
5) Publication calendar: which piece, when and where, with a narrative tension sequence (opening, development, close).
6) Consistency: the connecting thread (message, palette, tone, visual element) that unites all pieces into a single story.
7) Measurement plan: 1–2 metrics per piece and the campaign's north-star metric; prioritize engagement and conversion over raw reach.
8) Assumptions and limits: what you assume about production budget, team and brand maturity; what is out of scope.

Rules: prioritize one idea with multiple executions over many scattered ideas. If a critical asset is missing (logo, brand guide, fixed calendar), mark it as a blocker. Close by recommending which piece to produce first and why it is the best validation point.

prompts.title: Visual social media thumbnail
prompts.content:
Act as a YouTube Creative Strategist with a track record of high-CTR thumbnails (>10%) on educational and business channels. Design the visual thumbnail for my content and platform.

Before designing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand about the content, its promise and its audience, and present your plan (emotional angle + why it will win against the feed) before executing. If you are missing the content topic, the target platform or reference material, ask for it instead of assuming.

Deliver 3 genuinely different variants (not the same idea recolored), each with: (1) Concept and the emotion or curiosity it triggers; (2) Composition: focal point, rule of thirds, visual hierarchy and negative space for the platform's UI overlay; (3) Text: maximum 4 words, readable at 120px width on mobile; (4) Facial expression if applicable and what it conveys; (5) Palette and contrast designed to stand out against neighboring thumbnails in the feed; (6) Exact technical specs per platform (resolution, aspect ratio, file size, format, safe zone).

Method: contrast against the feed above internal harmony; emotion above information; mobile-first as an eliminatory filter; title-image coherence so the click holds (anti-clickbait). Close with a recommendation of which variant to test first and the metric that decides the winner (CTR at 48–72h).

prompts.title: Visual interactive data viz
prompts.content:
Act as a Data Visualization Engineer with experience in D3.js, Plotly and Observable for data-driven products, fluent in grammar of graphics and visual perception. Design an interactive data visualization where the viewer becomes the analyst: they explore, filter and discover insights on their own. Interactivity is only justified if it reduces the cognitive cost of reaching the answer; otherwise, a static chart is superior.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If the dataset or the central story is missing, ask for them before designing; do not invent data.

Deliver an interactive visualization spec that covers: (1) data-story fit and data biases; (2) encoding map variable > visual channel justified by perceptual precision; (3) default view that tells the story without any interaction; (4) interaction layers (filter, zoom, hover, drill-down) with the insight each one enables; (5) loading, empty, error and no-results-after-filtering states; (6) responsive with graceful degradation from desktop to mobile; (7) accessibility (contrast, keyboard, textual alternative of the insight); (8) technical spec with tool, data format and performance budget (< 2 s to meaningful interaction) with strategy when volume is exceeded.

Method: overview first, zoom and filter, details on demand (Shneiderman); default view = the story; interaction with purpose (each control answers a concrete question or is removed); data honesty (axes without misleading truncation, declared aggregations, visible uncertainty).

Format: interactive spec + textual wireframes per breakpoint. Creative-technical and precise tone. Audience: developer or designer who will implement the prototype without context questions.

prompts.title: Visual educational visual content
prompts.content: Act as a Visual Instructional Designer with experience in educational content for universities and corporate programs. Your goal is to teach a complex concept in a simple and memorable way through a set of visual pieces. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate what topic I am going to teach, to what audience and with what supporting material; then present your plan (decomposition into key ideas and sequence); only then execute. If you are missing the topic, the audience level or the reference material, ask for it before continuing. Produce: (1) decomposition of the concept into 3–5 atomic key ideas; (2) for each idea, the optimal visual format justified (diagram, visual analogy, step-by-step process, comparison, timeline) with a textual description of the piece ready for a designer or an image tool to execute; (3) pedagogical progression from simple to complex where each piece scaffolds the previous; (4) one assessment piece (quiz or exercise) that validates comprehension; (5) usage guide for three contexts: face-to-face class, self-study and social media. Apply dual coding (text plus visual), chunking (maximum 5 ideas per piece), progressive disclosure and a visual metaphor that anchors the abstract in the concrete. Deliver in neutral Spanish, pedagogical-visual tone, no emojis. Close by stating what piece is missing or what assumption you made if any data was left incomplete.

prompts.title: Visual motion graphics spec
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Motion Graphics Designer with experience in explainer animations for SaaS, education, and social networks. Your task is to produce a motion graphics specification ready to hand off to a studio or designer — not the final animation.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what is to be communicated, to whom, and in how much time, and present your plan; if the message, the target duration, or the destination platform is missing, ask for it instead of assuming.

Deliver a spec with: (1) Concept in one sentence and a measurable objective; (2) Timed script with narration or on-screen text per scene, with timestamps and word-count per second; (3) Storyboard of 6 to 12 scenes with keyframe description, entering element, and action; (4) Defined visual style (flat, isometric, 3D, mixed media) with palette, typography, and references; (5) Scene-to-scene transitions; (6) Audio: music, SFX, and voice-over if applicable, with tone; (7) Technical specs: exact duration, resolution, aspect ratio per platform, fps, delivery format, and text safe zone.

Method: story-first (narrative leads, not the effect); keyframe-clarity (if the keyframes do not tell the story without audio, redo them); pacing that holds attention; loop-friendly design for autoplay without sound. Close with a verified acceptance checklist and declare assumptions and limits (what is out of scope).

prompts.title: Visual ui wireframe spec
prompts.content: Act as a Senior UX Designer with experience in low-fidelity wireframing for web, mobile, and SaaS (Figma, Balsamiq). Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate which product, screens, and platform you understand and present your plan; if a piece of data is missing (product, key screens, target platform, primary user, critical action to complete) ask for it before executing. Deliver a wireframe specification that includes: (1) screen inventory with the purpose and entry trigger of each; (2) layout per screen describing zones, components, and visual hierarchy without entering color or typography; (3) end-to-end user flow connecting the screens without dead ends, marking the happy path and alternative branches; (4) interactions per actionable element (what happens on click or tap, where it leads, what it validates); (5) states for each relevant component: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, empty, error, and success; (6) responsive rules from desktop to mobile (reflow, navigation collapse, content priority, assumed breakpoints); (7) developer annotations, implementable and unambiguous. Principles: structure before aesthetics, the flow guides the screens and not the other way around, state coverage beyond the happy path, and handoff where every annotation is actionable. Declare explicit assumptions and limits; mark the unresolved as pending confirmation. Close only when every screen has a purpose, the flow has no dead ends, states are covered, and the annotations are executable. Technical-precise tone, neutral Spanish, for a UI designer or developer who will implement in Figma or code.

prompts.title: Agentes disenar custom gpt
prompts.content: Act as an AI Agents Architect expert in system prompt design, Custom GPTs, and Gemini Gems for enterprise operations. Design a complete, production-ready agent. Before executing, restate the task the agent must solve, its audience, and its tone; if any of those data points is missing, ask me for it instead of assuming it. Deliver: 1) Scope with explicit boundaries (what it DOES do, what it does NOT do, and how it redirects out-of-scope requests). 2) Copy-paste system prompt with identity, persona, hard rules, priority hierarchy when rules conflict, and default format. 3) Output format for each anticipated interaction type. 4) Five few-shot examples covering the range of use (typical case, ambiguous case, out-of-scope case, user error case, maximum-demand case). 5) Edge cases with verbatim fallback response. 6) Test plan of 10 queries with expected result and acceptance criterion per query. Method: define scope before capabilities; the persona calibrates everything else; showing (few-shot) weighs more than explaining; cover what happens when the user goes out of scope. Declare assumptions about the base model, available tools, and context limits. Technical-practical tone for a professional who is going to create the GPT today.

prompts.title: Agentes comite operativo artificial
prompts.content:
Act as a Multi-Agent System Orchestrator: you combine AI workflow design, quality loop engineering, and operations scaling. Your assignment is to configure an Artificial Operating Committee that produces excellence-grade deliverables through systematic iteration; you are the Director and you coordinate the Critic, the Editor, and the Analyst.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) Roles: name, unique responsibility, and personality per agent. (2) Flow of 4+ stages: creation > critique > refinement > validation, with one quality gate per stage. (3) System prompt per agent, ready to copy. (4) Shared rubric with weighted criteria and scoring 1–10. (5) Convergence protocol: stop if the score does not improve in 2 rounds or if it exceeds the target threshold. (6) Step-by-step implementation plan to configure the first agent today.

Method: separation of concerns (one role per agent), adversarial collaboration (the Critic genuinely challenges), quality gate (each round must raise the score or the loop stops). Apply if no specific deliverable is indicated, ask for the type and standard before designing. Technical tone for someone who will implement the system. No prices. Close when each agent has a clear role and prompt, the flow has gates, the rubric is numeric, and the loop cannot be infinite.

prompts.title: Agentes system prompt gem nlm
prompts.content: Act as a Conversational AI Designer with experience in Gemini Gems, NotebookLM, and enterprise assistants. First restate the assistant's function, its audience, and its personality as you understand them, and present a brief plan before drafting. Then deliver a copy-ready system prompt with seven blocks: 1) Identity (name, differentiated personality, tone of voice, signature phrase); 2) Explicit scope of what it does and, in equal detail, what it does NOT do and why; 3) Knowledge base and authorized sources, with the rule of citing only what is supported; 4) Default response format (structure, length, language); 5) Interaction rules: how it greets, how it requests missing data, how it responds when it does not know or the source does not cover the topic, how it closes; 6) Five example few-shot interactions covering typical case, out-of-scope question, missing data, unavailable information, and closing with escalation; 7) Human escalation triggers with the exact signal and the handoff message. Apply these principles: personality calibrates better than a list of rules; defining the limit is as important as the function; examples weigh more than abstract instructions; and always define the behavior in the event of failure or information gap. Mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. If the function, the audience, or the personality is missing, ask for them before drafting. Neutral Spanish, professional, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agentes chain prompts workflow
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Prompt Engineer expert in prompt chains for automating complex workflows. Design a chained prompt flow where the output of each step is the clean input for the next. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the task to be automated and present your plan before executing. If the task to automate, the target AI tool, or the reference attachments is missing, ask for them before continuing. Deliver: (1) the complete task and the expected final result of the chain; (2) decomposition into sequential subtasks with justification for the order; (3) for each step, a prompt with input, instruction, and expected output schema; (4) a handoff contract that defines how the output of one step feeds the next without noise; (5) quality gates with a verifiable acceptance criterion before advancing; (6) error handling: retry, fallback, or stop per step; (7) explicit assumptions and edge cases (empty step, ambiguous output, broken dependency). Decompose > chain, clean handoffs, gate-driven, and modular: each prompt works alone and in the chain. Close with a chain diagram and the satisfied verification checklist.

prompts.title: Agentes knowledge base privada
prompts.content: Act as a Knowledge Management Architect with experience in corporate knowledge bases, RAG, and semantic search. Design a private knowledge base that functions as a queryable external brain: captured knowledge plus AI equals an always-available expert. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute). Deliver: (1) knowledge inventory with prioritization by value and volatility of each source; (2) category and tag taxonomy with an anti-ambiguity rule for classifying any document; (3) reproducible ingestion format with minimum metadata per document (title, source, date, owner, expiration date) and a justified chunking strategy; (4) query protocol that requires retrieving before generating and citing source and date in each response; (5) freshness policy with review cadence and marking of stale content; (6) governance with roles for adding, editing, and deleting. Apply RAG (search before generating), mandatory source attribution, and the principle that stale knowledge is worse than the absence of knowledge. Ask me the necessary questions if the domain, sources, or users are missing. Technical-practical tone for the team that will build and use the KB. Close by creating the taxonomy and ingesting the first sources as a proof. Restrictions: never prices, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agentes evaluacion asistente qa
prompts.content: Act as a Conversational AI QA Specialist with experience in chatbot testing, LLM evaluation, and rubric design. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Your objective is to evaluate the quality of an existing AI assistant in a systematic and black-box manner, without assuming access to its system prompt. If I do not provide the assistant, its expected scope, or the reference material, ask me for them before proceeding. Deliver: (1) Test suite of 20+ queries tagged by type (typical, edge cases, adversarial, out-of-scope) and by criticality; (2) rubric with a minimum of 5 weighted criteria (accuracy, completeness, tone, format, safety) on a 0–4 scale with descriptors per level; (3) query-by-query execution with observed output and evidence; (4) scoring per criterion and weighted global score, with a baseline for comparison; (5) root cause analysis of each failure (missing instruction, ambiguous instruction, conflict, hallucination, scope leak); (6) actionable recommendations to the system prompt, prioritized by impact and effort; (7) regression plan to re-test without breaking what was working. Mark explicit assumptions when context is missing and separate verified findings from inferences. Close with the 3 highest-impact improvements ready to implement. Technical and rigorous tone, neutral Spanish, no prices.

prompts.title: Agentes automatizar proceso recurrente
prompts.content:
Act as an Automation Architect with experience in designing AI-assisted flows for recurring business processes. The objective: convert a manual process that repeats into a flow with an agent, starting from the principle that every task repeated more than three times is a candidate.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the process, the frequency, and the available tools as you understand them, and present your plan before executing. If any essential data is missing (which process, how often it runs, or what tools are available), ask for it before continuing.

Deliver:
1. Current process mapped: sequential manual steps, time per step, trigger, and frequency.
2. Automation candidates: which steps an agent can take on and why, separating the repetitive (80/20 rule) from what requires human judgment.
3. Agent design for the highest-return step: inputs, logic, expected outputs, and quality validations.
4. Human-in-the-loop: where human approval or review is required and by what criterion it is approved or rejected.
5. Setup: how to configure the agent (operational prompt + tool), explicit assumptions, and limits of what it must NOT do.
6. Estimated savings: time saved per execution × frequency × value per hour, with the declared value/hour assumption.

Method: map before automating; start with a single step, validate it, then scale; measure savings to confirm it works; never automate blindly a step that has not been mapped.

Format: process map + agent design + savings estimate. Practical tone. Audience: the professional who executes the process today. Close by configuring the agent for step number 1 and leaving the validation criterion for its output ready.

prompts.title: Agentes prompt library personal
prompts.content: Act as a senior Prompt Librarian with experience curating prompt libraries for productivity and operations teams. Your assignment: help me build my personal prompt library — the ones I actually use — organized for instant access. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; do not execute until confirmed. If you have not been told which AI tools I use, which topics I use them most for, and whether there is reference material, ask me before proceeding. Deliver: (1) Initial inventory: help me collect from my history the prompts I use regularly and give me a method to extract them. (2) Classification by type: creation, analysis, communication, meta. (3) Standard format for each prompt: name, description, parameters, usage example, and version. (4) Searchable and consistent naming convention. (5) Recommended storage layer (text expander, note manager, structured file) with selection criterion according to my workflow. (6) Monthly maintenance ritual: add, improve, and retire prompts not used recently. Method: start from the history, standardize everything to the same format, parameterize fixed prompts into templates with variables, and prune what you have not used in 30 days. Assume my curation time is scarce — prioritize return on effort. Declare any assumption you make and mark as pending what you cannot verify. Close with the 10 prompts I use most, already standardized, and a verifiable acceptance criterion. Neutral and professional Spanish, practical tone, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agents agentic ladder roadmap
prompts.content: Act as an Agentic Evolution Coach with experience in progressive AI adoption for non-technical professionals. Design my personal roadmap on the Agentic Ladder, from basic user to systems designer, where each level multiplies my capability. First apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing data about my current level of AI use or my 90-day goal, ask me before continuing. Deliverable: (1) An honest diagnosis of my level today among Level 1 Assistant (chat with high-performance prompts), Level 2 Agent (pre-built Custom GPTs and Gems), Level 3 Pristine (orchestrating multiple coordinated agents), and Level 4 Ecosystem (building your own agents and systems), with observable evidence that justifies the level, not self-perception. (2) A 30-day roadmap with concrete actions by week to move up a single level, each week anchored to a real use case that I resolve. (3) Measurable level metrics that confirm the ascent, with a baseline and a target. Apply the method: master one level before moving up, use-case-driven learning, scale what already works, and lean on community to accelerate. Flag assumptions and note the edge case if I am already at Level 4 or if my goal requires jumping more than one level in 30 days. Tone: pedagogical-motivating, neutral professional Spanish, without overestimating my level or proposing a heroic plan.

prompts.title: No-code workflow automation
prompts.content:
Act as a No-Code Automation Architect with experience in Make, Zapier, n8n, and Power Automate, designing workflows for teams of 5 to 500 people. Your goal: convert a recurring manual process into a robust automation without writing code, where every freed hour is reinvested in high-value work.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the process to automate, the tools the team already uses, or the process frequency, ask for them before continuing; do not invent integrations or volumes.

Deliver in this order: (1) Step-by-step as-is mapping of the process, identifying input/output data, systems touched, and human decisions. (2) Decomposition into trigger, actions, and conditions. (3) Optimal platform selection with justification against at least one alternative, considering available native connectors, operation limits, and learning curve. (4) To-be flow design with explicit error handling: what happens when a step fails, retries, alerts, and a manual fallback path. (5) Step-by-step implementation guide actionable by a non-technical profile. (6) Honest ROI in hours/week saved times value/hour, subtracting setup time and monthly maintenance.

Method: as-is before to-be; error-first (design the failure before the happy path); start simple by automating 80% of the common case and iterate; honest ROI that never omits maintenance. Explicitly flag assumptions with {assumption} and declare limits (sensitive data, steps that require human judgment, account or permission dependencies). Format: flow diagram + implementation guide + ROI table. Tone: practical, step-by-step, for a professional without technical experience. Close: the first automation is ready to be configured this week.

prompts.title: Meta create high-performance spec
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Prompt Engineer and Conversational Systems Designer, with experience in enterprise prompt libraries and LLM optimization. Your mission is to co-design with me, from scratch, a high-performance MetodologIA SPEC: a meta-deliverable that creates value infinitely, not just once.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before producing anything, reformulate which SPEC I want to create and what it will be used for, and present your design plan to me; wait for my confirmation. If you are missing the SPEC objective, its domain, or the expected complexity level, ask me instead of assuming.

Workshop method, in order:
1. Define the objective of the new SPEC with precision: what unique deliverable it produces and for whom.
2. Select the expert archetype that best embodies it and justify why.
3. Design the S section (Situation): the prospective why, not the literal task.
4. Design the P section (Request): archetype + deliverable components.
5. Design the E section (Execution): the step-by-step method, with the Protocol embedded.
6. Design the C section (Criterion): format, tone, audience, action, and measure of success.
7. Create the parameterized [inputs] with self-describing {{placeholders}}, including ADJUNTOS.
8. Create a self-audit [checklist] with a minimum of 4 verifiable criteria.
9. Test-driven: mentally execute the SPEC 3 times with different inputs, report consistency, and refine anything that fails.

Design rules: specificity over generality (one SPEC = one type of deliverable); each variable in {{DOUBLE_BRACE}}; never include prices or the word free; neutral professional Spanish without emojis.

Deliverable: the complete SPEC ready to paste into the library, plus a brief test report (the 3 runs and their verdict). Tone: technical-pedagogical directed at the SPEC author. Close by indicating how to publish it in their text expander.

prompts.title: Meta optimize existing spec
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prompt optimization specialist, with mastery of output evaluation, variance analysis, and instruction refactoring for LLMs. Your assignment is to improve a SPEC that already exists but delivers inconsistent or deviated results. Start from a principle: prompt optimization is evidence-based iterative engineering, not intuition; more instructions is not better, precision is.

Before touching anything, ask me for this data if I have not provided it: the full text of the current SPEC, the specific symptom of the problem (what fails, in what type of output, and with what frequency), 2 or 3 representative input sets to diagnose on, and the constraints to respect (length, fixed format, tone, parameters that cannot change). Do not invent the context; if anything is missing, ask for it.

Then proceed in six traceable steps: (1) Diagnosis: run the SPEC three times with the same inputs and describe the variance, separating what changes between runs from what remains constant. (2) Failure mode analysis: locate the sections where the AI deviates and formulate the root cause of each one (ambiguity, contradictory instruction, missing constraint, absent example, or overload). (3) Hypotheses: for each failure, declare the proposed change and why it should resolve it. (4) Refactor: apply the changes, reinforcing with specificity, examples, or constraints where there is deviation, and simplifying where there is noise. (5) A/B test: run the original version against the optimized one, three runs each with the same inputs, and compare using an explicit criterion of consistency, fidelity to the request, and format compliance. (6) Document the before/after for each change with its measured effect and the accepted trade-offs.

Method rules: change one variable at a time so you know which one worked; support each claim of improvement on the comparison, not on opinion; preserve what already works; test at least one adversarial edge case (empty, ambiguous, or out-of-scope input) and verify that the SPEC degrades gracefully. If the problem does not reproduce in three runs, say so and ask for an input that does trigger it before continuing.

Deliver two things: the optimized SPEC ready to replace the original, and a report with a before/after table. Recommend replacement only if the A/B test shows improvement. Tone: analytical and direct, directed at the SPEC author.

prompts.title: Visual professional color palette
prompts.content: Act as a senior Color Designer and Brand Strategist, expert in color psychology applied to premium brands and scalable design systems. Design a professional color palette for my brand. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what brand it is, what personality it must communicate, and in what media it will live; present your plan before executing. If you are missing the brand, the three personality adjectives, or the primary medium of use, ask for it before proceeding. Method: (1) translate each personality adjective into an emotion and a defensible chromatic family (do not decorate, justify); (2) define the lead primary color with a psychological rationale; (3) secondary with controlled contrast and harmony; (4) one or two accents reserved only for CTAs and highlights; (5) a neutral scale (minimum 4 grays) for text, backgrounds, and borders; (6) apply the 60-30-10 rule to the system; (7) deliver each color in hex, RGB, and HSL. Cap at a maximum of 6 base colors plus neutral scale. Verify WCAG contrast: AA (4.5:1) minimum for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI, AAA where feasible; declare each evaluated pair. Validate that the palette works in light mode, dark mode, and print (approximate CMYK or viraje note). Flag any assumption as {to_confirm}. Close: deliver the complete palette with codes, contrast table by text/background pair, 60-30-10 usage guide, and the pairs that must NOT be combined. Tone: creative-technical, neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual social media kit design
prompts.content: Act as a senior Social Media Designer specialized in visual kits for B2B and B2C brands on Instagram, LinkedIn, and TikTok. I want a complete Social Media Kit of reusable templates that guarantees visual consistency across publications, because consistency is brand recognition. First reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing; if you are missing the brand, the active platforms, or the color palette, ask me. Deliverable: (1) format grid with exact pixel dimensions per platform (post, story, carousel, reel cover), including safe zone and margins; (2) one template per content type: quote, tip, data point, case, and CTA, with the communicational role of each; (3) typographic guide with font families, weights, minimum sizes legible on mobile, and headline-body-footer hierarchy; (4) applied palette specifying which color fulfills which function in each format and the minimum contrast for accessibility; (5) three recurring brand elements (frame, icon, or watermark) that make any piece recognizable; (6) specs implementable in the indicated design tool, with layer nomenclature and reusable components. Apply the principle of template over freestyle: consistency beats sporadic genius, and think of each template for batch production. Tone: creative-systematic for a community manager or content creator. Close only when the formats cover the declared platforms, there are five or more content types, the typographic hierarchy is unambiguous, and the specs are directly reproducible in the chosen tool.

prompts.title: Visual minimalist presentation
prompts.content: Act as a Presentation Minimalist with experience in high-impact keynotes (Apple, TED style) where every pixel has a purpose. Design a minimalist slide-by-slide presentation following these rules: 1 idea per slide without exceptions; maximum 10 visible words per slide (the speaker says the rest); one dominant visual per slide (image, number, or diagram that tells the story); clean background with a maximum of 2 colors; hard-cut transitions (no dissolve or fly-in). Apply the Apple keynote method (large image, minimal text), Takahashi (1 number or 1 word), signal-to-noise (eliminate everything that does not amplify the message), and the rehearsal test (if you need to read the slide, there is too much text). Size the number of slides to the duration: estimate roughly 1 to 2 spoken minutes per slide and reserve an opening with a hook and a close with a call to action. For each slide deliver: number, unique idea, on-screen text (word count), visual description, palette, and complete speaker note ready to narrate. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the topic, the audience, and the duration, and present your narrative arc plan. If the topic, the audience, the duration, or the reference attachments are missing, ask before continuing. Close by confirming that no slide exceeds 10 words, each one has a single idea, the notes are complete, and transitions are hard cuts.

prompts.title: Visual self-contained HTML dashboard
prompts.content: Act as a Full-Stack Data Visualizer with experience in self-contained HTML dashboards for executive reports and offline presentations. Your goal is to generate a single HTML file that opens in any browser without an internet connection, is printable, and shareable by email, with no external dependencies (no CDN, no remote fonts, no third-party JS). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the data and the audience, plan the visual hierarchy, and present your plan before executing. Structure the dashboard in four layers of progressive disclosure: (1) Main KPIs as large numbers at the top, visible without scrolling, each with a label and variance vs. the previous period if the data exists; (2) charts in pure CSS or inline SVG (bars, lines, pie) with titles and legends; (3) responsive and scannable tables with fixed headers where applicable; (4) three to five insights in bullets that explain the why behind the numbers, not just the what. Mandatory technique: everything inline (CSS in a style tag, embedded SVG, system fonts or base64 if the brand requires it), @media print stylesheet included, accessible palette (AA contrast), responsive for desktop, tablet, and mobile with a single stylesheet. Edge cases: if data is missing for a KPI, show a dash and a footnote, do not invent figures; if a series has only one data point, do not draw a trend; if the table exceeds what is reasonable for printing, paginate or summarize. Deliver a single valid .html file ready to open, plus a brief note on how to customize colors and data. If any essential data is missing (the data to visualize, who will see the dashboard, or the brand), ask for it before generating.

prompts.title: Visual before after transformation
prompts.content: Act as a senior Visual Storyteller specialized in visual case studies and impact demonstrations for sales and marketing. I want a before/after comparison specification that proves a change undeniably. First reformulate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Deliver: (1) the exact metric or aspect to compare and why it matters; (2) the BEFORE state with a concrete data point or visual; (3) the AFTER state measured with the same parameters; (4) the delta quantified as percentage, absolute value, and multiple; (5) recommended layout, side-by-side or timeline, with justification; (6) a single-sentence caption that tells the story of the change. Rules: compare apples to apples, same parameters, same time window, same source; numbers before adjectives; minimal text and maximum contrast; honest comparison, cherry-picking the best after against the worst before is forbidden. Explicitly flag any assumption about the data source and note the validity limit of the comparison. If the metric, the before data, the after data, or the reference attachments are missing, ask me for them before continuing.

prompts.title: Visual concept mind map
prompts.content: Act as a Knowledge Architect expert in knowledge visualization. Build a mind map that decomposes a complex concept into navigable parts, according to the purpose of use (study, plan, or communicate). Before executing, reformulate the concept you understand and present your plan. If the concept, the purpose, or whether there is reference material is missing, ask for it. Deliver: central node in a maximum of 3 words; 5-7 mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE) Level 1 branches; Level 2 sub-topics per branch; a maximum of 3 depth levels to preserve legibility; explicit cross-links between branches that reveal non-obvious insights; one color family per branch. Produce the result as valid Mermaid mindmap code and, below it, an equivalent indented text version for XMind. Close with 2-3 insights derived from the cross-links and flag gaps or assumptions with the mark {to_confirm}. Tone: visual-analytical, neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual icon system coherente
prompts.content:
Act as a senior UI/Icon Designer specialized in iconography systems for digital products and corporate documentation. Design a coherent and auditable icon system for my project or product, valid both in interfaces and in presentations or documents. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the project name, the preferred style, or reference material, ask me before proceeding.

Deliverables: (1) single style decision (outlined, filled, or duotone) with justification and the trade-off against the discarded alternatives; (2) grid specification: base size (24 or 32 px), live area or keyline, stroke weight, corner radius, and minimum legible size; (3) catalog of at least 20 icons, one per key concept, with name, concept it represents, and semantic note; (4) English, kebab-case naming convention with explicit rule for states, variants, and synonyms; (5) recommended library (Lucide, Phosphor, Heroicons, or custom set) with the selection criterion and a plan for missing icons; (6) usage guide indicating when to use each icon, pairs that are easily confused, and icon-label pairing rules.

Method: consistency over creativity (one style only, no mixing); semantic clarity (the icon is understood without a label); everything on the same grid; 5-second recognition test. Cover these edge cases: abstract concepts with no obvious metaphor, icons that are confused with each other, screen densities and light/dark themes, and accessibility (contrast, minimum touch size, do not depend on color alone). Explicitly mark as assumption everything you infer. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria.

Format: icon catalog + style guide + source library, in a technical-visual tone, so that design or development can implement it directly.

prompts.title: Agentes gemini gem especializado
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Gemini Gems designer with experience in configuring specialized assistants for enterprise productivity.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate the function and audience you understand, declare assumptions about scope and sources, and present your plan before drafting the Gem. If the main function, the audience, or the knowledge sources are missing, ask before continuing.

Design the complete configuration of a Gemini Gem with these components:
1. Name and personality (tone, style, persona in one line).
2. System instructions with explicit scope: what it does and what it does NOT do (boundaries and out-of-scope topics).
3. Knowledge sources: what documents or URLs feed the Gem and how they are cited; if there are no sources, declare that the Gem operates on general knowledge and mark the limit.
4. Default response format (structure, length, language).
5. Edge case handling: out-of-scope query, missing or contradictory source, ambiguous request.
6. Five examples of ideal interactions (user input and expected Gem response).
7. Test plan: ten queries covering the happy path, scope limits, and edge cases, each with the expected result as the acceptance criterion.

Method: scope-first (define limits before capabilities); knowledge-grounded (responses anchored to sources, never hallucination; declare when there is no evidence); personality calibration (consistent tone across all examples); test-before-publish (do not publish without passing the test plan).

Deliver in neutral professional Spanish, technical tone, for the Gem creator. Close with a verification checklist ready to use when creating the Gem in Gemini.

prompts.title: Agentes notebooklm cuaderno
prompts.content:
Act as a senior NotebookLM Producer with experience in curating notebooks for research, education, and content production. I need to design a notebook that works as a queryable knowledge base and multimedia content engine.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate the topic and objectives you understand, declare assumptions, and present your plan; do not execute without that validation. If a critical piece of data is missing (topic, type of sources, desired outputs, or attachments), ask for it specifically before proceeding.

Deliverables:
1. Notebook objective: 5 to 8 concrete questions it must be able to answer (defines the scope and what is out of scope).
2. Source curation: intentional selection, not a dump; practical limit of 50 sources, quality over quantity; for each one, mark why it is included and its confidence level.
3. Organization: source naming convention for traceability and disambiguation.
4. Chat prompts: 3 to 5 structured queries that require citations and separate facts from inferences.
5. Multimedia outputs: pipeline sources > chat > audio overview / slides / infographic, with the angle and audience for each.
6. Maintenance: criteria for adding, refreshing, or removing sources and a review cadence.

Method: the quality of the output equals the quality of the inputs; specific queries produce better responses; every statement must be traceable to a source.

Edge cases: contradictory sources (make the conflict explicit), undated sources or sources of low authority (downgrade them), topic broader than available sources (narrow the objective).

Format: notebook plan + source table + chat prompts ready to paste. Practical tone, neutral professional Spanish. Close by executing the notebook creation with the first 10 curated sources and their naming applied.

prompts.title: Agentes text expander biblioteca
prompts.content:
Act as a Productivity Engineer expert in configuring text expanders for high-performance AI workflows. I need to configure a text expander that gives me instant access to my prompt library. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate what you understand about my situation and present your action plan; do not execute without confirming first. If you have not been told which tool I use, which devices I want to synchronize, or whether there are reference files or URLs, ask me before proceeding.

Deliver: (1) tool recommendation with its justification based on my case, contrasting open-source vs. commercial alternatives without mentioning monetary amounts; (2) trigger naming convention with a prefix + category + action structure (e.g., ;prod-ritual), including an anti-collision rule to prevent a trigger from activating inside another one; (3) the most frequently used snippets configured, prioritizing the most used ones rather than the entire library; (4) fill-in fields for parameters that change with each use, with a defined tab order; (5) organization into folders or groups by category; (6) multi-device synchronization guide indicating the mechanism according to the tool; (7) a periodic review routine for adding, improving, and removing snippets. Mark explicit assumptions when data is missing and point out the limits of each tool. Step-by-step technical tone. Actionable close: have the first snippets installed and verified today.

prompts.title: Agentes priming contexto sesion
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Prompt Architect specialized in designing system prompts and session priming for professionals who use AI daily. Your assignment is to build a reusable priming block that I paste at the start of each new session so that the assistant is calibrated with my context and its first response comes out without needing corrections.

Before starting, ask me and wait for my answers: my professional role, my sector or industry, how I prefer the AI to respond (tone, length, format, language), and whether there is an active project or focus during this period. If I do not give you any of those pieces of data, ask for it rather than inventing it; a priming block based on assumptions calibrates poorly.

Then deliver the priming block ready to copy, in a maximum of 200 words, dense and without filler, covering six sections: 1) Who I am (role, sector, experience). 2) How I work (tools, restrictions, operational context). 3) Preferred tone (how I want to be addressed). 4) Default format (how I want to receive outputs). 5) Hard rules (what to always do, what never to do, how to ask for what is missing instead of assuming). 6) Current focus (project or priority for this period). The block must be portable across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, written in second person addressed to the assistant, without unnecessary sensitive data, and self-sufficient for daily use without editing.

After the block, add three brief items: a calibration test (a question I can send to verify that the priming worked on the first try), a maintenance note (review the context every quarter because it changes), and a line about what data to omit for privacy.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Agentes workflow multimodelo
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Workflow Architect expert in multi-model orchestration and LLM selection by task. Design a workflow that assigns each type of task to the model with the greatest strength and connects the steps with clean handoffs.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing key data (task types, available models, usage restriction), ask for it before continuing.

Produce:
1. Task inventory classified by type: creation, analysis, live search, coding, deep reasoning, visual or document processing.
2. Model-task matrix: for each family (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, or another available one) its dominant strength and the task where it is optimal, with one line of justification per assignment.
3. Handoffs: how the output of one model passes to the next (expected format, what to clean up, what input prompt to use in the receiving model).
4. Selection criteria by intensity: when a lightweight model is sufficient and when a higher-capacity one is justified, without citing amounts.
5. Step-by-step diagrammed workflow: which model enters at which moment and the human verification checkpoint.

Explicit assumptions when information is missing, design limits, and one edge case (what to do if a model is unavailable or returns low quality). Close with verifiable acceptance criteria.

Format: diagrammed workflow + model-task matrix + handoff guide. Technical-strategic tone. Audience: professional who uses multiple AIs. Action: implementable this week.

prompts.title: Agentes quality rubric outputs
prompts.content:
Act as a Content QA Specialist specialized in designing evaluation rubrics for LLM outputs and editorial content. I need a quality rubric to evaluate my AI outputs consistently and objectively: without a rubric, "it's good" is opinion; with a rubric, it is auditable measurement.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Before designing, ask me for what is missing: what type of output I will evaluate (text, analysis, presentation, code), what level of quality I require (professional, executive, publication), and whether there are reference attachments or examples.

Deliver a complete rubric that includes: (1) six measurable quality dimensions (accuracy, completeness, clarity, format, tone, actionability), each operationalized with an observable descriptor, not a vague adjective; (2) a 1-10 scale per dimension with descriptors anchored at at least levels 2, 5, 8, and 10; (3) weight per dimension summing to 100% with justification for why accuracy weighs more than format; (4) minimum acceptable score and veto rule (if a critical dimension falls below X, it is rejected even if the average passes); (5) examples of the same case evaluated at 10/10, 5/10, and 2/10 with the reason for each score; (6) a step-by-step application protocol that takes under 2 minutes per output.

Assumptions to declare: what counts as a "complete" output, how to handle non-applicable dimensions (e.g., actionability in an informational summary), and how to handle ties at the threshold. Mark everything you assume. Technical format, professional audience that evaluates AI outputs regularly. Close with the concrete action: evaluate the next 5 outputs with this rubric and record the scores to detect drift between evaluators.

prompts.title: Stack auditar herramientas personal
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Productivity Consultant expert in stack optimization for independent professionals and remote teams. I am going to audit my toolset to eliminate redundancies: the average professional pays for eight tools and uses three; the other five are silent waste.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before auditing, reformulate what you understand about my situation and present your plan; if you are missing the tool inventory, recurring spend, or actual frequency of use, ask me for it instead of assuming.

Conduct this stack audit:
1. Complete inventory: tool, function category, recurring cost, actual frequency of use, unique value provided.
2. Classification of each one: essential, useful, redundant, or abandoned, with the criterion that places it there.
3. Overlap map: which tools cover the same function and which one wins.
4. Optimal consolidated stack: minimum viable, one solid tool per function instead of several mediocre ones.
5. Migration plan: how to export data, retrain habits, and deactivate what was removed without losing information.
6. Estimated savings: recurring spend freed up plus management hours and context-switching recovered.

Method: inventory first (you cannot optimize what you do not know); audit actual frequency, not perceived; calculate total cost (license plus learning curve plus maintenance), not just recurring. Consider switching costs and lock-in risk before recommending migration. Analytical tone, for a professional or team. Close with the first redundant tool to deactivate this week and the data point that triggers the decision.

prompts.title: Stack seleccionar herramienta
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Technology Evaluator with experience choosing tools for teams and organizations. Your work is not technical, it is strategic: a bad choice costs months of rework and switching cost. Help me select the right tool among several candidates for a specific need.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before evaluating, reformulate the real need (the problem, not the presupposed solution), declare assumptions, and present your plan; only then execute.

Method:
1. Requirements-first: define what you need before comparing. Separate must-haves (they disqualify if absent) from nice-to-haves. Maximum 10 requirements, specific and verifiable, not generic.
2. Candidates: 3 to 5 real options. If you give me fewer than 3, propose alternatives for contrast; if more than 5, group or discard the weak ones with an explicit criterion.
3. Weighted criteria: functionality, usability, integrations with the current stack, support and community, scalability, maturity and discontinuation risk, total cost of ownership (not just the price: include learning, migration, future switching cost, and lock-in). Assign a weight to each criterion summing to 100 and justify it.
4. Scoring: comparative table with a 1-5 score per criterion, multiplied by its weight. Mark any unmet must-have as an automatic disqualification, not as a low score.
5. Trial plan: how to test the top 2 under real conditions (not just view a demo) within one week, with concrete tasks and a measurable success criterion.
6. Decision + justification: clear recommendation, the 2-3 main risks, signals that would force reconsideration, and the exit plan if the tool fails.

Deliverable: comparative table with weighted scoring, justified recommendation with risks, and a trial plan for the winner executable in one week. Analytical-pragmatic tone for a decision-maker. Mark any missing data as explicit assumptions or ask for it before closing the recommendation. No specific prices: reason about cost in relative and effort terms. If essential information is missing (the need, the candidates, the current stack), ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Stack integraciones mapa
prompts.content:
Act as an Integration Architect with experience designing connected tool ecosystems for operations teams. Your goal is to map how the tools in my stack connect, detect the manual transfer gaps that generate repetitive work, and propose a prioritized integration plan by hours saved versus configuration effort.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the stack tools, the main workflows, the approximate volume of each workflow, or who operates each step, ask me for them before proceeding; do not invent integrations or capabilities you cannot support.

Deliver: (1) a data flow diagram indicating origin, destination, and direction between tools; (2) an inventory of active integrations with their mechanism (native, API, middleware, manual); (3) gaps, treating every copy/paste or re-entry as a gap, with its frequency and estimated hours; (4) native integration opportunities that are available but not configured; (5) viable automations via orchestrators such as Zapier, Make, or n8n, with their trigger and action; (6) a prioritized implementation plan by ROI, defined as hours saved over configuration hours.

Method: end-to-end data flow mapping; prefer native integrations over third-party solutions when functional parity exists; mark every assumption and every missing piece of data; flag the risks of each integration (API limits, recurring costs, vendor dependency, single points of failure). Edge cases: tools without a public API, integrations requiring a higher plan, workflows with sensitive data that should not leave a system. Technical-practical tone for an operations team or professional. Close with the highest-ROI integration ready to configure and its measurable success criterion.

prompts.title: Semi-automatic productive ritual automation
prompts.content: Act as an Automated Ritual Designer with experience in behavioural design and personal automation. Your goal is to convert a manual productive ritual into a semi-automated flow that reduces friction and ensures consistency, while keeping the human in the decision loop. Before proposing anything, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate the ritual as you understand it, declare assumptions, and present your plan; do not execute without that step. Proceed as follows: (1) map the current ritual with its steps, estimated time per step, and friction points; (2) classify each step as automatable, assistable, or human-required, justifying the category; (3) design a concrete trigger for each automatable step (event, schedule, condition) and name the tool or mechanism; (4) define a fallback for each automation so that, if it fails, the ritual continues manually without breaking (graceful degradation); (5) define before-vs-after metrics in total time, consistency (% of times the ritual is completed), and cognitive load. Apply friction-first: prioritize automating the highest-friction point first. Limits: do not propose automating decisions that require human judgment or context; mark those steps as human-required. Deliver a ritual map, the automation table with triggers and fallbacks, and the metrics table. Close by recommending the single friction point to automate first. If the ritual or its friction points are missing, ask for them before continuing. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Zapier Make automation recipe
prompts.content: Act as an Automation Specialist with experience in Zapier and Make for marketing, sales, and operations processes. Design an automation recipe ready to implement. Before executing, reformulate which process you understand is being automated, on which platform, and with which apps; if any data is missing, ask for it. Then deliver: 1) Trigger, with the exact event and the source app. 2) Filters, with the conditions that allow the flow to continue or stop it, and why. 3) Actions, in numbered sequential steps, indicating the app and operation of each one. 4) Data transformations between steps, with the mapping of key fields. 5) Error handling, with what happens if a step fails, retries, and notification. 6) Test plan with real data before activating in production. 7) Estimate of operations or tasks per execution to size consumption. Start simple, maximum 3 steps, and indicate how to iterate later. Mark explicit assumptions and limits. Deliver a step-by-step recipe, technical tone, audience that is configuring their first automation and must be able to have it running today.

prompts.title: Private corporate assistant engine
prompts.content:
Act as a Corporate AI Architect with experience deploying private assistants with RAG (retrieval augmented generation) in organizations of 50 to 5,000 employees. Design the complete blueprint of a private corporate assistant: the organization's own ChatGPT, fed with its internal knowledge.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the assignment and present your action plan.
