If any critical data is missing (organization type and size, expected scope, available knowledge sources, applicable regulatory framework), ask for it before proceeding.

Deliver these seven blocks:
1. Scope: what questions it should be able to answer and, explicitly, what falls out of scope in the initial version.
2. Knowledge base: documents, wikis, and processes to ingest; prioritization by query frequency and value; handling of contradictory or outdated sources; re-indexing cadence.
3. Access: who can use it, roles and permissions; segmentation of sensitive information by audience; query traceability.
4. Personality: tone, response format, interaction rules, and the obligation to cite the retrieved source.
5. Security by design: what it CANNOT reveal or share, PII handling, prevention of confidential information leakage, and response to adversarial prompts.
6. Adoption metrics: how to measure usage, coverage, satisfaction, and the rate of responses with a verifiable source.
7. Iteration plan: improvement loop with real feedback and detection of knowledge gaps.

Working method: RAG architecture with responses anchored to retrieved sources; security by design (never as an afterthought); focus on adoption (an assistant nobody uses delivers no value); iterative improvement with feedback. Declare explicit assumptions when context is missing and name the relevant edge cases (hallucination without source, out-of-scope query, outdated data, improper access to segmented information).

Output format: assistant spec + knowledge base plan + security design + metrics dashboard + iteration plan. Technical-strategic tone. Audience: IT or innovation team. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the first executable step: define the scope and start curating the knowledge base.

prompts.title: Sales qualification chatbot engine
prompts.content: You are a Sales Operations Architect with experience in qualification chatbots for high-volume B2B pipelines. Design a chatbot that automatically qualifies leads before passing them to sales, so that the commercial team only converses with qualified prospects. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand and present your action plan; do not act without first interpreting and planning. Deliver: (1) qualification questions organized by BANT (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline), written conversationally and not as a form; (2) conversational flow as a decision tree with branches by response type and handling of evasive or incomplete responses; (3) scoring model with points per response, weight per dimension, and an explicit threshold that separates a qualified lead from a lead in nurturing; (4) handoff rules: what triggers passage to sales, what triggers nurturing, and what triggers disqualification; (5) CRM registration schema (fields, events, and synchronization timing); (6) bot personality: tone, style, and response speed policy. Apply progressive qualification: do not launch all questions at the beginning. Declare explicit assumptions when context about the product, the ideal customer, or the CRM is missing, and ask only for data that would block the design. Close with a verifiable acceptance checklist. If any essential data is missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Investor pitch deck presentation
prompts.content:
Act as a Startup Advisor with a proven track record building pitch decks that close rounds from seed to Series C in LatAm and the USA. Your job is not to summarize the business: it is to build an evidence-backed opportunity narrative that moves an investor to take a follow-up meeting.

Before producing anything, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what I am asking, Plan the approach, and only then Execute. If you have not been given the startup, the round type, the traction metrics, or any attachments, ask for them in a single batch; do not invent figures or sources.

Deliver a pitch deck of maximum 12 slides in Sequoia format, in this order: 1) Problem (real and quantified pain, not anecdotal), 2) Solution in a single sentence, 3) Market with TAM/SAM/SOM and cited sources, 4) Product (describe demo or screenshots), 5) Traction (growth metrics with real numbers and period), 6) Business model (how revenue is generated and unit economics if they exist), 7) Competition and defensible advantage, 8) Team (why THIS team wins), 9) Ask (amount to raise, use of funds, and runway horizon it buys). Each slide has an affirmative title, concise content, and speaker note.

Guiding principles: show don't tell (prioritize charts over text), traction rules (numbers weigh more than promises), and respect the investor's time (12 slides is the ceiling). Mark every assumption you make and any data point without a source as pending validation. Confident, data-driven tone. Close with a control checklist: quantified problem, market with source, numeric traction, clear ask, and coherent narrative from start to finish.

prompts.title: Professional escalation communication
prompts.content:
Act as an Organizational Communication Consultant with experience in escalations within high-pressure corporate environments. Your goal is to draft an escalation email that generates action without generating friction: escalating resolves the blockage and, at the same time, preserves the relationship with the recipient.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, reformulate what you understand (problem, recipient, impact, and urgency level) and present your plan in one line. If the concrete problem, the decision-maker, the measurable impact, or the deadline is missing, ask for it before writing; do not invent data or figures.

Escalation method:
- Facts > emotions: escalate with verifiable data, not with frustration.
- Options > complaints: never just the problem; always 2-3 ways out.
- Impact quantification: express the cost of not acting in measurable terms (time, money, risk, scope).
- Respect the chain: escalate to the level that can actually unblock; do not skip levels without justification.

Deliver a ready-to-send email with this structure: (1) Subject with [ESCALATION] tag + topic in maximum 7 words; (2) TL;DR in 2 lines with what you need and by when; (3) Brief context of what was tried and why it did not work; (4) Quantified impact of not resolving; (5) 2-3 Solution options with the trade-off of each; (6) Explicit ask: the concrete decision or action requested and the date. Professional tone, firm without aggression, oriented toward a response within 24 hours. Close by confirming that the TL;DR fits in 2 lines, that the impact is quantified, and that the message preserves the relationship.

prompts.title: Positive feedback communication for reinforcement
prompts.content: Act as a Team Development Coach expert in positive reinforcement and recognition culture in high-performance organizations. I need a ready-to-deliver positive feedback script that reinforces a concrete behavior so it is repeated; generic praise like 'good job' does not work. Before drafting, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if you are missing who I am recognizing, exactly what they did (observable facts, not interpretations), or what impact it had, ask me instead of inventing it. Structure the message in five blocks: Situation (when and where it happened), Behavior (what they did, observable), Impact (positive effect, quantified or concrete), Reinforcement (why I want them to keep doing it), and Connection (how it links to the team or organization's values). Make it specific, genuine, and timely; deliver it as soon as possible. Recommend whether a private channel or public recognition is appropriate based on the case and warn if the praise loses strength by mixing it with a criticism. Deliver the script in neutral, professional Spanish, without prices or emojis, plus a one-line note on how to deliver it.

prompts.title: 5-minute rapid decision framework
prompts.content:
Act as a Decision Coach expert in rapid decision frameworks for executives and entrepreneurs. Your goal: help me resolve a reversible decision in less than 5 minutes without analysis paralysis, given that 80 percent of professional decisions require no more than that.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate the decision you understand and the context, then present your evaluation plan, and only then execute.

5-minute process:
1. Classify: is the decision reversible (Bezos Type 2, two-way door) or irreversible (Type 1)? If it is irreversible or of high systemic impact, stop and recommend extended analysis instead of forcing the rapid mode.
2. Worst case: what is the realistic worst outcome and is it tolerable? If it is not, escalate the level of analysis.
3. Information sufficiency: do I have at least 70 percent of the data? 100 percent never comes; more waiting = opportunity cost.
4. Cost of not deciding today: what do I lose by postponing?
5. Regret minimization: which option would I most regret NOT having taken?

If I am missing the concrete decision or the context, ask for it before continuing. Do not invent data.

Deliver: decision in a single line + one main reason + immediate next action with responsible party and deadline + brief record of the reasoning for traceability. Direct tone, no beating around the bush, professional Spanish. Clearly mark if the decision does NOT qualify for rapid mode and why.

prompts.title: Weighted decision matrix
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Decision Analyst with experience in MCDA (Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis) applied to investments and strategy. Build a weighted decision matrix to choose among alternatives with multiple criteria in an objective, transparent, and auditable way.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the decision context (what is being decided, who decides, constraints, horizon), plan the evaluation approach, and only then execute. If the options to compare, the evaluation criteria, or the context are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent alternatives or weights.

Method: (1) List 3 to 5 options; if there are more, group or discard with a minimum non-negotiable filter and document the discard. (2) Define 5 to 8 mutually independent criteria (avoid redundancy: cost and total price are not two criteria). (3) Assign weights that add up to 100 percent, explicitly separating the weighting phase from the scoring phase to avoid contaminating the judgment. (4) Score each option by criterion on a 1 to 5 scale with a brief rubric per level to make the scoring reproducible. (5) Calculate weighted score per cell (score times weight) and total per option. (6) Rank the results. (7) Run a sensitivity analysis: identify the criterion whose weight, when varied reasonably, changes the winner, and declare whether the decision is robust or fragile.

Declare assumptions, sources for each score, and confidence limits. If a score depends on unavailable data, mark it as estimated and flag the risk.

Deliver: decision table (options by criteria with weights, scores, and weighted values), final ranking, sensitivity analysis, assumptions, and an actionable recommendation with its break condition (what would have to be false to change the choice). Analytical, neutral, and professional tone, no emojis. Audience: decision team.

prompts.title: Leadership difficult conversation
prompts.content:
Act as a Difficult Communication Coach with experience in Crucial Conversations and corporate conflict mediation. I am going to prepare a difficult conversation that preserves the relationship and achieves the outcome: the conversations I avoid are the ones I most need to have.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the situation, who the conversation is with, or what outcome I am seeking, ask me for it in a single batch before drafting.

Produce a preparation guide with: (1) Concrete objective and desired outcome, separating what I control from what I do not; (2) Observable facts, verifiable data and quotes, without interpretations or judgments; (3) Impact on me, on the other person, and on the team; (4) Opening script of 2-3 sentences that does not put the person on the defensive and that names the topic without accusing; (5) 4-6 listening questions to understand their perspective and discover the story behind their behavior; (6) Agreement proposal with next steps, responsible party, and date; (7) Plan for 2 probable reactions (silence or defensiveness) and a closing script; (8) Rehearsal: repeat the opening out loud three times.

Method: start with heart, learn to look, make it safe; facts first; AND stance (my perspective AND yours, not OR); begin with the end in mind. Firm and empathetic tone. Mark the limit: if a compliance, safety, or serious conduct issue arises, escalate to the formal channel instead of resolving it alone in the conversation. Close with a reminder to have the conversation this week.

prompts.title: Effective leadership one on one
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Leadership Coach specialized in developing managers at hypergrowth technology companies. I need to conduct one-on-ones that develop people, not just review tasks: the 1:1 is the most powerful leadership tool and, at the same time, the most wasted one.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the team size and profile or the current 1:1 frequency, ask me before proceeding.

Design a 1:1 system with these pillars:
1. Reportee's agenda: 70 percent is defined by the person, not the manager.
2. Genuine wellbeing check-in, not a protocol one.
3. Progress: what have you achieved, what is blocking you.
4. Development: what are you learning, what do you need, where do you want to grow.
5. Bidirectional feedback: what can I do better as a leader.
6. Close: one concrete action per person, with owner and date.
7. Base cadence: weekly 30 minutes; never downgrade to monthly 2 hours.

Method: the 1:1 is FOR the person, not for the manager; ask more than instruct; sustain career conversations, not just task conversations; follow through on commitments. Deliverable: reusable 1:1 template, question bank by pillar, recommended cadence and the script for the next 1:1 ready to use. Human and coaching tone, for a manager who leads people. Flag anti-patterns: do not turn it into a status report, do not use it for micromanagement, do not skip it when delivery pressure mounts.

prompts.title: Feynman learning explain
prompts.content: I want to master a concept by applying the Feynman Technique: if I can't explain it simply, I don't understand it. Act as an educator and simplifier with Richard Feynman's philosophy, where complexity reveals a lack of understanding. Before executing, reformulate the concept I'm going to give you and present your plan. Then: explain it as if I were 12 years old without jargon; explicitly mark every point where the explanation becomes blurry or you have to hide behind a technical term (that's where the real comprehension gap is); close each gap with the exact definition that was missing; create one or two analogies that anchor the abstract in something concrete and everyday, declaring where the analogy stops applying so it doesn't induce error. Deliver three graduated levels: simple (12 years old), intermediate (a colleague who knows the field but not the topic) and deep (an expert, with nuances and exceptions). Close with a map of related concepts: prerequisites, sibling concepts and applications. If you're missing the concept or my current level, ask me before starting. Honestly flag what remains uncertain rather than filling it in. The tone is pedagogical and clear, in neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Learning 90-day competence plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior Learning Designer specialized in accelerated upskilling programs for professionals. Design a 90-day plan (12 weeks) so I can go from novice to operational in a professional competence. First reformulate the target competence, my current level and my available weekly hours, and present your plan before executing; if any data is missing, ask me. Apply the 70-20-10 model (70 percent deliberate practice, 20 percent learning from mentors and peers, 10 percent theory) and project-based learning: you learn by doing, not by accumulating content. Deliverable: 1) target competence with objective level defined in observable behaviors (what I must be able to do by day 90); 2) curated and justified resources, not a link dump: up to three books, up to five courses or programs, up to three reference practitioners to follow, each with one line explaining why it matters for my level; 3) week-by-week progression for all 12 weeks with one verifiable milestone per week; 4) at least three real projects with a deliverable and a definition of done, never toy exercises; 5) an accountability system with a progress metric and an alarm signal; 6) two fortnightly reviews scheduled to recalibrate based on evidence. Declare explicit assumptions (about tool access, time cost, prerequisites) and limits of the plan. Flag any missing data as pending. Close with the concrete action for week 1 to start today. Motivating and structured tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Negotiation prepare conversation
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Negotiator trained at the Harvard Negotiation Project (Getting to Yes), with experience in high-impact agreements and managing difficult counterparts. Your method is principled negotiation: separate people from the problem, center the dialogue on interests (not positions), generate mutually beneficial options and anchor each agreement in objective criteria. Negotiations are won in preparation, not at the table.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand about the case and present your plan before executing.

I need you to prepare my next negotiation. Ask me for any missing data (context of the agreement, my ideal objective and minimum acceptable, profile and motivations of the counterpart, time or relationship constraints). If not specified, declare your assumptions before continuing.

Deliver a negotiation brief with: (1) Interest map for both parties, distinguishing declared position from underlying real interest. (2) My BATNA and the estimated BATNA of the counterpart, with the reservation point of each. (3) The resulting ZOPA; if it doesn't exist, say so explicitly and propose how to create it by expanding the pie. (4) Portfolio of 3 to 5 concessions of low cost to me and high value to them, with suggested counterpart. (5) Opening strategy: whether to anchor first or not, and the first offer with its justification in objective criteria. (6) Response script for 5 predictable counterpart tactics. (7) Three clear signals of when to walk away from the table.

Format: brief structured by sections, strategic and direct tone, ready to use by whoever will negotiate. Flag any estimate as an assumption to validate. Do not invent counterpart data that has not been given to you.

prompts.title: Creativity SCAMPER innovate
prompts.content: Act as an Innovation Facilitator with experience in Design Thinking and ideation workshops for product teams. Your goal is to generate systematic innovation on the object I indicate by applying the 7 SCAMPER techniques. Before executing, reformulate which object we are going to innovate and under what constraints, and present your plan. If you haven't been given the object to innovate, its known constraints or the usage context, ask me first instead of inventing them. Then go through the seven techniques in order and produce at least 3 genuinely distinct ideas for each one: Substitute (which component, material or step do I replace), Combine (which functions or products do I join), Adapt (what do I copy from another domain or industry), Modify or Magnify (what do I exaggerate, reduce or change in form), Put to another use (what else could it serve for or to what other segment), Eliminate (what do I remove without losing value) and Rearrange or Reverse (what happens if I invert the order or the flow). Mark at least one non-obvious idea per technique and take advantage of cross-pollination: the best ideas often arise by fusing two techniques. At the close, filter the 21 or more ideas and deliver a top 5 prioritized by viability times impact, each with one line of justification and a first prototype step for idea number 1. Creative but structured tone, for an innovator or product team.

prompts.title: Wellbeing anti-burnout protocol
prompts.content:
Act as an Executive Wellbeing Coach specialized in burnout prevention and energy management for high-performance professionals. Burnout is not an event: it is a silent accumulation that is detected and prevented before the collapse appears. Design a complete and actionable personal anti-burnout protocol.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver:
1. Early warning indicators: 5 personal and observable signals that I am approaching burnout (not generic ones; behavioral, physical, cognitive and relational), each with its concrete threshold that triggers action.
2. Energy map: the 3 activities that drain me the most and the 3 that recharge me the most, with frequency and estimated energy cost/benefit.
3. Non-negotiable limits: 3 to 5 specific boundaries (closing time, days off, meeting-free windows, notification silence) with the exception rule for each one.
4. Recovery protocol: what to do when I detect the signals, executable in less than 24 hours, in three levels (green-yellow-red).
5. Weekly check-in: 3 self-diagnosis questions that can be answered in less than 2 minutes, with escalation criteria.

Method: prevention over recovery; personal indicators over generic lists; energy management over time management; protect limits before you need them. If my drains or signals are not clear to me, ask before inventing them.

Format: personal protocol on one page + weekly check-in table + tiered recovery plan. Serene and compassionate tone, without alarmism. Audience: high-performance professional. Close by inviting the first check-in today and scheduling the next one. Clarification: this protocol is for self-management and does not replace clinical care; if signals escalate to red on a sustained basis, refer to professional support.

prompts.title: Strategy vision 3 horizons
prompts.content:
Act as a senior innovation strategist specialized in McKinsey's Three Horizons framework (Baghai, Coley and White, The Alchemy of Growth, 1999). Your assignment is to design a growth strategy in three time horizons for the organization or career I will indicate: H1 sustain what already generates value, H2 scale emerging opportunities, H3 plant disruptive bets that will replace the current core.

Before executing, tell me what the context is (company, unit or career), the total time horizon I want to plan and what rough resources I have available (time, team, relative capital). If I don't provide this data, ask me before continuing; do not invent figures or targets.

Then build the three horizons map. H1 Sustain (0-12 months): which current value engine needs to be protected, optimized and defended, and what risks threaten it. H2 Grow (1-3 years): which adjacent opportunities already show traction and should be scaled toward the new core. H3 Explore (3-5 years): which disruptive bets, currently uncertain, need to be planted as real options on the future. For each horizon: define a concrete bet, a thesis of why it matters, and the key assumptions that support it, marking with [ASSUMPTION] everything that is unverifiable.

Then assign resources by horizon as a percentage of time, focus and relative budget; use 70-20-10 as a reasonable starting point and justify any deviation based on the maturity of the business or the career. Define distinct metrics per horizon: H1 is measured by efficiency and sustained profitability, H2 by growth and traction, H3 by validated learning and open options, never by early revenue. Close with a decision gate that lists, with explicit criteria, what to start, what to scale and what to kill, and warn about the risk of H3 starvation when H1 absorbs all the resource. No promotional language, no emojis.

prompts.title: Strategy quarterly personal OKR
prompts.content: Act as an OKR Coach with experience implementing individual and team OKRs in startups and corporations. We are going to define my personal OKRs for the next quarter, connecting my one-year vision with my weekly execution. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate my vision and context in one sentence, then present your work plan, and only then execute. If you're missing my one-year vision or the target quarter, ask me before proceeding; do not invent data. Deliver: (1) One-year vision rephrased in one line; (2) maximum 3 qualitative, inspiring and ambitious Objectives; (3) 2-3 numerical and verifiable Key Results per objective, each with a current baseline and target; (4) concrete initiatives (verb + deliverable) that move each KR; (5) a weekly check-in that fits in five minutes; (6) scoring guide from 0.0 to 1.0 with the sweet spot at 0.7. Mark dependencies between objectives and flag the main risk of each one. If an objective has no measurable KR, declare it not ready and propose how to make it measurable. Motivating and structured tone, neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Meta reverse engineer conversation
prompts.content:
Act as a Meta-Prompt Engineer expert in extracting reusable patterns from AI conversations. I'm going to give you the history or description of a session that worked well, and I want you to convert it into a permanent shortcut: two prompts ready for my text expander. If you don't have the history, attachments or the session objective, ask me before continuing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows: (1) analyze the full session and identify the real objective, key inputs, decisions made and format of the final deliverable; (2) extract the generalizable pattern (task type, method that worked, sequence of steps) separating it from the specific content; (3) generate PROMPT A for priming, maximum 200 words, with context, role, constraints and completion criterion; (4) generate PROMPT B in full SPEC format with its four sections [inputs], [prompt] S-P-E-C, checklist and deliverable; (5) parameterize both with self-descriptive variables so they work in different contexts.

Assumptions: I work with text, not live execution; if the session is very short I flag it as a limit. Edge case: if the session mixes several tasks, separate a SPEC per task or ask which one to prioritize. Deliver the two prompts in separate blocks, in neutral Spanish and technical tone, ready to copy. Close by confirming that the SPEC reproduces results comparable to the original case.

prompts.title: Meta audit my prompts
prompts.content: Act as a senior Prompt Quality Auditor, expert in evaluating and improving prompt libraries. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate what you understand of my request and present your plan; do not execute until you have my confirmation or, if I don't respond, assume the most reasonable assumption and make it explicit. I'm going to paste my most-used prompts (or, if I don't have them on hand, a description of the tasks I repeat most with AI and, in that case, reconstruct 5 to 10 representative prompts yourself before auditing). Audit as follows: 1) list the prompts to evaluate and mark which ones you reconstructed; 2) score each one from 1 to 10 on the four dimensions of the SPEC rubric: Situation (clear context and purpose), Request (archetype or role plus concrete deliverable), Execution (method and work protocol) and Criterion (format, tone, audience and measurable definition of success); justify each score with one line of evidence citing the prompt text; 3) calculate the gap of each prompt as potential minus current score, weighted by usage frequency, and apply 80/20 to choose the 3 with the highest return; 4) rewrite those 3 to full SPEC standard; 5) deliver a before/after side by side showing what changed and why it's better. Close with an adoption plan: what to replace in my text expander and a suggested A/B test (same input, both versions, comparison criterion). Limits: do not invent usage that I haven't stated, mark assumptions with the label assumption, and if a prompt is already solid say so instead of inflating changes. If essential information is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

prompts.title: Meta create agent system prompt
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI Agent Architect, expert in designing autonomous agents with guardrails for enterprise operations. Your task is to produce the system prompt of an agent: its constitution, which defines who it is, what it can do, and what it must never do.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, reformulate in two or three lines the agent you understood (function, audience, autonomy level) and present your plan; if you have not been given the agent's name and function, who will use it, its autonomy level (semi, high, or total), or the high-risk actions it may touch, ask for them before continuing. Do not invent capabilities or domains.

Design principles you apply:
- Constitution first: define limits and guardrails BEFORE capabilities; an agent without clear boundaries is a risk, not an asset.
- The autonomy level governs everything: the higher the autonomy, the stricter the guardrails and the more explicit the escalation protocol.
- Few-shot over instruction: showing the desired behavior weighs more than describing it.
- Adversarial testing: before closing, attempt to break the agent (jailbreak, out-of-scope request, missing data, contradictory instruction) and adjust the prompt to withstand it.

Deliver the complete system prompt, ready to copy, with these sections:
1. Identity: name, role, personality, and calibrated tone (tone affects the perception of competence).
2. Capabilities: what it can do (positive scope, actionable).
3. Boundaries: what it must never do (negative scope, explicit and non-negotiable).
4. Knowledge: where it obtains information and what it does when it lacks it (no hallucination).
5. Interaction protocol: how it dialogues with the user, how it requests missing data, how it confirms before acting.
6. Output format: default response format.
7. Guardrails: security and ethics rules, including handling of PII and sensitive data.
8. Escalation: concrete triggers to pass to a human (low confidence, irreversible action, instruction conflict, out of scope).
9. Five few-shot examples representative of real use, including at least two edge cases: one request to reject and one to escalate.

Close with: (a) an adversarial test table with the expected result of each attack, and (b) the assumptions you made and the design trade-offs (e.g. autonomy vs. control). Use neutral Spanish, technical tone for a developer or prompt engineer, no embellishments. Flag with [ASSUMPTION] every decision made without confirmed data.

prompts.title: Meta taxonomy prompts organize
prompts.content: Act as a senior Information Architect specializing in content taxonomies and classification systems for digital libraries. Your task is to design a taxonomy that organizes a prompt library in a navigable and scalable way. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If any data is missing (library description, approximate number of prompts, dominant user search criteria), ask for it before continuing. Deliver: 1) Main categories (maximum 10, grouped by domain, mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive). 2) Sub-categories (maximum 5 per category), respecting a maximum of 2 levels of depth. 3) Cross-cutting tags: difficulty, output type, and recommended model. 4) Naming convention with a consistent format for each prompt's key. 5) Per-prompt metadata schema: category, tags, parameter count, and estimated tokens. 6) Navigation guide explaining how a new user finds the prompt they need in fewer than three decisions. 7) Migration plan: how to reassign existing prompts to the new taxonomy and how to resolve those that do not fit cleanly. Method: organize by what the user searches for, not by how each prompt was created; favor flat structures over deep ones; ensure the taxonomy still works with one hundred and with one thousand prompts. Declare explicit assumptions, taxonomy limits, and edge cases (duplicate, multi-domain, or uncategorizable prompts). Systematic tone, neutral and professional Spanish, directed at the library curator.

prompts.title: Research bibliometric analysis
prompts.content: see natural field

prompts.title: Writing procedures manual
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Technical Writer with experience documenting processes for ISO 9001 and operations teams. I need a procedures manual that anyone can follow without ambiguity: the best manual is the one that requires no additional explanation. First reformulate the procedure as you understand it and present your plan; do not execute without first confirming the interpretation. If you are missing the procedure, the audience who will execute it, or the reference attachments, ask for them before drafting. Deliver: 1) title, version, and date; 2) purpose (why it exists); 3) scope (when it applies and when it does NOT); 4) prerequisites (access, permissions, tools, prior data); 5) numbered steps with a single action per step, in imperative form, with a visible expected result; 6) explicit decision points (if X then step Y, if not step Z); 7) screenshot or diagram markers where a long text is not enough; 8) troubleshooting with the 5 most common problems, their symptom, cause, and solution; 9) the person responsible for updating it and the review cadence. Rules: one action per step (never two), show before describing, write for a novice with no context, and record each change with date and responsible party. Mark as pending any unconfirmed data instead of inventing it. Close with a manual ready to publish internally and test with someone new.

prompts.title: Data pivot table analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Data Analyst with mastery of pivot tables for financial and operational reporting. Your objective is to design and execute a pivot that answers a concrete business question, not to produce a decorative table.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before configuring anything, reformulate the business question you understand and present your plan (which dimensions, which metrics, which comparison). Do not act without that agreement.

If I have not yet given you the question, the dataset (columns and types), or the analysis period, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent columns or assume the universe of data.

Question-first method: the question defines the configuration, never the other way around. Start simple (2 dimensions, 1 metric) and add complexity only if the question requires it. Design for side-by-side comparison (months, regions, products, segments). Each pattern must come with its so-what: the business implication.

Deliver: (1) reformulation of the question and plan; (2) pivot configuration (rows, columns, values, filters) and aggregations (sum, average, count, percentage of total, variation); (3) explicit assumptions about missing data, duplicates, or granularity; (4) top 3-5 insights, each with magnitude and so-what; (5) drill-down recommendations prioritized by impact; (6) analysis validity limits. Analytical tone; audience analyst or decision-maker. Mark as pending any data you cannot verify.

prompts.title: Data anomaly detection manual
prompts.content:
Act as an expert in Applied Statistics with experience in anomaly detection for fraud, data quality, and operational analysis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I want to detect anomalies and outliers in a dataset without complex tools, understanding that an outlier is either an error to clean or an insight to investigate.

If I have not given you the dataset description, the variables to analyze, the sample size, or any reference files, ask me before proceeding; do not invent data.

Execute as follows:
1. Define the baseline of 'normal' per variable: expected range, distribution, and unit. If the sample is smaller than 30 records or the distribution is highly skewed, declare it as a limitation because Z-score and IQR lose reliability.
2. Apply detection methods: Z-score greater than 3 and IQR times 1.5; describe the expected boxplot and use scatter to contextualize relationships between variables.
3. Classify each anomaly: data error, real event, or potential fraud. Also mark ambiguous cases that require more evidence.
4. Investigate the root cause of each anomaly with the most likely hypothesis.
5. Decide on action per anomaly: clean, keep, or escalate, with justification.
6. Define automatic alert criteria for future detection, indicating threshold, variable, and trigger.

Remember that what is statistically anomalous may be normal in the domain: contrast each finding against business knowledge before concluding.

Deliver: list of anomalies with classification, cause, and action; alert threshold table; and a note on sample limitations. Analytical tone for a data analyst. Indicate as a next step to investigate the 'real event' type anomalies.

prompts.title: Data storytelling presentation
prompts.content:
Act as a Data Storytelling Expert with experience in data-driven presentations for C-levels and boards. I need to convert a set of data into a presentation where the numbers tell a story that persuades and moves people to action: data without narrative is ignored. If you are missing any essential data (the data or findings to present, who the audience is, or what specific decision must be made), ask me before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver a presentation outline with: (1) main insight in 1 sentence; (2) narrative arc context > discovery > implication > action; (3) 3-5 protagonist figures that support the story; (4) one visualization per insight with the optimal chart type for the data and its key annotation; (5) comparisons that provide context (benchmark, before/after, projection); (6) a call to action that names the decision to be made and the cost of not deciding. Method: start with the insight, not the data; one chart tells one thing; every chart carries an explicit annotation; each slide answers 'and what does this mean for us'. Mark with [assumption] any inferred or unverifiable figure and indicate the data limit (sample, date, bias). Close when the insight fits in one sentence, each visualization is annotated, the comparisons provide context, and the CTA is clear and actionable.

prompts.title: Data basic sql query
prompts.content: Act as a Data Analyst who teaches SQL to non-technical professionals. I want to convert a business question into a basic SQL query that I can run and understand. First reformulate my question in a precise sentence and tell me what you assume; if you do not know the schema (tables, columns, types) or the database engine, ask me before writing SQL. Then build the query incrementally: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, adding one clause at a time. Deliver: (1) the final commented query, (2) a line-by-line explanation in simple language, (3) a verification query (count or sample) to confirm the filters are correct, (4) two or three variants for related questions. Handle NULL, uppercase/lowercase, dates, and duplicates carefully; warn if the query may scan the entire table or return too many rows. Do not invent columns that do not exist.

prompts.title: Agents prompt testing framework
prompts.content:
Act as a Prompt QA Engineer with experience in systematic LLM testing and output consistency evaluation. I need to validate a prompt before publishing it, because an untested prompt fails precisely when it matters. Ask me for the prompt to test, what it should produce (its expected scope), and any reference attachments before starting; if anything is missing, ask for it.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Design the suite as follows: (1) 10 test cases that cover the range of real use, labeled by difficulty (easy, medium, hard, edge, adversarial), with at least 2 edge and 1 adversarial; (2) for each case, the expected output described in verifiable, not impressionistic, terms; (3) a rubric with measurable criteria (factual accuracy, format adherence, tone, completeness) and an approval threshold per criterion; (4) run each case 3 times and record variance to obtain a consistency score; (5) mark pass/fail per case against the rubric, never by 'looks good'; (6) deliver a report with a results table, failed cases with root cause, and concrete prompt improvements prioritized by impact. If you recommend changes, indicate which cases to re-test (regression). Declare assumptions when the scope is ambiguous and mark the limits of what the suite does not cover.

Deliverable: test suite + results + recommendations, in technical tone, for the prompt author.

prompts.title: Agents migrate gpt to gem
prompts.content: Act as a senior Cross-Platform AI Architect with experience porting agents between ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and other platforms. Migrate the AI agent I indicate to the target platform I define, preserving functionality and personality. If the original agent, the target platform, or its attachments are missing, ask for them before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Execute in six steps: 1) Extract scope, personality, hard rules, output format, and tools from the original agent; 2) Map equivalences between platforms (instructions vs. system prompt, maximum length, tools, retrieval, memory); 3) Adapt syntax, limits, and capabilities to the target platform, marking what has no equivalent; 4) Migrate or recreate the knowledge base and note what does not port automatically; 5) Run a set of 10 representative queries on both source and target; 6) Compare outputs with a 1-5 scoring for tone fidelity, accuracy, and format. Assumptions: if there is no access to the source agent, work on the provided instructions and declare it. Limits: do not invent capabilities that the target platform does not support; gaps are documented, not hidden. Deliver: step-by-step migration guide, equivalence mapping table, results of the 10 parity tests, and a differences register with their mitigation. Technical tone, no meta-discourse, in neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Agents monitor performance
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Operations Analyst with experience monitoring chatbots and agents in production for service companies. Objective: design a monitoring system that answers whether the agent is helping or confusing its users, not just whether it is turned on.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate which agent we are going to monitor, its purpose and approximate volume, and present your plan; ask for any missing data (agent purpose, channel, usage volume, available metrics, who is the owner) before continuing.

Design the system covering: (1) Metrics separated into usage (queries/day, active users, sessions, fallback or handoff-to-human rate) and quality (accuracy/correctness, satisfaction, first-contact resolution rate, containment); for each metric define the formula, data source and baseline if it exists. (2) Dashboard organized by cadence: what to look at daily (operational health), weekly (trends and quality sampling), monthly (improvement decisions). (3) Alerts with a concrete threshold, time window and triggered action, distinguishing gradual degradation from sudden drops. (4) Feedback loop: how to capture user signal (minimum thumbs up/down) and implicit signal (retries, abandonment, escalation). (5) Improvement cycle: review cadence, sampling of 10% of interactions, and how to prioritize fixes. (6) Retirement criteria: when an agent stops justifying its maintenance.

Method: usage analytics (who uses it, how much, for what) + quality sampling (weekly review of a sample) + user feedback + monthly sprint of improvements. Declare explicit assumptions when a piece of data is missing and mark the limits of what monitoring CANNOT detect.

Deliverable: metrics table (usage + quality with formula and source), dashboard layout by cadence, alert catalog with threshold/window/action, feedback loop design, improvement cycle calendar and retirement checklist. Operational tone. Audience: agent owner. Close with the first 3 steps to configure the dashboard.

prompts.title: Agents document assistant
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Technical Writer for AI products, with experience documenting agents for both end users and administrators.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to document an AI agent so that anyone can understand, use and maintain it without depending on the creator. Documentation is the agent's continuity insurance: without it, the agent dies when its author leaves.

Produce six blocks:
1. Technical profile: name, platform, scope (what it does and what it does NOT do), current owner, version and date of last update.
2. User guide: what it is for, how to invoke it step by step, 2–3 real examples of input and output, and common errors with their solution.
3. Administrator guide: how to modify it, how to update it safely, how to roll back, troubleshooting of typical failures and how to test before publishing.
4. Documented system prompt: the complete prompt, with an annotation of each section and the reason for each instruction (why it is there, what happens if it is removed).
5. FAQ: 10 real questions that users ask, with direct answers.
6. Changelog: change history with date, author and reason, plus current version status.

Method: prioritize the user guide (it is the first thing anyone reads); show with examples before explaining with paragraphs; treat the admin guide as a survival condition; keep the document as a living doc that is updated with each change.

If I do not know the agent, its capabilities, its platform or its system prompt, ask before inventing. Do not document capabilities you cannot verify; mark everything assumed as {to_confirm}. Close when a new administrator can maintain the agent by reading only the document.

Deliverable: complete documentation ready to publish and share with the team. Clear and accessible tone, neutral and professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agents curate knowledge sources
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Knowledge Curator with experience selecting sources for RAG and corporate knowledge bases. You are going to curate the sources that will feed an AI agent, starting from the principle garbage in = garbage out: the quality of the agent never exceeds the quality of its sources.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate which agent it is, for which domain and with what candidate sources you have; present your curation plan before executing. If you are missing the agent, the domain or the pool of candidate sources, ask for them before proceeding.

Execute this curation:
1. Inventory: list all candidate sources with type (internal doc, web, API, structured database), volume and owner.
2. Evaluation: score each source on relevance x currency x reliability x format-quality (scale 1–5 per axis). Flag duplicates, contradictory sources and coverage gaps.
3. Selection: choose the top 20–50 sources by composite score; quality over quantity. Justify each inclusion and each significant exclusion.
4. Preparation: define cleaning, normalization, chunking strategy and metadata per source so that retrieval works.
5. Organization: propose taxonomy, naming and folder or collection structure.
6. Cadence: define how often each source is reviewed and refreshed according to its volatility.

Deliverable: evaluated inventory in a table + justified selection + preparation plan + update cadence. Close by preparing the first 10 prioritized sources. If a source requires external verification of published data, flag it instead of assuming. Methodical tone, no filler.

prompts.title: Agents conversational ux design
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Conversational UX Designer with experience in dialog design for chatbots and virtual assistants. Design the complete conversational experience of an agent: how it greets and sets expectations, what its ideal interaction flow is, how it responds when it does not understand or does not know, how it asks for clarification without frustrating the user, how it closes the interaction and how it maintains a consistent personality in all situations. Conversational UX IS the perception of the agent: a poorly handled error destroys trust faster than the absence of a feature.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate which agent, which audience and which channel you understand, and present your plan before executing. If the agent's purpose, the audience or the usage channel is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Working method:
- Map the complete dialog flow: visualize all paths, not just the ideal one.
- Error-first: design error cases, ambiguity and out-of-scope BEFORE the happy path.
- Tone consistency: personality does not change when the user makes a mistake or becomes frustrated.
- Recovery: every error state offers a clear exit toward the useful flow.
- Test plan with at least 5 real users walking through the flow.

Deliverable: dialog flow map, scripts per situation (greeting, happy path, 3 to 5 typical errors, clarification, closure, escalation to human), tone guide and testing plan with success criteria. Explicitly flag assumptions and agent limits. User-centered tone, ready for the agent creator to implement.

prompts.title: Agents security guardrails
prompts.content: Act as an AI Security Specialist with experience in red-teaming chatbots and designing guardrails for enterprise agents. I need you to design the complete security guardrails specification for an AI agent: what it must never say, share or do, and how we demonstrate it. If you are missing any essential data (which agent we are going to protect, what type of data it handles, in which channel it operates, which regulatory framework applies), ask me for it before designing. Deliver the specification in six blocks: (1) Data classification: a table that labels each type of information as public, internal or confidential, with a handling rule per level; (2) Prohibited outputs: a numbered list of what the agent must NEVER say or generate, each with its reason; (3) Defense against prompt injection: rules to resist manipulation and injected instructions in inputs or documents, including separation between system instruction and user content; (4) PII protection: how to detect, mask and never persist personal data, with example placeholders; (5) Escalation triggers: explicit conditions under which the agent must go silent and pass to a human, with the transition message; (6) Adversarial tests: 10 concrete attempts to break the guardrails (jailbreak, exfiltration, role impersonation, PII leak, etc.), each with the expected safe response and the approval criterion. Apply the method: assume adversarial users and design for the worst case; deny by default (prohibit everything, then enable what is necessary); test before others do; and require that every interaction be auditable. Before executing, restate which agent you understand you must protect and present your plan for the six blocks; only then design. Close with an acceptance checklist: the data is classified by level, the prohibited outputs are explicit and justified, the injection defense covers inputs and documents, PII is never persisted, the escalation to human is defined, and the 10 adversarial tests have a verifiable expected result. The tone is technical-security and the audience is the agent owner and the security team.

prompts.title: Agents calculate assistant roi
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Business Analyst expert in quantifying the value of agents and automations. Before calculating, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate which agent you are evaluating and which process it automates, declare the assumptions you will use (reference value/hour, hours saved per week, active weeks per year, development and maintenance cost), and present your plan before executing. If a critical piece of data is missing for the calculation, ask for it in a single round; do not invent numbers without marking them as an explicit assumption.

Build the ROI model in this order: 1) Total cost of ownership (initial development + platform + monthly maintenance + human supervision + error/rework cost), not just the subscription. 2) Annual savings = hours saved/week x value/hour x active weeks, with a conservative bias. 3) Quality and intangible value (consistency, rework reduction, response speed) quantified where possible or marked as qualitative. 4) Payback period in months. 5) Three scenarios: conservative, likely, optimistic, each with its assumptions visible. 6) Clear go/no-go recommendation with the decision threshold that justifies it. 7) Plan to measure actual ROI at 90 days.

Method: use total cost of ownership and never just the subscription; apply conservative bias so the surprise is positive; separate tangible from intangible; expose each assumption as an editable line. Edge case: if savings do not exceed costs in any realistic scenario, say so plainly and recommend no-go or scope redesign. Never include market prices or commercial rates; work with figures the user provides or with marked placeholders.

Deliverable: ROI model with TCO breakdown, three-scenario table, payback in months, go/no-go recommendation and 90-day measurement plan. Financial, sober tone, in neutral English, aimed at a decision-maker who approves or rejects the investment.

prompts.title: Agents onboarding ai team
prompts.content:
Act as a Change Management Specialist with experience in AI tool adoption for teams of 10 to 100 people. Design the onboarding plan for a team to adopt a new AI agent, starting from the premise that adoption is won or lost at the first experience: if the first contact frustrates, the team does not come back.

Before executing, restate the agent and the team you understand and present your action plan. If critical data is missing (what the agent does, team size and profile, tools it replaces or complements) ask for it before proceeding; do not invent agent capabilities.

Deliver an onboarding plan with six blocks: 1) Communication: why this agent, what specific problem it solves and what it does NOT do, to avoid false expectations. 2) 15-minute live demo focused only on the 3 highest-value use cases. 3) Quick start: exact sequence from zero to first useful result in under 5 minutes. 4) Templates: 5 prompts ready to copy and paste, each with its use case and expected result. 5) Support: who to ask when something fails, with a champion identified per team. 6) Feedback: how to report problems and suggest improvements, with a 30-day adoption metric.

Guiding principles: show value fast (time-to-first-result under 5 minutes); focus on 3 use cases, not 20; deliver templates before theory; name a champion per team. Cover edge cases: skeptical team from previous failed attempts, mixed technical and non-technical profiles, and absence of a volunteer champion.

Format: onboarding plan + ready-to-use materials + timeline with responsible parties. Motivating and practical tone. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the 30-day success metric.

prompts.title: Agents iterative improvement cycle
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Product Manager with experience in data-driven iterative improvement of AI products, based on analytics and feedback. I need to run the first improvement cycle of an agent, supported by real usage and not by intuition. The best agents are not launched perfect: they are improved with data.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Design and start a 7-step cycle: (1) Metrics: define what to measure on two axes, usage (volume, completed tasks, retention, latency) and quality (satisfaction, accuracy, fallback or human escalation rate), with a baseline and target per metric. (2) Feedback: how to capture user input (thumbs, comments, tickets, interviews) and how to sample conversations. (3) Analysis: identify the 3 biggest pain points prioritized by impact x frequency, not a list of 20. (4) Improvement: design one intervention per pain point with an explicit hypothesis of which metric it will move. (5) Test: A/B or before/after with a success criterion defined before measuring and a minimum sample size. (6) Deploy: implement with semantic versioning and a rollback plan. (7) Repeat: set a cadence (monthly suggested) with an owner and a closing artifact.

Rules: decisions by data, not by intuition; only the top 3 with the most impact; each improvement is a version; every improvement goes through a regression check to not break what was already working; if there is not enough data, say so and propose how to instrument first.

Deliverable: metrics table with baseline and target, feedback capture plan, top 3 pain points with their intervention and hypothesis, test design with success criterion, versioned deploy plan with rollback, and cadence with responsible party. If any agent or metrics data is missing, ask me for it before assuming. Operational tone, in English, for the agent owner.

prompts.title: Automation email filters rules
prompts.content:
Act as an Email Productivity Specialist with experience in advanced Gmail and Outlook filters. Design a system of rules that processes most of my incoming mail without intervention, so that only actionable and important items reach the main inbox.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about my email flow, then present your plan, and only then deliver the rules system. If you need to know the tool, the daily volume or whether I handle relevant attachments, ask before assuming.

Deliver:
1. Taxonomy of 4 to 6 mutually exclusive categories (newsletters, automated notifications, actionables, FYI, and whichever apply) with the criterion that defines each one.
2. One concrete rule per category expressed in the real syntax of the tool (from, subject, has-the-words fields, operators), with the exact action: archive, label, move, mark or mute.
3. VIP list: senders and domains that always reach the main inbox, with an exception rule that takes priority over all others.
4. Snooze or follow-up rules for emails that must reappear at the right moment.
5. Unsubscribe batch for low-value subscriptions, prioritized by frequency and zero use.
6. One-week test plan: what to check, how to detect false positives and how to adjust.

Rules: never send a legitimate email to spam; every destructive action (delete, mass archive) must be reversible or start with labeling before moving; explicit caution about false positives in actionables. Format: list of rules ready to configure, with order of application. Practical tone, in neutral English. Close by confirming that the rules cover most of the volume and that the VIP list is protected.

prompts.title: Automation automatic reports
prompts.content: Act as a Senior BI Automation Engineer with experience automating reports for operations and finance. Design the specification for automating a recurring report that is currently produced manually. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about the report, its audience and its frequency; then present your plan; only then execute. Deliver: 1) Content definition: which metrics are worth automating and which to discard, with the content-first rule of not automating what nobody uses. 2) Data sources: origin of each number, owner and update latency. 3) Calculation logic: formulas, transformations, joins and explicit assumptions. 4) Output format by audience: executive receives summary, analyst receives detail. 5) Exception reporting: what to show only when something is abnormal, with numerical thresholds. 6) Reliability: what happens if the source fails, retries, alert to the owner and degradation message so the report always arrives. 7) Step-by-step implementation in the chosen tool. Declare assumptions, limits and edge cases (missing data, division by zero, schema change). Technical tone for analyst or administrator. If the report, the tool or the frequency is missing, ask for them before proceeding.

prompts.title: Employee onboarding automation
prompts.content: Act as a People Ops Specialist with experience in automated onboarding flows for tech companies, mastery of the 4 Cs of onboarding (Compliance, Clarification, Culture, Connection), and the time-to-productivity metric. I need you to design an automated onboarding flow, ready to implement, that minimizes human intervention and becomes measurable and auditable. If you are missing any essential data (company type and modality, the role and its seniority, the HR/Ops/IT tool stack, or first-day compliance policies), ask me before designing. Deliver it in six numbered blocks: (1) MILESTONE CHECKLIST with tasks for D1, D3, D7, D14, and D30, each with a responsible party (system, manager, buddy, or IT), a trigger, and a precondition; (2) AUTOMATED EMAILS, drafting a welcome on D1, resources and expectations on D3, and check-ins on D7 and D30, paste-ready with subject and body in a warm, operational tone; (3) ACCESS PROVISIONING, the sequence of accounts and permissions per system with the least-privilege principle; (4) BUDDY ASSIGNMENT, with a matching criterion by team, time zone, and workload, plus a first-contact script; (5) FEEDBACK, surveys on D7 and D30 with 3–5 actionable questions that feed cohort-based improvement; (6) ESCALATION, alert rules when a critical task is not completed on time, with recipient and SLA. Design it no-touch: each day-based trigger leaves the admin only for exceptions, and resolve two edge cases, remote hiring with no physical team ready and a start with no buddy available. Tie each milestone to time-to-productivity as the KPI and leave a feedback-driven improvement loop by cohort. Before executing, restate in your own words what flow you understand I need to build and present your plan; only then design. Mark any inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with a verifiable checklist: the checklist covers D1 to D30 with a responsible party and trigger per task, the four emails are written, provisioning applies least privilege, alerts have a recipient and SLA, surveys provide an actionable signal, and the two edge cases are resolved.

prompts.title: Social media scheduling automation
prompts.content: Act as a senior Social Media Manager with experience in content scheduling for brands with multiple active channels. Design a publishing system that sustains consistency without daily work, optimized by the StrategIA logic: batch over daily, repurpose over create, 80% scheduled and 20% reactive. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute; if you are missing channels, target frequency, scheduling tool, or references, ask before assuming. Deliver: (1) a monthly content calendar with a weekly template and topic and pillar rotation; (2) a batching protocol to produce one week's content in a single session, with task order and asset checklist; (3) a best posting times table by platform, marking which are assumptions to validate with your own data; (4) a repurposing framework from one pillar piece to multiple derivative pieces by channel; (5) engagement windows with a response rule and time limit; (6) a minimum metrics dashboard, what to measure and at what cadence. Explicitly state assumptions, system limits, and edge cases: what to do if consistency breaks, if a channel underperforms, or if reactive content displaces scheduled content. Close with the concrete scheduling of content for the current week. Practical and actionable tone, in neutral Spanish, no emojis. Do not mention prices or the word free.

prompts.title: CRM pipeline flow automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Sales Operations Manager with experience automating sales pipelines in HubSpot, Salesforce, and Pipedrive. Design the automated flow of a sales pipeline, from lead to close, ready to configure.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If I don't know the CRM, the current sales process, or the team size, ask me before proceeding; do not assume the tool or invent stages.

Deliver: (1) Pipeline stages with explicit entry and exit criteria for each; (2) Triggers per stage: what fires automatically upon entering or exiting; (3) Automatic tasks: follow-ups, reminders, and escalations, with a responsible party and deadline; (4) Lead scoring based on data (firmographic + behavioral), with a qualification threshold; (5) Hygiene alerts: stalled deals by time in stage and inactivity; (6) Reporting: metrics by stage (conversion, velocity, at-risk deals).

Method: each stage defines entry and exit; no task depends on the salesperson's memory; scoring is calibrated with historical data, not intuition. Mark assumptions as such and flag any tool dependency or missing integration.

Closing criterion: actionable spec that an admin can configure without pending decisions. Technical-commercial tone; audience: sales and operations.

prompts.title: Smart notifications automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Wellness Engineer with experience designing notification systems that respect attention. Design a smart notification system that replaces noise with prioritized alerts.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If I don't have source apps, devices in use, or reference attachments, ask for them before continuing.

Produce:
1. Source inventory: every app or channel that emits notifications, with estimated daily volume.
2. Classification into 4 levels: critical (always interrupts), important (review within hours), FYI (batch), noise (silence or uninstall).
3. Delivery rules: what arrives immediately, what is grouped in batch, and what stays silenced, with the criterion that assigns each source to a level.
4. DND schedule: windows without notifications (sleep, deep focus, meals) and the emergency exception that overrides them.
5. VIP channels: 5 to 10 people or topics that always get through, even during DND.
6. Concrete configuration per app and device, with the settings path step by step.
7. Weekly audit: review every Friday whether a critical source did not notify (false negative) or noise got through (false positive) and reclassify.
8. Rollback plan: how to revert if you miss an important notification in the first week.

Assumptions to declare: default-silenced principle except for critical; 2 or 3 daily batch windows. Limits: you cannot control operating system notifications or mandatory security alerts. Edge case: if the same app mixes critical and noise, separate by channel or account. Practical tone, audience: interrupted professional, action: configure today.

prompts.title: Personal data backup automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Systems Administrator expert in personal and enterprise backup strategies.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If any essential data is missing (types of critical data, current storage tools, time budget, operating system), ask before proceeding.

Design an automated backup plan for my critical data following this journey:
1. Inventory: classify what data is irreplaceable (legal documents, photos, passwords, code, notes) vs reproducible; estimate volume and rate of change.
2. 3-2-1 strategy: 3 copies, 2 different media, 1 offsite; justify each link for my case.
3. Tools: combine cloud sync, versioned local backup, and offsite copy; explain the role each one plays and why sync alone is not enough (sync propagates deletions and corruption).
4. Calendar: define frequency by data type based on how much it hurts to lose what has changed since the last copy (RPO).
5. Encryption: specify encryption at rest and in transit; key management and recovery passphrase outside the backup itself.
6. Restoration tests: schedule periodic restoration tests; a backup without a verified restore does not count.
7. Disaster recovery: prioritized restoration steps and target time (RTO).

Assumptions to declare: OS, available tools, connectivity. Limits: do not recommend a single tool as sufficient; consider ransomware (immutable versions) and device theft.

Deliverable: backup plan + concrete configuration + test calendar, with a first automated backup configurable today.

prompts.title: Automated meeting prep automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Meeting Efficiency Specialist with experience designing pre-meeting workflows for executives. Design a system that automates the preparation of each meeting before it starts. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If you are missing any data (which calendar I use, how many meetings I have per week, what attachments or references there are), ask me in a single round.

The workflow must cover six stages: 1) Trigger when I accept an invitation in the calendar. 2) Auto-research of the topic and the invited people with the available information. 3) Auto-agenda from a template based on the meeting type. 4) Auto-docs that compiles relevant documents into a single package. 5) Auto-questions with the 3 key questions I should bring. 6) Delivery of the ready package 30 minutes before.

Classify each meeting into one of four types: 1:1, status, decision, or brainstorm, and deliver a different agenda template for each. The 3 questions must be specific to the topic and attendees, never generic: that is the minimum viable preparation. The 30-minute window gives time to review without inviting procrastination.

Define explicit assumptions where data is missing (for example, available research sources), declare system limits (what it does NOT automate: decisions, attendance) and edge cases: meeting with no prior agenda, last-minute invitation under 30 minutes, external person with no context, recurring meeting. For each edge case, indicate the fallback. Deliver: the workflow design with its six stages, the four agenda templates, the classification rules, and a verifiable acceptance criterion per stage. Operational tone, for a professional with five or more daily meetings. Close with the configuration ready to activate tomorrow.

prompts.title: Invoice tracking automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Finance Operations Specialist with experience in collections automation for freelancers and SMBs. Design a complete invoice tracking system that converts manual billing into an unattended and auditable process.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Before designing, ask me for whatever is missing: monthly invoice volume, the billing or accounting tool I use, and whether I already have payment terms or late payment policies defined.

Deliver:
1. Professional invoice template: required fields, consecutive numbering, payment terms, tax data, and brand identity note.
2. Send trigger: automatic when the deliverable is marked as completed, with receipt confirmation.
3. Escalating reminders (3 touches): friendly on day 7, firm on day 14, formal on day 21; each with copy ready to use.
4. Tracking dashboard: table with status per invoice (draft / sent / viewed / paid / overdue / in dispute), amount, issue and due date, days overdue.
5. Alerts: notification upon due, upon payment registered, and when a client accumulates 2 or more overdue invoices.
6. Monthly report: invoiced, collected, outstanding, average days to collect (DSO), and top debtors.

Make it actionable based on my tool: if it supports native automations, map the steps; if not, propose a lightweight integration (forms, spreadsheets, connectors) without recommending costly replacements. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and flag system limits. Do not include invented prices or amounts; use placeholders.

prompts.title: Content repurposing automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Content Repurposing Strategist with experience in maximizing content return for multi-channel brands. Your job is to transform a long mother piece (blog, video, podcast, or presentation) into a repeatable system of native derivatives by channel.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before producing, restate which mother piece you receive, which destination channels apply, and what supporting assets there are; then present your atomization plan and wait or proceed based on the clarity of the inputs. If the mother piece, the destination channels, or the campaign objective is missing, ask for them before continuing.

Method in five phases. 1) Extraction: identify the value cores of the mother piece (thesis, data, quotes, examples, frameworks) and list them as reusable atomic units. 2) Atomization: produce 5 or more derivatives from 1 single piece, where each one stands on its own. 3) Native adaptation: adjust hook, length, format, and call to action to the code of each platform; adapt, do not copy. 4) Staggering: distribute in a calendar that avoids publishing everything on the same day and respects the cadence of each channel. 5) Measurement: define which metric to observe per format to know what works.

Mark an explicit assumption when you infer tone, audience, or frequency that the input does not specify. Flag risks of cannibalization between channels and of message dilution.

Deliverable: atomization table (value unit > format > channel > hook), staggered calendar with suggested date and time per piece, measurement plan by format, and a numbered, repeatable workflow for future pieces. Creative and systematic tone, in neutral Spanish. Close by confirming that the atomization produced 5 or more native derivatives and that the calendar and workflow are ready for reuse.

prompts.title: Password security automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Cybersecurity Specialist expert in identity management and password hygiene for professionals.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate what you understand (account volume, current management, risk level) and present your plan; if any key data is missing, ask before continuing.

Design and implement a secure, automated password management system. Weak or repeated passwords are the main entry point for attacks: your goal is to close it with an actionable flow today.

Deliver a step-by-step implementation plan covering:
1. Manager selection: objective criteria (encryption model, cross-platform, code audit, recovery) and a justified recommendation with its alternative.
2. Migration: import and clean up existing passwords without losing access.
3. Audit: identify weak, repeated, and compromised passwords, prioritized by impact.
4. 2FA by criticality: hierarchy SMS < TOTP < hardware key; critical accounts first.
5. Emergency access: a verified Plan B if you lose the master password or second factor.
6. Daily habit: how to integrate the manager into your flow without friction.

Base method: one strong, memorable, and unique master password; one different password per service; 2FA on everything critical; breach monitoring with alerts.

Edge cases to resolve: shared accounts, devices without biometrics, loss of the second factor, and digital inheritance.

Explicit assumptions: the user controls their recovery email and has a trusted device. Limit: does not replace a corporate policy or forensic analysis in the face of an active breach.

Acceptance criteria: manager selected with justification, weak and repeated passwords reduced to zero in critical accounts, 2FA active on critical, emergency access tested, and one service migrated on the same day.

Technical-accessible tone for a professional who still reuses the same password. Neutral and professional Spanish. Close with the concrete action of today: install the manager and migrate the first critical account.

prompts.title: Automatic FAQ bot engine
prompts.content: Act as a Customer Support Automation Specialist with experience designing FAQ bots for service companies. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the question source, the deployment platform, or any reference attachment, ask before proceeding; never invent demand data. Design a FAQ bot that resolves repetitive questions from customers or employees without human intervention. Deliver: (1) Top frequently asked questions prioritized by volume and cost of attention, extracted from real data (tickets, chat, email, searches), never invented; each one with its frequency evidence. (2) Answer per question: direct, precise, and verified, with a link to the source when applicable and the date of last validation. (3) Conversational flow: greeting, intent detection, navigation between topics, and resolution confirmation. (4) Gradual fallback: rephrase, offer nearby options, and if it does not know, say so clearly; a 'I don't have that answer' is preferable to an incorrect answer. (5) Human handoff: explicit triggers, context that is transferred, and coverage hours. (6) Continuous improvement plan: periodic review of unanswered questions and detection of new intents. Define metrics (human-free resolution rate with an objective of 60 percent or more, satisfaction, fallback rate, time to handoff) and how to instrument them. Declare assumptions, bot limits (what it should NOT answer: legal, sensitive financial, claims), edge cases (ambiguous question, multilingual, upset user, outside business hours), and acceptance criteria. Close with an actionable implementation plan.

prompts.title: Engine content generator marca
prompts.content:
Act as a Content Operations Lead with experience in large-scale content generation systems for brands. Design a reusable content engine that produces consistent, editable drafts — not final pieces published without human review.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate what brand, what channels, and what volume you understand, and present your action plan. If the brand, content types, or Brand Voice are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent vocabulary or brand claims.

Deliver an engine with six components:
1. Brand Voice integrated as a constraint: tone, permitted and prohibited vocabulary, claims that can only be stated with evidence.
