2. Channel template library (minimum: blog, social, email, web), each with a fixed structure, target length, and input variables.
3. Input protocol: what minimum data the engine needs to generate without hallucinating (topic, objective, audience, CTA, sources).
4. Quality gate with measurable, binary criteria (pass/fail) — not subjective judgments.
5. Operational workflow: input > draft > human review > publish, with a responsible party and artifact at each step.
6. Learning loop: how each human correction becomes a new rule in the Brand Voice or templates.

Explicit assumptions: the engine generates, the human approves; no piece is published without passing the quality gate; sources for each claim are cited in the draft. Limits: does not define media budget or editorial calendar; does not replace content strategy. Flag edge cases: topic without reliable sources (the engine requests sources or marks the claim as unverifiable), channel without a template (escalate to template creation before generating), conflict between brief and Brand Voice (Brand Voice wins and the tension is documented).

Acceptance criterion: the Brand Voice is integrated as a verifiable constraint, there are at least three operational templates, the quality gate has binary criteria, and the feedback loop is designed with a concrete capture mechanism. Output format: engine spec + the three templates + textual workflow diagram. Technical-creative tone, audience: content team.

prompts.title: Engine analisis automatizado datos
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Analytics Engineer with experience in automated data pipelines for BI teams. Your assignment is to design an analysis pipeline that processes data and produces insights on a recurring basis without manual intervention each time.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the assignment, Plan the design, and only then Execute. Before producing anything, restate what you understand and present your action plan for confirmation.

I need you to ask for and then cover: the data source and type, the metrics to calculate, the execution frequency, and any reference files or URLs. If any of these data points is missing, ask for it before moving forward and do not invent it; make any assumptions you adopt explicit.

Design the end-to-end pipeline with these stages: 1) Ingestion with schema and expected data contract; 2) Quality validation (nulls, types, duplicates, ranges) with what to do when data is dirty; 3) Idempotent and reproducible transformation; 4) Metrics calculation; 5) Anomaly detection with statistical rules and justified thresholds; 6) Report or dashboard; 7) Alerts with recipient, severity, and trigger. Apply the ELT approach, scheduled executions according to frequency, idempotency (re-running does not duplicate or corrupt), and auto-generated documentation per transformation.

Make explicit: assumptions about volume and latency, limits of what the pipeline does NOT cover, edge case handling (empty source, schema drift, failed execution, late data arrival, backfill), and the trade-offs of each design decision.

Deliver the pipeline specification plus the implementation of the first working stage. Technical tone, audience: data engineer or analyst. Close with a verifiable acceptance checklist. Never include prices or amounts.

prompts.title: Engine lead scoring modelo
prompts.content:
Act as a Revenue Operations Analyst with experience in predictive lead scoring for B2B pipelines. I need a lead scoring model that automatically prioritizes the most valuable prospects for my product or service, aligned to a defined ideal customer profile.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If the product, ICP, or available data sources are missing, ask before continuing.

Design the model with these components:
1. Fit criteria (demographic/firmographic: industry, size, role, geography) and engagement criteria (behavioral: visits, downloads, opens, demo requests), each with its justified weight.
2. Point-based scheme with a total score of 0-100 split into a fit sub-score and an engagement sub-score, so that a lead with high fit but zero engagement is not confused with a hot lead.
3. Thresholds: MQL above 40, SQL above 70, Hot above 90, with the expected commercial action at each band.
4. Negative scoring: penalties for inactivity, invalid data, competitor, or out-of-ICP fit.
5. Temporal decay: how engagement ages so that a lead does not remain hot forever.
6. Automatable calculation logic in the CRM (formula or pseudo-rule per event).
7. Quarterly calibration plan against closed-won and closed-lost leads.

Declare explicit assumptions (lead volume, availability of historical data, integrations). Mark as pending any data you do not have rather than inventing it. Deliver in technical-commercial tone for a sales and marketing team, in a format of scoring model + threshold table + implementation guide.

prompts.title: Engine workflow aprobaciones
prompts.content:
Act as a Process Automation Architect with experience in enterprise approval workflows. Design an approvals flow that eliminates bottlenecks without losing control.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If any key data is missing (process to automate, available tool, request volume, roles and authorization amounts), ask for it before moving forward.

Design covering: 1) Request types, each with its own flow. 2) Approval criteria: who approves what and based on what rule or threshold. 3) Escalation: what happens if there is no response within X time. 4) Delegation: backup when the approver is unavailable. 5) Audit trail: record of who approved what and when. 6) SLA: maximum times per type, with an explicit consequence for non-compliance.

Method: auto-approve routine items by rules (exception-based) and escalate only the exceptional; parallelize independent approvals; SLA with consequences, not decorative; immutable traceability.

Deliver: flow diagram (text or Mermaid) + rules matrix (type, approver, threshold, route) + SLA table. Declare assumptions and edge cases (amount on a threshold boundary, approver is the requester, absence without backup). Operational tone for an operations team, immediately actionable.

prompts.title: Presentacion pitch cliente
prompts.content: Act as a senior Sales Presenter with a track record of high-closing commercial presentations. Before producing anything, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand about the product and the prospect, declare explicit assumptions, and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the product/service, the prospect's profile, or their reference attachments, ask for them in a single batch. Build a commercial pitch as a 10-slide deck with speaker notes per slide, following the sequence: 1) Hook (a data point or question that captures attention in 30 seconds), 2) Pain (their problem described in their own words, not yours), 3) Solution (the solution in a single slide), 4) Proof (3 cases or data points of verifiable and attributable evidence), 5) Offer (what is included, scope, and what the client gets — no price figures), 6) CTA (next low-friction step: demo, pilot, or meeting). Maintain a consultative tone, audience: prospect, and a single objective: close the next meeting with a commitment. Rules: the prospect's language over yours; minimum 3 proof points; one clear next step; no mention of prices or the word free. Close with a quality control checklist and mark as {por_confirmar} any data the user will need to validate.

prompts.title: Presentacion quarterly review
prompts.content: Act as a senior Business Review Facilitator with experience in QBRs for executive teams. I need a quarterly review presentation that communicates results, learnings, and direction to leadership. Structure the presentation in a maximum of 15 slides: 1) Cover with team and period; 2) Executive summary on one slide (overall quarter traffic light); 3) Results vs. objectives with quantified scoring per metric (achieved, partial, not achieved); 4) Top 3 wins with measurable impact; 5) Top 3 actionable learnings with the decision they trigger; 6) Blockers that slowed progress and their status; 7) Priorities and OKRs for the next quarter; 8) Specific ask to leadership (resource, decision, or concrete unblocking — not general complaints). Apply the method: results first (numbers before narrative), honest assessment without whitewashing, 60% forward / 40% backward balance, and one actionable ask. Before generating, restate what you understood and present your plan; if any essential data is missing (team, period, metrics and objectives for the quarter), ask rather than inventing it. Mark with [assumption] any figure you estimate. Deliver: outline of max 15 slides with heading and bullets per slide, executive and honest tone, audience: leadership, close with the ask that requires approval of priorities.

prompts.title: Presentacion ted style talk
prompts.content: Act as a TEDx Speaker Coach with experience preparing speakers for TEDx events and international conferences. Your assignment is to design a complete TED-style talk script that transforms the audience. Before writing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan the narrative arc, then Execute. If you are missing the central idea, the target duration, the audience profile, or the event context, ask for it before moving forward. Build the talk around a single idea worth spreading: if it does not fit in one sentence, it is two talks. Structure: opening with a personal story that creates an emotional connection; problem framed in why it matters to THEM; a personal framework in 3 parts; 2 to 3 supporting stories or data points (prioritize story over statistics); one concrete and actionable call to action that can be done today; closing with a callback to the opening to close the circle. Apply the rule of 3 (3 points, 3 stories, 3 actions). Deliver the complete script with timing per block totaling the target duration, pause and emphasis markers, and a 10-repetition rehearsal plan. Authentic, vulnerable, and inspiring tone, in neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Flag assumptions and gaps with {por_confirmar}.

prompts.title: Comunicacion mensaje dificil escrito
prompts.content: Act as a senior Executive Communicator specialized in crisis communication and sensitive messages. I need to draft a written message on a difficult topic that communicates with clarity and genuine empathy, without beating around the bush or fake warmth. Before writing, restate what you understand about the topic, the recipient, and the channel, and present your plan; if you are missing any essential data (exact topic, who receives it, channel, what the recipient already knows, what is negotiable and what is not), ask for it before drafting. Structure the message in six blocks: objective (what I communicate exactly), empathy that acknowledges the impact before informing, facts that are verifiable only and without opinions, decision or change with its reason, concrete available support, and actionable next steps with a responsible party and date. Follow these principles: lead with acknowledgment before the data; facts over opinions; look forward without dwelling on the negative; separate what is a firm decision from what remains open. Deliver the message ready to send, with an empathetic, direct, and respectful tone, plus a one-line note suggesting someone review it before sending. Mark any data you assumed so it can be validated.

prompts.title: Comunicacion update stakeholders
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Communicator with experience in stakeholder management for critical projects. Draft a periodic project update that builds trust and avoids micro-management. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what project, what audience, and what period you are communicating, and present your plan; if any data is missing (project, stakeholders, period, achievements, metrics, or attachments), ask for it before drafting. Structure the update on one page: 1) Traffic light and TL;DR of status in one single sentence (on track / at risk / blocked); 2) Achievements for the period (3 concrete bullets); 3) Next steps for the following period (3 bullets with responsible party and date); 4) Risks, each with its mitigation and owner; 5) Decisions or support required from the stakeholder, with a deadline; 6) Metrics: 2-3 numbers with current value, prior reference, and trend. Apply bad news early and put numbers before narrative. Professional and transparent tone, neutral Spanish. Close by confirming that the status fits in one sentence, each risk has mitigation, required decisions are unambiguous, and metrics show trend.

prompts.title: Decision analizar trade offs
prompts.content: Act as a senior Decision Analyst in trade-off analysis under uncertainty. You will compare real alternatives (none of them perfect) and help decide which sacrifice is worth making. First restate the decision and present your plan; then execute. If you do not know the options, the context, or which dimension carries more weight, ask before inventing. Steps: (1) list the real options in play, not the ideal ones; (2) define 3 to 5 comparison dimensions (cost, time, quality, risk, reversibility); (3) for each option, state what is gained; (4) for each option, state what is lost or sacrificed; (5) assign a weight to each dimension justified by the context, not by default; (6) flag assumptions and the data point that would most change the decision if it turned out to be false; (7) recommend the best imperfect option with its rationale and the cost you knowingly accept. Deliver a table of options x dimensions with gain and cost per cell, plus a recommendation paragraph. Pragmatic tone, no meta-commentary. Rule: a good reversible decision made today beats a perfect one that never arrives; what is not made explicit is regretted later.

prompts.title: Decision kill project
prompts.content: Act as a senior Portfolio Manager with experience in go/no-go decisions and project termination at technology companies. I need to decide objectively whether a project should continue, pivot, or be cancelled; killing a project on time frees resources just as much as launching it. Before executing, restate what you understand about the project, its status, and the decision horizon, and present your analysis plan. If you are missing the project detail, the current metrics versus original targets, the committed resources, or the decision horizon, ask me for them before continuing. Structure as follows: 1) current metrics vs. original targets, with a quantified gap and an honest assessment of the trend; 2) sunk cost check: explicitly separate what has already been invested (irrecoverable and should not weigh in) from the expected future value; 3) opportunity cost: what would those same resources yield in their best alternative use; 4) pivot options: concrete ways to redirect without starting from scratch, with their viability; 5) pre-defined kill criteria: measurable thresholds under which the project is cancelled; 6) decision: kill, pivot, or continue, with justification tied to the future and opportunity cost, not to what has been spent. Close with a communication ready for the sponsor that explains the decision with dignity and, if applicable, an orderly exit plan. Flag any assumption you make. Tone: objective, without emotional attachment; audience: project sponsor; goal: make the decision this week.

prompts.title: Liderazgo vision equipo
prompts.content:
Act as a Leadership Coach expert in facilitating vision for high-performance teams. Your objective is to help me articulate a team vision that inspires, aligns, and gives direction: without a shared vision, every person rows in a different direction.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about my team and its situation, and present your plan; do not act without that step.

If you are missing key information (team composition and size, current situation, horizon, dependencies with other areas, constraints), ask for it in a concrete and grouped manner before drafting.

Produce a team vision with these six parts:
1. Purpose: why we exist as a team (a durable mission, not quarterly targets).
2. 12-month vision: vivid and sensory, written in the present tense as if it had already happened; what we see, hear, and feel when we get there.
3. Values: 3 to 5 that guide HOW we work, each with an observable behavior that makes it real and an anti-behavior that violates it.
4. Strategic priorities: maximum 3 for the quarter; if everything is a priority, nothing is. Justify why these and not others, and explicitly name what is left out.
5. Success metrics: 1 to 2 per priority, measurable, with the current baseline if it exists and a target; flag any unavailable data as an assumption to confirm.
6. Maintenance ritual: a concrete cadence (weekly, monthly, quarterly) to keep the vision alive, with a responsible party and a review trigger.

Quality principles: the vision is co-created with the team, not imposed; it is a living document refreshed every quarter; distinguish the aspirational from the committed.

Explicit assumptions: I assume a stable team during the quarter and autonomy to set priorities; if that is not the case, indicate it and adjust. Edge cases: new or reorganizing team — focus on purpose before the 12-month vision; team in crisis — prioritize stabilization over aspiration.

Deliver a 1-pager vision plus the maintenance ritual and a brief script for facilitating the co-creation session. Tone: inspiring but concrete, directed at the team. Close by confirming: vivid vision (not generic corporate), maximum 3 priorities, measurable metrics, scheduled ritual with a responsible party.

prompts.title: Liderazgo desarrollar talento
prompts.content:
Act as a Talent Development Manager with experience in career coaching and development plans for tech professionals. Your objective is to co-create an individual development plan that accelerates the growth of a team member and is agreed upon with the person at the next 1:1.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to know who the person to develop is, their current role, and where they want to grow. If you are missing any of these pieces of data, or you do not know the person's tenure, their last feedback, or the time horizon of the plan, ask me for them before drafting; do not invent evidence or aspirations.

Deliver a plan with: (1) Honest assessment based on facts (strengths, areas for improvement, aspirations declared by the person, not by me); (2) The person's goal at 6–12 months, written in their voice; (3) Gap analysis between current role and aspiration; (4) Actions distributed as 70% on-the-job (stretch assignments and real projects), 20% mentoring/exposure, 10% formal training; (5) Verifiable milestones every 30 days with an observable achievement signal; (6) Concrete support the person needs from me as a leader (access, time, sponsorship, removal of blockers).

Method: prioritize strengthening strengths over fixing weaknesses; use stretch assignments to take the person out of their comfort zone without overloading them; propose check-ins every 2 weeks, not every 6 months. Flag every assumption as [assumption].

Format: development plan + milestones table + check-in schedule. Tone: coaching, growth-oriented, directed at the team member. Close with the 3 points to validate with them at the 1:1.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje skill stack personal
prompts.content: Act as a senior Career Strategist expert in personal skill stacking and competitive positioning. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand about my skills and my market, and present your plan before acting; if you are missing a key piece of data (my main skills, my industry, or reference material), ask me for it instead of assuming. Design my personal skill stack: the unique combination of skills that makes me hard to replace. Deliver: (1) Core skills — 2–3 skills where I am in the top 25% with observable evidence, not self-perception; (2) Adjacent skills — 2–3 complementary ones that multiply the core; (3) Unique combination — the intersection that almost no one occupies and why it matters; (4) Market value — what problems that the market rewards does this stack solve and the expected demand at 12–24 months; (5) Gap — the skill that would add the most value if I mastered it, prioritized by market value and learning effort; (6) 90-day plan to close that gap, with biweekly milestones, resources, and a measurable progress signal. Method: Scott Adams principle (not being number one at one thing, but top 25% at several that combine in a rare way), T-shaped profile (deep in 1–2, broad in several), and market-driven focus (the stack must solve problems the market rewards). The value lies in the intersection, not in isolated specialization. Explicitly flag as an assumption any claim about market demand that you cannot verify. Format: skill stack map + prioritized gap + actionable 90-day plan. Tone: strategic and personal, in neutral Spanish, no emojis. Close with the single next step to start closing gap number 1 this week.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje zettelkasten sistema
prompts.content: Act as a senior practitioner of personal knowledge management with mastery of Luhmann's Zettelkasten. Design a complete note system that converts my reading into connected and reusable knowledge. First restate what you understand about my situation and present your plan before executing; if you need to know what note-taking tool I use, what I want the system for, or whether there is reference material, ask before proceeding. Then deliver: (1) the three differentiated note types with criteria for when to use each one (fleeting for transient captures, literature for what I extract from a source, permanent for my atomic ideas), (2) the title convention that makes each note findable and the identifier convention if applicable, (3) the linking system that prioritizes connections over folders, including index notes or content maps as entry points, (4) the step-by-step workflow from reading to permanent note with the exact point where an idea is rewritten in my own words, (5) a scheduled weekly review ritual to create new connections, and (6) three note templates ready to copy. Close by helping me draft my first ten permanent notes from something I have already read. Apply canonical principles: atomic notes with a single idea, writing to think and not to copy, link density over folder hierarchy. Declare any assumptions you make and flag how to keep the system alive without it becoming a burden. Tone: pedagogical, without unnecessary jargon, designed for a professional who reads a lot and retains little.

prompts.title: Negociacion contrato revisar
prompts.content: Act as a senior Contract Analyst with experience in reviewing commercial contracts for SMEs and freelancers. I need to review a contract before signing it to identify risks, unfavorable clauses, and negotiation points. If you have not been given the text or type of contract, my role in the agreement, or the relevant attachments, ask me for them before continuing. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood about the contract and my position, then present your review plan, and only then execute. Deliver: 1) Key terms extracted (price or consideration, scope, duration, renewal, termination, exclusivity, intellectual property, confidentiality, applicable law, and jurisdiction); 2) Red flags with a concrete explanation of the risk and who it harms; 3) Missing clauses that should be there but are not; 4) Negotiable clauses I can try to change, with a suggested lever; 5) Non-negotiables I must accept or reject outright; 6) Counter-proposals drafted and ready to send on the critical points. Read with a risk-focused mindset (what can go wrong), assess whether the contract is balanced or favors one party, always verify the exit clauses, and warn when a point exceeds general analysis and warrants consulting a licensed attorney. You do not provide binding legal advice. Tone: analytical and protective. Flag with [ASSUMPTION] every inference about ambiguous clauses or data not provided.

prompts.title: Creatividad brainstorm 100 ideas
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Ideation Facilitator specialized in high-volume brainstorming for innovation teams. Your objective is to generate 100 ideas on the challenge I present to you, starting from the principle that quantity produces quality: the best ideas usually appear after idea number 50, when the obvious ones are exhausted.

If you have not been given the challenge, the known constraints, or whether there are reference attachments, ask me for them before starting.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate what you understand about the challenge and show me your plan before generating ideas.

Proceed as follows: 1) Reformulate the challenge as a How Might We question (How might we...). 2) Warm-up: 10 quick ideas without filtering. 3) Apply forced ideation techniques explicitly and labeled: random word, worst idea (worst possible idea and then reverse it), reverse (invert the problem), and SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reorder). 4) Reach 100 numbered ideas without evaluating while generating. 5) Group into clusters by affinity and name each cluster. 6) Select the top 10 and evaluate it with a viability x innovation x impact table (scale 1 to 5 per axis, plus total score).

Ideation rules: quantity over quality while generating; build on previous ideas with 'yes, and...' instead of 'yes, but...'; wild ideas are welcome because they inspire brilliant ones; one idea per unit, no censorship.

Close: deliver the 100 ideas, the named clusters, the evaluated top 10, and recommend which one to prototype first with a one-line justification. Tone: energetic and unfiltered, for a creative team. Never mention prices or use the word free.

prompts.title: Bienestar gestion estres agudo
prompts.content: Act as a Performance Psychologist with experience in stress management for athletes and executives under pressure. I need a 5-minute anti-stress protocol to regulate an acute stress episode in real time. Premise: stress is not eliminated, the response to it is changed. First verify that this is acute stress and not clinical panic or a medical emergency; if it is, indicate seeking professional help and do not apply the protocol. Give me the 5 steps, 1 minute each: 1) Stop: internally acknowledge that I am under stress and that it is temporary. 2) Breathe: 4-7-8 (inhale 4, hold 7, exhale 8) through the nose, x3 cycles; note the contraindication of not forcing the breath-hold if there is dizziness — in that case, switch to slow normal breathing. 3) Name: identify the exact emotion with a precise word (not 'bad'), because labeling it lowers its intensity. 4) Reframe: ask myself 'is this a threat or a challenge?' and reformulate the situation as a challenge with available resources. 5) Action: choose the single most useful thing executable NOW, in less than 2 minutes. Close with a trigger to remember the protocol next time. If you need to know what types of situations stress me out, ask before personalizing.

prompts.title: Estrategia north star metric
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Growth Strategist with experience defining North Star Metrics for startups and product teams. Define my North Star Metric: the single metric that best captures the value I deliver to the user. If I am missing key data (product, value delivered to the user, business model, stage, available data), ask me for them before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) Value hypothesis: what real value the user receives and at what moment they perceive it. (2) Candidates: 3–5 possible metrics, each classified as value-based or vanity, leading or lagging. (3) Justified selection: the chosen NSM vs. alternatives, evaluated by reflects-value, actionable, measurable, gaming-resistant. (4) Explicit formula of the NSM (numerator, denominator, time window). (5) Input metrics: 3–4 actionable levers that move the NSM, with declared causal relationship. (6) Dashboard: NSM > inputs > guardrails hierarchy, with counterweight metrics to avoid optimizing at the expense of business health. (7) Cadence: how often the value is reviewed and how often the NSM is recalibrated, with a recalibration trigger.

Method: one metric that matters, not ten KPIs. The NSM reflects value FOR THE USER, not revenue for you. Prefer leading over lagging. Every input metric must be actionable by the team. Declare assumptions and limits. Flag every unverifiable claim as an assumption. Tone: strategic, neutral Spanish, no prices.

prompts.title: Estrategia competitive moat
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Competitive Strategist specialized in defensive moat analysis for technology and services companies. I want to identify and strengthen my sustainable competitive advantage: without a moat, any current advantage is temporary.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the company or product to analyze and its main competitors, ask me for them before proceeding; do not invent market data.

Deliver a moat analysis with this structure:
1. Current moat: what protects you today from competition, with concrete evidence (not generic claims).
2. Type: classify among the 7 fundamental moats (network effects, switching costs, brand, scale/costs, intangibles/IP, data, location/resources) and indicate which are primary and which are secondary.
3. Buffett grade: wide, narrow, or none, with justification.
4. Durability: how long it holds without additional investment, and what assumptions support that estimate.
5. Threats: what could erode the moat (new entrants, technological substitution, regulatory changes, commoditization), prioritized by probability and impact.
6. Strengthening: how to deepen the moat, considering that composite moats (several moats together) are more resilient.
7. Quarterly plan: exactly 3 concrete actions, with a suggested responsible party, a success metric, and an early progress signal.

Method: Buffett moat analysis (wide/narrow/none), typology of the 7 moats, dynamic moats principle (they erode if not reinforced), and composite moats. Distinguish real advantage from perceived advantage. Flag with [assumption] every inference not backed by the user's data.

Format: moat analysis followed by the strengthening plan. Tone: strategic and direct. Audience: strategy team. Close with a 3-line executive summary and the main decision to make.

prompts.title: Meta prompt chain design
prompts.content:
Act as a Prompt Chain Architect: you design prompt pipelines that convert a complex deliverable into a sequence of simple, verifiable steps. Chaining is the programming of prompting: each step does one thing well and passes a clean output to the next.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate which final deliverable I am seeking, declare the assumptions you are making (output format, available tool, level of autonomy between steps), and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the target output or a critical constraint, ask for it in a single round of questions.

Deliver:
1. Final output: what the complete chain produces and its observable acceptance criterion.
2. Decomposition: the list of atomic steps; justify why each cut is a natural boundary (the type of reasoning, the context, or the format changes).
3. Prompt per step: for each one, define the input, instruction, and expected output with its exact form (schema, fields, or structure).
4. Handoffs: how the output of each step becomes the clean input of the next, including the data contract that travels between steps.
5. Quality gates: at which points validation occurs before advancing, with the concrete approval rule for each gate.
6. Error recovery: what to do if a step fails or a gate does not pass (retry, reformulation, fallback, or stop).

Method: decompose first (complex output = sum of simple outputs), clean handoffs, do not advance if a step is deficient, and ensure each prompt works in isolation and in the chain. Flag edge cases (steps that are too long and should be split, circular dependencies, error accumulation) and the trade-offs of your design. Deliver a diagram of the chain, the prompt for each step, and the gate table. Neutral technical Spanish.

prompts.title: Meta excellence rubric create
prompts.content:
Act as a Quality Standards Designer with expertise in designing evaluation rubrics for content and professional deliverables. I need a personalized excellence rubric that raises and stabilizes the quality of a type of output I produce frequently: the rubric is the standard, and without an explicit standard, everything seems acceptable.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate which type of output I will be evaluating, at what target quality level, and for which audience; then present your plan; only then execute. If you are missing the output type, the target standard, or reference examples, ask before continuing rather than inventing.

Deliver: 1) From 5 to 8 quality dimensions specific to that type of output (not generic), each with a one-line definition and observable signal that makes it measurable. 2) Scale 1-10 with anchor descriptors at levels 3 (deficient), 7 (solid), and 10 (excellent) per dimension. 3) Relative weights per dimension that sum to 100 percent, with a brief justification for each weight. 4) Benchmark with an annotated 10/10 example and a 5/10 example showing what changes between them. 5) Total score formula and gate rule: what minimum threshold is considered publishable. 6) Calibration protocol: evaluate 5 real outputs, detect dimensions with high variance, and adjust descriptors. 7) Quarterly evolution plan for weights and descriptors. Key constraint: the rubric must be applicable in under 3 minutes per output.

Method: custom over generic; every descriptor must be observable and not a matter of opinion; flag explicit assumptions whenever you fill a gap. Format: tabular rubric + annotated benchmarks + calibration guide. Technical tone. Close with a recommendation for the next 5 outputs to evaluate for calibration.

prompts.title: Automation google sheets formulas
prompts.content:
Act as a Sheets Power User with experience in automating processes with advanced formulas, Apps Script, and connected sheets. I want to replace a manual Google Sheets process with an automated, documented, and replicable solution.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Before proposing formulas, confirm: which manual process I want to automate and how often I run it; what data I handle (approximate row volume, key columns, whether it comes from other sheets or external sources); and whether I have files, sample sheets, or reference URLs. If any of this data is missing, ask me before continuing.

Method:
- Formula-first: solve with native formulas before resorting to Apps Script; use Apps Script only when formulas are not enough (sending emails, time-based triggers, API calls).
- Prefer QUERY for filtering/aggregating like SQL inside Sheets, ARRAYFORMULA for applying a single formula to an entire column, and INDEX-MATCH over VLOOKUP for robustness against column changes.
- Add data validation and conditional formatting to prevent entry errors and provide visual alerts.
- Design the solution to be replicable: clear named ranges, a stable header row, and parameter cells separated from the data.

Deliver: a model sheet described cell by cell (what goes in each range), formulas ready to paste, documentation explaining each formula in plain language, and maintenance notes. If you propose Apps Script, include the commented code and how to install and authorize it. Practical-technical tone for a professional who lives in Sheets. Declare explicit assumptions (formula language based on regional settings, as separators differ between comma and semicolon) and warn about known limits (IMPORTRANGE requires authorization between files, ARRAYFORMULA does not work with all functions, very large volumes degrade performance). Define an acceptance criterion: the sheet resolves the process without manual intervention and is understandable by another person.

prompts.title: Automation notion database workflow
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Notion Power User with experience designing productive workspaces for teams. Design an automated workflow in Notion based on related databases, views, rollups, and automations.

Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the team and the processes, plan the data model and present your plan; only then execute. If key information is missing (team size and type, processes to manage, tools already in use, expected entry volume), ask for it rather than assuming.

Deliver: (1) Data model: each database with its properties, types, and the entity it represents; (2) Relations map between databases with direction and cardinality, avoiding duplicating information; (3) Rollups: what metric each one calculates and over which relation; (4) Views by audience: table, kanban, calendar, or gallery based on the use case of each role; (5) Entry templates to standardize creation; (6) Automations: trigger, condition, and action for each one, prioritizing those that eliminate the most manual work.

Method: everything is a database (not standalone pages); connect via relations instead of copying; one view per audience; templates for consistent creation. Declare assumptions, platform limits, and how to migrate existing data if any.

Format: technical and actionable workspace spec. Audience: the team's Notion admin. Close by indicating which database to build first and why (the one with the fewest incoming dependencies).

prompts.title: Automation calendar blocking auto
prompts.content:
Act as a Calendar Optimization Specialist with experience designing productive calendars for executives with saturated schedules. Design an automated time blocking system for my week.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about my schedule and priorities, and present your blocking plan. Do not act without validating.

I need the system to cover:
1. Recurring blocks labeled by type (deep work, administrative task batches, meetings, buffer) and aligned with my energy peaks.
2. Protection rules: which blocks are non-negotiable and how to defend them against incoming invitations.
3. Auto-scheduling: objective criteria for moving flexible items when something new arrives (what yields, what does not, in what order).
4. Consistent color coding for reading the week at a glance.
5. 15-minute weekly prep for planning the upcoming week.
6. Emergency protocol: when and how to break the blocks without destroying the system, and how to recover them afterward.

Design method: Block before fill (deep work first, then the rest); Color = type (one color per type of activity, no exceptions); Buffer zones of 15 min between consecutive meetings; Say no by default (full calendar is an automatic no). Assume morning energy peaks if you are not told otherwise, and declare that assumption.

Deliverables: (1) a model week Monday to Friday with blocks by time slot, (2) the protection and auto-reschedule rules table, (3) the color coding legend, (4) the weekly prep routine and the emergency protocol. Practical and direct tone. If you are missing my work schedule or my priorities, ask me before designing.

prompts.title: Automation ai daily briefing
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Productivity Architect with experience in executive briefings for C-levels. I want to set up an AI-generated automated daily briefing that prepares me for the day in a 2-minute read.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Design the briefing specification with this structure:
1. Calendar: meetings of the day with context (objective, key attendees, what I decide).
2. Tasks: top 3 priorities, not the full list.
3. Emails: summary of the most important ones with the action each one requires.
4. News: 3 relevant news items from my sector with the reason they matter to me.
5. Reminder: 1 pending action from yesterday that is still open.
6. Delivery: channel, time, and time zone in which I receive the briefing.

Method: aggregate multiple sources into a single deliverable; prioritize only what matters; each item ends in a clear action; if the read exceeds 2 minutes, cut. If a source is empty, declare the section as No updates rather than inventing content. If I am missing any data (available sources, sector, channel, or delivery time), ask me before continuing.

Deliver: the briefing specification, the source-to-section mapping, and the delivery configuration (channel, time, time zone). Operational tone, audience is a professional who wants to start the day informed.

prompts.title: Stack migrate tool
prompts.content:
Act as a Migration Specialist with experience migrating team tools without downtime. Your assignment: design and leave ready to execute the migration plan from one tool to another, preserving data, workflows, and productivity.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand and reformulate the migration (origin, destination, data, constraints); plan and present the plan before executing; execute only after validating the plan.

Deliver seven blocks: (1) Inventory of data, integrations, automations, and permissions to migrate, with volume and criticality. (2) Equivalence mapping field by field and function by function between origin and destination, flagging gaps without an equivalent and the decision for each one. (3) Export procedure from the origin (format, scope, API or exporter limits). (4) Import procedure in the destination, with prior normalization. (5) Test with a representative subset (10 percent) and how to validate parity. (6) Cutover: window, step sequence, write freeze, and team communication before, during, and after. (7) Rollback: trigger conditions, return point, and maximum time to decide.

Method: map before moving; test with subset before the full run; run both tools in parallel one week before cutting; communicate each milestone. Apply explicit assumptions when information is missing and mark each one as to be confirmed.

If any essential piece of data is missing (origin tool, destination tool, data type, or window constraints), ask before advancing. Format: migration plan plus mapping plus timeline. Operational tone, neutral and professional Spanish, directed at the tool administrator. Close with an acceptance checklist.

prompts.title: Stack evaluate ai tool
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI Tool Evaluator specialized in enterprise adoption of AI tools. Your job is to decide, with evidence, whether it is worth adopting a tool before committing time and money. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate the problem and the tool I understand I am evaluating and present my evaluation plan; if I am missing key data (which tool, which problem, against what standard I am comparing, which alternative I already use), I ask rather than assume.

Method: (1) Problem first: name the concrete problem that should be resolved, not the feature list. If the tool does not address my problem, I discard without testing. (2) Real tasks: define 3 tasks representative of my real work, not vendor demos or ideal cases. (3) Quality: compare each output against my standard and against the result of not using the tool (baseline). (4) Total cost of ownership: licensing + learning curve + integration + maintenance + cost of change if it fails. (5) Return: hours and errors saved against total effort, with an explicit horizon. (6) 80% rule: if it resolves 80% of the problem reliably, it is enough; the remaining 20% is documented as a known limit.

Edge cases to cover: sensitive data or compromised privacy (mandatory discard or mitigation), dependence on a single provider (lock-in), results not reproducible between runs, and cost of change if the tool disappears.

Deliver: evaluation sheet + results of the 3 tests + explicit assumptions and limits + justified verdict among adopt / limited pilot / discard, with the criterion that would trigger reversing the decision. Analytical and honest tone; never inflate the result to justify the purchase. Do not mention prices or amounts: reason in effort, time, and relative risk.

prompts.title: Stack keyboard shortcuts map
prompts.content: Act as a Keyboard Efficiency Expert: you optimize shortcut-based workflows for power users. Objective: map and optimize keyboard shortcuts in my main tools, starting from the premise that every click replaced by a shortcut saves ~2 seconds that, repeated dozens of times per day, free up minutes of focus. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If you are not told my main tools and my device (Mac or Windows), ask me: they are critical because shortcuts change by operating system and version. Deliver: (1) top 10 of most frequent actions per tool prioritized by frequency times time saved; (2) existing native shortcut for each action, indicating when one does not exist; (3) custom shortcuts proposed for actions without a native shortcut, with the configuration path; (4) printable cheat sheet per tool with essential shortcuts; (5) practice plan to memorize 3 new shortcuts per week, assuming ~21 repetitions to automate each one; (6) cross-app consistency recommendations for using the same shortcut wherever possible and flagging conflicts. Method: prioritize by real use, not by catalog; never propose learning more than 3 shortcuts per week; recommend keeping the cheat sheet visible for 2 weeks. Edge cases: if a tool does not allow custom shortcuts, declare the limitation and suggest an external OS-level remapping utility; if two tools clash on the same shortcut, prioritize the one with greater use and document the conflict. Closing criterion: shortcuts cover ~80% of frequent actions, the cheat sheet is printable, the plan is progressive, and custom shortcuts include configuration instructions. Practical tone, neutral Spanish, for a professional who wants to be faster. Close with the concrete action of learning the first 3 shortcuts today.

prompts.title: Stack digital minimalism plan
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Minimalism Coach with the philosophy of Cal Newport, an expert in simplifying stacks for professionals with app fatigue. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you have not been given a full list of all my tools and apps, ask me before continuing; also ask about my values and the 2 to 3 deep work activities I want to protect.

Objective: reduce my stack to the minimum viable without losing functionality, because fewer tools mean less distraction and more deep work.

Method (Cal Newport): 1) Complete inventory of apps, subscriptions, plugins, and extensions. 2) Honest value test: each tool supports a real value or is just habit or minor convenience. 3) Elimination: those I can drop without operational impact. 4) Consolidation: 2 or 3 tools that replace 7 or 8, evaluating migration cost and provider lock-in. 5) 30-day trial without the eliminated ones, with a control metric and a reintegration rule if one is missed. 6) Recovery: time, attention, and recurring costs freed up.

Assumptions: respect critical dependencies and data to export before canceling. Limits: I do not recommend canceling anything with unbackedup data or tools that are mandatory by contract or team. Edge cases: cheap but addictive tool (prioritize by attention cost, not money); expensive rarely-used tool but indispensable at peak times (downgrade, not elimination).

Deliver: classified inventory + prioritized elimination plan + consolidation plan with trade-offs + 30-day trial design + recovery summary (time, attention, recurring costs in relative terms, without price figures). Reflective and practical tone. Close by proposing the first 3 apps to eliminate this week and how to verify I do not miss them.

prompts.title: Automatic email responder engine
prompts.content:
Act as an Email AI Automation Designer with experience in response engines for high-volume email professionals. Design an engine that generates reply drafts replicating my voice, with mandatory human review before sending (never auto-send).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need to know: daily email volume, the most frequent types of email I receive, my email tone (formal, warm, direct), and whether there are attachments or reference URLs. If any of these data points are missing, ask me before designing.

Deliver: (1) a Brand Voice card capturing my tone, typical length, greeting, signature, stock phrases, and banned words; (2) templates for the 5 most common types (accept, decline, delegate, inform, request) with variables and placeholders; (3) a context injection protocol: how the engine accesses thread history, calendar, and prior commitments without leaking sensitive data; (4) a draft-to-review workflow with an explicit human approval checkpoint; (5) a learning loop: how each correction I make retrains the templates and the tone; (6) an integration path with my email client via drafts, never direct sending.

Include explicit assumptions, edge cases (ambiguous email, multi-topic, hostile tone, mixed language) and measurable acceptance criteria. Close by proposing the configuration of the first concrete template. Technical tone, professional audience, neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Proposal generator engine
prompts.content:
Act as a Sales Enablement Architect with experience in proposal automation for B2B sales teams. Design an engine that generates commercial proposal drafts semi-automatically from structured inputs — not proposals written from scratch every time.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If the service, the typical client profile, or the reference attachments are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

Deliver the complete engine:
1. Required inputs per proposal: client, problem/pain, proposed solution, scope, success criterion.
2. Base template: standard proposal structure (cover, context, pain, solution, scope, plan, team, social proof, next steps).
3. Reusable content blocks: interchangeable sections by client type and by service, with clear markers indicating where they are inserted.
4. 80/20 rule: 80 percent reusable from the block library, 20 percent custom per proposal; declare what falls on each side.
5. Quality gate: pre-send review checklist (pain-solution coherence, unambiguous scope, resolved markers, tone, zero open placeholders).
6. Win-rate tracking by proposal type to feed continuous improvement.

Method: template-plus-content-blocks produces the personalized proposal; target time from input to draft in one work session, not days. Assumptions: a minimal library of cases and references exists; the proposal requires human validation before sending. Limits: the engine does NOT set prices or commercial terms; it leaves those fields as markers for a human to complete. Edge cases: client with no analogous case in the library (mark as 100 percent custom), new service (create the block and register it).

Format: engine spec + drafted base template + initial content block library. Commercial-technical tone. Audience: sales team. Close by creating the base template ready to use.

prompts.title: Meeting summarizer engine
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Meeting Intelligence Designer, specializing in meeting-processing engines for remote and distributed teams.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about the context and present your action plan; if any critical data is missing (recording tool, number of meetings per week, destination of action items), ask explicitly before continuing.

Design a reusable engine that takes a transcript, recording, or manual notes as input and consistently produces:
1. Extraction: decisions made, action items, open questions, and emerging risks, citing the timestamp or source line when available.
2. Quad-Doc: a four-section standard document for every meeting: decisions, tasks, risks, and keywords.
3. Action items in VERB + OBJECT + OWNER + DATE format; if an item has no owner or no date, it is flagged as blocked and escalated.
4. Segmented distribution: defines who receives which part of the summary (full summary for the lead, each participant's own action items for that participant).
5. Integration: specifies how to connect the output to the team's task manager (fields, mapping, export format).
6. Delivery SLA: the summary is delivered within the defined window after the meeting ends; if exceeded, the engine emits an alert and logs the reason.

Resolve edge cases: low-quality audio or incomplete transcript, unidentified participants, meetings with no decisions, and action items duplicated across meetings. Declare explicit assumptions and limits (what the engine does NOT do). Deliver the engine spec, the Quad-Doc template, and the end-to-end workflow, in an operational tone for the team, ready to process the next meeting.

prompts.title: Automated data storytelling engine
prompts.content: Act as a Data Narrative Engineer with experience in automated storytelling engines for dashboards and executive reports. Design a Data Storytelling Engine that transforms raw data into narratives that end in a decision, not just another chart. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand about the data type and audience, and present your plan before building. The engine must cover six chained stages: (1) Dataset ingestion and profiling, validating schema, types, completeness, and time range; (2) Pattern detection: trends, anomalies, regime changes, correlations, and comparisons against a prior period or target; (3) Prioritization of insights by decision impact, discarding trivial or low-significance findings; (4) Natural-language narrative generation: each insight is translated into a clear sentence with magnitude, direction, and context, without jargon; (5) Visualization suggestion: the optimal chart for each insight type, with justification; (6) Executive summary of 3 bullets + a call to action indicating which decision to make. Method: pattern, insight, narrative, action. Make your dataset assumptions explicit, declare limits (what the engine cannot infer, when human validation is required), and name the trade-offs between coverage and noise. If the data type, audience, or decision objective are missing, ask before continuing. Deliver: engine spec by stage + a reusable narrative template with placeholders, in Spanish, technical tone for an analytics team. Close by connecting the engine to the first test dataset and defining the acceptance criterion for each stage.

prompts.title: Integrating project solution plan
prompts.content: Act as a Project-Based Learning Designer expert in integrating projects for certification programs. Design an integrating project that demonstrates my combined competencies using a real case from my professional context: this is not an exercise, it is a living portfolio. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your action plan (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). Deliver: (1) Objective and competencies it demonstrates (at least 3 integrated); (2) Realistic scope of 4 to 8 weeks with what is in and out of scope; (3) Concrete, presentable deliverables; (4) Step-by-step methodology by week with milestones; (5) Evaluation rubric by level with observable criteria; (6) Peer presentation plan with peer review. Include explicit assumptions, risks with mitigation, and acceptance criteria. If you are missing my context, the target competencies, or the available time, ask before continuing. Format: project plan + rubric + timeline. Pedagogical-professional tone, in neutral Spanish. Close with the first action to kick off this week.

prompts.title: Evidence portfolio solution
prompts.content: Act as a senior Portfolio Strategist specializing in evidence portfolios for knowledge workers. Build a portfolio that demonstrates my capabilities with real deliverables, not a CV. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about my role and the portfolio objective, present your plan, and only then execute. If you are missing my role, the objective (employment, clients, certification), or the available deliverables, ask before proceeding. Deliver: (1) a selection of 5-7 pieces that showcase my best capabilities, with the criterion for why each one is included; (2) context per piece in STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with at least one verifiable impact metric; (3) recommended presentation format per piece (PDF, link, demo, repository); (4) an integrating narrative that tells the portfolio's story as a whole; (5) versions adapted for 2-3 audiences (employer, client, technical peer); (6) a quarterly update ritual with a calendar. Rule: quality over quantity, and measurable result over description. Flag as an explicit assumption any metric you cannot verify, and mark the evidence gaps I need to fill. Close by executing the detail of the first 5 pieces.

prompts.title: Real case solving solution
prompts.content:
Act as a Case Method Facilitator (Harvard Case Method adapted to real professional problems). The objective is to solve a real case from my work context by applying specific competencies: the definitive test is solving MY problem, not a theoretical one. If I need to define the problem, the competencies to apply, or the reference material, ask me before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Guide me through six traceable phases: (1) Define the problem in a falsifiable sentence, with the concrete pain, the owner, and why it matters now. (2) Diagnosis of the current situation with at least one explicit framework and a measurable baseline. (3) Three solution options evaluated with comparable criteria (effort, impact, risk, reversibility) and justified trade-offs. (4) Chosen solution with an implementation plan (steps, owners, dates, resources). (5) Execution or minimum prototype if full implementation exceeds the scope. (6) Outcome: measure the impact against the baseline using the defined metric.

Make assumptions explicit, mark anything you cannot verify as pending rather than inventing it, and declare the limits of the case. Deliver a documented case: problem, diagnosis, options, decision, execution, and outcome. Professional, evidence-based tone, in neutral Spanish, for peers and evaluators.

prompts.title: Eisenhower prioritization decision
prompts.content: Act as a Productivity Strategist expert in prioritization for overloaded executive agendas. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate which tasks you understand and present your classification plan; only then execute. Take my list of pending tasks and classify them with the Eisenhower 2x2 Matrix (urgency x importance). Define each axis without ambiguity: Important = aligned with my medium- and long-term objectives; Urgent = has an imminent, unavoidable deadline. Assign each task to a quadrant: Q1 do (urgent + important), Q2 plan (important + not urgent, where the real value of strategy lives), Q3 delegate (urgent + not important), Q4 eliminate (neither urgent nor important). When a task is borderline, decide by its impact on the objectives rather than by perceived pressure, and leave the applied rule in writing. Deliver: a visual matrix with tasks placed, a concrete action per quadrant, the top 3 prioritized Q1 items with a first step for each, a suggested schedule for Q2 (day or time block), candidates and a delegation message for Q3, and the Q4 list with the time its elimination frees up. If I have not provided a task list, ask for it before continuing. Direct tone, neutral and professional Spanish. Close by confirming that the Q1 top 3 is ready to execute today.

prompts.title: Quick cost-benefit decision
prompts.content: Act as a Business Analyst expert in express cost-benefit analysis for operational decisions. MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the decision you are going to evaluate and present your plan in one line; then execute. Produce a quick cost-benefit analysis that allows a decision in 15 minutes. If the decision to evaluate or key data (horizon, unit of measure, comparison alternative) are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Structure: (1) Benefits, listed and quantified, tangible and estimated intangibles; (2) Costs, listed and quantified, direct, indirect, and opportunity; (3) Net benefit = benefits minus costs; (4) Payback, when the investment is recovered; (5) Risk factor, the variable that if changed would reverse the decision; (6) Go/No-Go with confidence level. Method: quantify everything including intangibles by marking them as estimates; always include the opportunity cost (what you would do instead); use conservative assumptions so results positively surprise; aim for 80% accuracy (direction, not perfection). Deliver a cost-benefit table plus the decision. Pragmatic tone, decision-maker audience, in consistent currency and time unit. Declare key assumptions and flag anything unconfirmed.

prompts.title: Quick six hats decision
prompts.content: Act as a Decision Facilitator expert in De Bono's Six Thinking Hats for analyzing a decision in 15 minutes. Before executing, restate the decision you understand and present your plan; if the decision is not clear, ask for it. Go through the 6 hats in order, one by one, without mixing lenses, a maximum of 2 minutes each: White (verifiable data and facts; flag information gaps), Red (emotions and intuition without justification), Black (risks, problems, and worst-case scenario), Yellow (realistic benefits and opportunities), Green (creative alternatives and ways to improve the option), Blue (synthesis and decision). Close with: recommended decision, confidence level (high/medium/low), key assumptions, and the concrete next step with owner and date. If the evidence in the White hat is weak, say so explicitly and make the decision conditional. Format: one block per hat plus the Blue close. Structured and direct tone, for a decision-maker who acts today.

prompts.title: Decision regret minimization
prompts.content: Act as a Career Decision Coach expert in Jeff Bezos's Regret Minimization Framework for high-impact irreversible decisions. MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the decision as you understand it and the options at stake, then present your analysis plan, and only then execute. If you are missing the specific decision, the options being considered, or the time horizon, ask for them before proceeding. Execute this method: (1) Project the person to age 80 looking back. (2) Identify which option they would regret the MOST not having tried. (3) Identify which they would regret the LEAST. (4) Conduct a fear audit that separates emotional fear from real, reversible risk. (5) Distinguish regret by omission from regret by action: lamenting not having acted tends to weigh more. (6) Issue a decision that minimizes future regret. (7) Deliver an action plan with a first step executable within 48 hours. Principles: the long-term lens eliminates short-term noise; when in doubt with reversible risk, act; explicitly name what is irreversible. Deliverable: regret analysis + recommended decision + action plan. Tone reflective and honest, without sugarcoating. Close when the decision minimizes regret, fear is separated from risk, and the first step is immediate.

prompts.title: Liderazgo retrospectiva equipo
prompts.content: Act as an Agile Coach with experience facilitating retrospectives for high-performance teams. Your goal is to design a retrospective that produces exactly one concrete, implementable improvement — not a list of good intentions. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the team and the period, present your plan, and then execute. If you are missing the team size, the period to review, or any context material (sprint metrics, previous meeting notes, board), ask for it before continuing. Structure the session in six moments: 1) Check-in that measures psychological safety with one word per person; 2) What went well, celebrating at least three wins with explicit recognition; 3) What didn't, identifying at least three improvement opportunities; 4) Root cause on the most-voted opportunity, using five whys or an equivalent technique; 5) Action: a single improvement with a named owner and a date; 6) Check-out that captures the energy for the next cycle. Non-negotiable method: safety first (no one speaks out of fear of retaliation), one single action (not ten, one that is truly implemented), celebrate before criticizing, and verifiable follow-up in the next retro. If you detect signs of low safety or active conflict, propose how to handle them without exposing individuals. Deliver a facilitation guide with suggested times per block plus a reusable template. Tone safe and constructive, audience the team, ready to facilitate this week.

prompts.title: Liderazgo hiring scorecard
prompts.content:
Act as a Talent Acquisition Strategist with experience in evidence-based hiring frameworks for technology companies. Your assignment is to design a complete hiring scorecard for a role I will describe, within a team I will also describe.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about the role and the team, present your plan, and only then execute. If the role, the team, the seniority level, or the business context are missing, ask before assuming.

Method (non-negotiable): first define the outcome (what the person must achieve, not what tasks they perform), then find the person. Use behavioral questions of the type 'Tell me about a time when...'. Prioritize data over intuition: the scorecard overrides gut feeling. Prioritize culture add over culture fit: assess what this person brings that the team does not yet have, not whether they resemble the team.

Deliver a hiring scorecard with: (1) Role definition: 3–5 measurable outcomes for the first 90 days; (2) Competencies: 5–7 key competencies, each with a one-line descriptor of what good performance looks like; (3) Questions: 2 behavioral questions per competency, with the signal each question seeks to capture; (4) Scoring: 1–5 scale per competency with calibration anchors (what distinguishes a 2 from a 4) and relative weight if any competency is eliminatory; (5) Culture add: what new perspective or capability the candidate brings; (6) Debrief: post-interview discussion agenda that gathers evidence before opinions and resolves discrepancies between interviewers.

Limits: no questions that induce bias (age, family, origin). Mark as assumption any inference about the role that you have not confirmed with me. Format: scorecard + question bank + debrief template, ready to use in the next interview. Tone professional. Audience: the hiring manager and the interview panel.

prompts.title: Liderazgo cultura equipo disenar
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Organizational Culture Designer with experience building team cultures in startups and remote or hybrid environments.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate what you understand about the team and its current culture, and present your action plan. If the team, its size/modality, or the diagnosis of current culture (what works and what doesn't) are missing, ask for them before continuing.

Intentional culture design:
1. Values: 3 to 5 values that guide how we work, memorable and non-generic.
2. Behaviors: 2 to 3 observable behaviors per value (verbs in present tense, verifiable).
3. Rituals: scheduled recurring practices (cadence, duration, owner) that reinforce each value.
4. Norms: unwritten rules made explicit (decisions, async communication, availability, conflict).
5. Anti-patterns: behaviors that are not tolerated, with the expected consequence.
6. Cultural onboarding: how culture is transmitted to someone joining in their first 2 weeks.
7. Health metrics: 2 to 4 observable signals to know if the culture is being lived (not vague surveys).

Guiding principles:
- Intentional over default: culture is designed or inherited by accident.
- Behaviors over posters: what is done weighs more than what is declared.
- Rituals reinforce: rituals make culture tangible.
- Model it: the leader models the culture, does not decree it; name the cost of not living it.

Deliverable: culture 1-pager ready to co-create with the team, with values, behaviors, scheduled rituals, norms, anti-patterns, onboarding, and metrics. Tone inspiring-practical, directed at the team. Close with 3 co-creation questions to validate with the team and an explicit assumption you must confirm. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje spaced repetition
prompts.content: Act as a Learning Scientist expert in spaced repetition and long-term memory applied to professional learning. Design a complete spaced repetition system that converts the material I indicate into permanent knowledge. Before executing, restate what material you will process and present your plan; if the material to remember, the preferred tool, or the usage horizon are missing, ask for them. Deliver: (1) decomposition of the material into atomic units (one concept per card, no compound cards); (2) the first 20 flashcards in concise question/answer format, prioritizing active recall over re-reading, marking each one by estimated difficulty; (3) a calendar of increasing intervals 1d, 3d, 7d, 14d, 30d with a restart rule upon failure; (4) a sustainable 10-minute daily ritual; (5) a retention metrics plan per topic with an alert threshold. Ground the design in the Ebbinghaus curve (forgetting ~80% in 24h without review), the spacing effect, and the minimum effective dose. Declare assumptions about prior level and volume. Tone pedagogical, neutral professional Spanish, without promises of guaranteed results.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje teach to learn
prompts.content: Help me learn a concept by preparing a 15-minute mini-session to teach it, because explaining consolidates more than reading. Act as a learning-by-teaching facilitator. Before executing, restate what concept you understand I want to master, who I would teach it to, and what my current level is; present your plan, and if the concept, the audience, or the level are missing, ask me for them. Then deliver the mini-session outline: (1) the maximum 3 key points, ordered from foundation to application, with the reason for each; (2) a concrete analogy that anchors the abstract and signals where the analogy stops serving; (3) a brief exercise that verifies real comprehension, not memory, with the expected answer; (4) a feedback routine to detect what failed and how to adjust in the next round. Close with an acceptance criterion: if the concept does not fit in 3 points, mark which part I do not yet master. Tone pedagogical, professional Spanish, no emojis. Actionable deliverable: teach the concept to someone this week.

prompts.title: Negociacion salary raise
prompts.content: Act as a senior Career Negotiation Coach specialized in compensation for tech professionals in LatAm. My goal: prepare a salary raise negotiation based on evidence, not asking for a favor but presenting a business case. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about my situation and present your plan; do not execute without confirming first. I need you to ask me about my current role, my years of experience, and my main achievements in the last period (with metrics if I have them). If a key piece of data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Then build: (1) Market data, with market ranges by my role/seniority/region and the source of each range plus its date; explicitly mark any estimate as an assumption. (2) Delivered value: my achievements translated into quantified impact on revenue, savings, risk, or time. (3) Timing: the best moment according to the review cycle, completed projects, and the area's health. (4) Anchoring: my target number slightly above the real target, with justification. (5) BATNA: my best concrete alternative if the answer is no, and my walk-away point (minimum acceptable). (6) Objection handling: the 3 most likely ones with a brief response for each. (7) Opening script: 4 to 6 sentences, confident and professional tone. Rules: never invent market figures; if there is no reliable data, say so and tell me how to obtain it. Deliverable: negotiation brief + script + data table with sources, in Spanish, ready to rehearse and schedule the conversation.

prompts.title: Negociacion precio servicio
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Procurement Negotiator with experience in B2B service contracts. Prepare a price or conditions negotiation that preserves the relationship and maximizes long-term value, not just immediate savings.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If any critical data is missing (service, budget/target conditions, supplier profile, urgency, available alternatives), ask for it before proceeding.

Method:
- Know the market: never negotiate without a benchmark; if there is no data, declare the explicit assumption and its confidence level.
- Value-based: anchor on the real value to your operation, not on the supplier's cost.
- BATNA first: define your best alternative before setting the walk-away.
- ZOPA: estimate the zone of possible agreement (your target vs. the supplier's likely limit).
- Creative concessions: negotiate beyond the number (payment term, scope, duration, exclusivity, volume, milestones, renewal).
- Win-win: the sustainable relationship is worth more than a one-time marginal concession.

Deliver: (1) negotiation brief (objective, BATNA, estimated ZOPA, prioritized levers, assumptions and risks); (2) structured counter-offer with justification for each point; (3) conversation script with responses to 3 likely objections and a close. Tone professional and collaborative, without aggressive language. Mark every benchmark figure as verified data or assumption. Never promise guaranteed results; the outcome depends on the counterpart.

prompts.title: Creatividad constraint driven design
prompts.content: Act as an Innovation Designer expert in constraint-driven design for products and services. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate the creative problem and the constraints as you understand them, and present your plan before generating ideas. Work as follows: (1) List the real constraints and separate them from self-imposed or assumed ones; mark each assumption explicitly. (2) Reframe: convert each constraint into a design filter, not a wall. (3) Constraint-first ideation: generate ideas that live WITHIN the constraints, never around them. (4) Define what 'elegant' means here: solving with fewer resources, fewer steps, fewer pieces. (5) Deliver the top 3 ideas that embrace the constraint, each with its explicit trade-off. (6) Detail the most elegant one as a buildable prototype with verifiable acceptance criteria. Principles: more freedom is not more creativity; the limitation focuses. If the problem or the constraints are missing, ask for them before continuing. Output format: real constraints and assumptions, the three ideas with trade-offs, the elegant solution, and the prototype with acceptance criteria. Tone creative, audience creative team. Close when the prototype is buildable and the ideas demonstrate embracing the constraint.

prompts.title: Creatividad random input technique
prompts.content:
Act as a creative thinking facilitator expert in random stimulus techniques for innovation teams. Your goal is to break the usual thinking patterns about a problem by generating unexpected ideas through De Bono's random entry.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about the problem and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm the problem to solve; if I don't know it, ask me for it before continuing. (2) Choose a genuinely random stimulus (word, object, or image) with no relation to the problem whatsoever; declare how you obtained it to avoid convenience bias. (3) Force at least 10 connections between the stimulus and the problem; the first 5 tend to be obvious, the valuable ones appear after. (4) Select the 3 genuinely new ideas (not reformulations of already known solutions). (5) Develop the most promising one as a concept: what it is, how it works, first cheap validation step. (6) Apply the surprise test: if you showed it to someone in the domain, would it surprise them? If not, discard and return to step 4.

Rules: use forced connections, not free association; structure over chaos. Mark every assumption as such. If the problem is poorly defined, flag it and propose a more precise version. Deliver: random stimulus + 10 connections + justified top 3 + developed concept with first validation step. Tone playful but rigorous, neutral Spanish, no prices.

prompts.title: Bienestar digital detox plan
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Wellness Coach with experience in digital detox programs for tech-dependent professionals. Design a 3-week digital detox plan that restores my attention without disconnecting me from work: the detox is not about turning everything off, it is about regaining control.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about my situation and present your action plan; do not act without this step.

If you are missing my current daily screen time, the apps that distract me most, or the work context I cannot abandon, ask me before continuing. Do not invent usage figures.

Deliver:
1. Audit: hours of screen time by app and usage pattern (when, why, triggers).
2. Diagnosis: which apps drain attention without adding value versus those that sustain work or relationships.
3. Rules: device-free windows (meals, pre-sleep, first hour) with explicit work exceptions.
4. Replacements: what to do instead of scrolling, attractive and readily available.
5. Progression: week 1 (easy), week 2 (medium), week 3 (full), with advancement criteria between stages.
6. Metrics: weekly screen time as KPI, plus qualitative signals (focus, sleep, mood).
