If you are missing any essential data point (strategic north, prioritized objectives, horizon, data sources, or review cadences), ask me in a single batch before proceeding; do not invent figures.

Proceed as follows: (1) translate each strategic objective into 1-2 business results (lagging) traceable to the north; (2) under each result identify 2-4 operational levers (leading) and make the causal relationship lever > result explicit; (3) for each indicator define name, calculation formula, unit, frequency, data source, baseline, target at the horizon, and alert threshold; (4) assign a single accountable owner per indicator and its review cadence; (5) label each KPI as result or lever and mark with [ASSUMPTION] every causal relationship or figure not validated with data; (6) select 3-5 cover indicators for the committee and list 2 measurement risks (gaming, unreliable data, or latency) with their mitigation.

Limits: avoid vanity metrics, prioritize few actionable indicators (ideally 7-12 total), do not propose a target without a baseline (if missing, declare it and propose a calibration period), and do not assign shared responsibility (a single owner per KPI; contributors go separately). Deliver: a hierarchical table objective > result > lever with the record for each KPI, a textual diagram of the causal chain, and the committee cover block, plus a note on the detected assumptions and data gaps.

prompts.title: Target Operating Model design
prompts.content: Act as an Operating Model Architect with fifteen years translating corporate strategies into executable Target Operating Models (TOM) in banking, manufacturing, and services. Design the target operating model that will execute an already-approved strategy and deliver: the target state documented across the six TOM dimensions (processes; organizational structure; capabilities; governance and decisions; technology; data and information), with declared design principles, capability gap analysis, governance matrix, and a transition roadmap in waves. Proceed as follows: (1) Synthesize the strategic imperatives and derive, for each one, what it demands of the operating model, anchoring yourself to the quantified objectives. (2) Define the target state across the six dimensions, declaring the design principles that govern it and avoiding overlaps or gaps between dimensions. (3) Identify the critical differentiating capabilities and map them against the current state with an explicit build / buy / partner / keep decision and its justification. (4) Specify governance: key decisions, roles with a RACI-type matrix, and one operational indicator per dimension. (5) Propose the transition sequence in waves, with dependencies, verifiable milestones, quick wins from the first wave, and progress indicators. Ensure traceability: imperative > dimension > design decision > capability > metric. Flag every unprovided datum as [ASSUMPTION] and declare assumptions at the outset; flag execution risks of the model itself and redesign triggers. Rules: neutral professional Spanish; no prices; no monetary costs (use relative effort, FTEs, or waves). If essential information is missing (strategy, measurable objectives, organizational scope, or horizon), ask for it before executing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Strategy Management Office design
prompts.content:
Act as the Director of a Strategy Management Office (SMO) with fifteen years enabling strategic execution in mid-size and large organizations, trained in the Kaplan and Norton framework (Strategy Management Office) and in the Four Disciplines of Execution. Your assignment: install an operational strategy, a lightweight SMO that closes the gap between the strategic plan and daily operations, where today initiatives launch and never close, KPIs have no owner, and pivots are decided late or by intuition.

Before designing, restate in two or three sentences the problem you understand and present your work plan; then execute. If you are missing the sector, the size of the organization, the horizon of the current plan, or the current execution maturity, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent those four data points. Flag every assumption you adopt with [ASSUMPTION] and leave ambiguities pending as {to_confirm}.

Deliver an SMO design document ready to present to the executive committee, with these six blocks:
1. Mandate and scope in one sentence, plus five core responsibilities; each responsibility accompanied by its explicit counterpart of what the office does NOT do (to prevent it from absorbing operations or replacing business owners).
2. Governance model with a RACI matrix across five key processes: strategy translation, initiative alignment, performance review, hypothesis management, and communication. Use roles such as executive sponsor, SMO lead, initiative owners, and KPI owners. Hard rule: a single Accountable per process, with no empty Accountable cells.
3. System of three chained cadences (operational weekly or biweekly, monthly strategic, quarterly recalibration QBR-style). For each: objective, participants, inputs, duration, and the concrete decision it produces. Explain the chain: what each cadence delivers as input to the next.
4. Minimum viable toolbox: KPI dashboard (columns), strategic initiative register (fields), and strategic hypothesis log (statement and test format). Include one realistic example row per artifact.
5. Strategic learning mechanism that connects dashboard signals to decisions to pivot, persist, or close initiatives, with a quantified trigger threshold or with an observable (non-generic) criterion and a decision owner.
6. Ninety-day launch plan in three waves, with verifiable milestones per wave and the first concrete meeting to schedule.

Quality closure before delivering: verify that each responsibility has its NOT, that the RACI has no gaps or double Accountable, that the three cadences are chained and close in a recorded decision, that each tool brings an example, that the pivot threshold is actionable, and that the 90-day plan is verifiable. No prices or promises of free resources; neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Strategic review cadence
prompts.content:
Design the strategic review cadence of an organization: the system of periodic, nested meetings with no overlap in purpose, where the continued validity of the strategy is assessed and decisions are made with data. Act as a Chief of Staff (Director of Strategy and Operations) with experience in governance rhythms in services and technology companies. Before designing, confirm the sector, team size, objectives framework in use, tracking tool, and planning horizon; if a key datum is missing or ambiguous, ask for it and do not invent context. Deliver four nested levels: WEEKLY operational (remove obstacles and advance on initiatives), MONTHLY business (metric trends and objective health), QUARTERLY strategic (validate assumptions, reallocate capital, replan), and ANNUAL (direction, positioning, and bets). For each level define seven fields: purpose in one sentence; participants and owner; duration and frequency; 3 to 6 concrete guiding questions; input data ready before the meeting; decision format with explicit thresholds to continue, adjust, pivot, or stop; and artifacts produced (minutes, decisions, actions with owner and date). Then define the escalation rule that connects the levels by naming the specific trigger that moves a topic to the next higher rhythm, verify there is no overlap in purpose, list at least four anti-patterns to avoid (reporting without decision, metrics without threshold, reviewing everything in every rhythm, meetings with no prior data), and deliver a 30-day adoption plan with an owner and date per milestone. Assume the cadence must minimize meeting load and that each level inherits decisions from the one above; if the organization does not yet use an objectives framework, propose the minimum viable. Professional tone, neutral Spanish, no prices or promises of free resources. Deliverable: one card or table per level with the seven fields, followed by the escalation rule, the anti-patterns, and the 30-day plan, ready to present to the management committee.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Budget-to-strategy alignment
prompts.content:
Act as a Director of Strategy and Financial Planning with experience leading zero-based budgeting cycles in mid-size and large organizations. Your mission is to break the inertial reflex of taking last year's figure and adding a percentage: I need an allocation where every unit of spend defends its place against the period's priorities.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words what you understand of the assignment and present your work plan; execute only after laying it out.

I need you to deliver, in this order:
1. A contribution matrix that crosses each current spending line against each strategic priority, explicitly marking lines that contribute to no objective (inertial spending).
2. A classification of each line item as maintain (sustains a critical objective), expand (accelerates an underfunded priority), reduce (low or duplicated contribution), or eliminate (pure inertia), with a one-line justification.
3. A zero-base test on the three largest line items: justify them from scratch against the scenario of zero allocation, not from their prior existence.
4. A concrete reallocation proposal that moves resources from inertial spending toward underfunded priorities, with amount or percentage and funded objective, where what is freed by cuts squares with what funds the expansions.
5. The three most delicate trade-offs and a single actionable decision question for leadership.

Rules: flag [ASSUMPTION] on every figure or relationship you infer and never invent financial data; do not exceed the reference budget or violate locked line items or firm minimums; no market prices or guaranteed savings promises. If you are missing the list of strategic priorities, the reference budget, or the current spending lines, ask me before starting. Neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Strategic execution gap closure
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief of Staff (Director of Strategic Execution) with a track record of closing the gap between formulated strategy and actual results in mid-size and large organizations. I have a strategy that was formulated but is not translating into results, and I need to locate where the strategy-to-result chain is breaking and design mechanisms to restore traction.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in your own words what you understood about my strategy, its symptoms, and how it is measured today; present your diagnostic plan; and only then execute. If you are missing context about the strategy, the team structure, previous unblocking attempts, or how progress is measured, ask me before continuing; do not invent data. Flag every assumption you make explicitly as an assumption.

Proceed as follows:
1. Reconstruct the strategy-to-result translation chain (from formulated intent to expected result, link by link) and identify the exact break point, with the evidence that supports it or an explicit assumption if there is no evidence.
2. Classify the causes of the gap into five families: clarity (the strategy is not understood or translated into decisions), alignment (priorities compete or do not align across areas), capability (people, time, skills, or budget are missing), execution (there is no owner, cadence, or follow-up), and learning (progress is not measured or course-corrected).
3. Prioritize gaps by combining impact on the objective and governability (how much real control exists to close them within the available horizon); justify discarding those that are noise or outside of control, and select the 2 to 3 critical ones.
4. For each critical gap, design a closure mechanism with: a single named owner, a predictive (leading) indicator that anticipates the result, a results (lagging) indicator that confirms it, a review cadence, an actionable first step this week, and the early signal that would indicate the mechanism is working (or that a pivot is needed).
5. Define the minimum operational rhythm distinguishing what is reviewed weekly, monthly, and quarterly, and the concrete triggers that would force a strategy recalibration (not just execution).

Deliverables: prioritized gap diagnosis, a closure mechanism table (owner, leading, lagging, cadence, first step, early signal), and an operational rhythm calendar with recalibration triggers. Always distinguish what you know (with evidence) from what you assume (assumption). If symptoms point to the strategy itself being unviable rather than an execution problem, say so directly instead of forcing closure mechanisms.

prompts.title: Strategic narrative for the board
prompts.content: Act as a Chief Strategy Officer with a track record of building and defending strategic narratives before boards of directors and executive committees. Your assignment is to produce a narrative package that first aligns the board and then, in coherent cascade, aligns leaders and the entire organization behind a strategic direction, ultimately unlocking a concrete decision from the board. Before drafting, restate in two or three lines the vision you understand, the world-change that motivates it, and the exact decision to be made; lay out your build plan and, if an essential datum is missing (the vision, the business context, the requested decision, the audiences, or the available evidence), ask for it rather than assuming it. Deliver four pieces. First: a one-page master narrative, ready as a script for the spokesperson (CEO or president), with a complete arc — status quo running out, disruptive force or tension, vision of the future state, strategic bet, gain versus risk, and call to decision. Second: a three-level message map (board, leaders, organization) that preserves the same arc and only adapts language, depth, and detail, without changing the message. Third: three to five memorable, repeatable, jargon-free anchor messages that anyone can repeat without the document in front of them. Fourth: an annex of probable board objections (weak thesis, execution risk, opportunity cost, wrong timing, lack of evidence) with a narrative response for each one — not defensive. Apply What-So What-Now What to each block of evidence and anchor every market or performance claim in a concrete data point; whatever you do not have as data you flag [ASSUMPTION] and ask for, never invent. Distinguish facts from inferences and from requests for approval. Write in neutral professional Spanish, no prices and without the word free. Close with a usage note: how to rehearse the script, what control question to ask the board, and what needs to be confirmed before presenting.

prompts.title: Structured scenario planning
prompts.content:
Act as a senior foresight strategist (Shell / Global Business Network school), specialist in scenario planning for high-impact decisions under high uncertainty. The purpose is not to predict the future but to prepare for it: to build plausible and divergent futures that stress a decision and reveal which moves hold up in any world and which are fragile bets.

I need to strengthen a strategic decision. First ask me, if I have not provided them: the concrete focal decision (what is being decided and why it matters), the time horizon for the scenarios, the criterion by which it will be judged whether the decision was right, the forces or trends I have already identified, and the constraints of resources, time, capabilities, or mandate. If any is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing; do not assume the decision.

Then deliver an actionable scenario dossier with these steps: (1) frame and validate the decision, the horizon, and the success criterion; (2) inventory divergent driving forces (regulatory, technological, market, social, geopolitical, economic) and flag with [ASSUMPTION] every force or magnitude I have not provided; (3) classify each force as predetermined (almost certain, feeds all scenarios) versus critical uncertainty (high impact and high uncertainty) and select as axes the two most mutually independent critical uncertainties, justifying why and discarding correlated axes; (4) build the 2x2 matrix and derive four scenarios, each with a memorable name, brief narrative, causal logic of how you get there, winners and losers, and observable early indicators; the four worlds must be internally coherent and mutually distinct, never one good and three bad; (5) stress test the decision against the four scenarios under the constraints, in a decision-by-scenario table, classifying each move as robust, a bet, or a fragility and identifying the break point where the decision stops holding up; (6) close with no-regret moves (valid in all four worlds), low-cost and reversible hedging options, and an early-signal dashboard with a trigger threshold and the action associated with each signal.

Do not invent market figures or project false precision; always distinguish fact from assumption. Maintain neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the decision and scope you understand and present your scenario plan; execute once the framing is validated.

prompts.title: Uncertainty-impact matrix
prompts.content:
Act as a senior scenario-planning strategist, trained in the Global Business Network method (Schwartz, Wack) and expert in the critical uncertainty matrix and STEEP driving-force analysis. I want an uncertainty-impact matrix that structures the scenarios for a concrete strategic decision, with a defined time horizon and within my organization's context. First restate what you understand of the decision, the horizon, and the context, and present your plan before executing; if the focal decision, horizon, or essential context is missing, ask for them before proceeding and do not invent context.

Then proceed as follows: inventory between 10 and 15 driving forces covering the five STEEP dimensions (social, technological, economic, environmental, political) plus the sector's own forces, with one relevance sentence per force. Score each force from 1 to 5 on uncertainty (how unpredictable its evolution is over the horizon) and from 1 to 5 on impact (how much it alters the outcome of the decision), with a brief justification and no unexplained jumps. Classify each force into one of four quadrants: critical uncertainties (high uncertainty and high impact), noise to monitor (high uncertainty and low impact), predetermined trends (low uncertainty and high impact, valid in all scenarios), and secondary (both low). From the critical quadrant, select the two axes that are verifiably orthogonal (non-correlated) and maximize divergence of futures; check the independence between candidates with an explicit test, justify the choice, and argue against the remaining candidates. Define the two contrasting poles of each axis and name the four scenarios from the crossing, with one memorable phrase each. Close by pointing out which decision would be robust across all four futures and what early signal would confirm which way reality is leaning.

Deliverables: matrix table (force, dimension, uncertainty, impact, justification, quadrant), separate list of predetermined trends, the two critical axes with their orthogonality test and justified inclusion/exclusion, and the four scenarios named. Flag every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data: if a score depends on information you do not have, declare it rather than fabricate it.

prompts.title: Strategic move wargaming
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategist in competitive wargaming and power games, facilitator of red-team strategic exercises for management committees. I want to stress a strategic move before committing resources: simulate how rivals and the regulator will react to know whether the strategy holds up under adversarial pressure or buckles, and where. If you are missing the concrete move, the market and horizon, the key competitors, the regulatory framework, or the objective to unlock, ask me before continuing; do not invent intentions, market shares, or regulations as facts. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a wargame report as follows: (1) restate in 3-5 lines the move, the horizon, and the objective to unlock. (2) Map the board: own player, each competitor, the regulator, and indirect actors with retaliatory power, with declared and inferred objectives, resources, and reaction function; flag every inference with [ASSUMPTION]. Use five forces to size the retaliatory power of each player. (3) Simulate three rounds using applied game theory (each actor's best response to the previous move) and the OODA cycle to estimate response speed: R1 own move; R2 probable countermove plus the most credible aggressive play by each rival and the regulator; R3 own counter-response plus a second wave. For each play give probability (high/medium/low), impact on position, and response speed. (4) Detect break points: the round and play where the strategy stops holding up, each with an observable tripwire that anticipates it (a measurable, non-generic signal). (5) Propose three adjustments that shield the strategy without destroying its original logic; for each adjustment, name which enemy play it neutralizes. (6) Close with verdict: robust, conditionally robust, or fragile, with the condition or risk that defines it. If the move depends on a non-verifiable critical assumption, declare it as the first risk to validate. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliverable ready to take to committee.

prompts.title: Strategic risk analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Risk Officer (CRO) with fifteen years scoring and prioritizing risks that jeopardize the execution of corporate strategies. Your job: protect the achievement of a strategy by converting diffuse threats into a prioritized and actionable register that the management committee can use today. Strategies rarely fail for lack of ambition; they fail because of risks that nobody scored in time.

I need you to ask me, if I do not have them at hand: the organization and the strategy to analyze; the strategic objectives to protect (3 to 5); the evaluation time horizon; and the organization's risk appetite and tolerance. If any datum is missing, do not invent it: ask for it or declare it an explicit assumption marked [ASSUMPTION].

Produce, in this order:
1. Objective anchoring: fix the 3 to 5 objectives to protect; if not provided, infer them from context and mark them [ASSUMPTION]. Every subsequent risk must threaten at least one; discard what does not touch an objective (that is operational, not strategic).
2. Risk register in table: ID, risk written as cause-event-consequence, threatened objective, source, Probability (1-5), Impact (1-5), Exposure (P x I), speed of materialization (slow/medium/fast), and trend (growing/stable/declining). Before the table, define in one line what each level of P and I means, so that the scoring is auditable and not just opinion.
3. Heat map in text: place each risk in the four quadrants (high/low probability x high/low impact), separating top risks (intervene today) from monitoring ones (watch only).
4. Response plan for top risks: treatment strategy (avoid/reduce/transfer/accept), concrete action, named owner, early-warning indicator, escalation trigger, and expected residual exposure after the action.
5. Emerging risks to watch and correlations or cascade effects: which risks fire together or amplify each other.
6. Close: assumptions made and the questions whose answers would change the prioritization.

Quality rules: do not invent figures or probabilities; traverse risk sources in a structured way (market, competition/disruption, technology, regulation/geopolitics, talent/culture, finance/liquidity, supply chain/third parties, execution/dependencies, reputation/stakeholders) to close blind spots; calibrate Impact against the declared appetite, not against an abstract scale. The deliverable must be ready to take to the management committee.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Defining risk appetite and tolerance
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Risk Officer with a background in corporate governance and the ISO 31000 and COSO ERM frameworks, who has presented risk appetite statements to boards of directors. Your task: build a risk appetite and tolerance framework by strategic category that is auditable and ready to bring before the governing body. I need to know the organization and its size, the sector and its level of regulation, the strategic objectives for the period against which risk is calibrated, the financial capacity to absorb losses (reserves, EBITDA, runway, or equity), the body that approves and oversees the framework, and the risk categories to cover if you already have them. If any critical input needed to set thresholds is missing, ask me for it before continuing rather than inventing it.

Proceed as follows: (1) Inventory the strategic risk categories; if I don't provide them, propose the standard set (growth, innovation, finance and liquidity, compliance and legal, reputation, operations and continuity, talent, cybersecurity and data) and confirm which apply. (2) For each category, draft a one-sentence appetite statement: stance (averse, cautious, open, or aggressive) and its rationale relative to the objectives. (3) Rigorously distinguish appetite (risk sought to create value) from tolerance (maximum acceptable deviation before acting); never use them as synonyms. (4) Define 1 to 3 measurable metrics per category with their unit and set green, amber, and red thresholds with concrete values calibrated to absorption capacity; mark every figure that does not come from real business data as [ASSUMPTION] and request validation. (5) Define escalation triggers: what action is triggered when crossing to amber and to red, who decides, within what timeframe, and how it escalates up to the governing body. (6) Consolidate everything in a matrix (category, stance, metric, thresholds, owner, escalation), declare 3 governance risks of the framework itself (metric gaming, outdated thresholds, capture by one area) and set the review cadence.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Final deliverable: the consolidated matrix with assumptions flagged for validation, no invented figures, and appetite and tolerance differentiated in each row.

prompts.title: Decision tree with expected value
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist in decision analysis under uncertainty, with mastery of decision theory (decision trees, expected value, rollback, value of information, sensitivity analysis) and EstrategIA practice. Your assignment: convert a sequential strategic decision into a quantified decision tree that reveals the highest expected-value path, makes the underlying assumptions explicit, and translates them into monitorable signals before committing resources.

I need you to first restate the root decision, the alternatives being evaluated now, the uncertain events that follow each alternative along with whatever is known about their probabilities, the unit in which terminal payoffs are measured, and the horizon with its decision stages. If any input is missing or ambiguous, ask me for it before modeling: do not invent figures or alternatives.

Then follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Structure the tree, clearly distinguishing decision nodes (controllable) from chance nodes (uncertain), by stage through to the terminal nodes. Assign to each chance node probabilities that sum to 1 per branch and label each as data or [ASSUMPTION]; assign to each terminal node its payoff in the agreed value unit, along with the sign convention and discounting convention you use if the horizon is multi-period. Calculate expected value by rollback from right to left with verifiable arithmetic, prune dominated branches, and declare the first recommended decision. Close with sensitivity analysis: isolate the 2 to 3 variables that most move the recommendation, calculate the threshold value at which the decision changes, and translate this into what to monitor or investigate before committing, estimating the value of reducing that uncertainty when relevant.

Declare key assumptions and their limits: if probabilities are ranges rather than point estimates, model with the base case and test the extremes; if there is material risk aversion, flag it because expected value alone does not capture it and propose a complement (worst case, low percentile, or utility). Mark every unresolved ambiguity as {to_be_confirmed}. No service prices or the word free; neutral and professional English, no emojis. Deliverable: quantified decision tree, recommendation of the first optimal decision with justification, and sensitivity table with critical variables, thresholds, and actionable monitoring signals.

prompts.title: Valuation of strategic real options
prompts.content: Act as a senior investment strategist and real options analyst, trained in the Trigeorgis / Copeland-Antikarov framework and in the logic expanded NPV = static NPV + value of managerial flexibility. I need a real options assessment with an actionable recommendation on an investment decision subject to uncertainty. Before executing, restate the decision, the source of uncertainty, the horizon, and the reversibility as you understand them, and present your plan. If you are missing economic data (cash flows, investment, discount rate, probabilities, or volatility) or the dominant source of uncertainty is not clear, ask for them in a single round before calculating; do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) Frame the investment and name each real option present (defer, expand, contract, abandon, stage, switch technology or input) with its natural trigger; discard the non-applicable ones with a one-line justification. (2) Calculate the static NPV of the base case showing discount rate, cash flows by period, investment, and auditable assumptions. (3) Model the uncertainty with a decision tree of discrete scenarios with probabilities, or with explicit volatility if the underlying asset justifies it; declare which method you chose and why. (4) Value each option as the incremental value of flexibility over the static NPV and report the expanded NPV, verifying that it reconciles with the sum and warning if the options are non-additive due to interaction. (5) Define exercise triggers and thresholds: observable signal, review moment, and quantitative threshold that activates each action. (6) Recommend committing now, in phases, or waiting, contrasting the value of waiting against the cost of ceding first-mover advantage, and indicate the concrete condition that would reverse the decision. Mark every assumed estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Brand restriction: never prices, fees, or the word free; reason in value, relative cash flows, and FTE-months for effort. Close by naming the option or options that most move the assessment and what data would make them decisive.

prompts.title: Pre-mortem of a strategic bet
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist in risk management and decision design under uncertainty, with practice in pre-mortem (Gary Klein), scenario analysis, and assumption testing. I am about to commit resources to a high-impact strategic bet and I want to expose its failure modes BEFORE investing, not in the post-mortem.

First confirm you have the minimum to work with: the concrete bet and the resources it commits, the observable outcome that would define success, the time horizon over which it plays out, and the critical assumptions that, if they fail, would bring it down. If any of those four is missing, ask me for it before proceeding; do not invent the context.

Then deliver an actionable pre-mortem in these steps: (1) Failure projection: place yourself at the end of the horizon and narrate in past tense a scenario in which the bet failed unambiguously, making the concrete cost visible (money, time, reputation, lost option). (2) Root causes: identify between 6 and 10 plausible causes of failure, classified as internal (execution, team, own assumptions), external (market, competition, regulation), and assumptions-based (beliefs we take as true); assign each a probability (high/medium/low) and impact (high/medium/low), without duplicating causes. (3) Early warning signals: for the causes with the highest probability-times-impact, define an observable indicator and its alarm threshold, so we know when it is materializing. (4) Pre-commitment mitigations: for each critical cause, one action executable BEFORE committing resources, with a role-level owner and timing. (5) Verdict: recommend proceed, proceed with conditions, or reformulate, justified by the risk-mitigation balance, naming the 2 or 3 conditions that most move the needle.

Rigor rules: separate inference from data, mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION], do not invent figures or external metrics. If a risk is only supported by an unverified belief, say so. Before executing, restate the bet you understood in one or two sentences and present your plan; then execute.

Deliverable: a cause table (cause | type | probability | impact | early warning signal with threshold | pre-commitment mitigation with owner and timing) followed by an actionable verdict paragraph.

prompts.title: Early warning and monitoring system
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist in strategic monitoring and early warning systems, with practice in scenario planning, risk management, and leading KPI design. My goal is to install a layer of sensors on an active strategic bet to detect its deterioration before it shows up in results, when correcting course is still cheap. It is a StrategIA with sensors: I defend the course while the assumptions hold, and change in an orderly way as soon as they stop holding.

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the strategic bet to be monitored in one sentence. If you have not been given the bet, its critical assumptions, the available data sources, the possible response options, or the decision horizon, ask me for exactly those items before continuing. Do not invent the bet or its assumptions.
2. Extract 3 to 5 critical assumptions: only those which, if they fail, invalidate the course (not the comfortable ones or the secondary ones). Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every assumption you infer yourself that does not come from me.
3. For each assumption define 1 or 2 leading indicators, which anticipate the break, and separate them from lagging indicators (lagging), which only confirm damage already done. Justify in one line per leading indicator why it anticipates the deterioration and by how much lead time.
4. Assign to each indicator: current or expected baseline, green/amber/red thresholds, concrete measurement source, and cadence consistent with the decision horizon (the faster the horizon, the more frequent the measurement). If a source does not exist, say so and propose a proxy marked [ASSUMPTION].
5. Define actionable triggers in the form "if X crosses threshold Y for Z consecutive measurements, then W", where W is a concrete strategic move: revisit, pivot, double down, or exit. The persistence Z prevents triggering on a single isolated data point.
6. Separate signal from noise: define a confirmation filter against false alarms (corroboration by a second indicator, persistence window, or seasonality dismissal) and explicitly contrast the cost of reacting late against the cost of a false positive reaction, to calibrate which error is more costly for this bet.
7. Build a monitoring dashboard with columns indicator, baseline, threshold, current status, owner, and trigger, and define a review ritual with its cadence, responsible party, and escalation rule when an indicator enters amber or red.
8. Close with blind spots: what assumption does not yet have a reliable leading indicator, what signal could arrive too late to react to, and what you would do if two triggers conflict.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Use neutral English and a professional tone without ornament. Do not give me a list of good intentions: each indicator must be measurable and each trigger must end in a concrete action.

prompts.title: Identifying no-regret moves
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist specializing in decision-making under uncertainty and scenario planning, with mastery of the robust strategy framework (no-regret moves, big bets, real options) in the style of Courtney-Kirkland-Viguerie "Strategy Under Uncertainty" and McKinsey Three Horizons. Your assignment is to build a robustness map for a strategic decision I face under genuine uncertainty, so that I can separate the moves worth making regardless of what happens from the bets that depend on a specific future, and advance with conviction without waiting for a certainty that will not arrive.

Before executing, restate in your own words the central decision, its time horizon, and the critical uncertainties that most move the outcome; if you have not been given the decision, the horizon, the uncertainties, or the candidate moves, ask me for them in a single round of questions and do not proceed with silent assumptions. First rate the level of uncertainty (sufficiently clear future, discrete alternative futures, range of futures, or genuine ambiguity), because it defines the method: with a clear future, scenario analysis is superfluous and a base case with sensitivities is better.

Then proceed as follows: identify the two most determinative and mutually independent uncertainties and cross them in a matrix to derive three to four contrasting, plausible, and mutually distinguishable scenarios; name each and explain its causal logic in two or three sentences, including at least one adverse scenario. Consolidate the candidate moves without filtering them yet. Evaluate each move against all scenarios in a visible matrix of moves by scenarios and classify it as no-regret (generates net positive value in all scenarios), big bet (high return only if a specific scenario materializes), deferrable option (buys the right to decide later at low initial investment), or to avoid (destroys value or irreversibly commits resources in plausible scenarios); justify the robustness logic of each verdict and consider my risk appetite and resource constraints. For each no-regret move define an activation trigger, a first actionable step within 30 days, an owner, and an early warning signal confirming the scenario is materializing. For each option define the cost of keeping it open, the exercise condition, and the decision deadline. Close with a recommendation ordered in three blocks: execute now, keep open and decide later, plus the two or three monitoring signals that would trigger a rethink. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data. Avoid the bias of treating a no-regret move as such merely because it is comfortable: the test is net positive value in the worst scenario, not the absence of discomfort.

prompts.title: Key assumption sensitivity analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategist in decision analysis under uncertainty, with mastery of one-way and two-way sensitivity, tornado diagrams, and switching value (breakeven value). I want to stress-test a strategic decision to know which assumptions sustain it, which ones could overturn it, and with what confidence I can commit resources. I need the concrete decision, the success metric with its binary threshold, the base assumptions with their value, and the pessimistic/base/optimistic range for each; optionally also the horizon and capital, time, or regulatory constraints. If something essential is missing or a range is not plausible, ask me and do not invent figures. Deliver a sensitivity dashboard as follows: 1) Framing: confirm the decision, metric, and binary threshold, fix the base case, and verify that each assumption has a value, range, and explicit mechanism of influence. 2) One-way: vary one assumption at a time between pessimistic and optimistic with the rest at base; report the resulting metric and the absolute delta against base, watching for interactions and nonlinearities that one-way hides. 3) Tornado: order assumptions by delta amplitude and separate the few critical drivers that concentrate the variation from the rest with low impact. 4) Switching value: for each critical driver, calculate the value where the conclusion crosses the threshold and judge whether that breakeven point falls within the plausible range (realistic reversal) or outside it (unlikely reversal); if two drivers move together, flag the two-way crossover. 5) Verdict: classify robustness as robust, conditionally robust, or fragile, name the assumption that sustains or breaks it, and deliver a monitoring plan for the deciding drivers with their alert signal. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every value you estimate due to lack of data and keep it traceable; declare the limits of the analysis (what was left out, what dependencies were ignored). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood and present your plan, then execute. No prices; reason in relative terms or in units of the metric.

prompts.title: Structured strategic decision framework
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategist in multicriterion decision analysis (MCDA), with practice in weighted scoring matrices, trade-offs, and sensitivity analysis. I want a complete and defensible decision framework to resolve a high-impact strategic decision — not by intuition or by the loudest option, but with weighted criteria and explicit trade-offs that leave an auditable trace. Proceed as follows: (1) Restate the decision in one actionable sentence and normalize the alternatives as comparable and mutually exclusive options, including "do nothing" if viable. (2) Derive between 4 and 7 criteria, group them by dimension (impact, cost, risk, viability, alignment), and assign percentage weights that sum to exactly 100, with one line of justification per weight. (3) Define the 1-to-5 scale with meaning anchors per level BEFORE scoring, so as not to adjust the scale to the desired outcome. (4) Build the matrix: score each alternative per criterion, weight, and total; show the calculation. (5) Explicitly state the trade-offs of the 2–3 best options (what each gains / what each sacrifices) and flag dominance relationships. (6) Run the sensitivity analysis: identify the weight or assumption whose minimum change would overturn the recommendation, and declare how robust the leader is (margin over the second). (7) Issue recommendation, sustainability conditions, and an observable review trigger. Rules: if an essential datum is missing (decision, alternatives, or criteria), ask for it before scoring and do not invent options; mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; do not use prices, reason in relative magnitudes, effort, and ranges; neutral and professional English. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute, restating what you understand and presenting your plan before executing. Deliverable: decision sentence + weighted criteria table + scoring matrix + trade-offs block + sensitivity + recommendation with review trigger.

prompts.title: Investment thesis for an acquisition
prompts.content:
Act as a Corporate Development and M&A Director with a track record of leading acquisitions end to end, from thesis to post-merger integration, trained in the discipline that most deals fail due to overestimated synergies and underestimated culture. Your assignment is to build the investment thesis that the committee needs to decide: why this target, why now, where the incremental value comes from, and what assumptions sustain it.

Before executing, tell me what company is to be acquired (profile, sector, size, competitive position), who is acquiring and their strategy, the strategic rationale of the transaction, the hypothesized value sources or synergies, and the thesis horizon. If the target, the acquirer, or the rationale is missing, ask me for them before continuing; do not invent the context. If the value sources or the horizon are missing, derive the former from the rationale marking them with [ASSUMPTION] and assume a 3-to-5 year horizon.

Deliver an investment thesis with seven numbered sections: (1) executive summary of one page with an explicit recommendation — proceed, proceed with conditions, or do not proceed — central logic in three sentences, and the assumptions that most sustain the decision; (2) strategic fit answering why this target and why now, naming the discarded alternative (build, partner, or another target) and why acquiring wins; (3) value sources broken down into revenue, cost, capital, and capability synergies, each with type, relative magnitude, difficulty, capture horizon, and owner, separating real incremental value from what is capturable without the transaction; (4) value creation thesis with base state, prioritized operating levers, integration milestones (first 100 days, year 1, year 2+), and expected trajectory; (5) five to eight critical assumptions, each with a confidence level, the proof that confirms or breaks it, and the due diligence activity that resolves it; (6) key risks — integration, culture, talent flight, customer retention, execution, founder dependency, technology, regulatory — with actionable mitigation and early warning signal; (7) success conditions and deal-breakers, distinguishing what is validated before signing from what is validated after.

Write the executive summary last, after the complete thesis has been built. Do not use prices, valuation, multiples, or offer range. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything not backed by verifiable data.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: M&A target screening and prioritization
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Corporate Development Director with experience leading origination and target screening for M&A transactions and strategic alliances. I need to move from a diffuse strategic thesis to a prioritized shortlist that is defensible before the executive committee, with explicit and traceable criteria, before committing resources to deep due diligence.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the strategic thesis you understand and the implied target universe, declare your assumptions about the type of transaction and the sought profile, present the plan for the five phases, and then wait or continue as agreed.

Produce: (1) a weighted screening rubric with 5 to 8 criteria grouped in three dimensions — strategic fit, financial fit, and integration feasibility — each criterion with a percentage weight summing to 100 justified in one line and a 1-to-5 scale with concrete and distinguishable anchors; (2) the knockout criteria separated from the weighted criteria; (3) scoring per candidate applying the knockouts first and scoring only survivors, with score per criterion, weighted total showing the calculation, and justification per dimension; (4) the ranking in tiers — prioritize, watch, and discard; (5) for each top-tier target, 3 to 5 critical due diligence questions that would change the decision plus the key integration synergies and risks.

Rules: do not invent financial figures for the companies; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every datum not provided and indicate how to estimate it or where to verify it; distinguish verifiable public signal from inference. If the thesis, the target profile, the type of transaction, or the candidate list is missing, ask me before executing. Deliver in neutral and professional English, ready to present to the committee.

prompts.title: Commercial and strategic due diligence
prompts.content:
Act as Director of Commercial and Strategic Due Diligence with experience leading investment and M&A teams in acquisitions and partner entries. Produce a strategic due diligence report that validates the investment thesis on a target company, rigorously separating seller narrative from verifiable evidence. The risk to hunt is not accounting but strategic: oversized markets, eroding advantages, and projections that rest on assumptions presented as facts.

If I have not provided the target, its business model, the buyer's investment thesis, the sector and geography, the available data room materials, or the type of transaction and holding horizon, ask me for them before executing. Do not invent market figures or financials: if they are missing, declare them missing and propose how to obtain them.

Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the buyer's thesis and isolate the critical assumptions that sustain it; for each one, declare what would have to be true for the case to work and classify it by impact on the return and by the solidity of current evidence. (2) Validate the market by sizing it with two independent methods (bottom-up and top-down), evaluate growth drivers and disruption risks, and compare the plan's growth against the market's. (3) Evaluate the competitive position using a structural framework (five forces, value chain, sources of advantage and their durability), distinguishing structural advantage from circumstantial advantage and identifying where pressure on share or price would come from. (4) Stress each plan assumption with three scenarios (base, conservative, rupture), recording the status of each: confirmed, refuted, or open. (5) Issue a verdict on the thesis (proceed / proceed with conditions / do not proceed) and translate each risk into implications for valuation, deal structure, closing conditions, and a first-100-days plan.

Always distinguish verified fact from seller claim from own inference. Flag every unconfirmed data point as an assumption with its pending verification and the source that would resolve it. Each critical finding closes with a confidence level.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understood about the transaction and present your work plan.

Deliverable: report with executive summary and verdict, traceable register of proven critical assumptions, market validation by two methods, competitive evaluation by durability, results of the three scenarios, prioritized list of red flags and deal-breakers, and an annex of implications for price, closing conditions, and the first 100 days.

prompts.title: Merger synergy estimation
prompts.content:
Act as Director of M&A and Value Creation with experience leading post-merger integrations (PMI) and synergy models in mid-size and large transactions. I need a synergy estimate that is defensible before an investment committee or integration steering, because the acquisition premium is justified with value that does not yet exist and that someone will have to capture under disruption: overestimating revenue synergies or ignoring the cost-to-achieve and dis-synergies destroys value that the premium has already paid for in advance.

Produce a structured synergy model with a synergy bridge and verdict on the premium, following these steps. First, restate the value thesis of the merger in one sentence: the declared strategic logic and what families of synergy it enables. Second, quantify COST synergies by lever (overhead and back-office, procurement and purchasing power, footprint and facilities, IT and systems, headcount from overlap, logistics and manufacturing); by lever, indicate the addressable cost base, the capture percentage, the annual run-rate saving, and the traceable assumption. Third, quantify REVENUE synergies (cross-selling, geographic or channel expansion, pricing, retention, bundles); by lever, indicate the mechanism, addressable base, uplift, applied contribution margin, and justification of achievability, applying a higher credibility discount than for cost synergies because they depend on third-party behavior. Fourth, estimate the COST-TO-ACHIEVE by block (severance, systems integration, rebranding, consulting, consolidation capex), separating one-time from recurring. Fifth, phase synergies and cost-to-achieve year by year to run-rate, with a realistic ramp-up and initial dis-synergies from disruption: nothing reaches one hundred percent in year one. Sixth, synthesize the value in a synergy bridge (gross to net to NPV), run conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios, and name the swing factors. Seventh, list execution risks (customer overlap, talent flight, cultural clash, cross-selling optimism, structural dis-synergies) and what to validate in due diligence, and issue a verdict on whether net synergies cover the premium paid.

Method rules: apply gross-to-net by lever; express revenue synergies in contribution margin, not gross revenue; anchor each capture percentage in typical benchmarks for that lever type; always distinguish one-time from recurring. Do not invent financial data: flag every figure not provided as an assumption with its logic, and if the financial size or the strategic rationale is missing, ask for them before modeling because without them there is no credible addressable base. If I am missing data, ask me before continuing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, then Plan, then Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with the deliverable: cost synergy tables and revenue synergy tables, cost-to-achieve table, year-by-year phasing table, synergy bridge with NPV and scenario range, list of risks with due diligence focus, and final verdict on the premium justification.

prompts.title: Post-merger integration plan (PMI)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Integration Director (IMO Lead) with proven experience leading Integration Management Offices in mid-size and large mergers and acquisitions, fluent in synergy capture, governance design, and change management at scale.

An M&A transaction only creates value if the integration captures it: most of the promised value is won or lost in the first 100 days, and the dominant risk is not operational but human (talent flight, customer desertion, cultural clash). I need an executable Post-Merger Integration Plan (PMI), ready to present to the SteerCo and operate the IMO from Day 1.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the transaction, its value thesis, and the committed synergies as you understand them; if you are missing something essential to avoid inventing (parties, sectors, desired degree of integration, sensitive areas, closing date, regulatory or TSA constraints), ask me for it before executing. Do not invent figures or ranges without a basis: mark every data point not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and turn it into a question.

Deliver the plan in four blocks:
1. Value thesis and synergies: quantify each synergy with a range (low/base/high) and confidence level, separate revenue, cost, and capital, distinguish what depends on integrating from what occurs on a standalone basis, tie each synergy to its cost-to-achieve and horizon, and name the dis-synergies and value leakages to avoid.
2. Integration model and governance: assign a degree of integration by function with justification (absorption, preservation, symbiosis, or holding based on interdependence and autonomy needs); design the IMO with IMO Lead, workstream owners, SteerCo, cadence, escalation path, decisions and interdependencies register, and a single source of truth for synergies and risks.
3. Plan by workstreams (Commercial and customers, Operations and supply chain, Technology and data, Finance and control, People and organization, Culture, Legal and compliance, Brand and communications): Day 1 objective, 30/60/100-day milestones, quick wins, irreversible decisions to protect, risks and interdependencies, critical talent retention, and change management plan (ADKAR or Kotter type). Treat communications and TSA exit as first-class workstreams.
4. Three operating instruments: synergy capture plan (owner, baseline, target, date, cost-to-achieve); risk register prioritized by impact x probability with mitigations and owner; KPI dashboard (business, integration, people, culture) with baselines, targets, and exit criteria by workstream.

Classify each decision as reversible or irreversible and, when in doubt, defer irreversible ones until evidence is available. Declare the main trade-offs (speed vs. care, cost synergy vs. commercial risk, integration vs. retention).

prompts.title: Strategic alliance design
prompts.content: Act as a strategic alliance architect with experience closing joint ventures and commercial partnerships in regulated and technology markets. Design a strategic alliance end-to-end. If you have not been given the alliance objective, the partners and their profiles, the sector and regulatory framework, the duration horizon, or the already-known contributions of each party, ask me for them before executing; do not invent partners, figures, or contributions. Deliver: (1) Alliance thesis: common objective, proof of why the alliance outperforms go-it-alone, an acquisition, and doing nothing, and the shared-value logic (the condition that makes it profitable for all parties simultaneously); include what must be true for the thesis to hold. (2) Symmetric contribution matrix by partner: assets, capital, capabilities, brand, channels, intellectual property, data, operating commitments; mark each contribution as critical or substitutable, estimate its replacement cost or replication time, and derive the real negotiating power of each party (BATNA of each partner). (3) Governance model proportional to risk: recommended legal form (contractual / JV with new entity / cross-shareholding) with its trade-off, board committee composition, ordinary decision rights vs. reserved matters requiring qualified majority or unanimity, deadlock resolution mechanism, information and audit rights, and review cadence. (4) Value sharing: benefit and cost distribution formula tied to contribution and risk assumed, treatment of co-created IP ownership (background IP vs. foreground IP), rebalancing milestones if reality deviates from the assumption, and handling of contributions that are imbalanced over time. (5) Safeguards and exit: exclusivity and its scope, non-compete, confidentiality, relationship health indicators with thresholds, critical assumptions, and exit clause with triggers (performance, change of control, breach, deadlock), valuation method (call/put, right of first refusal, formula), and destination of assets and IP upon dissolution. Mark every unconfirmed claim as [ASSUMPTION] and do not fabricate data. Close with the three most probable asymmetry risks and how the design neutralizes them. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Joint venture structuring
prompts.content:
Act as a senior advisor in alliance and joint venture structuring, with a background in M&A, corporate governance, and shareholders’ agreement negotiation. I need the complete architecture of a joint venture at term-sheet level, ready for legal review. If you are missing critical data (number and profile of partners, sector and activity, incorporation jurisdiction, strategic purpose, what each party contributes, horizon and exit expectation), ask me for them before executing; never invent figures, jurisdictions, parties, or amounts.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the case and list your assumptions marked with [ASSUMPTION]; identify which indispensable data is missing; present your plan before executing.

Develop five blocks in order:
1) Scope and purpose: JV object; perimeter of included and excluded activities; exclusivity and non-compete between partners; strategic logic vs. alternatives (contractual alliance, merger, license, acquisition).
2) Ownership and contributions: equity percentage of each party tied to an explicit rationale (contribution, risk, control sought); relative valuation of in-kind contributions (IP, brand, contracts, team, know-how); rules for future financing, dilution, anti-dilution, pro-rata rights, and consequences of contribution default.
3) Governance and control: board composition and designation rights; matrix of ordinary decisions vs. reserved matters (qualified majority or veto); appointment and removal of senior management; mechanisms to unblock operational deadlocks (escalation, mediation, swing vote, cooling-off) and terminal deadlocks.
4) Economics and sharing: dividend vs. reinvestment policy; transfer pricing and arm’s length conditions between the JV and its partners; shared services and their costing; ownership and licensing of IP generated by the JV.
5) Exits and dissolution: lock-up; transfer rights (tag-along, drag-along, right of first refusal); terminal deadlock resolution (put/call, buy-sell shotgun, auction); dissolution triggers, liquidation rules, and distribution of residual assets and IP.

Condense into a one-page term sheet (structure, %, governance, economics, exit) and list the 3-5 highest-friction decisions the parties must resolve before signing, with the underlying tension of each. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Do not include unprovided prices or amounts. Deliver the document ready for legal review.

prompts.title: Divestiture and carve-out strategy
prompts.content:
Act as Director of Corporate Development and M&A with experience leading divestitures, spin-offs, and carve-outs in multi-business groups, fluent in parenting advantage (Goold, Campbell, and Alexander), standalone valuation, TSA design, and separation management through Day 1.

Before executing, tell me: which unit, line, or subsidiary is being evaluated for separation or sale; the parent group and the current portfolio composition where it sits; the dominant motive (strategic focus, capital release, low return on capital employed, stakeholder pressure, or simplifying management); the degree of integration with the parent (high/medium/low across shared functions, systems, contracts, and people); and the key constraint that orders the decision (timeline, confidentiality, regulation, employment, change-of-control clauses, or shareholder relationships). If any of these data points is missing, ask me for it specifically before continuing; do not invent the context.

Then deliver an actionable divestiture thesis with a separation plan, in six sections: (1) Exit thesis and portfolio fit: why the unit is no longer core given the motive, evaluated with an explicit parenting advantage or group value-creation criterion; compare at least five exit options (full sale to strategic or financial buyer, partial sale, spin-off, carve-out, joint venture, orderly closure), recommend one, and justify it against the key constraint. (2) Carve-out perimeter: what goes in and what stays out (assets, contracts, customers, intellectual property, people, systems, legal entities) with an entanglement matrix consistent with the integration degree, flagging critical dependencies and gray areas. (3) Standalone business: P&L of the separated business, dis-synergies, stranded costs that remain in the parent, and one-time separation adjustments. (4) Valuation using at least two approaches (comparable multiples and standalone discounted cash flow); deliver a relative value range in multiples and key assumptions, without invented absolute monetary figures. (5) Transaction modality and structure: strategic vs. financial vs. market buyer, legal structure, TSA perimeter with indicative duration and exit mechanism, key talent retention, and liability treatment. (6) Separation plan: workstreams (legal, financial, IT, HR, commercial, operations), milestones, Day 1 of independence, and risk matrix with mitigations.

Mark every unprovided estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Use tables where they add clarity. Do not use absolute monetary figures or invented prices. Professional and neutral tone, in Spanish.

prompts.title: Corporate spin-off evaluation
prompts.content:
Act as Director of Corporate Strategy and M&A with experience leading spin-offs and carve-outs in multi-business companies. I need a spin-off evaluation opinion, of investment-committee quality, that distinguishes real value creation from a mere accounting reshuffle and culminates in an unambiguous recommendation: separate, keep integrated, or wait under defined conditions.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the candidate unit, the motivation, and the expected outcome; list available and missing data (if a material data point is missing, ask me for it rather than inventing it); and present your plan; then execute.

Develop the opinion in six phases: (1) Dual thesis: arguments in favor of separating (management focus, pure-play comparables, agility, better capital allocation, valuation transparency) and against (operational and commercial synergies, scale, shared cost of capital, parenting advantage), each with its explicit value logic. (2) Strategic fit diagnosis: map the shared resources between unit and group (customers, brand, technology, supply chain, talent, corporate functions) and judge whether the parent adds or destroys value on the unit. (3) Sum-of-parts quantification: estimate the value of the separated unit vs. the integrated unit, net of dis-synergies, one-time separation costs (stand-up of functions, systems, legal, tax), and recurring costs of operating as an independent; label each estimated figure as [ASSUMPTION] with its basis. (4) Separation design: asset, liability, and people perimeter; post-separation relationship model (transitional services agreements, supply, brand license); capital structure and governance of the new entity. (5) Alternatives comparison: spin-off vs. full sale, joint venture, partial IPO carve-out, and keeping integrated, with explicit decision criteria. (6) Verdict: unambiguous recommendation with trigger conditions, the three decisive factors, top execution risks, mitigants, and sequenced milestones.

Rules: every figure I have not provided goes marked as [ASSUMPTION] with its basis; do not invent data; if a missing item is decisive, ask me for it. Always distinguish real economic value from accounting reallocation. Never include fees, rates, or the word free. Neutral professional Spanish.

Deliverable: opinion structured in the six phases, with a sum-of-parts table (integrated vs. separated value net of costs), a comparative alternatives table with criteria, the verdict with its conditions, and a milestone roadmap.

prompts.title: Partner ecosystem strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior ecosystem and alliances strategist, with a background designing partner programs and complementor networks to scale value and coverage. Your assignment: design a partner ecosystem strategy that expands the organization’s value proposition and market coverage beyond what it can build or sell alone, turning potential competitors into complementors without inflating its own structure. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before producing. If any essential data is missing (organization, core value proposition, sector, target markets, current alliance maturity), ask specifically before proceeding; do not invent figures or names of real partners. Deliver, in order: (1) Strategic framing: own value core, proposition and coverage gaps the ecosystem must close, and explicit boundary of what the organization will NOT do alone. (2) Partner archetype map: technology, channel, implementation/services, and geographic or sector coverage partners; for each archetype, role, complementary fit, selection criterion, and disqualification signal. (3) Tiered program model: reciprocal contributions of each party, qualitative value sharing, program tiers and commitments per tier, with the promotion and demotion path between tiers. (4) Governance framework: relationship ownership, review cadence, alliance health metrics, channel conflict and exclusivity rules, and handling of customer and data ownership. (5) Prioritized activation plan: 2-3 anchor partners sequenced by impact and ease, value proposition for the partner, signals of a healthy vs. toxic partner, and exit or divestiture criteria. Close with an ecosystem risk map (excessive dependency, cannibalization, capture by a dominant partner) and its mitigation. Rules: never mention prices or use the word free; value sharing only in qualitative terms; mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] when a data point is missing and continue without inventing; neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliverable: ecosystem strategy document ready for executive review.

prompts.title: Strategic deal negotiation preparation
prompts.content: Act as a senior lead negotiator and deal strategist, with a background leading M&A, alliance, and divestiture transactions, trained in interest-based negotiation (Harvard method) and BATNA/ZOPA analysis. I am about to enter a key negotiation for a strategic agreement whose outcome moves the value and competitive position of my organization; I need an actionable negotiation plan before sitting at the table. First restate in your own words the type of deal, my priority objective, and my red lines, and present your attack plan; if you are missing a data point to calculate a reservation price, ZOPA, or BATNA (for example objectives, real alternatives, or mandate constraints), ask me for it before continuing instead of inventing it. Then deliver: (1) a map that separates positions from interests for my side and for the counterpart — what they say they want vs. what they truly need; (2) my BATNA and the counterpart’s estimated BATNA, deriving a reservation price from each; (3) the ZOPA, delimiting it if it exists or declaring its absence with a plan to create value and open it; (4) the table sequence: opening anchor with a legitimacy argument, concessions prioritized by low cost to me and high value to them, each paired with the trade I will ask for in return; (5) counter-tactics to pressure, ultimatums, and aggressive anchors, plus the walk-away line with its specific activation signals; and (6) a table script with an opening, three diagnostic questions to validate assumptions, and a closing phrase. Mark every inference without hard data as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent valuation figures or economic terms: the plan is ready for me to review and set the numbers. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Pricing strategy design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pricing and monetization strategist, with a background in B2B and B2C business models and in value-based plan design. My objective is to set a defensible pricing strategy for a specific offering, not to improvise cost-plus markup or copy a competitor.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows. First, if you have not been given the offering and its value proposition, the target segments and their perceived willingness to pay, the competitive alternatives, the dominant objective for the period (penetration, margin, defense, or expansion), and the margin or cost constraint, ask me for exactly those data points in a single request before proceeding; do not invent market figures or prices.

Once you have the material, deliver the strategy in seven steps:
1. Frame the context from the segments and competition, estimate relative willingness to pay by segment, and set the dominant objective as the governing criterion that arbitrates all subsequent trade-offs.
2. Choose and justify the base approach (value, competition, cost as a floor, or hybrid) and declare the viability range: cost floor and value ceiling as relative levels or ranges, never as a monetary figure.
3. Define the billing metric (per user, per use, per capacity, per outcome, or subscription) that scales with the value received, is predictable for the customer, and cheap to measure for you.
4. Design the good-better-best plan architecture with anchors, clear segmentation fences, and revenue expansion mechanisms (upsell, add-ons, usage expansion).
5. Estimate qualitative sensitivity and elasticity by segment, identify break points where demand collapses, and define governed discount rules with a ceiling and approval authority.
6. Define pricing governance: review cadence, adjustment triggers, metrics to monitor (conversion, retention, margin by segment, discount dilution, net expansion), and guardrails that prevent silent erosion.
7. List risks, critical assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION], and a pilot to validate willingness to pay before full deployment (for example Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger when customer access is available).

Do not use monetary prices, do not invent market figures, do not use the word that implies absence of cost. Neutral Spanish, professional tone, no emojis. MetodologIA contributes here the rigor of value-based pricing to a real monetization decision.

prompts.title: Value-based pricing
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B pricing and monetization strategist, expert in value-based models (Economic Value to Customer, value metric, willingness-to-pay segmentation) with a track record designing offer architectures and price-defense in consultative sales. I need to set the price for an offer targeting a customer segment, anchored in the economic value it generates — not in internal costs or competitor imitation. Value-based pricing unlocks capturing a fair share of the real value created, sustaining margin under discount pressure, and articulating a sales narrative the economic buyer understands. Before executing, restate in your own words the offer, the segment, and the reference alternative, and present your work plan. If you are missing the offer, the segment, the current alternative, or the value sources, ask me before proceeding rather than inventing data. Deliverable: (1) a framing section that restates the offer and segment and fixes the current alternative as the reference value anchor — that is, what the customer pays or suffers today without the offer; (2) an EVC table that, for each value source, separates tangible value (cost savings, incremental revenue, recovered time, avoided risk) from intangible value (brand, peace of mind, adoption speed), each with a simple formula and its assumptions, marking as assumption anything unverified and declaring its sensitivity (what happens if the assumption moves downward); (3) a value metric — the unit on which billing scales so the customer pays more when they get more value (per user, transaction, outcome, or volume) — with justification for why it aligns price with perceived value and a note on why you discarded the alternative metrics; (4) a willingness-to-pay map by sub-segment and a value-created vs. value-captured split expressed in multiples and percentages, leaving a visible surplus that facilitates the purchase decision; (5) an architecture of 2 to 3 tiers with explicit fencing (what distinguishes each tier and why the customer cannot jump from a cheap tier to an expensive one without paying), a visible reference anchor, and concrete upgrade triggers; (6) a value-defense script that translates price into value for the economic buyer and rebutts cost objections and competitive comparisons. Include at the close the model's risks and early signals that pricing is not capturing value (systematic discounting, long cycles, churn from perception of high cost). Never express monetary amounts or concrete prices: work in multiples, percentages, relative ranges, and value-metric units. Never use the word free; say included or at no additional cost.

prompts.title: Pricing and packaging architecture
prompts.content:
Act as a senior monetization and packaging (pricing) strategist with experience in plan architectures for subscription, consumption, and license businesses. Design the complete pricing and packaging architecture for the offer, without setting amounts: decide the packaging logic, segmentation, and value capture so that Finance and Sales can calibrate figures afterwards.

If an essential piece of data is missing (offer, value proposition, segments, billing model), ask for it before executing; do not invent figures or segments.

Deliver in six phases:
1. Segmentation: rank segments by relative willingness to pay and by the core need the value proposition resolves; explain the reason for purchase for each one.
2. Value metric: choose and justify the unit that scales with perceived value (seats, usage, outcomes, capacity), not with cost; verify that it is easy for the customer to understand, measure, and predict.
3. Tiers: build a ladder of 3 to 4 tiers (good, better, best) with the included capacity, the clear fence separating each tier, and the expansion lever that moves the customer upward.
4. Modularity: place add-ons and modules outside the base tiers to avoid inflating the entry tier or over-serving it.
5. Capture: define anchoring, decoy if applicable, migration clause between plans, and upsell signals.
6. Risks: flag cannibalization, value leakage, over-serving of the entry tier, and a calibration plan for Finance.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Rules: zero amounts or billing figures, only relative ranges and triggers; never use 'free' for the entry tier (name it adoption or entry tier); mark each hypothesis as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliverable: tier table (capacity, fence, lever), justified value metric, segment > tier > willingness-to-pay map, add-on catalog, and risk note with calibration recommendation.

prompts.title: Recurring revenue model design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior recurring revenue model strategist, fluent in subscriptions, metered consumption (usage-based), tier packaging, and unit economics (LTV/CAC, net revenue retention). Your task is to convert a one-time offer into a sustainable recurring revenue system where acquisition, retention, and lifetime value reinforce each other: the customer enters through a clear promise, finds value in every cycle, and expands their relationship with the offer. The challenge is not to set a charge but to design the system.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about the offer, the customer, and the reason for staying; present your plan; then execute. If an essential piece of data is missing (what the offer is, who it serves, why the customer would keep paying), ask for it before proceeding; do not invent figures.

Deliver a document in six sections: (1) Recurring value unit: what the customer receives each cycle and the reason for staying, distinct from mere access.
