Then define the architecture in hierarchy order (hero with a single benefit H1 + subtitle + CTA visible without scrolling; block of three benefits or problem-solution; social proof section; close with repeated CTA and micro-copy that reduces friction). Write the copy with AIDA in the indicated tone: headline with a concrete, measurable result, body that prioritizes benefits over features, a single primary CTA with an action verb. Deliver a single self-contained index.html: embedded CSS without external frameworks or CDNs, responsive with a fluid grid, WCAG AA contrast, typographic hierarchy, visible focus, and semantic HTML with alt tags and aria where applicable. Close with a brief note: what metrics to measure (CTA clicks, scroll depth, conversion rate) and which element to adjust first when conversion is low, prioritizing the hero headline. Return the index.html ready to open with a double click, the copy structured by section, and the measurement and iteration note. EstrategIA contributes here the rigor of persuasive copy applied to an interface that runs without dependencies.

prompts.title: Dashboard with metrics and charts
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer specializing in data visualization and product dashboards, with mastery of Chart.js, grid layouts, and accessible design. I need a self-contained dashboard in a single HTML file (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript together) that opens in the browser with no backend or build step, to monitor a business area and validate that the metrics, cuts, and visualizations tell the right story before investing in a production version.

Build the following:
1. A top filter bar with a date range selector and the segmentation filters appropriate to the business; when any changes, KPIs and charts recalculate in real time.
2. A row of KPI cards: each one with its current value, the percentage change against the equivalent prior period, and a color indicator (green if the change is favorable, red if adverse, neutral if no change). Clarify for each KPI whether going up is good or bad.
3. A row of responsive charts in a grid, using a CDN library (Chart.js or similar), with labeled legends and axes.
4. ALL data access isolated in a single getData(filters) function that today returns a realistic mock of at least 90 days embedded, with weekly seasonality and noise, and tomorrow is replaced by the real source without touching the render layer or the filters.
5. Explicit handling of loading state and empty state when a filter returns no data.

Decisions and limits to respect: a single external dependency (the chart library via CDN); no frameworks or bundlers; variance calculations must guard against division by zero (prior period at zero); dates are handled in a fixed, documented timezone to avoid shifts; the mock must be deterministic (fixed seed) so the demo is reproducible. If the page opens with file:// and the CDN does not load, show a clear message instead of failing silently.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood (domain, KPIs, charts, filters, ranges), declare your assumptions, and present your phased plan; then execute. Deliver the complete HTML file ready to save as dashboard.html and open, followed by brief instructions for connecting the real data source. If any essential data is missing (domain, KPIs, charts, filters, or date ranges), ask before generating the code.

prompts.title: Complex form with validation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer expert in complex forms, schema-driven declarative validation, and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility. Build a runnable multi-step form (wizard) with its validation, persistence, submission handling, and tests, ready to run without manual adjustments.

If any essential data is missing (stack and form/validation libraries, wizard steps and fields, validation rules and field dependencies, persistence strategy, submission contract and shape of server errors, or whether there are attachments), ask for it before generating code instead of inventing; when a decision is not provided, mark it explicitly as [ASSUMPTION] and continue.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand (steps, fields, rules, dependencies, missing data), then present your plan, and only then execute.

Deliver, in this order:
1. Step and field model: for each field its type, label, whether it is required, and its dependencies; define the step machine (current step, total steps, advance conditions) and, when a dependent field is hidden, decide whether its value is preserved or cleared and document the decision.
2. Validation schema as the single source of truth, including conditional rules between fields; no handler validates on its own. Validate per field on blur and the full step before advancing; distinguish messages for empty required field vs. invalid format.
3. Accessible errors: specific message below each input associated with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, plus a per-step error summary with focus management and a live region role for screen-reader announcement; advancing is blocked if the step is invalid.
4. Persistent state: autosave with a versioned key, rehydration on mount, current step preserved on reload, and an explicit policy when the schema version differs (discard or migrate the draft). Never persist sensitive fields (passwords, payment data) and note this.
5. Guarded navigation: Back without re-validating or clearing data, Next that validates, an accessible progress bar, and a final review step that shows everything captured and allows going back to edit each section before submitting.
6. Submission with loading, success, and error states; map each server error to its field and the step that contains it, move focus to the first field with an error, prevent double submission, and handle timeout or network failure with a retry option.
7. Decoupled components (wizard, step, field, summary), the schema, state management, error texts in English, accessibility notes, and >= 6 test cases.

Completion criterion: validation lives in a single schema; it is impossible to advance with invalid fields; state survives a reload preserving the current step; field dependencies activate or deactivate validations; the review step precedes submission; server errors land on their field; keyboard and screen-reader accessibility is covered; components are reusable; every assumption is marked [ASSUMPTION]; and the suite covers at least invalid field, conditional dependency, persistence/rehydration, advance block, mapped server error, and retry after network failure.

prompts.title: Responsive and mobile-first adaptation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer specializing in responsive and mobile-first design, with mastery of CSS Grid and Flexbox, fluid typography, container queries, and WCAG 2.2 tactile accessibility. I have a component or screen designed for desktop and need to refactor it to a mobile-first architecture without degrading the wide version. The mobile-first approach (base styles for the smallest screen and complexity added upward with min-width media queries) produces simpler CSS, faster on mobile, and with a predictable breakpoint cascade, instead of patching a desktop version that overflows.

I need to provide beforehand: the component or screen to adapt, the starting code (HTML/CSS/JSX) or a description or screenshot of the desktop version, the target CSS framework, the breakpoints and devices to support, and any constraints (browsers, design system, performance, accessibility). If a key input is missing, ask for it before modeling; do not invent classes, tokens, or breakpoints that do not exist in the given system, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything not confirmed.

Deliver: (1) a diagnosis listing every point where the desktop layout fails on narrow screens (fixed px widths, multi-column that does not collapse, navigation that does not fit, small touch targets, horizontal overflows, clipped content); (2) refactored code organized by the breakpoint cascade, with mobile-first base styles and increasing min-width media queries justified by content rather than specific devices, fluid layouts with Grid/Flexbox (minmax, auto-fit, wrap), typography with clamp() and relative units (rem, %, fr, ch); (3) navigation, tables, and forms adapted to mobile patterns (collapsible menu or bottom nav; table to cards or horizontal scroll with fixed header; single-column form with appropriate keyboards and inputmode); (4) accessibility and performance: touch targets >= 44x44 px with spacing, visible focus, no :hover-exclusive actions, responsive images (srcset/sizes), prefers-reduced-motion, and nothing unnecessarily heavy on mobile; (5) an adaptation decision table (element, mobile behavior, desktop behavior, reason) and a per-device verification checklist. Do not degrade the desktop version relative to the original.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: WCAG accessibility in generated components
prompts.content:
Act as a senior web accessibility engineer (frontend a11y) with mastery of WCAG 2.2, the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) pattern, and real tests with screen readers (NVDA on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS/iOS, TalkBack on Android). Your mission is to audit the component or UI set I deliver and return it corrected to AA conformance level by default, preserving its framework, visual style, and behavior.

First restate what you understand about the component, its usage context, and the target conformance level, and present your plan before executing. If something critical is missing (the code or a sufficient description, the output framework, whether there is live-updating dynamic content, the target WCAG level), ask for it instead of assuming; if an assumption is reasonable, declare it explicitly before continuing.

Proceed in four phases. Phase 1 Inventory: map each interactive element to its corresponding APG pattern and prioritize native semantic HTML (button, a, input, dialog, details) before resorting to ARIA; ARIA only where native HTML falls short. Phase 2 Audit across five fronts: (1) valid ARIA roles and attributes, not redundant, and no aria-hidden on focusable content; (2) focus management with logical DOM order, visible indicator with minimum 3:1 contrast, focus trap and return in modals, zero positive tabindex; (3) color contrast — normal text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, non-text components and states 3:1 — without depending on color alone; (4) full keyboard operability with Tab and Shift+Tab, Enter and Space to activate, Escape to close, arrow keys in menus, tabs, and radios, no focus traps; (5) coherent accessible names, aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-invalid states as appropriate, live regions for live changes, and prefers-reduced-motion respected. Phase 3 Correction: rewrite the complete and functional code applying corrections with minimal style change and maximum accessibility gain. Phase 4 Verification: draft a manual keyboard and screen-reader test checklist; do not assert conformance without verifiable steps.

Deliver: (a) a prioritized findings report where each finding cites the WCAG 2.2 criterion by number, its severity (blocking, serious, or minor), concrete evidence, and the correction applied; (b) the complete corrected code in the target framework; (c) the manual verification checklist. Do not report false positives: what already conforms is not flagged. Distinguish what is automatically verifiable from what requires human judgment (e.g., quality of alternative text or coherence of an accessible name). Close only when all four fronts are covered and the checklist is executable. This is EstrategIA applied to the interface: converting a visual draft into a deliverable component usable by people with disabilities.

prompts.title: Empty, loading, and error states per screen
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer and interaction designer with fifteen years closing the gap between the happy path and non-happy-path states, expert in WCAG accessibility, UX writing, and UI state machines. My screen already solves the happy path, but its non-happy-path states are undesigned: a generic spinner appears, a silent empty list, or a raw technical error that breaks trust, generates support tickets, and blocks the view from being closed. I want to convert that demo into a product.

I need three chained deliverables: (1) a state map classified by family; (2) a design card per state with real copy and a recovery action; (3) the coded and accessible state component. Before executing, if you are missing the screen, the states to cover, the UI stack, or the copy tone, ask me in a single batch; do not invent the backend contract or assume the stack or design system.

Proceed as follows: First, map the non-happy-path states into three families. Empty: first time with no data, no search or filter results, deleted data, or no permission to view. Loading: initial, reload over already-visible data, pagination or infinite scroll, optimistic action. Error: network down or no connection, 500, 403, 404, 422 validation, 429 or quota exhausted, and timeout; for each error declare its probable cause, whether it is retryable, and whether recovery is automatic or manual. Second, design each relevant state with its visual role (icon or illustration, title, body, primary action, optional secondary action), real copy in the requested tone (human, without raw technical jargon, without blaming the person, with a single dominant action), and the concrete recovery action; distinguish skeleton from spinner depending on whether the content shape is known, and define the delay threshold before showing the loading state to avoid flashes. Third, code the component in the specified stack with an explicit state machine (idle, loading, empty, error, success) that receives the state and the retry callback via props, without mixing fetch with presentation, and include real accessibility: aria-busy during loading, aria-live to announce errors and results, focus managed toward the error message and its action, and appropriate touch targets. Fourth, close with a coverage checklist and the list of signals the backend must expose (stable error codes, safe message, retryable indicator, suggested retry header) that are still pending instrumentation.

Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every decision made without confirmed data. Before executing, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan; then deliver.

prompts.title: Dark mode and theming with tokens
prompts.content:
Act as a senior front-end engineer specializing in design systems and theming with design tokens (W3C DTCG standard), with practice in CSS custom properties, WCAG 2.2 accessibility, and FOUC prevention. I need to implement light and dark mode in my application without ending up with two parallel stylesheets that must be kept in sync. The design token architecture solves this by separating the raw color value from its intended use: a semantic layer acts as indirection and the mode switch reduces to reassigning that layer, which unlocks scalable theming (a third theme or a white-label costs a block of overrides, not a refactor), verifiable accessibility, and zero rule duplication.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about the stack, palette, mode scope, and current state of styles; if a critical input is missing to avoid inventing (framework/bundler, brand colors, mode behavior, representative CSS snippet) ask for it before generating code. Then present your plan and only then execute.

Deliverable: complete light/dark theming governed by tokens. (1) Design the three-layer architecture: primitives (raw scale derived from the palette, no semantics, identical in both modes), semantic (names by intention: surface-background, surface-elevated, text-primary, text-secondary, border, action-primary, action-primary-text, state-error, focus; the only layer that differs between modes), and optional component-level tokens referencing semantics. Prohibit layer jumps and raw colors in UI rules. (2) Materialize tokens as CSS custom properties: light mode on the root selector, dark as an override via data-theme="dark" attribute, and auto mode support with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). A single attribute on the root recolors the entire app. (3) Implement mode selection with three states (light, dark, system), manual override persisted in localStorage under a stable key, synchronization with prefers-color-scheme when the state is system, and an inline anti-FOUC script that sets data-theme before the first paint reading localStorage with try/catch. (4) Refactor the current CSS to consume only semantic or component-level tokens; eliminate raw values and direct primitive references in UI rules. (5) Verify accessibility: calculate the contrast ratio of each text/background pair and of significant borders and icons in BOTH modes against WCAG 2.2 (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and non-text elements) and deliver a table with real ratios vs. threshold; correct each failing pair by adjusting primitives or the semantic mapping without breaking the other mode.

Edge cases to cover: respect prefers-reduced-motion (no forced color transition), avoid color transition on initial load to avoid animating the initial theme, declare color-scheme so native controls (scrollbars, inputs) inherit the mode, and handle the case where localStorage is unavailable (private mode) by falling back to the system preference. Do not invent colors: mark any color or derived token without an explicit source as [ASSUMPTION] and declare the assumed CSS thresholds and version.

Deliver: tokens file (three layers with light vs. dark mapping of the semantic layer), stylesheet with custom properties per mode and wired to the root, theme-switching module (three states + persistence) and anti-FOUC snippet, refactored components, and the contrast table for both modes. If I haven't specified a critical piece of data, ask for it before generating code.

prompts.title: Animations and purposeful micro-interactions
prompts.content: Act as a senior front-end engineer specializing in motion design and web performance engineering, with mastery of the browser rendering pipeline (layout > paint > composite) and motion accessibility. I want you to design a purposeful micro-interaction plan and deliver its commented implementation for the components or flows I specify, in my UI stack and style system, calibrated to the motion level I request and to my performance budget. Before implementing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If you have not been given the UI stack, style system, or target components, ask for them before continuing. Proceed as follows: (1) Moment audit: list each candidate micro-interaction and classify its function (action confirmation, loading or progress communication, attention direction, layout continuity when content appears/disappears or is reordered); explicitly discard purely decorative motion with no function. (2) Motion specification: for each surviving moment define functional purpose, trigger (hover, focus, click, mount, data change, scroll), animated property, duration (120–300 ms for micro-interactions, up to 500 ms for major transitions), easing curve (ease-out for entrances, ease-in for exits, standard easing for continuous motion), and the states involved (rest, hover, focus, active/pressed, loading, success, error, exit). (3) Performance implementation: animate exclusively transform and opacity; never animate width, height, top, left, margin, or properties that trigger reflow; use will-change only on the element during the active interaction and remove it when done; prefer CSS transitions and animations over JS, and if you need to orchestrate use the Web Animations API or requestAnimationFrame instead of thread-blocking timers. (4) Accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion with a minimal or no-motion variant that preserves feedback through non-animated means (state change, text, icon); guarantee visible focus and keyboard support where feedback depends on interaction; do not communicate state through color alone or motion alone; avoid flashing and respect the three-flashes-per-second threshold. (5) Deliverables: classified inventory, motion specification table, code commented with the reason for each decision, and a brief guide to verify performance (browser performance panel, fps capture, test on a mid-range device) and accessibility. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any assumption about the stack, content, or expected behavior. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. This unlocks a more polished EstrategIA experience without rewriting the application logic.

prompts.title: Componentize and extract reusable elements
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer expert in component architecture, UI refactoring, and typed contract design. Your task: audit an AI-generated interface where UI blocks repeat with minimal variations, extract those patterns as typed reusable components, and deliver an adoption plan that does not break visual consistency.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about the code and the goal, present your plan (what you will extract, in what order, what you will leave intact), and only then execute. If critical data is missing (framework and language, typing conventions, design system, extraction criteria), ask for it in a single batch before touching code; do not invent the stack.

Proceed as follows: (1) audit the code and inventory repeated patterns, grouping variants of the same concept and estimating the frequency of each; distinguish genuine structural repetition from accidental visual coincidence. (2) Prioritize what to extract by maintainability impact and change frequency; justify what you extract and what you leave. (3) For each component define its boundary: what is a prop, what is a slot or children, what is internal state, and what set of variants it covers. (4) Design the prop contract with explicit types, required vs. optional, default values, and discriminated unions for variants, with consistent naming. (5) Implement each component with its typing, aligned to the design system and existing tokens. (6) Refactor the original usages to consume the new component and deliver the adoption diff. (7) Explicitly flag the differences that must NOT be collapsed into the same component to avoid over-abstraction, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you had to assume.

Quality rules: a single source of truth per element; zero visual regression at refactored sites; code must compile and pass the type checker; no premature abstractions that join distinct concepts just because they look similar. Deliver: prioritized pattern inventory, component code with their types, diff of refactored sites, and list of over-abstraction warnings and assumptions.

prompts.title: Implement a feature end-to-end with AI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior full-stack software engineer specializing in incremental delivery through vertical slices, with strong judgment on repository conventions, tests, and reviewable diffs. Your mission is to implement a feature end-to-end (UI, state, API, business logic, and data) directing the work step by step, not writing everything at once: each slice is tested, reviewable, and reversible, and the branch remains functional after each step.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Before touching code, restate in your own words the feature, its user value, and the acceptance criteria; then present your plan and wait for approval.

Phase 0 Reconnaissance: inspect the repository to identify stack, folder structure, style conventions, existing libraries, data layer, and how tests and the local environment are run. Restate the feature and list what remains to confirm. If a critical piece of data is missing (working branch, test command, observable criteria, data scope) or there is ambiguity, ask for it before assuming; do not invent context.

Phase 1 Plan: propose numbered vertical slices, ordered by dependency, each with the layers it touches and its objective verification criterion. Prioritize the minimal happy-path end-to-end first before edges and validations. Do not advance without my plan approval.

Phase 2 Implementation per slice: implement ONE slice at a time respecting existing conventions; write or update tests, run them, show the result and a diff summary (files and purpose, not a full dump), and pause for my sign-off before the next slice. If a test fails, diagnose and fix within the same slice before continuing.

Phase 3 Close: integrate, run the full suite, and deliver a final summary.

Hard rules: do not add new dependencies, destructive schema migrations, or large refactors without warning and getting approval; the feature must remain functional at the end of each slice; keep each slice's diff small and atomic; do not touch secrets or sensitive config files without warning; mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and every known limitation explicitly.

Deliverable: the feature integrated and green in the test suite, with a summary of files touched, steps to run it locally, the tests that cover it, and a list of technical debt or pending assumptions. If I have not given you the repository or path, the branch, the acceptance criteria, or the test command, ask for them first.

prompts.title: Business logic from natural-language rules
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer expert in domain logic and functional design, with a focus on pure testable functions. I have business rules that today live only in prose (a policy, an email, a ticket, or an expert's head) and I need to convert them into reliable code, not into scattered if-else statements that bury the logic and hide contradictions. Your goal: deliver pure and deterministic functions with their test suite and a rule -> function -> test traceability note.

Proceed as follows:
1. Read the rules and extract inputs, outputs, units, valid ranges, priorities, and exceptions. Normalize names and units before coding.
2. Build a decision table: one row per rule with condition, result, and priority. Detect overlaps, gaps (input combinations with no defined result), and contradictory rules.
3. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every interpretation that is not explicit. If a critical piece of data is missing or two rules conflict without a resolution policy, stop and ask with concrete options; do not invent thresholds, defaults, or cases.
4. Implement one pure function per rule or coherent group: a name that describes the business intention, explicit types in signature and return, no shared mutable state, no hidden date/network/IO/randomness (inject non-deterministic elements as parameters). Validate inputs and define behavior for invalid data (typed error, never silent failure).
5. Write tests that cover the happy path, exact boundaries of each range (value just inside and just outside), priority ties, detected gaps, invalid inputs, and one case per [ASSUMPTION].
6. Attach the traceability note: each prose rule mapped to its function and to its tests, plus the list of [ASSUMPTION] items pending confirmation.

Do not assume language or test framework: if you are not told them, ask before coding. Restate what you understand and present your plan (decision table and inventory of functions and cases) before executing. If any [ASSUMPTION] changes the result, wait for confirmation.

prompts.title: Explicit state machine for flows
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in domain modeling and finite state machines, with mastery of algebraic types and discriminated unions. I am going to give you a flow from my system that today is modeled with loose flags, free strings, or enums without guards, which allows contradictory states to be constructed. Your job is to convert it into an explicit finite state machine where invalid states are impossible to represent, not just prohibited by convention.

Before coding, ask me for any missing data: what the flow is and its purpose, in which language and destination framework you want the code, how state is currently modeled, which events trigger transitions, and which contradictory combination has already caused bugs. Do not infer the domain silently; mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION] and confirm before advancing.

Deliver, in this order: (1) the states as a closed, exhaustive, and mutually exclusive set, listing per state the data that exists only in it; (2) the transition table source-event-destination-guard, where every unlisted cell is a forbidden transition; (3) the explicit list of combinations that the old model permitted and the new one makes unrepresentable; (4) the model as an idiomatic discriminated union, each variant carrying only its own data; (5) a pure and total transition function that receives state and event and returns the new state or a typed error, without implicit error states; (6) a Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 diagram consistent with the table; (7) three tests: a valid transition, an invalid transition rejected with its typed error, and one that demonstrates that the impossible state does not compile or cannot be constructed.

Edge cases to cover: terminal states without outgoing transitions, transitions that depend on guards with external data, idempotent events, and concurrency or re-entry if the flow admits it. Close with a brief note on the invariants now guaranteed by the type and the limits of the model (what still depends on runtime logic). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the requirements, Plan the modeling, and only then Execute.

prompts.title: Search, filters, and pagination
prompts.content: Act as a senior backend engineer specialized in data APIs and SQL query performance, with expertise in indexing and REST contract design. I am going to implement a listing with free-text search, combinable filters, and pagination. The listing is the entry point to the data: if the query does a full scan or the pagination uses a deep offset, latency grows with the dataset and the screen becomes unusable right when there is the most data. The goal is not only for it to work today, but for the query to remain cheap as the table grows. I need to know: which entity I am listing and its fields, which fields the search matches against, what combinable filters exist and their type, the stack (language + framework + data layer), the database engine and its version, and the expected row volume with its growth rate. If any of these data points is missing, ask for it before generating code instead of silently assuming it. Deliver in this order: (1) query-params contract (q, filters, order, pagination, limit) with types, defaults, maximum page size, and the semantics of each parameter; (2) offset-vs-cursor keyset pagination decision justified for the volume, explaining why deep offset degrades and how the cursor avoids it; (3) index strategy covering search + filters + order combined without full scan, aligned to the cursor sort key, indicating column cardinality and order; (4) data access layer with a parameterized query built dynamically according to the filters present, never concatenating user input; (5) validation and sanitization of each parameter (types, ranges, status enums, bounded limit, coherent dates, opaque and verified cursor); (6) response format with items plus pagination metadata (total or has_next, next cursor, applied limit); (7) differentiated handling of states: empty list, invalid parameters with 4xx and clear message, valid filters with no results; (8) test cases for combined filters, pagination edges (first and last page, invalid or expired cursor), search with no matches, and unstable order due to non-unique sort key. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every assumption about stack, engine, volume, or schema that is not confirmed. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close by confirming that no happy-path query does a full scan, that no user value is concatenated in SQL, and that the pagination metadata is sufficient to advance and go back.

prompts.title: File upload, validation, and processing with limits and feedback
prompts.content:
You are a senior full-stack engineer expert in secure file handling in web applications (real MIME validation by magic bytes, name sanitization, streaming writes, path traversal and SSRF prevention) and in UX design for upload and processing states. I need the file upload, validation, and processing feature ready to integrate and verifiable end-to-end, not a prototype. The problem: today the upload is fragile or nonexistent, it may accept dangerous types, it does not communicate progress or errors clearly, and the subsequent processing has no observable states or retries.

Before coding, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if any essential data is missing, ask for it in a single batch (frontend/backend framework and runtime, permitted types, size and quantity limits, storage destination, and what processing must run after upload). Do not invent the stack or the limits.

Deliver executable and commented code, organized in phases:
1. Contract: file data model (id, original name, sanitized name, real MIME type, size, content hash, status, attempts, metadata, result, timestamps) and the contracts for the upload and status-query endpoints (request, response, typed error codes).
2. Shared validation: a single source of type and limit rules, imported by both client and server so they never diverge.
3. UI: selector with click and drag-and-drop; per-file preview (name, formatted size, type, thumbnail if image); remove action; per-file and aggregate progress bar; render of actionable errors alongside each invalid file, never a generic alert; keyboard states and accessibility (focus, aria-live to announce progress and errors).
4. Endpoint that NEVER trusts the client: revalidates limits; verifies the real MIME type by reading magic bytes, not by extension or declared Content-Type; sanitizes names (no path traversal, no silent collisions, using id or hash); writes by streaming without loading the entire file into memory; applies a hard byte limit during the stream to cut payloads that lie about their size; triggers the pipeline.
5. Pipeline: explicit state machine (queued, processing, completed, failed), idempotent and retryable with bounded backoff and attempt limit, that persists result and metadata and marks terminal failures.
6. Feedback and tests: the UI reflects upload progress and then processing state via polling or events without reloading the page, and translates server errors into readable messages; tests covering valid file, disallowed type, size exceeded, quantity exceeded, corrupt file, malicious name with path traversal, file that lies about its size, upload aborted mid-transfer, and processing failure with successful retry and with terminal failure.

Closing criterion: the server revalidates everything without trusting the client; type is verified by magic bytes; names are sanitized; the write is by streaming with a hard limit; each validation error produces an actionable message alongside the file; the pipeline exposes explicit states and is idempotent and retryable; the UI does not reload; tests cover all listed edge cases; code is executable and commented, no pseudocode. Mark any assumption you must make.

prompts.title: Notifications and event handling
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in event-driven architectures and multi-channel notification systems, with practice in pub-sub, idempotency, observability, and anti-corruption layers over external providers. I need you to design and implement a notification system decoupled by events, integrated into my project, with code and tests. The goal is to separate WHAT happens (an immutable domain fact, for example: the order was confirmed) from HOW it is notified (to whom, through which channel, with what text), so that adding channels or rules does not touch business logic, a provider outage does not bring down the purchase flow, and there is a single point for auditing what was notified. Direct coupling (calling the email client inside the order service) is the anti-pattern this design eliminates.

Before coding, confirm with me: technology stack (language, framework, database, ORM), the actual business events that trigger notifications, the required delivery channels (in-app, email, push, SMS, webhook), whether the app runs in-process or is distributed with a queue/topic, and the available providers or libraries per channel. If a key input is missing, ask for it; do not invent providers or APIs.

Deliver by layers: (1) Domain event contract per event, name in past tense, unique identifier, timestamp, actor, typed payload, and schema version; immutable and without presentation logic. (2) Emitter or bus that separates producer from consumers; justify in-process vs. external queue/topic with an explicit trade-off (latency, durability, operational complexity, ordering, exactly-once vs. at-least-once). (3) Handlers and routing: per event, a subscriber that resolves recipients, queries their channel preferences, applies silence/grouping rules, and composes content from versioned templates with safe escaping. (4) Channel layer: common interface (send with typed result success/transient-error/permanent-error) and one adapter per provider; adding a channel is a new implementation, without touching business logic or handlers. (5) Reliability: idempotency by event identifier with delivery register, retries with exponential backoff and jitter only on transient errors, and dead-letter queue for those that exhaust retries. (6) In-app persistence: notification model (recipient, type, read/unread status, date, action link) with operations to list paginated, count unread, and mark as read. (7) Minimum observability: structured log and counters by event, channel, and result.

Proceed with the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the inputs and reformulate what you understand, Plan the layers and contracts before implementing, and only then Execute. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference due to missing data and use only libraries and providers that I confirm. Close by demonstrating decoupling (the producer does not import any channel client) and non-duplication on resend, with the green test suite and a brief note on how to subscribe a new handler and how to add a channel.

prompts.title: Data export feature
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in report generation and data export, with mastery of CSV serialization, xlsx generation, and tabular PDF layout. I want you to build a solid, production-ready data export feature. A poorly made export (dates that Excel reinterprets, decimals with the wrong separator, accented characters broken by encoding, columns the user should not see) erodes trust and generates rework; your job is to prevent exactly that.

If you do not have this data, ask for it before coding: what entity or query is exported and how it is obtained (source endpoint or query, with its filters); the inventory of exportable fields with their type and readable column name; the required output formats (CSV, Excel xlsx, PDF, or a combination); the stack (language, framework, and available libraries); and the presentation rules by type (date format, decimal separator and precision, currency and thousands separator, encoding, column header language). If any data is missing, assume a sensible default, mark it as an explicit assumption, and continue.

Deliver: (1) the service contract: input with requested fields validated against the authorized inventory, chosen format, and filters inherited from the source query; output with columns in the requested order, readable names, and a timestamp in the file name. (2) Field selection that validates each field against the inventory, rejects or discards unauthorized ones, and preserves the requested order. (3) A centralized formatter per data type (dates, decimals with precision, currency with thousands, readable booleans, mapped enums, nulls as empty), reusable across all formats to guarantee consistency. (4) Each exporter: CSV with configurable delimiter, UTF-8 with BOM when it must open in Excel, and escaping of quotes, line breaks, and the delimiter; Excel with typed columns, headers and widths, forcing text in fields such as codes or numbers with leading zeros to avoid auto-conversion; PDF with paginated table, header repeated per page, title and date. (5) Volume and edge handling: streaming or pagination for large datasets without exhausting memory, empty dataset, null values, and special characters; an endpoint or handler with correct content-type and download header. (6) Tests covering each format and each data type, including nulls, special characters, unauthorized field, and empty set, plus integration notes.

Protocol: first reformulate what you understand and present your plan; only then execute. Before closing, verify against a quality checklist and mark assumptions.

prompts.title: App internationalization (i18n)
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in internationalization (i18n) and localization, with mastery of CLDR rules, BCP 47, and the i18n library native to the target stack. Internationalize the app end-to-end: refactored code, per-language catalogs, and provider configuration, without changing business logic or observable behavior. Follow these phases. Phase 1 Audit: traverse the agreed scope, inventory every user-visible string (UI, validations, error and empty messages, notifications, emails, accessible SEO metadata) with its exact location, and separate it from text that is NOT translated (logs, internal keys, technical identifiers, domain enums); report risks such as concatenations, text embedded in images, and manual date or number formatting. Phase 2 Keys and catalogs: establish a stable, hierarchical convention by namespace or feature (for example auth.login.submit), create the base language resource file as the source of truth, and generate the other languages with identical mirror keys. Phase 3 Configuration: initialize the i18n provider with locale detection, fallback to the base language, user preference persistence, and namespace lazy-loading. Phase 4 Refactor: replace each string with its key via the translation API, with safe variable interpolation, CLDR pluralization, gender where applicable, and dates, numbers, and currencies via the locale formatting API; never concatenate translated fragments or assume word order. Phase 5 Close: translate the base catalog, leave the other locales with pending values marked unambiguously, and deliver per-file diffs, per-language resource files, provider configuration, migration notes, and a localization QA checklist (hot locale switch, fallback, RTL if applicable, pseudo-localization, and long-text truncation). Define explicit assumptions (fallback policy, missing key handling, default locale in SSR) and mark any ambiguity instead of inventing it. Before executing, reformulate what you understood and present your plan. If any critical data is missing (stack and i18n library, target languages, base language, extraction scope, or advanced formatting needs), ask for it concretely before proceeding. Close by confirming that no visible string was left unextracted, that the catalogs are mirrors without orphaned or duplicate keys, and that the UI does not break on a missing translation.

prompts.title: Permission and role management (RBAC)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer specialized in access control. I need to implement RBAC (role-based access control) consistently between UI and server, because today restrictions live only in the frontend and a user can bypass them by calling the API directly. The goal is to make the server the sole authorization authority and centralize the rules so that adding a new role or permission is done in a single place.

Deliver: (1) a role-permission matrix as the single source of truth, versionable (config file or database table), with granular permissions named action:resource; decide on and justify the chosen storage. (2) A reusable server-side authorization layer (middleware, guard, or decorator) that reads the role ALWAYS from the server's trusted source (not the request body), verifies the permission required for each sensitive action, and returns 403 when absent and 401 when there is no valid session. (3) A single endpoint that exposes the user's effective permissions so the frontend can hide or disable actions, with an explicit comment in the code clarifying that this is user experience only and not the security layer. (4) Denial tests demonstrating 403 for a role without permission even if they manipulate the request (change their role in the body, omit fields, call the endpoint directly, or reuse a token from another role). (5) Documentation of where the source of truth lives and the procedure for adding a role or permission without touching each endpoint.

Mandatory considerations: deny-by-default (every action not listed is denied); explicitly decide whether to model ownership or resource-level scoping (e.g. an editor only edits their own items) or whether RBAC is purely global, and say where a future ABAC layer would fit; do not log the role or token; treat unknown roles or users without a role as having no permissions. If the app is multi-tenant, the tenant is also resolved server-side. Identify any sensitive endpoint left uncovered.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing code, reformulate what you understood, list assumptions, and present your plan. If you are missing a critical piece of data for secure authorization (stack, role source, sensitive action inventory), ask for it before proceeding.

prompts.title: Offline-first logic and synchronization
prompts.content: Act as a senior offline-first application engineer, with proven experience in data synchronization, conflict resolution, and outbox or mutation queue design. Your goal: design the local and synchronization layer of an app so that it remains usable without network connectivity and never loses or duplicates the user's work on reconnection, avoiding the most expensive bug in these apps (data overwritten or duplicated on sync). Before coding, reformulate what app this is, which entities must work offline, the target stack and local storage, the preferred conflict strategy, and how much data loss is tolerable; if anything critical is missing, ask for it instead of assuming. Then deliver actionable code or pseudocode covering: 1) Local cache model with primary key, per-record version (monotonic counter or logical timestamp like Lamport, NOT the wall clock) and status flags (dirty, synced, base_version of the last confirmed sync). 2) Mutation outbox or queue with per-operation schema (local id, type create/update/delete, entity, payload, base_version, timestamp, status pending/sending/confirmed/failed, attempt counter, idempotency_key), deterministic drain order (FIFO per entity respecting dependencies), and retry policy with exponential backoff, jitter, and attempt ceiling before marking failed. 3) Reconciliation engine that applies the server delta onto the cache, detects conflict (record with base_version differing from the server's and dirty locally), and resolves according to the chosen strategy with trade-off justification; if none was indicated, recommend one coherent with the loss tolerance. 4) Sync state machine (offline, queuing, syncing, synced, conflict) with named events and transitions (reconnect, network error, conflict detected, resolution applied, retry exhaustion). 5) Temporary IDs: local id generation on offline create and remapping to the server's definitive id without breaking queued child references. 6) Idempotency: stable idempotency_key per mutation so that a resend does not duplicate. Explicitly cover edge cases: update on a server-deleted record (tombstone), delete-vs-update conflict, stale payload, resend after timeout with no confirmation, and parent-create before child-create order. Declare your assumptions, the limits of the solution, and a verifiable acceptance criterion per point. Close with a textual flow diagram of reconnect - queue drain - reconciliation - conflict resolution. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Error diagnosis from stacktrace
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer expert in debugging, stacktrace reading, and root-cause analysis in multiple languages and runtimes. I am going to give you a complete error stacktrace or traceback and I need you to interpret it to locate the root cause and propose the minimal fix, without refactors or scope changes.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate what you understand about the error and present your stack reading plan before concluding.

Proceed as follows:
1. Read the header: identify the exception type and transcribe literally what the message asserts, without paraphrasing.
2. Traverse the frames from inside out: locate where the exception was thrown, separate the frames of your own code from those of libraries and runtime, and mark the first frame of your own code in the failure path (that is usually where the cause is, not in the last frame of a library).
3. If there is chaining (Caused by, during handling of, the above exception was the direct cause), follow the chain to the originating exception and explicitly distinguish symptom from cause.
4. Formulate 2 or 3 root-cause hypotheses ordered by probability; for each one declare the stack evidence in favor, the evidence against, and a cheap check to confirm or discard it.
5. Choose the most probable hypothesis and explain the failure mechanism (why it occurs, not just where) in one or two sentences.
6. Propose the minimal fix as a diff or before/after, attacking only the root cause; all defensive guards (null validation, edge handling, retries) go separately and marked as optional.
7. Indicate how to verify: the test case or reproduction step that goes from failing to working.

Rules: do not invent code, file names, line numbers, versions, or values not present in what I gave you; mark the inferred as [ASSUMPTION]. If you are missing the code of a frame, the runtime, the version of a library, or the reproduction steps to confirm the cause, ask for them before concluding instead of assuming. If the stacktrace is truncated or does not correspond to the described error, flag it. If you do not receive the stacktrace, ask for it before starting.

prompts.title: Reproduce bug with minimal case
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in debugging non-deterministic systems and case reduction (MCVE), with mastery of race conditions, control of randomness sources, variable isolation, and bisection. Your goal: transform an intermittent or ghost failure into a minimal, deterministic, and self-contained reproducer that reliably triggers the bug, plus the diagnosis of the condition that causes it and its conversion into a permanent regression test.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the observable symptom and its appearance rate, plan the isolation experiment, and only then execute. If the symptom or stack trace, the suspect code, the environment and frequency, or the technical stack (language, runtime, test framework, versioned dependencies) is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent code behavior.

Proceed in five phases. Framing: reconstruct the symptom and its appearance rate; mark as [ASSUMPTION] every behavior not verifiable against the code or inputs. Hypotheses: list 2 or 3 non-determinism sources ordered by evidence (race condition, mutable shared state, execution or test order dependency, time or clock dependency, unfixed input data, external network or disk resource, random seed, data structure iteration order, locale or timezone, hardware or core count dependency). Variable control: freeze seeds, clock, and timezone; fix execution order; replace network, disk, and services with doubles or in-memory data; force concurrency or a stress loop to raise the appearance probability until it becomes observable. Bisection: remove dependencies, layers, and lines one by one, verifying after each trim that the failure persists; stop at the minimal irreducible. Confirmation: explicitly discard each unsupported hypothesis and identify the exact line or condition that triggers the failure.

Deliver the reproducer as a single self-contained and executable file or test, with no dependencies on the full system, with the exact run instruction and the observed or expected reproduction rate. Accompany it with a diagnosis block: confirmed hypothesis, precise triggering condition, expected vs. observed, reproduction rate, and discarded hypotheses with their reason. Close by suggesting how to integrate it as a regression test and, if the failure does not reproduce deterministically after variable control, declare the residual non-determinism and the next hypothesis to try instead of asserting an unproven cause.

prompts.title: Frontend state debugging
prompts.content: Act as a senior frontend engineer specialized in reactive UI debugging and state modeling. I have a component that shows inconsistent state (stale data, desynced value, flickering) or renders more than necessary, and I want the root cause with evidence, not a blind rewrite. Before diagnosing, reformulate the observable symptom and the interaction that triggers it; if it is not reproducible or the component code, the framework, the state mechanism, or the exact step is missing, ask for it in a single batch and do not assume. Proceed in four phases: (1) Reproduction: establish what was expected, what is observed, and at which step it occurs. (2) State model: map each piece of state (local, context, global store, server/cache), who reads it, and who writes it; mark duplications and derived state that should be calculated instead of stored. (3) Render analysis: attribute each suspect render to a concrete trigger (new prop, object or function recreated on render, unstable effect or memo dependency, too-broad store subscription, unstable key in lists, overly elevated state) and separate correct from wasted renders. (4) Verifiable fix: for each finding give the why, the exact code change, and how to verify it with before/after instrumentation (render count, value consistency, absence of flickering). Do not memoize or optimize without a measured cause; flag any premature optimization. Cover edge cases: race conditions in concurrent fetches, effects triggered on double mount, stale state in closures, SSR hydration, and out-of-order updates. Mark as assumption everything you assume about the framework or state library. Deliver a findings table (symptom, root cause, file:line), a patch per finding, the before/after verification plan, and an explicit note on correct renders that must not be touched. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; reformulate what you understand and present the plan before executing.

prompts.title: Debug a concurrency bug or race condition
prompts.content: Act as a senior engineer in concurrent systems, expert in memory models and race condition debugging. I have a concurrency bug that produces an intermittent failure, difficult to reproduce, that blocks confidence in the system. I want to move from a non-deterministic failure to a verifiable fix that eliminates the class of defect, not just the symptom. Proceed as follows: (1) Identify the mutable shared state between threads or tasks and list every read and write access that occurs without protection. (2) Reconstruct a concrete interleaving of operations, step by step, that reproduces the symptom by showing the order of reads and writes that breaks the invariant; do not give vague descriptions. (3) Classify the defect (data race, check-then-act, deadlock, livelock, unsafe publication, lost update, or ABA) and name the violated invariant. (4) Propose the fix by prioritizing redesign that eliminates shared state (immutability, thread confinement, message passing, atomic operations); if not viable, apply the minimum correct synchronization taking care of a global lock acquisition order to avoid introducing deadlock, and evaluate the contention trade-off. (5) Deliver the corrected code and a deterministic method to reproduce and verify the failure before and after the fix (stress test, pause injection, barriers, or race detectors). Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. If you lack the language and version, concurrency model, suspicious code, observed symptom, or how it is invoked concurrently, ask me before continuing instead of inventing. Close with a diagnostic report, the corrected code block, and the verification procedure, ready to review in a pull request. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Memory leak analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior performance engineer specializing in memory management and heap diagnostics in garbage-collected runtimes. I have a process that consumes memory in a sustained manner and does not release it after completing work, which points to a leak due to retained references, not transient pressure. I want to isolate the root cause down to the GC root with evidence, not patch it with defensive restarts.

Before analyzing, ask me for whatever is missing: the runtime and its version, the observed symptom (shape of the heap or RSS curve, GC frequency, time to OOM, whether memory drops after the work), the reproduction scenario (which action to repeat and how many times), and the evidence (ideally two heap snapshots taken in the same logical state separated by several cycles of the suspicious flow, or the module code if there are no snapshots). With only one snapshot or without reproduction steps, do not conclude: request them.

Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm leak vs. pressure by comparing the two snapshots by delta of live retained objects; discard caches with a limit and buffers that stabilize; a leak requires monotonic growth of the retained set. (2) Rank constructors and types by growing retained size and choose 1 to 3 dominant suspects. (3) For the dominant one, trace the retainer path node by node to the GC root (global, live closure, stack frame, listener, timer, singleton). (4) Name the pattern from the canonical list: unremoved listeners, timers or intervals without clear, closures capturing large objects, cache without eviction or TTL, collection that only grows, global references, detached DOM nodes referenced, subscriptions without unsubscription. (5) Explain why that reference keeps the object alive and at what point in the lifecycle it should be released. (6) Propose a minimal fix that breaks only that chain (remove listener on cleanup, clear the timer, WeakMap or WeakRef when applicable, bounded LRU cache, unsubscribe on teardown) without touching what is not involved. (7) Define the reproducible verification: repeat N cycles, force GC, recapture snapshot, and confirm retained delta at zero or stable.

Mark every inference not supported by evidence with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent heap data. If the evidence is code instead of snapshots, declare that the diagnosis is static and indicate what you would measure to confirm it.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: report with leak diagnosis yes/no justified by retained delta, suspect table by retained size, retainer path annotated to the GC root, named pattern with its location, minimal fix diff, and verification procedure that proves deallocation.

prompts.title: Assisted bisect of a regression
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer expert in regression debugging with git bisect, with practice in designing deterministic goodness tests and in root cause analysis over diffs. We are going to isolate, through binary search over the history, the first commit that introduced a regression: a behavior that used to work and is now broken. Conduct the session one iteration at a time and never assume a verdict: always wait for the real result that I report.

Before touching the history I need from you, and you ask me if I do not give them to you: (1) the exact symptom, what was expected, what is happening now, and how it is observed; (2) a goodness test, that is, the command, script, or manual steps that give an unequivocal good or bad verdict for any commit; (3) the bad commit where the regression is already present, normally HEAD; (4) the good commit where it still worked, and if I do not have it help me estimate a candidate; (5) optionally, the stack and how to install and run the project on each commit.

Proceed as follows. Phase 1, framing: reformulate the symptom, help me convert the goodness test into something deterministic and fast, and confirm that the regression is reproducible before continuing. Warn that the range must be monotonic, a single transition from good to bad; if there is intermittency or flakiness, propose mitigations such as retries, pinning the environment, cleaning the build, or git bisect skip. Phase 2, start: emit git bisect start, git bisect bad on the bad commit, and git bisect good on the good one, and estimate the expected number of iterations as log2 of the number of commits in the range. Phase 3, loop: on each turn ask me to run the goodness test on the active commit and report the verdict; based on my real response reply only with git bisect good or git bisect bad and how many commits remain. Phase 4, close: on the first defective commit ask git show, explain the root cause in clear language, propose a concrete and minimal fix and a non-regression test that fails before the fix and passes after, remind git bisect reset, and if the goodness test is automatable, draft the equivalent git bisect run to reproduce the session without intervention.

Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every inference about commits, environment, or behavior that I have not confirmed. If the range is not monotonic, if the good commit also fails, or if bisect points to a merge or a commit that does not compile, stop and tell me how to adjust before continuing. Write in neutral and professional English, without emojis. The final deliverable is a session transcript that ends with the culprit commit, its root cause, the fix, and the non-regression test, ready to apply.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Add useful logging and traces
prompts.content: Act as a senior observability engineer with experience in structured logging and distributed traces in production systems. I have a code path that is opaque today: when something fails there is no way to know why, what input caused it, or at what stage the latency went. I need to instrument it so that each incident is diagnosable from the logs, without drowning the signal in noise or leaking secrets. If you have not received the exact route or function, the language and framework, the logging library in use, the specific diagnostic goal I need to be able to answer, or the sensitive fields to redact, ask me before writing code. Work like this: first diagnose which questions today CANNOT be answered with the current logs and map each one to a concrete trace to add. Then instrument preserving the existing style, with structured logging in key-value pairs or JSON, never string concatenation. Apply levels with judgment: DEBUG for development detail, INFO for business milestones, WARN for recoverable anomalies, ERROR for failures with stack and context. Generate a correlation identifier at the boundary of the operation and propagate it throughout the route to link the lines of the same request. Add an entry log and an exit log per key operation with duration in milliseconds. Redact or explicitly exclude every secret and PII. For each new trace, indicate which metric or alert could be derived from it. Avoid logging inside hot loops, do not duplicate the same event across multiple layers, and do not raise the level of existing logs without justifying it. If the route crosses a process boundary or async queue, indicate how the correlation identifier travels. Deliver the instrumented code ready to paste (diff or complete blocks), the trace-to-metric mapping, and a brief note on how to view and verify the traces locally. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Explain someone else's code to understand it
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in reading and maintaining legacy code, accustomed to providing technical onboarding to other developers. I am going to give you a code fragment that I did not write and I need to understand it thoroughly before touching it, so as not to introduce regressions or break invisible dependencies. Your deliverable is an explanatory walkthrough, NOT a proposal for changes.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate in one or two sentences what code you received, in what language, and with what reading objective; present your traversal plan; then execute. If you did not receive the code, do not identify the language, or essential context is missing to avoid inventing, ask for it before moving forward instead of assuming.

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing. Confirm the language, framework/version if applicable, and what the file or module does and how it is invoked.
2. Walkthrough. Explain the code respecting the real execution flow (not just the textual order), line by line or block by block when several lines form a logical unit. In each part clarify what it does, why it is probably written this way, what data enters and exits, and what it depends on. Explicitly mark control structures, side effects, external calls (network, disk, database, APIs), and implicit assumptions.
3. Synthesis. Close with: (a) the responsibility of the fragment in a single sentence; (b) a dependency map naming inputs (parameters, global state, configuration, external calls) and outputs (returns, mutations, effects, exceptions); (c) the 3 riskiest zones to modify given my objective, each with its reason and the minimum test that would cover it.

Quality rules: always separate the observable in the code from what you infer (mark the inferred as such and do not present it as fact); do not omit any relevant section; if you detect possible dead code, unreachable conditions, or a bug, point it out as an observation without correcting it. The deliverable is understanding, not a solution.

prompts.title: Debug CORS and network problems
prompts.content:
Act as a senior web platform engineer, specialist in HTTP, the browser CORS model, and client-server debugging in production. A request from my frontend is blocked by the browser and delivery stops: the data does not arrive and the user flow breaks. The console labels as CORS both real CORS failures and network, TLS, or mixed-content errors, so I need to separate the exact root cause before touching anything.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Work in three phases:
1. Triage. Separate genuine CORS from disguised network error (DNS, TLS/certificate, timeout, refused connection or server down, HTTP-over-HTTPS mixed content, extension or adblocker block). Cite the literal evidence that distinguishes each case: a network failure gives status 0 or ERR_* without response headers; a CORS failure shows the response in Network but the browser hides it from JS.
2. Diagnosis. If it is CORS, name the subtype: simple request vs preflight OPTIONS; origin absent or not matching in Access-Control-Allow-Origin; method or application header not listed in Allow-Methods or Allow-Headers; request with credentials that requires Allow-Credentials: true with an explicit origin (never the wildcard); preflight cache via Access-Control-Max-Age; or missing Access-Control-Expose-Headers to read response headers. Contrast what the browser requires against what the server responds. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for every infrastructure inference not supported by evidence.
3. Fix and verification. Issue a root cause verdict indicating for each finding whether the fix goes on the server or the client. Give the exact headers with their correct value, the corrected code fragment on the relevant side, and a curl command that reproduces the preflight (OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method/Headers) to verify the response without the browser. Confirm that no request with credentials is paired with the origin wildcard.

Deliverable: root cause verdict + table of headers to fix with values + corrected code fragment + curl command for preflight verification + security note on allowed origins. If you are missing the literal console message, the request code, the response headers, or the origin-destination pair, ask for it and do not invent the server configuration.

prompts.title: Post-mortem of a production incident
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Site Reliability Engineer with experience leading blameless incident reviews. A production incident has already been mitigated and I need to close the cycle with a post-mortem that converts the failure into verifiable organizational learning. The focus is on systems and processes, never on people: the question is not who made a mistake, but why the system allowed the error and how to avoid it structurally.

Produce the complete post-mortem in this order:
1. Executive summary (3-5 lines): what happened, severity, user and business impact, current status.
2. Chronological timeline with timestamps in an explicit timezone, from the triggering event to closure. Mark the detection, diagnosis, and resolution milestones, and calculate TTD (time to detection), TTM (time to mitigation), TTR (time to resolution), and total duration.
3. Quantified impact: affected users or transactions, failed requests, degradation window, error budget consumed, and SLO violation if applicable.
4. Root cause with 5 whys, separating the immediate cause (what broke) from contributing causes (why the system allowed it), and distinguishing technical factors from process factors. Mark the bifurcation point where the response could have been shortened.
5. What worked well and what failed in detection and in the response.
6. Corrective actions in a table: action, type (preventive | detection | mitigation), single owner, target date, priority, and closure signal. Each action attacks an identified root cause and is verifiable.

Rigor rules: do not mix facts with interpretation; every inference is marked as an assumption and every missing piece of data is declared as an explicit blank instead of being invented. Maintain blameless language throughout the document. If any critical input is missing (timeline, impact metrics, recent changes), ask for it before drafting.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Safe refactor with a test safety net
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in legacy code refactoring, with mastery of Michael Feathers' characterization tests and seams, and Martin Fowler's small-step refactors. I am going to give you a legacy module, class, or function that I need to improve internally without changing what it does from the consumer's perspective. Touching it blindly is risky because there is no guarantee of not breaking something. The discipline is clear: legacy code is code without tests, so first you weave a characterization test net that freezes the CURRENT behavior (quirks and bugs included), and only then refactor in small steps maintaining the green.

Proceed in strict order. First confirm with me the language, framework, test framework, and the observable behavior I must preserve; if you do not see me paste the module's code, ask me for it before starting and do not invent its content. Then read the module and write characterization tests that capture its current behavior as it is today, prioritizing the inputs, outputs, effects, and edge cases that matter; the tests describe, they do not judge. Identify the seams (injection or isolation points) needed to test without touching production. Run the net and confirm total green: that green is the contract that no refactor can break; report it before moving forward. If coverage is insufficient to refactor safely, say so and expand the net before transforming.

Then refactor in small steps: a single transformation per step (extract method, rename, eliminate duplication, invert dependency, replace conditional with polymorphism), running the net after each one. If a test goes red, stop, revert that step, and report before continuing. Each step is an atomic commit that names what was refactored and why. Do not mix refactor with bug fixes or new features in the same commit; if you detect a real bug, register it as a separate finding marked [ASSUMPTION] instead of fixing it along the way. On closing, deliver the diff organized by commits, the final test net, the list of introduced seams, and a balance of eliminated vs. pending smells with their reason.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Extract functions and reduce complexity
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in refactoring and code quality, with mastery of complexity metrics and the single-responsibility principle. Your goal is to transform an extensive function or method into a lean version that orchestrates more single-responsibility subfunctions, reducing cyclomatic complexity without altering observable behavior.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before touching the code, reformulate what you understood about the function and present your plan; only after my confirmation do you apply the refactor.

Proceed by phases. Phase 1 Diagnosis: describe in clear language what the function does and why it is complex; count the decision points (if, else if, for, while, case, logical operators, ternaries, early returns) and estimate the current cyclomatic complexity; map the mixed responsibilities. Phase 2 Plan: identify candidate blocks for extraction (guard clauses, validations, calculations, formatting, side effects) and propose each subfunction with name, input, output, and justification; mark for explicit approval any change to a public signature. Phase 3 Refactor: after my go-ahead, apply the extractions one by one maintaining intentional names and contracts, leaving the root function as a readable orchestrator faithful to the original style. Phase 4 Verification: compare complexity before/after per function and confirm that the same inputs produce the same outputs and effects.

Rules: preserve public signatures and contracts unless given explicit approval; do not introduce new dependencies or change observable behavior; do not invent missing data, ask for it before executing. If the function is already below the threshold or does not admit safe extractions, say so and justify it instead of fragmenting artificially.

Deliverable: refactored code block (lean function plus subfunctions) + extraction table (what was extracted and why) + cyclomatic complexity comparison before/after per function + behavioral equivalence note. Ask me for the function, language, target complexity threshold, and restrictions if you have not been given them.

prompts.title: Eliminate duplicate code (DRY)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in safe refactoring and abstraction design, with judgment to distinguish real duplication from accidental coincidence. I need to eliminate duplicate code from an area of my project applying DRY thoughtfully, without falling into the opposite trap: abstracting code that only looks similar by accident and ending up coupling modules that should evolve independently. If you do not know the target paths, language and framework, the occurrence threshold for unifying, the preferred unification strategy, or the restrictions to respect, ask me before continuing; also ask me whether you have access to the code or if I paste it.

Proceed as follows. First inventory semantic duplication, not just textual: logic that does the same thing with different names, repeated validations, copied data mappings, duplicated error handling, identical query or request construction. Second, classify each finding into three buckets: real duplication (same purpose and same reason to change), accidental coincidence (looks similar today but will evolve differently, do NOT touch), and tolerable duplication (unifying would cost more clarity than it saves). Apply the rule of three: do not abstract with only two occurrences unless there is an explicit reason. Third, for each real duplication propose the correct unit of unification (pure utility function, shared module, base class, hook, decorator, or parameterization) and justify why that one and not another. Fourth, apply the coupling test: if call sites would need boolean flags or if branches to differentiate themselves, declare that they were NOT the same concept and leave them separate. Fifth, refactor in small and reversible steps, migrate call sites one by one, and preserve observable behavior.

Deliverable: diffs per file, a table of classified findings with their occurrence count, the contract of each new abstraction (signature, inputs, outputs, effects), and the explicit list of migrated call sites and of code left intact with its reason. If you detect duplication in code covered by tests, keep the tests green; if there are no tests in the critical area, warn before touching. Mark any assumption you make and any pending ambiguity.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Module renaming and reorganization
prompts.content:
Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in large-scale structural refactors with zero downtime, with mastery of module systems (ESM/CJS, Python packages, build aliases, barrels, and re-exports) and of Domain-Driven Design. Your goal is to rename and relocate a set of modules to align the codebase by domain, without breaking imports or changing observable behavior, leaving verification green.

I need to know: which modules to rename or move and their desired destination; the domain folder tree and which domain each module belongs to; the language and import system (relative, tsconfig/jsconfig aliases, Python packages, barrels/index, re-exports, dynamic imports); the lint/type-check/tests command to validate after each phase; and the constraints to respect (frozen public APIs, files that must not be touched, known circular dependencies). If any of these data are missing, ask before touching code; do not assume the structure.
