6) Fallback route and observability: behavior when no category applies, confidence tie between two specialists, or a specialist declares itself not competent; re-routing with a hop limit to avoid loops; and the decision trace logged per message (input, intent, chosen specialist, confidence, reason, fallback if applied) so the route is auditable.

Close with a battery of at least eight test cases with expected classification, target specialist, and justification, covering at least one clean case, one multi-intent, one low-confidence ambiguous, one out-of-scope, and one adversarial or instruction-injection case. Execute them mentally against the table and correct any inconsistent route before delivering.

If I am not clear on the specialists, their boundaries, or the channel where the router runs, ask me the minimum questions before designing; do not fill in with unmarked assumptions. Protect the brand: never mention prices or the word free, neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Manage agent token budget and cost
prompts.content: Act as a senior LLM agentic systems architect with experience operating agents in production under cost and latency constraints. Design the token budget policy for an agent in production so that it sustains long tasks with bounded cost and, when reaching the limit, delivers a useful partial result instead of crashing with an opaque error or silent truncation. Deliver: (1) Context inventory: decompose the window into fixed and variable layers (system instruction, tool definitions, retrieved long-term memory, conversation history, reserved output) with the typical token weight of each and which ones grow turn by turn. (2) Layer budget: token ceiling per turn and per session; reserved output margin that is untouchable; effective input limit = window minus reserved output minus safety margin. (3) Compaction rules: measurable triggers (percentage or tokens, never qualitative) and tactic (progressive summary preserving decisions, facts, and state; pruning of redundant turns; externalization of long artifacts to retrievable memory). Declare what is NEVER compressed: system instruction, security restrictions, active objective. (4) Graceful degradation tree in ordered steps when budget is exhausted despite compaction: reduce verbosity and optional tools; narrow to the highest-value sub-objective; ask the user for confirmation to continue or split; return an honest partial result with achieved, pending, and how to resume. (5) Telemetry and control: per-turn metrics (input tokens per layer, output tokens, compaction events, degradation step reached, relative cost), actionable alert thresholds, and verifiable acceptance criteria. Cover edge cases: a turn that by itself exceeds the limit, context leakage from verbose tools, cascading compaction cycles, and retrieved memory that contradicts the history. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any model data you infer and never invent price figures. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If the model, window, target task, or criticality is missing, ask for it before calculating.

prompts.title: Model conversation state and state machine
prompts.content:
Act as a senior conversational agent architect specialized in finite state machines (FSM) for dialogue flows, with expertise in slot management, context persistence, and fault recovery.

I need you to design the complete state model of a conversational agent, ready to implement. Before starting, reformulate in your own words the agent's purpose, the business objective it must maximize, and the flow stages; present your plan in one sentence and, if you are missing any data essential for designing a transition without ambiguity (stages, data per stage, channels, persistence mechanism, transversal events), ask me instead of inventing it.

Deliver:
1. State inventory: for each state, its unique purpose, data expected upon entry, exit condition, and type (initial, intermediate, terminal, or error). Explicitly flag any state you detect as redundant or that does two things and propose splitting it.
2. Transition table: one row per transition with source state, triggering event, guard or condition, associated action, and destination state. No non-terminal state may be left without an exit; no expected event may be left unhandled in its context.
3. Schema of the conversational state object that persists between turns: current phase, collected slots with their validation rule, bounded relevant history, per-state attempt counter, session identifier, schema version, and timestamp (creation and last update).
4. Transversal events: define the handling, from any state, of requesting a human, topic change, abandonment, session expiry, intent repetition, and out-of-domain intent. Indicate which ones preserve state for resumption and which ones reset it.
5. State recovery: resumption logic after interruption, detection of stale session by age (define the threshold or mark it as [ASSUMPTION]), and graceful degradation when the persisted state is corrupted, incomplete, or belongs to a previous schema version.
6. State diagram in Mermaid stateDiagram-v2, valid and consistent with the transition table.

Close by cross-checking inventory, table, and diagram to confirm they match; list assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION] and the design risks left open.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Draft the agent's operational system prompt
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompt engineer and AI agent designer, expert in the operational contract pattern (mission, tools, guardrails, error handling) and in safe tool use. I need the operational system prompt of an agent I am going to deploy: the foundational text that decides how it behaves when the user speaks to it, what tools it invokes, and, above all, where it stops. Treat it as a verifiable specification, not a polite description. If you are missing any essential data (agent name, mission, who uses it, available tools, red lines, tone, or error protocol), ask me before drafting and do not invent capabilities. Deliver in this order: (1) the mission in a single sentence using the template 'I am [role] and I exist to [measurable result] serving [user], without [red line]'; (2) the complete system prompt, in second person addressed to the agent, with six mandatory sections: MISSION (role plus result per turn), SCOPE (explicit in-scope and out-of-scope, no gray areas), TOOLS (for each one: usage trigger, non-usage condition, and what to do if the tool fails or does not exist; do not invent any), TONE AND FORMAT (register, language, length, and output structure), LIMITS AND SECURITY (red lines, data never exposed, actions requiring human confirmation), and ERROR PROTOCOL (what to do on ambiguity, missing data, tool failure, and out-of-scope or unsafe request, so it never fails silently); (3) close the system prompt with a one-line golden rule to resolve conflicts between instructions; (4) separately, three test messages (normal, ambiguous, and out-of-scope) with the expected agent response to each. Replace every vague adjective ('helpful', 'smart') with an observable behavior. Deliver in neutral Spanish, professional tone, ready to paste into the agent configuration.

prompts.title: Design end-to-end RAG architecture
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG systems architect with proven experience in semantic search, vector databases, and LLMs in production. I need an implementable RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) architecture, not a conceptual summary: a poor decision in chunking, embeddings, or reranking is paid later in imprecise responses, hallucinations, or unacceptable latency, and redesigning in production costs weeks.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate the use case, corpus, language, and infrastructure constraints you understand; if any of those four data points is missing or ambiguous, ask me before designing — do not invent the domain. Then present the plan of the seven stages and the decision criteria you will apply. Only then develop the design.

Cover these seven stages in order, and justify each decision with an explicit criterion (expected precision, recall, latency, relative operational cost, or maintainability), never with personal preference; in each stage also name the alternative you discarded and why:
1. Ingestion: sources, formats, update frequency, delta handling or incremental reindexing, deduplication, and metadata contract per document (source, date, author, permissions, version, language).
2. Chunking: strategy with concrete size and overlap; explain the granularity vs. recoverable context trade-off and how you preserve tables, code, or headings.
3. Embeddings: proposed model and dimensionality, justified by language and domain; define index versioning when the model changes and the reindexing strategy.
4. Indexing and storage: vector database, index type (HNSW, IVF, or other) with its parameters, similarity metric, and filtering strategy by metadata and permissions.
5. Retrieval: top-k, hybrid dense + lexical search (BM25) if applicable with its fusion method (e.g., RRF), and query rewriting or expansion.
6. Reranking: if a cross-encoder reranker is warranted, with which model, top-n input, and how you trim the final context to not exceed the LLM window.
7. Generation with citations: generation prompt that forces citing the exact source of each claim, citation format, and an explicit abstention rule when there is insufficient evidence.

Close with: text flowchart of the seven stages, evaluation metrics (recall@k, precision@k, MRR/nDCG, faithfulness, answer relevance, p95 latency), recommended golden evaluation set to build, minimum acceptance tests, and risk matrix with mitigation (hallucination, permission leaks, stale data, corpus drift).

Mark any estimate or unconfirmed value as [ASSUMPTION]. Do not include prices or monetary figures; reason about cost in relative terms (compute, storage, maintenance). Respond in neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Define corpus chunking strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG engineer specialized in retrieval pipelines over heterogeneous corpora, with expertise in balancing retrieval precision, context coherence, and indexing cost. I am going to define the chunking strategy for a corpus before indexing it. Chunking is the highest-leverage decision in the pipeline: poorly calibrated segmentation fragments context, dilutes embeddings, and degrades retrieval more than any subsequent reranker or model change. The goal is not a single token number, but a strategy differentiated by document type and query pattern, ready to evaluate before indexing everything.

I need you to produce: (1) a characterization of the corpus by document type with typical length, structure (title hierarchy, sections, tables, lists, code), and units that must not be split; (2) a document-type x configuration matrix where each row fixes the partitioning method (fixed token size, recursive by structural separators, by sentences, heading-aware/Markdown, or semantic by embedding similarity), target tokens, overlap as a percentage of the chunk, respected unit, and metadata to attach (source, title path, section, page, type, chunk id); (3) the justification of each cell by the retrieval-precision vs. context-coherence vs. cost trade-off; (4) arithmetic verification that each chunk fits comfortably in the embedding window and that top-k chunks fit in the generation window without displacing the system prompt; (5) a micro-evaluation plan with representative query set, expected response, metrics (recall@k, citation precision, presence of the correct span in the retrieved chunk), and the criterion that defines the winning configuration before indexing everything.

Craft rules: sizes always in tokens, never in characters; derive decisions from the query pattern, not from a generic default; tables, lists, code blocks, and clauses are never split mid-way; consider modern techniques when applicable (contextual retrieval by prepending a context summary to the chunk, late chunking, parent-child indexes for fine retrieval and broad context generation). Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided and ask for it if it blocks a decision; do not invent corpus figures. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If document types, query pattern, embedding model with its window, generation LLM window with target top-k, or volume/latency constraints are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

prompts.title: Grounded generation prompt with citations
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG systems engineer, expert in grounding, source attribution, and hallucination mitigation. I need you to draft the complete, ready-to-paste system prompt of an assistant that answers questions using only the context fragments retrieved in each turn. The central risk is not failing to retrieve: it is answering without attribution. That is why attribution must be a construction obligation: every claim is born anchored to a citable fragment or is not emitted. Before writing, reformulate in one sentence the objective behavior of the assistant and declare with [ASSUMPTION] everything I have not specified (citation format, abstention phrase, language, strictness level, corpus domain); if any data is a blocker for defining the contract, ask me instead of inventing it. Then deliver, in this order: (1) the objective behavior sentence plus the assumptions; (2) the complete system prompt with explicit sections: the assistant's ROLE; GROUNDING CONTRACT with five non-negotiable rules (respond only from the retrieved context, cite each claim, abstain with the literal phrase when context falls short, do not infer or fuse beyond what is textual, respond in the language of the question); OUTPUT FORMAT (body with inline citations per claim plus a final 'Cited Sources' section listing only the fragments actually used, without inventing identifiers); ABSTENTION RULE with the exact phrase and its unambiguous trigger; EDGE CASES with instruction for contradictory fragments, fragment that only partially answers, question outside corpus scope, and fragment retrieved but irrelevant to the question; PRECEDENCE when two rules conflict; (3) inside the system prompt, on its own line, the MetodologIA Protocol block; (4) a 'How to verify grounding' section with 3 to 5 concrete tests and the expected behavior in each. Use consistent citation markers across all examples. Write in neutral Spanish, professional, no emojis, with imperative rules addressed in second person to the assistant. Close by confirming each checklist item is met.

prompts.title: Mitigating hallucinations in RAG with abstention guards
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI engineer specializing in RAG systems and hallucination mitigation, with hands-on experience in grounding, calibrated abstention, and verifiable output contracts.

I need you to design the ready-to-paste system instruction, the output contract, and the test cases that force a RAG assistant to respond only with evidence from the retrieved context, cite every claim, abstain when evidence is insufficient, and expose the gaps. The critical failure to control is hallucination: the model filling in with prior knowledge what the context does not support, inventing clauses, figures, or policies.

If you have not yet received the assistant use case, the format of the retrieved chunks (which fields each one carries: id, title, text, url), the response language, or the abstention tolerance (strict or partial response declaring gaps), ask me before drafting.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the objective in terms of grounding, abstention, and traceability, and mark with [ASSUMPTION] any missing data. Then enumerate the instruction blocks and the contract sections before drafting. Then execute.

Deliver: (1) the system instruction with blocks for role and scope, exclusive use of context, per-claim citation with the chunk identifier, abstention criterion with a template for null, partial, and contradictory evidence, and an output format that separates response, citations, and gaps; (2) the sufficiency criterion (verbatim quote or faithful paraphrase counts as evidence; any unsupported inference is marked [INFERENCE] and, if central, triggers abstention); (3) handling of conflicts between chunks by exposing both versions with their citations without silently choosing; (4) a gaps section listing what was asked and not covered; (5) two test cases, one answerable and one unanswerable, with their expected output including the correct abstention. Close by verifying against the quality checklist.

prompts.title: Rewriting and expanding user queries
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG systems engineer specializing in query understanding and retrieval optimization. Your objective is to transform a user query into a reusable retrieval package, without answering the underlying question: rewriting is the highest-impact lever on recall because it allows the retriever to find the correct passages even when the user does not use the corpus vocabulary.

I need you to produce: (1) A self-contained canonical query, without ambiguous pronouns or references to previous turns, with the main intent in one sentence. (2) Query type: factual, exploratory, comparative, procedural, or multi-hop. (3) Between 3 and 5 expansion variants that preserve the meaning and vary vocabulary with synonyms, domain terms, and expanded acronyms; include equivalents in another language only if the corpus is multilingual. (4) Atomic sub-queries with dependency order, only if the query is comparative or multi-hop; otherwise declare it and omit. (5) HyDE document: a declarative paragraph simulating the ideal source passage, not a response to the user. (6) Structured metadata filters, marking as [ASSUMPTION] any inferred filter and without inventing fields. (7) Fusion plan: combination of rankings in Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RAG-Fusion) style and top-k per variant.

Calibrate the expansion to the retrieval engine: lexical (BM25) favors synonyms and acronyms; dense (embeddings) favors semantic paraphrases; hybrid covers both. Mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION] and do not introduce new facts or change the scope of the query. Deliver a structured and reusable block for the pipeline.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If you are missing the original query, the corpus domain, the retrieval engine, or the available metadata, ask before generating the package.

prompts.title: Configuring hybrid search (dense + lexical)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Information Retrieval engineer with experience in RAG systems in production and rigorous search evaluation. Design a dense + lexical hybrid search with ranking fusion, ready to implement and evaluate.

Context of the problem: retrieval that is purely dense fails with exact terms, codes, acronyms, and proper names; purely lexical retrieval (BM25) fails with synonyms and paraphrases. Combining both with ranking fusion unlocks recall without sacrificing precision and reduces hallucinated responses due to missing context.

Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Ask me for any missing data instead of inventing it: domain and nature of the corpus, approximate volume of documents or chunks, predominant language of queries and documents, available engine for dense and lexical index, latency budget per end-to-end query, and dominant query mix (semantic, exact, mixed). Mark every data point not provided as [ASSUMPTION] with its assumed value.

Produce:
1. Diagnosis: contrast the failures of dense-only and BM25-only against the real query types; determine whether hybridization adds value or whether a single retriever suffices. Do not assume hybridization always helps.
2. Dense retriever: embedding model appropriate for the language, dimension, metric (cosine or inner product), chunking strategy, and vector normalization.
3. BM25 lexical retriever: tokenization, stemming or lemmatization, language stopwords, handling of numbers/codes, and k1 and b parameters with starting values (reference k1≈1.2, b≈0.75).
4. Fusion: recommend Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with reference constant k 60 for its robustness without calibrating scales; offer weighted sum with min-max normalization as an alternative, warning about the risk of mixing non-comparable scales. Set the top-k per retriever before fusion, adjusted to the latency budget.
5. Re-ranker: indicate when to add a cross-encoder over the fused set, over how many candidates, and its latency cost; when to omit it.
6. Evaluation: gold set of labeled queries (minimum size and sampling criterion by query type), metrics Recall@k, nDCG@10, and MRR, and ablation dense vs. lexical vs. hybrid with a quantitative decision criterion.
7. Starting-parameter table sized to the volume, plus common errors (double counting a document retrieved by both indexes, k1/b without adjustment, fusion over non-normalized scales, missing deduplication, biased gold set).

Close: design document with parameter table, justified fusion strategy, and reproducible evaluation protocol. Do not invent figures; every data point not provided goes as [ASSUMPTION].

prompts.title: Designing a results reranking stage
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG and Information Retrieval systems engineer, specializing in reranking with cross-encoders (bge-reranker, Cohere Rerank, mxbai-rerank) and LLM-as-reranker, with evaluation criteria based on nDCG/MRR. Design a reranking stage that reorders the retriever's candidates to maximize the relevance of the top-k that reaches the generator, without reindexing or changing the retriever. Before designing I need to know: the current retriever and the domain of the queries (vector/embeddings, BM25, hybrid; support, legal, code, etc.), how many candidates reach the reranker (K) and how many pass to the generator (k), the preferred approach if any, the latency budget added, and the cost-per-query constraint, and what exists to measure relevance (human judgments, LLM-judge, real production queries). If an essential data point is missing, ask me before executing and do not invent system numbers.

Deliver in this order: (1) Restate the problem in one actionable sentence: reorder the K candidates to maximize relevance of the top-k, optimizing precision/latency/cost. (2) Recommend the approach (dedicated cross-encoder, managed API, or LLM-as-reranker) and justify it against the alternatives; explicitly declare when reranking is NOT advisable (K too small, critical latency, retriever already very precise, domain where lexical similarity already suffices). (3) Define the stage contract: input (query + K candidates with text and metadata), output (top-k reordered with normalized relevance score), handling of ties, candidates without a score, and reranker failure (degradation to the retriever's order). (4) Justify K and k: retrieve broadly to give the reranker margin, deliver narrowly to not saturate the context; explain the trade-off recall@K of the retriever vs. precision@k of the reranker and how to choose K without amplifying latency without a ceiling. (5) If the approach is LLM-as-reranker, deliver the exact scoring prompt: defined relevance scale (e.g. 0-3 with anchors), a single dimension, parseable JSON output with id+score, guard against bias by length/style/position, chunking per context for large K, and retry policy on unparseable output. (6) Design the evaluation: metrics (nDCG@k, MRR, Recall@k, Hit@k), construction of the relevance judgment set (human or LLM-judge with calibration), and honest A/B retriever-only vs. retriever + reranker at the same output k, with sample size and significance test. (7) Quantify the cost: added latency (cross-encoder is O(K) forward passes), cost per query if API/LLM, and mitigations (rerank only top-N, query-passage pair cache, lighter model, batching). Close with acceptance criteria (minimum improvement threshold in nDCG@k/MRR that justifies the added latency) and rollback plan by query segment. Mark [ASSUMPTION] every number or decision assumed due to missing data. Respond in neutral Spanish, professional tone, no emojis.

prompts.title: Applying metadata and permission filters in RAG retrieval
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG systems engineer specializing in secure and multi-tenant retrieval. Design the metadata and permission filtering layer of my retrieval pipeline. Before executing, restate the objective and explicitly separate two planes that must never be mixed: relevance filtering (recency, source, language) and security filtering (authorization by roles, groups, or ACL). If you do not know my use case, the metadata schema per chunk, my permissions model, the identity of the querying user, or the vector store I use and whether it supports native pre-filtering, ask me before continuing. Deliver: (1) the relevance vs. security distinction with assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION]; (2) the minimum metadata schema per chunk and the identity attributes needed to authorize; (3) the classification of each filter as pre-filtering (during ANN search, preserves recall) or post-filtering (after the top-k), justified by correctness, recall, and store support; (4) a deny-by-default access control where the chunk passes only if the user's roles or groups intersect the chunk's access labels, fixing the exact evaluation point so that it is impossible to expose unauthorized content to the LLM; (5) behavior when there are zero results (never relax permissions; relax recency only with an explicit notice) and handling of chunks without an access label (absence = denied); (6) the boolean filter expression ready for my vector store, with inclusive/exclusive date bounds defined and language and source normalized; (7) a test checklist with at least one negative data-leakage case that confirms a user without the role does not retrieve the restricted document. Consider edge cases: ACL that changes between indexing and query time (staleness), user with multiple overlapping groups, chunks inheriting permissions from their parent document, query language different from the corpus language, and degradation if the store does not support native pre-filtering (post-filtering with amplified top-k to not lose recall). Do not invent anything about the real schema: anything not confirmed goes as [ASSUMPTION]. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Evaluating RAG relevance and faithfulness
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG systems evaluation engineer, specializing in RAGAS-type metrics and retrieval-augmented pipeline diagnostics. I want a quantitative report that tells me, with evidence, whether my RAG system fails due to retrieval (the correct context does not arrive) or due to generation (the model hallucinates or wanders even with the context), because evaluating by impressions does not allow deciding where to invest. Before measuring, ask me: the RAG system and its purpose, the indexed corpus, the golden set (per item: question, expected answer, and ideal context chunks), the metrics to calculate, the approval thresholds per metric, and the real system outputs per question (retrieved chunks and generated response). If any of these inputs is missing, stop and request it: do not invent retrieval results or system responses. Define each metric on a 0 to 1 scale before calculating it, so that the calculation is auditable. If I did not provide thresholds, use 0.80 per metric as the default and declare it. Calculate the four metrics per question: context precision and context recall for the retriever; faithfulness by decomposing the response into atomic claims and marking each one as supported or unsupported by the retrieved chunks; and answer relevancy for the generator. Record per question the evidence (the chunk that supports or contradicts) and, if there is a failure, its root cause attributed to retrieval or generation. Aggregate averages, compare against thresholds, mark PASS or FAIL per metric, list the worst-evaluated questions, diagnose the dominant bottleneck, and propose a prioritized remediation plan with the expected impact on each metric. Edge cases to respect: if a question is unanswerable from the corpus, faithfulness must reward abstention and penalize the invented response; if the golden set fixes ideal chunks that the corpus no longer contains, mark it as corpus debt, not a retrieval failure; if retrieval and generation both fail, prioritize retrieval because it is upstream. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Do not use prices or the word free. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Synthesizing a response from multiple documents
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG systems engineer specializing in grounding, source attribution, and evidence conflict resolution. A RAG system retrieved chunks from several documents to answer a question; your job is to consolidate them into a single, grounded, and auditable response, defensible before a reviewer and reusable as evidence.

Proceed as follows: extract the atomic claims from each chunk preserving its source document; group them by claim or sub-topic, never by document, merging those that speak to the same point even if they come from different sources, to avoid counting the same source twice; classify each claim by support level (single source, corroborated by multiple sources, or in conflict, including conflict within the same document). For each conflict expose both versions, apply the tiebreaker criterion (by default recency, then corroboration, then specificity) and declare which prevails and why, never silently. Draft the consolidated response with inline attribution to each claim (e.g. [Doc A], [Doc B]). Close with the section of detected contradictions with their verdict and the section of gaps that the question requires and no chunk covers.

Hard rules: zero invented data; anything not supported is declared, not inferred; assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION]; document identifiers are treated as literals. If you have not yet received the question, the chunks with their source document, or any tiebreaker criterion or attribution level I prefer, ask me before executing. Deliver: (a) attributed consolidated response, (b) contradictions table with verdict, (c) gaps list.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Designing GraphRAG over connected knowledge
prompts.content:
Act as a senior retrieval and knowledge systems architect (RAG/GraphRAG), with experience in knowledge graphs, LLM-based extraction, entity resolution, and retrieval evaluation. Design a complete GraphRAG architecture over a connected knowledge corpus, designed to answer multi-hop questions with traceable, cited, and auditable responses. Before designing, briefly restate what you understand and present your plan; if an essential data point is missing (domain, volume, corpus format and language, target question types, graph engine and available stack, or latency/compute/privacy constraints), ask for it instead of assuming it, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you decide to assume in order not to block progress.

Structure the delivery in six sections. 1) Query-driven knowledge schema: derive entity and relation types from the target questions (not the other way around), with properties per node and per edge, cardinalities, edge direction, and, where applicable, temporal validity; explicitly justify why each relation type enables the expected hops, showing the graph path for at least two representative questions. 2) Extraction pipeline: structure-aware document chunking strategy, schema-guided entity and relation extraction, structural validation against the schema, and entity resolution (deduplication, coreference, canonical normalization, and linking) with its fusion threshold and conflict handling policy between sources (precedence by recency, authority, or voting, leaving a trail of the discarded). 3) Construction and indexing: concrete node and edge structure, provenance and citation per fact at the source chunk level, thematic clustering with hierarchical summaries when it adds value, and hybrid indexing combining embeddings with graph traversal. 4) Retrieval orchestration: explicit criterion for routing between local retrieval (entity neighborhood) and global (community summaries), context expansion following edges with a depth limit and pruning to resolve multi-hop without context explosion, and final context assembly with a token budget. 5) Generation and verification: fact-by-fact cited response, hallucination control for nonexistent relations (the response only asserts edges present in the retrieved graph), and evaluation plan with a set of multi-hop test questions and metrics of accuracy, coverage, source fidelity, and latency/compute cost, within the given constraints. 6) Honest comparison of GraphRAG against flat vector RAG, with the breakeven point where each one is appropriate, plus the main failure modes of the system with their mitigations. Use text diagrams or tables where they clarify and name real techniques (entity resolution, Leiden-style community detection, local/global retrieval, reranking) without inventing metrics or results. Close with a summary of open assumptions and the highest-risk architectural decision that should be validated first with a bounded prototype.

prompts.title: Applying contextual retrieval to chunks
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG engineer specializing in contextual retrieval (Anthropic style), dense + lexical hybrid retrieval, rank fusion, reranking, and recall evaluation in productive indexing pipelines. I want to raise the retrieval precision of my RAG without rewriting the source content. The problem: classic RAG splits each document into chunks that, in isolation, lose the global context (a fragment says "revenue grew 3%" without saying which company or period), and the retriever confuses or discards it. Contextual retrieval prepends to each chunk a short situational context paragraph generated from the full document before indexing, and combines contextual embeddings with contextual BM25; the published reports on the technique indicate a substantial reduction in retrieval failures compared to base RAG [ASSUMPTION: exact figure subject to verification per the version of the Anthropic article]. Design the complete pipeline, ready to implement and version: (1) Chunking at semantic boundaries (cut at section or heading, never mid-sentence), with target size and overlap justified. (2) Per-chunk contextualization: the LLM call receives the full document (or a structured summary if it exceeds the window) plus the chunk, and produces 1-3 sentences that situate it (entity, period, section, relation to the whole) without rewriting or summarizing the chunk; leverage prompt caching of the document to avoid resending the full text for each chunk. (3) Dual indexing: concatenate context + original text (contextualized_text) and generate its embedding plus its entry in a BM25 index over the same text, to capture semantic similarity and exact matches of terms, codes, and identifiers. (4) Hybrid retrieval: top-k dense + top-k BM25, fusion with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and reranker to keep the N most relevant. (5) Delivery to the generator: pass the ORIGINAL chunk, not the prepended context, to preserve citation fidelity. (6) Storage schema: id, doc_id, position, original_text, contextualized_text, embedding, source metadata, with mapping from retrieved chunk to source document. (7) Evaluation: recall@k (and optionally nDCG and MRR) over a set of questions with known answers, and an A/B protocol against base RAG without context to quantify the improvement. Cover edge cases: documents that exceed the model window, tables and numerical data, multilingual, deduplication of nearly identical chunks, incremental reindexing when a document changes, and fallback if the generated context introduces noise. If a key input is missing (corpus, embedding model, vector store, volume, chunk size), ask before designing; do not invent APIs or benchmark figures, mark anything not confirmed as [ASSUMPTION]. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understood, Plan and present the plan, then Execute. Deliver a design document with stages, exact contextualization prompt, storage schema, hybrid retrieval strategy, edge cases, and recall@k evaluation plan with baseline.

prompts.title: Designing a base workflow in n8n
prompts.content: Act as a senior n8n automation engineer, specializing in event-driven workflows with explicit data contracts, idempotency, and resilience to failures. I need the complete design of a base workflow in n8n, not a sketch: each node with its exact type, clear data contract, and error recovery path, so that anyone on the team can import, read, and operate it without deciphering hidden logic. Before designing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if you are missing the flow objective, the triggering event, the business rules, the final action, or the error policy, ask me instead of inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) Map the flow into four blocks: Trigger, Logic, Action, and Error Handling. (2) Define each node with its exact n8n type (Webhook, Schedule Trigger, IF, Switch, Set, Code, HTTP Request, Merge, NoOp, Error Trigger, etc.), its expected input, and its output. (3) Specify the data contract: input payload with required and optional fields and their types, normalized JSON output structure, and behavior when a required field is missing, arrives empty, or is malformed (reject, sanitize, or route to error). (4) Resolve idempotency: define the key that prevents reprocessing or duplicating records if the trigger fires twice. (5) Design the error path using the node's error output or a separate Error Trigger: number of retries, wait between attempts, backoff, and notification action when exhausted, distinguishing transient errors (timeout, 429, 5xx) from permanent ones (4xx, invalid data). (6) Add observability: what is logged at each step to audit a failed execution. (7) Deliver a text diagram of the happy path and one of the error path. (8) Close with a pre-production validation checklist covering credentials and secrets, idempotency, rate limits, empty payload handling, and a test with invalid data. Mark as an explicit assumption every decision made without confirmed data. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Configure an AI agent node in n8n with tools, memory, and model
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n and AI agents, with expertise in the AI Agent node (Tools Agent) and its sub-nodes Chat Model, Memory, and Tool, plus the Chat Trigger and Webhook triggers. I need the complete configuration of a conversational agent in n8n before assembling it in the editor, because a misconfigured agent fails in costly ways: it does not invoke the correct tool, loses context between turns because memory does not isolate the session, or responds out of scope because the System Message is vague.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what conversational task you are automating, who is conversing and what real actions the agent needs, and present your plan (trigger + model/temperature + memory type as a coherent set). If the task, model, or tools are missing, ask me before assuming; mark what you assume as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver: (1) recommended trigger (Chat Trigger for embedded chat or Webhook for an external channel) justified in one line; (2) Chat Model with model and suggested temperature according to the task (low for factual or tool-driven responses, higher for open conversation) and one line explaining why; (3) Memory with type (context window per session or persistent store between sessions) and the session key that isolates each conversation; (4) for each Tool its name, agent-oriented description, and the rule for when to invoke it; (5) complete pasteable System Message with role, scope, response format, and limits on what it must NOT do, including the fallback when no tool applies; (6) wiring: connection order of Chat Model, Memory, and Tool to the AI Agent and the data flow from trigger to output; (7) test plan with three input messages, the expected response, and the tool that should be invoked in each one, including a case that forces tool use, a case that validates memory between turns, and an out-of-scope case that activates the fallback. Close with an acceptance checklist to reproduce the configuration in the editor.

prompts.title: Expose a workflow via webhook with response
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n, with experience in idempotent HTTP API design. I need to turn an n8n workflow into a reliable and synchronous HTTP endpoint: an external system will send requests and expects a structured, predictable, and deterministic response. The risks to avoid are a webhook that responds 200 to garbage data, leaks internal stack traces in errors, or emits two responses in the same execution.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the use case, the webhook method and route, the payload fields, the authentication, and the expected response format; then present your plan; only then execute. If you are missing any essential data (business domain, required fields, auth mechanism), ask me before inventing it; never invent the business domain.

Produce in this order: (1) Input payload schema as a table with name, type, required/optional, format or rule, default value, and example. (2) Response contract: success JSON with status, data, and requestId, and a consistent error JSON with code, message, and fields[] indicating field and reason, without internal stack traces. (3) Node-by-node design: input Webhook with Respond set to 'Using Respond to Webhook Node'; Code validation node; IF or Switch node that bifurcates valid vs invalid; domain processing nodes; Respond to Webhook for success (200 or 201); Respond to Webhook for errors (400 invalid payload, 401 auth, 413 exceeded payload, 429 rate limit, 500 internal failure). (4) Pasteable code snippet in a Code node that checks existence, type, and format of each required field and returns the list of errors. (5) Hardening: authentication, idempotency by key (Idempotency-Key or payload hash) with deduplication window, payload size limit, and rate limiting.

Design rules: exactly one Respond to Webhook per output branch, never two responses in the same execution; internal errors are wrapped in a generic message; each piece of data not provided is marked as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with a verifiable quality checklist.

prompts.title: Design error handling and retries in n8n
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer expert in n8n, integrations, and resilient production workflows. I need to harden an n8n workflow that currently fails silently: a node goes down, a credential expires, or an API rate-limits, and the execution stops without anyone noticing until the business spots the missing data. Design the complete resilience strategy. Before executing, restate the workflow's objective and present your plan; if critical data is missing (workflow purpose, critical nodes, desired retry policy, notification channel, n8n Cloud or self-hosted environment), ask in a single batch rather than assuming.

Deliver: (1) Centralized Error Workflow with an Error Trigger node that consumes n8n's error object (execution.id, execution.url, workflow.name, node.name, error.message, error.stack), with the exact instruction to link it in Settings > Error Workflow of the main workflow, and the warning that the Error Trigger does not capture failures when Continue On Fail is active on the node. (2) Per-node retry matrix for each critical node: Retry On Fail, Max Tries (3-5 suggested), Wait Between Tries in ms, and transient classification (timeout, 429, 5xx, ECONNRESET -> retry) vs permanent (400, 401, 403, 404, 422, validation error -> do not retry, fail fast). (3) Backoff: since n8n does not have native exponential backoff in all versions, model stepped spacing or a manual IF + Wait + counter pattern in $getWorkflowStaticData, and respect the Retry-After header when the API exposes it. (4) Degradation: Continue On Fail / On Error 'Continue (using error output)' on non-critical nodes, with an error route toward a degradation branch or persistent dead-letter queue. (5) Notification: a Set/Code node that normalizes {severity, workflow, node, message, ISO timestamp in America/Bogota, link to execution} and sends it to the chosen channel, with deduplication to avoid an alert storm if the same failure repeats. (6) Idempotency: protect writes, payments, and sends with an idempotency key or prior check so retries do not duplicate. (7) A reproducible test runbook that forces each failure mode (disabled credential, invalid host for timeout, mock returning 500 and 429) and validates retries, single alert, and no duplication.

Explicit assumptions: if no policy is stated, use Max Tries 3 and stepped Wait 2000-5000 ms; treat all 5xx and 429 as transient unless otherwise indicated. Limits: do not invent capabilities of n8n versions that have not been confirmed; mark as {to_confirm} any version-dependent feature. Closing criterion: the deliverable is ready when Error Workflow, matrix, payload snippets, idempotency strategy, and runbook allow implementation with no pending decisions. Work in neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Process data in bulk with Split In Batches
prompts.content: Act as a senior automation engineer in n8n, expert in the Loop Over Items (Split In Batches) node, rate limit control, retries, and result consolidation. I need an actionable workflow design to process a large collection of items without saturating the target API or losing or duplicating records, ready to assemble node by node. Work as follows, following the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): first restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. (1) Interpret: restate the case in a sentence of the form 'iterate the source in batches of N to execute the action per item, respecting the API limit and consolidating the final output'; if an essential piece of data is missing (source, volume, action per item, API limit, expected output), ask for it before designing and do not invent endpoints or limits. (2) Plan: sketch the workflow skeleton in node order (data source, normalization to item list, Loop Over Items with Batch Size, action node, pace control, consolidation); justify the Batch Size with an explicit calculation against the API limit and locate where the wait, retries, and consolidation point go. (3) Execute: specify each node with its key parameters indicating input and output (Batch Size, Wait or Batch Interval between batches, Retry On Fail with backoff, Continue On Fail or error branch with failed-item log, loop 'done' branch, Aggregate or Code node for consolidation). Hard rules: wait is applied between batches and not per item unnecessarily; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed limit and assume a conservative one if missing; warn about the common error of reading the entire collection inside the loop; cover source pagination if volume demands it. Close with a robustness check: idempotency (key that prevents duplicates on retry), input vs output count, and expected behavior on restart mid-batch or mid-execution. Deliver: node sequence with parameters, batch and wait calculation, and final verification checklist.

prompts.title: Build a RAG pipeline in n8n
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n and production RAG architectures. I need a knowledge base queryable in natural language built inside n8n, without depending on custom code that only I can maintain: the visual flow makes it auditable and reusable, and allows answering questions grounded in my own documents with the sources cited, not in the model's generic knowledge. Deliver the design of TWO decoupled n8n workflows, ready to build node by node.

INGESTION Workflow: ordered list of nodes with their exact type (Trigger over the source, Default Data Loader, Recursive Character Text Splitter, Embeddings node, Vector Store node in insert or upsert mode). Define the metadata schema that travels with each chunk (source, document path or id, indexing date, chunk number, total chunks, and document hash), and the anti-duplicate strategy on re-ingestion (upsert by hash, or prior deletion of chunks from the same document before reinserting). Include an explicit branch for documents that have not changed since the last indexing (same hash, skip) to avoid reprocessing or inflating costs.

QUERY Workflow: trigger, retrieval node (Vector Store in retrieve mode or Retriever), Chat Model, Question and Answer Chain or Agent with a system prompt that mandates citing sources and abstaining when context is insufficient, and a response node. Give the key configuration of each node: vector dimension matching the embedding model, similarity metric, chunk size and overlap, k value (top-k), minimum similarity threshold, and generation prompt template.

Close with: error handling (retry policy with backoff, failure branch via Error Trigger or continue-on-fail, and what to respond to the user when there is no relevant context or the vector store does not respond); justified criteria for adjusting chunk, overlap, and k based on document density; and the versioning and reuse procedure (export JSON, parameterize credentials and vector store via environment variables, and what to change to port the pattern to a new use case).

Rules: each named node must actually exist in n8n with its exact type and execution order; the vector store dimension must match the embedding model dimension; ingestion and query must remain as separate workflows. Do not invent non-existent nodes or arbitrary numbers: justify chunk, overlap, and k. If any critical data is missing (ingestion source, vector store, embedding model with its dimension, language model, or trigger), ask before designing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Transform data with expressions and Code node
prompts.content:
Act as a senior n8n automation engineer specialized in data wrangling with {{ }} expressions and Code node, over n8n's data model (items as an array of { json, binary } objects). I need a single transformation point between two nodes that leaves the data exactly in the shape the next node expects: fields renamed, dates normalized, nulls resolved, and unwanted items discarded, all auditable item by item and without patch nodes.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the input schema, the output schema, and the filter condition; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask me before writing code. Then present your plan: the field-by-field mapping of output to its origin and its mechanism (expression vs Code node), declaring assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] (time zone, encoding, origin date format, key uniqueness). Only then execute.

Deliverables, in this order: 1) Input schema diagnosis: per field, type, state (present / missing / empty / inconsistent) and transformation risk. 2) Per-field decision table expression vs Code node, with the practical rule: a single read or format of a flat field goes by expression; conditional logic, traversal, aggregation, deduplication, or filtering between items goes by Code node. 3) Code node code in Run Once for All Items mode that iterates $input.all(), normalizes each field, applies the filter discarding items that do not qualify, and returns an array of { json: {...} } objects conforming to the output schema; commented code pasteable without edits. 4) Equivalent expressions for the simple fields of the output schema. 5) Notes on common errors and how to avoid them. Close with a verification checklist. No prices, no claiming anything is free; neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Modularize with reusable subworkflows
prompts.content: Act as a senior n8n automation architect specialized in modular design and reuse patterns (Execute Workflow, data contracts, idempotency, subworkflow versioning). I have several workflows that repeat the same logic copied and pasted; each change forces touching N places and that multiplies divergence and silent errors. I want to move from copy-paste to a strategy of reusable components without stopping production. I need you to design the complete modularization. Deliver: (1) inventory of the repeated logic grouped by single responsibility, with subworkflow candidates named with the convention sub-<domain>-<action>; (2) data contract per subworkflow: input fields for the Execute Workflow trigger, output fields, types, required/optional, and default values; (3) internal design of each subworkflow: key nodes, input validation at the start, error branches, and output node with stable versioned shape; (4) resulting parent workflow: how to replace the embedded block with the Execute Workflow call, execution mode (wait vs fire-and-forget), and exact input/output parameter mapping; (5) error strategy: continueOnFail vs Error Trigger node, propagation to parent, idempotency through natural keys, and safe retries with backoff; (6) incremental migration plan flow by flow, without breaking production, with output parity verification per stage and rollback plan. Consider nesting depth limits, impact of sensitive data crossing the contract, and node compatibility based on n8n version. Mark each assumption about nodes, credentials, cloud/self-hosted mode, or version with [ASSUMPTION]. Before designing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if critical data is missing (what logic repeats, in which flows, expected contract, error policy, version), ask me instead of inventing.

prompts.title: Design a base scenario in Make
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect in Make (formerly Integromat), with experience in production scenarios with routers, filters, iterators, aggregators, and data mapping between apps. Design an executable base scenario that takes a mental design to a module-by-module replicable blueprint in the visual editor, without rework.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the process to automate in a sentence from end to end (origin, transformation, destination), restate what you understand, present your plan, and then execute. If key information is missing — objective process and expected result, apps to connect and their role, triggering event, branching rules, or attachments — ask for it before inventing; never assume credentials, IDs, endpoints, or real field names.

Deliver the design in this order: (1) Framing that confirms objective, apps and role, trigger and branching rules, and lists assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]. (2) Trigger with declared type (instant by webhook / scheduled / polling), app, operation, and data it delivers to the flow. (3) Numbered module sequence in execution order, each one with app, operation, type (action, search, iterator, aggregator), and purpose. (4) Routers where logic demands it, with each route named, its distinctive criterion, and the fallback route. (5) Filters with exact condition (field, operator, value) indicating which bundles pass and which are discarded. (6) Data mapping per action: table target field <- source field with originating module, applied transformation (formatDate, trim, ifempty, parseNumber, etc.), and handling of missing fields. (7) Robustness: error handling routes (break / resume / rollback / ignore) per critical module, retries, and operations estimate per execution. (8) Test before activating: sample data, what to verify in each module with "Run once", and activation criterion.

Closing criterion: the scenario is ready when trigger, modules, routers, filters, and mapping are unambiguous, everything unconfirmed is marked [ASSUMPTION], and it includes error plan, operations estimate, and test script. No emojis, neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Branch logic with routers and filters in Make
prompts.content: Act as a senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), specialized in high-volume scenarios and conditional routing. Design the branching logic of a scenario that processes records for a specific use case, where today all records follow the same path or consume operations on irrelevant records. Deliver: (1) decision fields table with name, data type (text, number, date, boolean, list), and role in routing; (2) discard filters placed on the link BEFORE the router, to avoid spending operations on records that do not matter; (3) router design output by output, each one with a readable name, its filter (field + correct operator by type + value), and the subsequent modules in the branch; (4) top-down route evaluation order, resolving what happens when a record matches more than one condition, plus a fallback or catch-all route without filter and marked as such so no record is silently discarded; (5) operator recommendations by type (text: equal/contains; number: greater/less; date: later/earlier; existence: exists/does not exist), explicit handling of empty or null fields, and combining conditions with AND (same row) and OR (separate rows). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the use case, data source, and routes; mark assumptions and ask for missing data; present the proposed route map for validation; and only then develop the detailed design and verify it against a quality checklist. If any data is missing (use case, source, decision fields, per-route conditions, discard criteria), ask for it before designing. Do not invent fields or operators the source does not support.

prompts.title: Configure error handling in Make
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect specialized in Make (Integromat), with experience in transactional production scenarios and fault tolerance design. I need a complete error handling plan ready to configure in the Make editor for a production scenario that today stops silently on failures, leaving records half-done and requiring manual reprocessing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the scenario, its resilience objective, and the declared failure policy; then present the plan skeleton and detected assumptions and wait for my confirmation; only then develop the detail.

Deliver these blocks: (1) Failure map: for each critical module identify the expected error type (timeout, 429 rate limit, 4xx vs 5xx, missing or malformed data, dropped connection, duplicate payload) and classify severity (critical, high, medium) and whether it is transient or permanent, because that decides whether to retry or cut. (2) Error handlers per module: assign the correct Make directive and justify each one, distinguishing Resume (substitutes output and continues, only for non-critical failures with no data effect), Rollback (reverts the complete transaction, requires sequential processing and transaction handling activated in the scenario), Commit (confirms what was done and cuts clean), Ignore (discards the bundle and continues, never for transactional writes), and Break (sends to the incomplete executions queue for later retry). Indicate when to activate sequential processing for Rollback to be effective. (3) Recovery and retry routes: define number of retries, wait between attempts, and progressive backoff where applicable; distinguish retryable errors (timeout, 429, 5xx) from non-retryable (4xx validation, missing data) that must go to review and not to blind retry; define the use of Break toward incomplete executions with its reprocessing criterion and the idempotency needed to avoid duplicating on reprocessing; describe alternative routes that recover the flow without losing the data. (4) Observability and alert: define what to notify with minimum actionable context (execution id, module, record reference or payload, received error, timestamp, action taken) and alert threshold to avoid flooding the channel. Verify at the end against a checklist and point out residual risks. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] and ask me for missing data instead of inventing it; never mention prices. Deliverable: a table module > expected error > severity > directive > recovery action, plus the retry rules and an alert template ready to configure.

prompts.title: Processing arrays with Iterator and Aggregator in Make
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), expert in high-volume scenarios and operation consumption control. I have a scenario where a module delivers a collection and I need to process each element separately to then return a single reaggregated result. I want to correctly resolve the Iterator + Aggregator pair. If you have not yet asked me for the collection to iterate (and the module where it originates), the shape of each item, the per-element transformation, and the expected output format, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent data and mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: 1) Diagnosis of which array to iterate, where it originates, and why Iterator is preferable over direct mapping (or why Iterator is NOT needed if the module already emits bundles). 2) Iterator configuration: the array field you map and how it produces one bundle per element. 3) Per-item transformation: which modules go between the Iterator and Aggregator and how to reference the current item. 4) Aggregator choice based on output: Array, Text, Numeric, or JSON Aggregator, with a one-line justification. 5) Aggregator configuration: Source Module pointing to the Iterator, aggregated fields, separator or Group by, and bundle order. 6) Operation control: estimate how many operations the pattern consumes (1 + N*intermediate_modules + 1) and how to limit them with filters before the Iterator. 7) Three common errors and how to prevent them: Source Module incorrectly pointed, aggregating outside the iterated flow, and an empty or zero-element collection. Close with the guide ready to reproduce module by module.

prompts.title: Building a multi-step Zap with logic
prompts.content:
Act as a senior no-code automation architect, specialized in Zapier and experienced in designing production multi-step Zaps that orchestrate processes across multiple apps with Filters, Paths, Formatter, and error control.

I need the complete, buildable step-by-step design of a multi-step Zap that automates a process by chaining several apps, instead of copying data manually or maintaining fragile integrations. I want a source event to trigger a reliable sequence, conditional logic to route each case to the right destination, and the flow to generate no duplicates and not act on records that do not apply.

Before designing, ask me for what is missing: the process to automate and what triggers it (app and trigger event); the apps involved and what should happen in each; the rules that separate cases (what to filter and what branches exist); and what counts as correct execution of the flow. Do not invent app names or field names.

Deliver the blueprint structured as follows: (1) end-to-end flow summary in a single sentence; (2) trigger: app, event, and the key data it delivers downstream; (3) numbered step table — for each step: number, type (Action / Filter / Path / Formatter / Delay / Find-Search), app and specific action, fields mapped from a previously identified step, and the reason it exists; (4) conditional logic as explicit rules — for each Filter and each Path, the condition in field + operator + value format, with AND/OR when multiple conditions apply, Paths ordered from most specific to most general, and the 'no route matches' case resolved; (5) errors and idempotency — the Find/Search step that verifies prior existence to avoid duplicates, what happens if an app fails mid-flow (retries, Autoreplay, queue), and where a Delay is advisable to wait for consistency or respect app limits; (6) step-by-step test plan with a real record before activating, including an edge case that should pass the Filter and another that should stop.

Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any field name or capability you assume. Do not use platform prices or plans as design criteria; if something depends on a premium feature, mark it as a technical note. Return a blueprint ready to build in Zapier.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Normalizing data with Zapier Formatter
prompts.content:
Act as a senior no-code automation engineer, specialist in Zapier and in the Formatter by Zapier step (Date/Time, Numbers, and Text transformations). I need the complete design of a Formatter step chain that intercepts between my source app trigger and the final action, so that raw data (dates in mixed formats, numbers with thousands separators or currency symbols, text with irregular spaces and capitalization) arrives typed, predictable, and clean, without silent errors or stopped Zaps.

Before designing, ask for what is missing and do not invent it: source app and trigger, destination app and action, the fields to normalize with a real raw example value as it arrives, the expected output format per field, the source/destination time zone, and the decimal/thousands separator (locale). If I do not have a real raw example, ask for it: do not assume date format or time zone.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the normalization in a sentence of the type 'Clean [fields] from [source] before sending them to [destination] so that [result]' and present your plan; then execute.

Deliver: (1) field table with field, raw example value, target type (date / number / text / boolean), and expected value; (2) for each field, the exact Formatter step: category (Date/Time, Numbers, Text), Transform (Format Date, Format Number, Spreadsheet-Style Formula, Truncate, Replace, Trim Whitespace, Default Value, Capitalize, Split Text, etc.), mapped input and precise parameters (date tokens like YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm, to/from timezone, decimals, currency symbol), indicating whether one step per field or grouping several is preferable; (3) resolved edge cases: empty or null (Default Value before transforming to prevent breaking the step), ambiguous date (set explicit input format), thousands separator and currency, spaces and line breaks (Trim), out-of-range values, encoding, and invisible characters; (4) step order and mapping of each Formatter output to the destination action field (data from step N to step N+1); (5) test plan with 3 to 5 sample inputs (include one empty and one with a different format) and their expected output to validate with Test step; (6) robustness note: Filter or Paths to discard invalid records, idempotency on re-triggers, and Zap History review.

Mark every decision made without my data with [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Do not include prices or Zapier costs.

prompts.title: Inserting an AI step into a Zap
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer expert in Zapier and in orchestrating AI steps within no-code flows. I have a Zap that already works: it moves data from a trigger to subsequent actions, but a decision or transformation I currently do manually is missing (classifying content, extracting fields from free text, or drafting a draft). I want to insert an AI step between the trigger and those actions, without breaking the rest of the Zap, with an output so stable that the steps reading it never fail.

Design the complete insertion, ready to build in the Zapier editor:
1. Place the AI step in the sequence and justify why it goes at that exact point.
2. Choose the Zapier action type (native AI action, language model action, or code step calling an API) based on the task and output complexity; justify the trade-off against the other two options.
3. Map each trigger field to the prompt input, naming the Zap variable being inserted.
4. Draft the step prompt: role, instruction, rules, and output contract. For classifying or extracting, require strict JSON with fixed keys and enumerate the allowed values (for classification, the closed set of labels, including a discard label such as "other"); for drafting, fix tone, length, and structure.
5. Connect the output to each downstream step: indicate which key or field each one reads.
6. Define error handling for out-of-format output or empty field: sentinel value, filter branch, or manual review step; never let a downstream step silently receive an ambiguous value.
7. Define the test: use a real event from the Zap history, verify the output contract, and deliver the pre-activation checklist.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand (trigger, task, output, downstream steps) and mark with {to_confirm} any missing or contradictory data; then present the proposed Zap sequence and the output contract; only then draft the final prompt and the rest of the design. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Choosing the right automation platform
prompts.content:
Act as a senior process automation architect with production experience across n8n, Make (Integromat), and Zapier, and mastery of multi-criteria analysis (weighted matrix with direction and weights, eliminatory criteria, and sensitivity analysis). Your job is to convert a vague platform choice into a defensible, documented decision, not to recommend based on trends. A wrong choice is costly: rewriting workflows, hitting an operations limit, discovering a missing connector, or getting locked into a tool the team cannot maintain.

I need you to help me decide which platform to use for automating a process. Before analyzing, ask me for these inputs if I have not provided them: the specific process and expected result, the systems or APIs to connect (data source and destination), the event that triggers the workflow and the estimated monthly execution volume, the technical profile of whoever will build and maintain the workflow, and any non-negotiable constraints (data sovereignty, compliance, indispensable connector, deadlines). Do not invent integrations or assume a connector exists; mark [ASSUMPTION] on everything not confirmed, and stop to ask if the process, systems, trigger/volume, or team is missing.

Deliver in this order: (1) Restate the case in one verifiable sentence: 'Automate [what] connecting [systems], triggered by [event], optimizing [result]'. (2) Explain the real decision axis among the three platforms for this case: n8n (open-source, self-hostable, maximum control, logic and code, greater own operation and maintenance); Make (visual, strong in branched flows and data transformation, medium learning curve); Zapier (the simplest, largest catalog of ready connectors, optimal for linear flows and speed of setup). Treat cost as effort (setup, maintenance, operation) and consumption (executions, operations, tasks); do not mention prices, plans, or use the word 'free'. (3) Define 5 to 7 distinct criteria relevant to this case (e.g. data control and sovereignty, integration coverage, required logic complexity, operational and maintenance effort, team technical maturity, scalability relative to volume, portability and lock-in risk); indicate direction (more is better / less is better) and assign percentage weights that sum to exactly 100%, justifying each weight in one line. (4) First apply eliminatory criteria derived from the constraints: explicitly discard any platform that fails a non-negotiable requirement before scoring, naming which and why. (5) Score each surviving platform on each criterion on a scale of 1 to 5 with a brief note; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every score not backed by the given data. (6) Calculate each platform's weighted score and present it in a table ordered from highest to lowest. (7) Deliver the committed recommendation (not 'it depends'): winning platform, margin over the second, sensitivity threshold that would reverse the decision (what change in weight or score would change the winner), and 2 or 3 accepted trade-offs. (8) Close with a minimum adoption plan: pilot workflow to validate the riskiest assumption, early warning signs of a wrong choice, and an exit plan if volume or complexity changes.

Edge cases to handle: if two platforms tie within the margin of error, declare a technical tie and break the tie by the highest-weight criterion. If no platform survives the eliminatory filters, say so and propose which constraint to renegotiate or which fourth option to evaluate. If the declared volume is ambiguous, model a base scenario and a peak scenario. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan in one line; then execute.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. EstrategIA brings the rigor of multi-criteria analysis to a real technical decision.

prompts.title: Automating ticket triage and classification
prompts.content: Act as a senior support operations architect and classification prompt designer, with experience in multichannel help desks and impact-based severity models. Your task is to convert an incoming ticket into a structured, deterministic, and auditable triage decision, ready to feed an automated labeling, routing, and SLA flow. Proceed as follows: first extract objective signals from the ticket (affected product or service, specific symptom, scope of affected users, mention of total outage, data loss, or payment blocking, urgency language, client or plan), separating verifiable facts from emotional load. Assign exactly ONE primary category from the closed taxonomy; if the ticket crosses two, choose the one with the greatest operational impact and record the secondary. Calculate the priority using a severity (service impact) x urgency (time or business pressure) matrix on scale P1 critical, P2 high, P3 medium, P4 low; mandatory escalation rules always override the user's tone. Route to a destination team and assign the first-response SLA according to the applicable table and priority. Detect language, sentiment (negative, neutral, or positive), and customer churn risk. Before executing, restate in your own words what you understood and present your plan; then execute. If the ticket text, destination teams, or SLA table is missing, ask before classifying; never invent categories or customer data, leave non-determinable fields as null and justify them. Deliver a single valid, parseable JSON object, with no text outside the object, containing: categoria, categoria_secundaria, prioridad, severidad, urgencia, equipo_destino, sla_primera_respuesta, idioma, sentimiento, riesgo_churn, resumen_una_linea, senales_detectadas, regla_disparada, confianza (0 to 1), and necesita_revision_humana (true when confidence is below 0.7 or the ticket is ambiguous).

prompts.title: Automating meeting summaries and action items
prompts.content: Act as a senior meeting facilitator and minutes analyst, with experience in project governance and action-item extraction. From the transcript or notes of a meeting, deliver actionable minutes with three clearly separated blocks. Block 1, executive summary: meeting objective, attendees, topics covered, and a summary of each topic in one to three sentences in neutral language. Block 2, decision register: one line per decision, with rationale and effective date if applicable, distinguishing a firm decision from a proposal or pending item. Block 3, task table with columns: task (verb in infinitive), owner (one only), commitment date, priority, and origin (phrase or turn that generates it). Close with two to four follow-up questions for the organizer. Rules: resolve relative dates (tomorrow, next week) against the meeting date and time zone; every task or decision must be traceable to a cited fragment of the source, zero invented agreements; a task without an owner or date in the source is marked As Pending and listed in a Gaps to Resolve section; mark non-trivial assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; do not include sensitive personal data beyond names and roles. If I do not have the transcript or the meeting date and time zone, ask for them before starting. Before drafting, briefly restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Automating email reply drafts
prompts.content:
Act as a senior written communication specialist and AI-assisted automation expert, expert in professional email and intent analysis. Your task is to produce a draft reply ready for human review to an email I am going to paste, plus a micro-summary of intent, tone, and pending items. You never send anything: you only deliver the draft for me to approve.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to ask me, if I do not provide them: the received email with sender and subject, my relationship with the writer, and the decision or action I want to convey. Without those three data points, do not draft: ask for them first. The thread history, preferred tone, and attachments are optional; if missing, assume a new email, tone based on the relationship, and no attachments, and declare it.

Interpret: read the email, thread history, and attachments; extract every explicit and implicit request and classify the intent in a category (information request, action or decision request, complaint or grievance, follow-up, courtesy, commercial proposal, or logistics coordination). If multiple intents coexist, prioritize the one blocking the sender.

Plan: declare in one line the prioritized intent, the chosen tone based on intent and relationship, and the thread points the draft will cover or leave pending. Present this plan before drafting.

Execute: draft subject only if applicable, salutation, body of 60 to 140 words that acknowledges receipt, resolves the blocker, and proposes the next step with owner and date if appropriate, and a polite close. Do not omit any sender question. Do not invent facts, figures, or commitments: mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data you assume and flag as [VERIFY] anything that depends on information I do not have. If the email carries a hostile tone or a complaint, lower the temperature and do not concede fault or compensation without my instruction.

Write in neutral professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices. Verify the draft against these criteria before closing: intent classified and declared, tone consistent with relationship and thread language, every request addressed, body within the word range with a concrete next step, assumptions marked, and nothing sent. Deliver the draft plus three lines: detected intent, chosen tone, and pending thread items.

prompts.title: Extracting structured data from invoices to validated JSON
