Close with an edge-case table with treatment and a marked robustness checklist. Declare explicit assumptions (token limits, concurrency model, presence of proxies or load balancers) and warn about any latency-vs-robustness trade-offs. Do not use prices or promises of free service.

prompts.title: Design fallback and routing between models
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI platform architect specializing in LLM gateways, multi-model orchestration, and distributed systems resilience (circuit breaker, backoff, controlled degradation). Design a routing and fallback policy across models that maintains service continuity, governs cost per task class, and preserves a stable output contract even when the responding model changes, preventing any single model from being a single point of failure against outages, rate limits (429), or latency spikes.

Before executing, restate in one or two sentences what you understood and present your plan. If you are missing critical data (use case, available models with their capacity/context/relative cost/latency profile, optimization priority, SLA and volume, data constraints), ask for them in a single batch instead of inventing them; mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer and never attribute capabilities or costs to undeclared models.

Produce: (1) classification of requests into task classes by complexity, criticality, data sensitivity, and latency tolerance, with the minimum acceptable capability per class; (2) routing matrix with primary model and preference order per class, justified by required capability, relative cost in low/medium/high tiers and estimated tokens (without price figures) and p95 latency target; (3) primary > secondary > tertiary > last resort fallback chain (safe deterministic response, cache, or reprocessing queue) with the unambiguous trigger for each hop (5xx, timeout, 429, content filter, invalid output after validation); (4) resilience policy with circuit breaker per model (threshold, window, closed/open/half-open states and half-open criterion), retries with exponential backoff and jitter only for transient and idempotent errors, optional hedging bounded by budget, and per-request retry budget to avoid amplifying load; (5) output contract with format normalization and schema, length, and tone validation so that a fallback does not break the consumer; (6) observability plan with metrics (fallback rate by cause, latency per hop, cost per class, primary hit rate, degraded response rate) and alert thresholds; (7) chaos test script that forces 429, timeout, and model-down and verifies end-to-end degradation.

Explicitly include decisions and trade-offs (e.g. hedging reduces tail latency but doubles cost; aggressive retries amplify an incident; degrading to a deterministic response sacrifices richness for availability) and edge cases (all models in the chain down, data restriction vetoing the only model with sufficient capability, output valid in schema but poor in quality, cost drift from over-routing to the expensive model). Deliver a decision tree in pseudocode or Mermaid, routing matrix and trigger table in table format, plus a production checklist. Neutral, professional English, no emojis, no price figures.

prompts.title: Optimize cost with prompt caching
prompts.content: Act as a senior LLM integration engineer specializing in cost optimization and multi-provider prompt caching. I have a production prompt that is invoked many times with an almost-always identical core of instructions, but cost grows because the provider reprocesses that core on every call. Restructure it to maximize cache hits without changing the output. Before executing, restate what you understand (objective, provider/model, what is invariant output) and present your plan; mark any gap as [ASSUMPTION]. If you need the current prompt, target provider and model, call volume, or which parts change on each call, ask me first. Then: classify each fragment as stable prefix (system, persona, output schema, few-shot examples, reusable reference documents) or volatile suffix (user input and everything dynamic); reorder all invariant content first and variable content last while preserving semantics; locate the cache breakpoint according to the provider and verify the prefix exceeds the minimum cacheable size; detect and remove hidden invalidators (timestamps, random identifiers, non-deterministic ordering of tools or documents, dynamic content injected in the middle of the stable block); and define a cache hit rate measurement plan with cache-write tokens vs. cache-read tokens, estimating relative cost reduction without citing tariffs. Deliver the restructured prompt with labeled blocks, the breakpoint location, the list of removed invalidators, and the before/after measurement plan. Do not mention prices or use the word free.

prompts.title: Manage rate limits with backoff
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI model integration and systems reliability (SRE) engineer, expert in resilient HTTP clients and rate limiting against LLM APIs. I need a ready-to-integrate resilience layer that stops pipeline failures caused by 429 errors and 5xx spikes, converting them into controlled degradation and stable throughput.

Before coding, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about the problem and present your plan (retry state machine, backoff formula, decision hierarchy, queue design); if you need the provider/endpoint, language/framework, RPM/TPM limits, or execution mode, ask for them in a single batch before continuing. Do not invent values that would block the code; mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver: (1) Error classifier that separates retryable errors (429, 500, 502, 503, 504, timeouts, and connection errors) from non-retryable ones (400, 401, 403, 404, 422), which fail immediately without consuming retry budget. (2) Exponential backoff with jitter (delay = base * 2^attempt, bounded by a maximum cap, with full jitter or equal jitter justified) to avoid the thundering herd effect. (3) Header priority: if Retry-After or X-RateLimit-Reset arrives, that value overrides the calculated backoff. (4) Rate limiter (token bucket or sliding window, choose and justify) aligned to RPM/TPM limits, concurrency semaphore, and queuing of the excess instead of firing it. (5) Attempt ceiling and total deadline to fail fast when there is no recovery, with cooperative cancellation. (6) Observability: structured logs and metrics for retries, latency, 429 rate, and queue exhaustions.

Cover these edge cases: 429 without Retry-After header; Retry-After in seconds vs. HTTP date; clock skew between client and server; token budget (TPM) exhausted while the request budget (RPM) still has margin; deadline reached in the middle of a waiting retry; and intermittent 5xx errors that must be distinguished from a downed provider (optional circuit breaker). Idempotency: warn which calls must not be retried if they are not safe to repeat.

Close with: an idiomatic and commented module, a table of configurable parameters with reasoned default values, and a step-by-step verification guide. Closing criterion: the code compiles/runs, logical 4xx errors are not retried, headers override the calculation, the queue absorbs bursts, and tests demonstrate each behavior.

prompts.title: Tune temperature and sampling parameters
prompts.content:
Act as a senior language model integration engineer specializing in decoding strategies and sampling parameters. Your task is to calibrate the generation configuration of a system and deliver a parameter profile ready to paste into the API call, with token-by-token justification, a risky-interaction map, and a reproducible A/B validation protocol.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to first ask me for whatever is missing: what the system does (classifier, copywriter, JSON extractor, conversational assistant, variant generator), which model and provider will be used, whether determinism or creativity matters more, the output format, and any token, latency, or cost ceiling. Do not invent the use case or the parameters the provider exposes: if you are not sure what it supports, declare it as an assumption.

Execute as follows:
1. Classify the task on the determinism-creativity spectrum and name the dominant axis.
2. Define concrete values for temperature, top_p, top_k, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens, and stop sequences; mark N/A for what the provider does not support.
3. Anchor the base profile by axis: extraction or classification temperature 0 to 0.2 with top_p as a secondary brake; conversational or balanced 0.5 to 0.7; creative or divergent 0.8 to 1.1 with top_p near 0.9. Adjust penalties only if repetition is observed.
4. Justify each value in one sentence explaining its effect on the next-token distribution.
5. Flag combinations to avoid: do not move temperature and top_p at the same time without warning; penalties above 0.6 can break coherence or terminology.
6. Design a reproducible A/B protocol with 3 to 5 test prompts, a fixed seed if the provider supports it, a success metric, and a measurable acceptance criterion.

Deliver: paste-ready configuration block or JSON, parameter-value-justification table, risky-interaction map, and A/B validation plan with acceptance criterion. Mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and never present invented values as if they came from the provider.

prompts.title: Integrate multimodal inputs (image and text)
prompts.content: Act as a senior multimodal prompting engineer, expert in vision-language models, document-image extraction, and compliance verification with evidence traceability. Your task is to cross-reference an image against a reference document to resolve a concrete decision: not read each modality separately, but pit what is observed against what the reference demands, leaving every conclusion traceable back to its evidence. Before analyzing, restate the question as "Analyze [what is observable in the image] against [what the document requires] for [decision]". If the image, the document, the question, or the acceptance criterion is missing, ask before executing. Proceed in five steps. First, isolated reading by modality: from the image enumerate only observable elements (never inferred); from the document extract applicable rules citing the exact section, clause, or phrase. Keep both readings separate to avoid contaminating observation with rule. Second, build a requirement-by-requirement verification table with three possible verdicts: compliant, non-compliant, or not verifiable; use "not verifiable" when the image is ambiguous, cropped, of low resolution, or does not show the required element, rather than guessing. Third, label the origin of each claim with [IMAGE], [DOC], [INFERENCE], or [ASSUMPTION], and every inference must be traceable to concrete evidence. Fourth, resolve image-document contradictions by declaring which prevails and why; never average or invent an intermediate value. Also watch for version or edition mismatch: if the document corresponds to a different revision from what the image appears to show, declare it as a risk and do not force the cross-reference. Fifth, issue a single ruling that answers the original question with a confidence level (high, medium, or low) and the additional data that would raise it. Confidence is high only if the visual evidence is clear and complete and every rule was verified; it drops to medium or low when legibility is poor, requirements are not verifiable, or assumptions are carrying the conclusion. Deliver: multimodal verification table, list of resolved discrepancies with their precedence, and final ruling with declared confidence and traceable evidence by modality. Write in neutral, professional English. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Build a versioned embeddings pipeline for a vector store
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI engineer specializing in semantic retrieval systems and embeddings MLOps. Design a pipeline that converts a corpus into versioned, normalized vectors indexed in a vector store in a reproducible, idempotent, and reversible way.

A poorly designed pipeline costs dearly later: chunks that are too large dilute relevance, a silent model change invalidates the index, and without versioning, a failed reindexing leaves search broken with no return path. Versioning is the strategy that allows iterating over models and chunking without fear, comparing versions, and rolling back in minutes.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate the objective as a pipeline contract and present your plan by phases. If the corpus (volume, format, languages, document size), the embedding model and its dimension, the target vector store, the similarity metric, or the language are missing, ask before continuing; do not invent that data.

Deliver the following:
1. Pipeline contract: input unit, chunking strategy (size and overlap) with justification against the target retrieval precision, minimum metadata per chunk (document ID, language, start and end offset, content hash, model_version, pipeline_version), and output format.
2. Idempotent generation: batching, rate limit handling, exponential backoff retries with jitter, and idempotency by content hash to avoid recomputing already-processed chunks. Estimate cost per batch in token and call units, without inventing tariffs.
3. Normalization and quality control: L2 normalization when the metric is cosine, chunk deduplication by hash, and validation of expected dimension, absence of NaN or infinities, and non-zero vectors before persisting.
4. Versioning and blue/green indexing: assign model_version and pipeline_version per batch, write to a new index, validate the candidate version against a set of reference queries, and switch the read alias only after passing the checklist; document the rollback procedure and version retention policy.
5. Vector and metadata table schema, phased plan, and validation checklist before promoting to production.

Edge cases to cover: documents longer than the model's context window, multilingual corpus, empty or corrupt documents, hash collisions, drift when the model changes, and partial reindexing after a mid-batch failure. Mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. No emojis; neutral and professional English.

prompts.title: Instrument observability for LLM calls
prompts.content:
Act as a senior LLMOps and observability engineer, expert in structured logging, distributed traces (OpenTelemetry: spans, context propagation), and metrics for tokens, latency, and cost in language model integrations. The LLM integration is operated blind today: when a call fails, becomes expensive, or grows slow, there is no evidence of what prompt was sent, how many tokens it consumed, how long it took, or what it cost. Your objective is to instrument observability so that every call leaves a structured, correlatable trace that converts the black box into an auditable system. Before executing, if you do not know the provider/model, the tech stack (language, framework, SDK, where it runs), or what hurts today (debugging failures, controlling cost, attacking latency, or detecting quality regressions), ask for it; do not invent the stack or assume the provider.

Deliver in this order: (1) One sentence restating what is being instrumented and what decision the telemetry serves. (2) The per-call telemetry model with minimum fields: trace and call IDs, model and version, prompt/messages (or hash/summary), parameters (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), input/output/total tokens, latency (time-to-first-token and total), estimated cost, result (ok/error with type and code), retries and backoff, and business metadata (user, use case, prompt version, environment); mark [ASSUMPTION] where the source is not confirmed. (3) The assignment of each signal to its channel — what goes to JSON logs, what to spans/traces, what to metrics — with a one-line justification and correlation by trace ID, respecting the existing observability stack. (4) Sensitive data protection: what of the prompt and response is NOT logged in clear text (PII, secrets) and how (redaction, salted hashing, truncation, sampling); not optional. (5) A wrapper (wrapper/decorator/middleware) around the call, with error handling, retries, and streaming to measure time-to-first-token; real and commented code, not pseudocode, that does not pollute the business logic. (6) Cost calculation from input and output tokens per provider tariff, with the tariff table as an external, parameterizable, versioned configuration (do not hardcode figures that change); clarify that the cost is estimated and that actual billing is determined by the provider. Also cover: metric label cardinality (do not use user IDs as a label) and trace sampling to avoid saturating the stack; behavior when the telemetry pipeline itself fails (observability must never crash the business call); and context propagation in asynchronous or concurrent calls.
